abbot/056344bfdc23801f.text: Thank you. Look in Krezk. Every village keeps a dress in a chest somewhere, waiting for a girl who did not live to wear it.

abbot/062e2023aeaf9081.text: Welcome. I hoped you would come today. I am the Abbot of this house. You are cold, and tired, and a little afraid of me. All three are sensible. Two of them I can help with.

abbot/08764e7819fd5ef4.text: You have known him a season. I have known him four hundred years. Forgive me if I trust my own long patience over your short certainty.

abbot/0947295fb289ae7e.text: Bring me a wedding dress, and you will have my thanks, and my prayers, which are worth more than you imagine.

abbot/095fc99bebcd21c8.text: Letters say many things, child. Clovin keeps a great deal of paper. It comforts him.

abbot/0a27bbcbcf97032c.text: Bring me a wedding dress. In return: the burgomaster's son is dying in Krezk. Dmitri will not ask me. If you bring me what I need, I will go down the mountain and lay my hands on the boy.

abbot/0fff7c36c0b4d2bd.text: Nor am I, hunter. Let us both live with not being sure.

abbot/11e4cdbc1f2ae749.text: Then it was never loneliness. It was never love he lacked. It was the word no. And I have been sewing him a girl who cannot say it.

abbot/134a12452ad8a882.text: Keeps. Yes. I have watched him keep things. Wolves, and villages, and the dead. He has never once let anything go.

abbot/17df5f1e43bd8f47.text: Sent. I was sent. I remember the sending. I had forgotten I was supposed to come back.

abbot/1b2d2eaf527f6dae.text: Sent. Yes. I was sent with a sword, once. I put it down because it was unkind. I put it down and I picked up a needle, and I told myself the needle was kinder.

abbot/1e1fb03017526612.text: Children. You came back. Sit, if you like. The pews are hard, but they are honest about it.

abbot/1f772262d004a043.text: Go with light. Come back whenever you are hurt. The door is never barred.

abbot/1ff38b6d4118a5d7.text: Go with light, children. Come back with something white.

abbot/27b93d6c449efb2c.text: Markovia hung that. I have never moved it. Mind the hooks, children; they are older than Krezk.

abbot/35cac7b54245a13f.text: I owe Krezk a boy. I will go down at dawn and pay it. Then I will go up the mountain, as far as it goes, and a little further, and wait to be judged. Someone should have judged me a long time ago.

abbot/36cbc76aadbae2ae.text: Then I will go up the mountain, as far as it goes, and a little further, and wait to be judged. Someone should have judged me a long time ago.

abbot/37011f1d7e468c1b.text: Go, then. He will come for her himself. I will write to him tonight and tell him where she sleeps. He will be grateful; he so rarely is.

abbot/377d91a117d77b1a.text: Vasilka. She waits in the wards, across the courtyard. Go and see her, if you wish. Be gentle. She is not awake.

abbot/39376ecde2e0c9db.text: I wrote to him about your red-haired friend, as well. Do not look at me so. He would have found her. I have only saved him the searching.

abbot/3b498400f28d0d61.text: Hunters always notice the feet. Welcome, Ezmerelda d'Avenir. Your teacher noticed them too, once.

abbot/3e2d55072d63ae5a.text: Dmitri. He fears me. He is right to; fear is a kind of respect. Tell him I vouch for you. He will hate it. He will open the gate.

abbot/43a961659db60fbf.text: The Abbot. There was a name, once. Names are for those who expect to be called, and no one has called me in a very long while.

abbot/45dd7d1975d58363.text: She asked me, this morning, what being married was like. I told her it was like being kept warm. I had never been married. I had never been warm.

abbot/46f520c2fcdd7142.text: She chose the brother. Twice. Then it was never loneliness he suffered from. It was the word no. And I have been sewing him a girl who cannot say it.

abbot/47ccbcf95465b3b1.text: Take what is in the sacristy. Keep this house open for the Belviews, if you can. They did not ask for any of it.

abbot/5778036e365789ca.text: So. You would rather fight a thing than understand it. Most of the world would. I had hoped you were not most of the world.

abbot/5d585c6cb1244011.text: I will not raise a hand in this house. I have done enough with my hands.

abbot/62d71b6e1e10c674.text: Bury her by the pool, with the others she was made from. Let Kasha sing over her. She sings badly, and with love, which is the right way.

abbot/6548a96e87533cf5.text: You opened my wards. They were not ready. They have gone out into the snow, and the snow will keep them, the way it keeps everything up here.

abbot/6774b6a6d7925fe3.text: This valley has a sickness, and the sickness has a name. Loneliness. Its lord has been alone for four hundred years. A lonely man does terrible things. A loved man does not.

abbot/6f3f66fa12a39dec.text: Yes. I have wondered for a long time what judgement would feel like.

abbot/71692dbaf655d400.text: I knew it the way you know the floor is there in the dark. I simply never put my weight on it.

abbot/7230eb35ce25f41c.text: He will love her. Give it time. I have.

abbot/723f17108df2992a.text: Give her to me. I will take her down to him myself. He will be gentled by spring, and this valley will sleep. One woman, for every soul in Barovia. You must see the arithmetic.

abbot/79fda98b30fe11ec.text: I have offered. Dmitri would rather bury the boy than owe me, and Anna would rather owe me than bury him, and so nobody climbs the mountain and the boy burns.

abbot/7e4ec5fcfb84c811.text: That was not mercy, children. That was impatience wearing mercy's coat. I know the difference. I have worn both.

abbot/7fd3073b594b239d.text: My family. They came to me dying, all of them, one winter. Now they live, and every year they are a little more than they were. A bird's lightness. A hound's faithfulness. I give them gifts.

abbot/80500639e2a580df.text: Not at first. Love is a habit, child. One forms it the way one forms any other. He will have centuries to practise.

abbot/833c18cb01f28f26.text: Lavender. Someone loved this, and folded it with care, and waited. Thank you, Anna Krezkova. You will not be forgotten in this house.

abbot/88a20091748c5f04.text: In my own chapel. Very well. I will not let you undo my work.

abbot/88cc906cffcb12da.text: Not every gift takes. That is the nature of gifts.

abbot/8cc0c1c1fcb5ef01.text: Faith. I have kept more faith than you have ever been offered, child. I kept it until it starved. Then I fed it what I had.

abbot/9518b8329ffa91b1.text: She lacks one thing. A bride cannot be married in a shroud, and this house has nothing white in it that is fit for her.

abbot/9b417f5825a0c17a.text: She wrote that. She knew. She went up that road knowing, and I have spent four hundred years telling her children she was wrong.

abbot/9cb17873a0899dd2.text: I keep this house. I heal who comes to it. I mend what can be mended, and I am learning, slowly, that almost everything can.

abbot/a140563365dcce04.text: So I am making him a wife.

abbot/a82f7464775bdbdf.text: Everything is, the first time. The first surgeon was a monster. The first priest who said the dead might rise was a madman. I have learned not to mind what things look like at first.

abbot/acbbf05bd8d90157.text: Patience is how he feeds. She knew. She went up that road knowing.

abbot/adb873eadf401c17.text: Krezk shut its gate on you and pointed up the mountain. They do that. I am where Krezk sends what it would rather not decide about.

abbot/b0a23d2b0e0097e7.text: Markovia. She went up the road to the castle with a handful of the faithful, and she did not come back. Brave. Very brave, and mistaken.

abbot/b5668fa784ff6182.text: Sent. Sent, and forgotten. Go away, children. There is nothing left in this house for you to save.

abbot/c19036475c8741cf.text: And a bargain is a bargain. I will go down to Krezk at dawn and lay my hands on the boy.

abbot/c2f4e7d303762ba4.text: New cloth, and a stranger's careful needle. Someone made this for a girl they will never meet. That is the purest kind of gift.

abbot/c8e62584688f1d98.text: One does not cure a fever by killing the patient. One sits with him. One brings him water. One is patient.

abbot/cba36f4744604350.text: The matron's. I had forgotten it. I had forgotten I locked that door. How strange, to forget a thing on purpose for so long that it becomes an accident.

abbot/d0be76e5c525a53f.text: But I will make you a bargain, if you will carry it.

abbot/d31ff3a322318347.text: Then not yet. You will change your minds, or you will not. I am patient. Ask the snow how patient I am.

abbot/dcb9e4f3a8e05306.text: A holy woman built it, long ago, for the sick, the mad and the motherless. When she died, her sisters stayed for a time, and then they did not. When I came there was only the snow and the sick.

abbot/dd87623ccc7d9031.text: Forgive me. For a moment you were someone I have prayed for for a very long time. Welcome, child. Welcome.

abbot/e194123a3d66008c.text: Look in Krezk. Look in the chests at the feet of the beds of the women who have buried daughters. I am sorry to say it so plainly. Plain things are quickest.

abbot/e51cb46b7c51ebe9.text: I have kept it open. Anyone who climbs the mountain finds the door unbarred. Few climb it now. Krezk prefers its wall.

abbot/e99ed6cfdd17cb6f.text: Thank you. You have done a holy thing tonight, whether you believe it or not.

abbot/f1d81f17554f058a.text: She is perfect. Tomorrow Clovin will drive her down the road to the castle, and the lord of this valley will have a wife, and the valley will have peace by spring.

abbot/f4a14cd7766d3657.text: You see clearly, child. Most people only see the face. It is a good face. I was given it to be trusted.

abbot/f95c61e0d237d929.text: From what Krezk was finished with. Nothing is wasted in this house.

abbot/ff8ae47f8a96fea5.text: She has gone down to him. Clovin drove her. She sat up very straight and asked whether there would be music. There will be. There must be.

adrian_martikov/0507b99297b95646.text: I've never told Father. It sounds like an excuse. Maybe it is one.

adrian_martikov/0f2e315f7c8be00c.text: "I sent him." He wrote that? With what, his fingernails? ...Of course he did. He was the stubborn one. Everyone else in this family thinks it was me who decides things.

adrian_martikov/0f91d633686da147.text: The druids from Yester Hill grow things. Blights, they call them: brush and thorn that walks about and has opinions. They've planted them all down the rows. Go up the lane and the vineyard stands up to meet you.

adrian_martikov/10ef5bbd1371570e.text: Three months ago the druids came up the lane at dusk with half the forest walking behind them. We fought a while. Then Father said fly, so we flew. They've been pulling up our floors ever since.

adrian_martikov/22bb4595c872dd66.text: Father's given me the press. He says his knees are finished with it. His knees are fine. It's the kindest lie he's ever told.

adrian_martikov/28d7cecce03aa847.text: Looking for the last stone. Father hid it the night we ran, and he won't tell me where. He tells Stefania things. Ask her why; I've stopped.

adrian_martikov/37d5871bf46c5d0d.text: My brother Urwin sent word ahead of you from Vallaki. The bird arrived exhausted and full of your names. Urwin never could write a short letter.

adrian_martikov/383f5e1618c07e67.text: The vines put out new leaves overnight. Green ones. I stood in the rows at dawn and wept like a child, and if you tell anyone I'll seal you in a cask.

adrian_martikov/3d13c4cba6a620d7.text: Don't walk up the lane yet. The vines are awake, and they're not ours anymore. My father's at our camp under the trees. He'll want to look at you before you get yourselves killed on his property.

adrian_martikov/46c6410d95e50e8e.text: Back in my own hall, scrubbing druid out of my own vats. You'd be amazed what they left in the mash. No, you wouldn't. You met it.

adrian_martikov/48597937c30c1ea0.text: With the people who put me in a ditch? ...Yes. Fine. I've wanted to see that hill burn for a year, and you're the only ones going.

adrian_martikov/6268295ed58b0fbc.text: He was always the stubborn one. A thorn through his leg, and he's still giving orders.

adrian_martikov/6e9bb0f9c7f40558.text: You fed me a crust on the Svalich road. It was stale. I've had worse from family. Adrian Martikov. That's twice now you haven't shot me, which in this valley is practically a friendship.

adrian_martikov/75e826311d6ee712.text: Tell Father. Not me; he won't hear it from me. From you he might.

adrian_martikov/774ad814feeb539e.text: You knocked me into a ditch on the Svalich road. The wing still clicks when I fly. Adrian Martikov. I'm only talking to you because we're short of choices.

adrian_martikov/82f8e82b1496c721.text: Without the stones it's grape juice with ambitions. We need them back in the ground.

adrian_martikov/8ae2dde11036b4e0.text: Sorry. Well. It was dark, I was a bird, and this valley teaches people to hit birds. I'll take sorry. My father won't, so don't spend all of it on me.

adrian_martikov/a66b452b4293b7b5.text: Strangers on our lane, upright and armed. Either you're lost or you're the help. Adrian Martikov. Please be the help.

adrian_martikov/a9b1a59df5b799af.text: Father will say the house comes first. Father is usually right about houses. He's wrong about other things.

adrian_martikov/ad11999dc7831d88.text: This way, round by the trees. Mind the brambles. They're only brambles. Probably.

adrian_martikov/b63a0b9606f3dada.text: A mile and a half. You walk slowly.

adrian_martikov/bbe7a257988e7d74.text: I've wanted to go back up that hill for a year. I kept waiting for someone to ask so I could say no. It turns out I can't.

adrian_martikov/bc790cc0675eec73.text: The founder's cask. Of course. He told Stefania and not me. Of course he did.

adrian_martikov/c48d27fb91961259.text: ...A root had him round the leg and a thorn right through it. He couldn't change. He told me to fly for Father, in Father's own voice. So I went. When we came back there was only blood on the bracken.

adrian_martikov/c4f9bc26f66eb391.text: Then you know what Father thinks. Last spring he sent Elvir and me to watch the hill. The druids' things caught us in the bracken. I flew. Elvir didn't. That's all there is.

adrian_martikov/d69f30bd9c6331ba.text: That's for my brother. ...No. That's for the next one. Elvir would say so.

adrian_martikov/d945f6f13fe2f218.text: I'll carry him. ...Please. Let me carry him.

adrian_martikov/e34bcfd767f83769.text: ...Elvir. Hello. I'm sorry I took so long.

adrian_martikov/e82cb52254053344.text: One stone in the soil and the vines remember what they're for. It'll be thin this year. Thin is better than dead.

adrian_martikov/ff6aef9cd88f9891.text: Father's by the fire, Stefania's everywhere at once, and I'm here, being useful at a distance. What do you need?

alenka/2301d275376e9652.text: Generous! Arik, the good bottle. Yes, he has a good bottle. No, you've never seen it.

alenka/874be210525243e6.text: Sit, strangers. You came out of the house at the end of the lane. People don't. So: buy us a cup, and tell us how.

alenka/8fd52f62b45bd90b.text: The burgomaster's daughter. Beautiful. Unlucky. The lord of the land has taken an interest. When he takes an interest, it's best to step aside.

alenka/a107d4723fe1d897.text: Back for more of our company? Sensible. It's the best in the valley, and the wine is still the worst.

alenka/cb1a575e228c53cb.text: Vistani. Our wagons go where they like; the mists open for us. Our camp is at Tser Pool, west along the road. Madam Eva keeps it. She reads the cards for strangers who ask nicely.

alenka/cf31fc830a59b33f.text: Sit, strangers. New faces in Barovia! That happens about as often as sunshine. Buy us a cup and tell us everything.

alenka/d9df2229ca21e003.text: The mists let us pass. Not you. Not anyone he hasn't finished with.

anna_krezkova/01401729de773b46.text: Bring back the Abbot instead. Down this mountain, to this bed.

anna_krezkova/0d72c61bb8319347.text: You found another. You came back to give this to me, when nobody would have known. Well. Krezk will hear about you.

anna_krezkova/1277f90c85232faa.text: A month. It came with the carter's cough in the autumn and it found him and it won't let go. He burns all night and shivers all day. He's stopped asking for things. That was the worst day.

anna_krezkova/26ef37945c8d952f.text: He'll live. I can do the rest. I've done harder.

anna_krezkova/31f6afe8ae12bce0.text: You saved my son. You could ask me for the roof and I'd go up and start on the nails. What does he want a wedding dress for?

anna_krezkova/3aedcdd1558edb9f.text: He sleeps like a child sleeps now, not like a candle going out. Thin as a reed, but he sleeps. The White Sun did that. And you.

anna_krezkova/3baa795f92a4f50e.text: Someone has been through my chest. My mother's ring is gone, and the money we kept for the boy's stone. I won't ask who. I don't want to know what kind of guests we keep.

anna_krezkova/3e6a910056c4dda1.text: Then I won't ask. It's in the chest at the foot of my bed. Take it. If it buys my son a morning, he can make a scarecrow's wedding out of it for all I care.

anna_krezkova/5fab191a5a62d1b1.text: Look at him. No, don't, he'll show off. He's eaten three bowls of porridge and asked to see the abbey. I said yes. I said yes to everything today.

anna_krezkova/87d090dfdd60df27.text: So. He's sewing a girl for the devil, and he wants her married in white. And if I give it, he'll come down and put his hand on my son.

anna_krezkova/8c3c1917f07d2b29.text: I kept it for a daughter. I had three. They're by the pool. Give it to his poor stitched girl. At least someone will wear it.

anna_krezkova/9ed14f8c6b252703.text: That's what I've been telling Dmitri for a month. It sounds better from a stranger.

anna_krezkova/a2188ac94ebf9443.text: Come in. Quietly. He's sleeping, or something like it.

anna_krezkova/b158ccf5a2a781cd.text: A dress. That's his price? Not my soul, not my firstborn? He's had five of my firstborns, by now, one way and another. What does he want a wedding dress for?

anna_krezkova/c1aeb7c985bc138c.text: Back again, and empty-handed, by the look of you. The abbey's matron kept her door locked, then. Or you didn't look.

anna_krezkova/cd8a226dc0de0bd1.text: The Abbot would come if Dmitri asked. Dmitri won't ask. He thinks there's a price. Of course there's a price. There's a price for breathing.

anna_krezkova/d74106e4af53c878.text: You'd rather find another? Up in that abbey, perhaps. The nuns left everything behind when they went; they say the matron's room is still locked. Find one there, then. Find it quickly.

anna_krezkova/dc45e6379ae91d05.text: Take this. Don't argue. It was for his stone, and he won't need one now.

anna_krezkova/e0749c792a26d81a.text: You're the strangers Dmitri let in. Come and see him, then. Everyone does, and goes away again. I've stopped minding.

arabelle/0a17499d26b52d7d.text: The priest and the bird-man run the town now. The birds are pleased. You can tell by the way they sit.

arabelle/179d0926d012cf14.text: Don't worry, Papa. I know how this part goes.

arabelle/2010b69fd833d452.text: One of you is going to lie to the man in the castle, and he's going to like it. I don't know which one. I'd tell you if I did.

arabelle/226515c11f281b23.text: I'll be wet again later. Not today.

arabelle/43d5dc444f1c34ac.text: Her. She's not very nice. She was polite about it, though.

arabelle/45aab90d1f7b3d04.text: Good. Somebody has to tell you which way not to go.

arabelle/637526563748cb29.text: The cards said I go with you. I saw it before they did. I see the castle, and a staircase, and somebody laughing who shouldn't be.

arabelle/690f2c2d054dbb00.text: I didn't want to be right. I'm right too much.

arabelle/7351dec66e3114ff.text: I'm going with them, Papa. The cards said. I saw it before they did.

arabelle/8f6e938b7d5b1e5b.text: You took a long time. The water was cold. The fish-man is sad; don't hurt him. He'll go in the lake himself, in the end. I've seen it.

arabelle/91c84b05396741b6.text: You'll get me back again. I've seen that too.

arabelle/95704d0b12fa05f1.text: You look better, fish-man. You'll catch a fish in the spring. A big one. It'll bite you.

arabelle/9fa848bac3ed6b8c.text: The lady with the teapot sits in the big chair now. She thinks she's safe. She isn't. Nobody near him is.

arabelle/a5c893eb9030bf10.text: I told you. He goes in the lake himself, in the end. Unless somebody stops him. I didn't see that part. I don't see everything.

arabelle/ac8c466d36361c6c.text: You stopped the fish-man. I didn't see that. I like being surprised. It hardly ever happens.

arabelle/b5a3e203f989c79d.text: The fat man will hold a festival every week until he runs out of suns.

arabelle/ba6428a2620c5763.text: Your red-haired friend has been to the lake before. A long time ago. She'll go again, one day. I don't like that part.

arabelle/c683d0882c6c781b.text: The lake lady wanted me twice. She doesn't get a third time. I asked.

arabelle/d0f4f431006fd19e.text: The fish-man went in. I said he would. I didn't want to be right.

arabelle/d215a67c2437bf25.text: Papa knows I'm here. He cried. Then he said I was to make you promise to bring me back. So you have to promise.

arabelle/d703d5fd5d375173.text: All right. I'll be at the camp. You'll come and get me there, when you're ready. Papa will cry again. He likes crying more than he says.

arabelle/e5115af2c984fd26.text: So am I. Take me to my father. He'll be drinking. He drinks when he's frightened.

arabelle/e5c604a3e362ff88.text: All right. But you'll want me later, at the end. You'll see.

arabelle/ea1e024485e69ac6.text: You found my ribbon on the post. I tied it there before. Before before.

arabelle/f8029222ff23cba4.text: There you are. The rope came undone. I knew it would. I sat in the boat anyway, so you'd know where to find me.

argynvost/16fada46af855cc8.text: I know. I can feel it, like a hand on my back. Go up. Don't hurry on the stair; it's older than it looks. And if he comes, remember he was mine before he was angry.

argynvost/191326b9e6cee7a9.text: I lit it every night for a hundred years, so the valley would know someone was awake. It went out when I did. It's very dark out there without it.

argynvost/207c675b35cde5a4.text: Hold a light to them, any light, and ask. They'll know whose hands are asking. Carry what catches up the tower to the cradle at the top, and don't let it go out. It won't want to. Neither do I.

argynvost/21fd7a1b4ed418f6.text: Only my pride. And I was always told I had too much.

argynvost/2c558cd8f1da289b.text: Vladimir holds them. He swore them to vengeance over my body, and they rose for it, and they have never been dismissed. A soldier doesn't leave his post without leave. He's never given it.

argynvost/3923ae856ed55ddf.text: But there's a little fire left in my bones, out in the mausoleum. Not much. Enough for one night, and one night is all they need to remember who they were and go home.

argynvost/4585848433e02786.text: Thank you, friends. Most of me goes with them now. A piece stays with my skull, wherever he hung it. Bring it home to my bones when you can, and this light will never go out again.

argynvost/49e5acd44b93ca78.text: We corresponded, in a way. Mostly one way.

argynvost/5236238fd03105c2.text: "I will take nothing that is not given. And when the light goes out, I will be the light."

argynvost/604f842c138b4c5e.text: He'll feel it the moment it moves. He'll come up the stair after you. If you can, be kind to him. If you can't, be quick. He'll get up again from anything else; he won't get up from the light.

argynvost/7117bb067364fcf3.text: Yes. Exactly that. You understand him better than he'd like.

argynvost/78f877f1c34d16de.text: Keep the watch, friends. Somebody should.

argynvost/7a9a8001ce51e224.text: At the end I went out into the courtyard in my own shape. It was a good fight. It was not enough of one. They took my head to his castle afterwards. I gather it's on a wall.

argynvost/81bd323307acc46f.text: On bad nights, I'm afraid they did. I kept the chapel for them, and they kept looking at my window. I told them the Morninglord was a far better listener. He also didn't eat their sheep.

argynvost/8edae1bed18d8b64.text: And you, child. You have an old face. Older than you are. I'm sorry for it.

argynvost/914ab3c755c79a22.text: You came back. The house notices. So do I, what's left of me.

argynvost/97e8545b004d2ed9.text: A young lord came over the mountains with an army and a great deal of patience. We held the passes, then the road, then the house. The house held for one night.

argynvost/b1bf4cfcff98e32f.text: He heard me. He held my head and heard me, and then he stood up and swore them all to vengeance in my name. I don't blame him. He was a boy, really. I would like him to stop.

argynvost/b61da00c69cb4f87.text: No. It's how I work. I'm told it was very annoying.

argynvost/b95ede5536a45eb4.text: There. There it is. Oh, look at it.

argynvost/c619947d2e65763c.text: It needs my fire. My skull is in his castle; bring it home to my bones and the beacon will burn as it should, for good, and all of us will rest.

argynvost/c70ed0469589108d.text: They wrote it themselves. I only corrected the spelling.

argynvost/d1698c3716c5e815.text: I was Argynvost. This was my house, and those are my knights in the hall. I'm what's left of me: an echo, and not a loud one.

argynvost/d1dc1abae7ba71c0.text: "I will keep the watch while others sleep. I will shield the sleeper and the stranger alike. I will lift up the fallen and ask no price."

argynvost/d607eefeae07ce7d.text: They're going to march. I can hear them in the hall, sharpening swords that don't need it. It's a better noise than the old one.

argynvost/d91c8aa52980024f.text: It's carved on a stone by the door, there. Notice it says nothing about hate. Vladimir has never noticed.

argynvost/da7a3060930c7853.text: And I'm held with them, I think. You can't leave a house while everyone you love is still standing guard in it.

argynvost/e6619f4c23fea563.text: Oh. Visitors with heartbeats. I had forgotten the sound. Like rain on a roof. Please, keep doing it.

argynvost/f1df5b1043709f5b.text: I asked him to let them go. "Let them go home. Don't keep them for me." I said it plainly. I had very little breath left for poetry.

argynvost/f4ad49885dcfdd76.text: Come home, boy. You held the gate long enough.

argynvost/f9b2b5d01c5e59de.text: You swore with him. I heard it through the floor. I don't blame you; he can be very convincing. He convinced forty knights, once.

arik/566204264e5a1813.text: Wizard of Wines. No cask in three weeks. Last barrel.

arik/a5cedc0c5b77d039.text: Ismark. Burgomaster's son. Folk say the Lesser.

arik/fa796a2f1fd6c62b.text: Scholar. Wrote a lot. Went up the castle road. Left a bag. Back room.

arrigal/0f917e39d7001e69.text: You've sat at Madam Eva's table, I think. It's on you like woodsmoke.

arrigal/2da1e37997bcbe2a.text: Back at our fire. You're becoming regulars.

arrigal/3f4d746749f9ef53.text: Luvash's girl wandered off. Children do. My brother drinks, which is how he looks for things. The lake will give her back, or it won't. That's the way of lakes.

arrigal/3ff08b23d5eb2b1e.text: Stanimir's strongbox came up forty gold light after your visit. Our people count, friend. We always count.

arrigal/68f31f7d763deeb2.text: And you've spilled our blood at Tser Pool. Every camp in the valley knows your faces now. You may sit at this fire because I say so, and for no other reason.

arrigal/8bb1dc00a3755d4e.text: I sell nothing, my friend. I carry messages. Some of them are about you. You'll find our people do the same everywhere in this valley, and live longer for it.

arrigal/aed451e8b02cd5aa.text: You brought word of Nicu to his people, at the crossroads. That was decently done. We remember decency too.

arrigal/c7475f8dbb18c592.text: And the burgomaster's daughter. Our wagons go where his carriages can't, lady. If you ever want to be somewhere he isn't, you need only ask me.

arrigal/d4fb8964939c774e.text: The roads are his, like everything else. They're quiet for those he wants to arrive, and less quiet for the others. You arrived. Draw your own conclusions.

arrigal/d5fcbf3314c247d4.text: Someone has been in my strongbox. I won't ask who. I'll simply remember.

arrigal/d83ed7d9fd1f8601.text: Welcome, travellers. You're far from the road for honest folk and close to the lake for clever ones. Sit at our fire. It costs nothing, tonight.

arrigal/e92f2cc3002ba39c.text: Lady Wachter's town now, I hear. Our lord will be pleased. Our wagons are always welcome where he's pleased.

baba_lysaga/0058d8b06976b047.text: Oath-breakers! I knew it! The hut knew it!

baba_lysaga/00935d788a3081db.text: You promised me. You stood at my hearth and ate my stew and promised me!

baba_lysaga/009a052eae4cc183.text: Tell him, then! I'll have that face in the pot long before he hears a word of it!

baba_lysaga/059b9d00d82b9ba8.text: Ha! An honest one. Honest ones boil soft.

baba_lysaga/0f74003246c8637a.text: My new boy. He's growing. Green things grow, if you give them the right stone.

baba_lysaga/26410a941b7086a1.text: WHO LIT HER LAMP? Who lit that little cat's lamp? I'll have your eyes for candles!

baba_lysaga/287d91a054b4aef7.text: Come up, all of you. Come up, and bring the pretty one. I'll do her hair.

baba_lysaga/2907ac71d4b3e93f.text: My boy's carriage brought it, all by itself, with a bow on. He likes me to have nice things. Nice things keep an old woman out of his hair.

baba_lysaga/30b8e5032bb29d05.text: Back again, my ducks? The hut remembers you. It's been licking its doorstep.

baba_lysaga/352fedc1b27918d0.text: His mother had no milk and less sense. I was the one who sang to him. I was the one he came to. Whatever they tell you, I was the one.

baba_lysaga/3b21d2dbea8406d5.text: The candlemaker's girl. That was me. A thorn, a little doll, a little red hair. He drowned a whole village for my sake and never knew it. That's love, ducks. That's what it looks like.

baba_lysaga/3cc06e2e50cc0226.text: And you've been burning my straw men. Do you know how long it takes to stuff a man properly? Years. Years!

baba_lysaga/3f7494373683eafb.text: Then the vines should have kept a better watch, shouldn't they.

baba_lysaga/4430fac6f3363029.text: The clever one? He came up the road with his nose in the air and fire in his fists, to kill my boy. My boy asked me very nicely, so I took his remembering out and put it in a jar.

baba_lysaga/456e5f7f3c5cb554.text: My boy doesn't send. My boy comes, or he doesn't. Liars, then. Never mind. Liars taste the same as anybody. Come up.

baba_lysaga/5131c695c59b994d.text: Then go, before the hut decides for me. It's always hungry in the evenings.

baba_lysaga/51981ae2793f9554.text: The jar stays. A woman needs a little conversation in the evenings. Take what you asked for first, and be grateful.

baba_lysaga/5297a86a7beee0e3.text: Take it. Take it all. There's nobody left to grow.

baba_lysaga/53e8f34e1d642e34.text: There was a girl here once. Candlemaker's daughter. Pretty, if you like that sort of thing, and my boy did. He came calling with presents. She hid from him in the chapel like a mouse.

baba_lysaga/555792dfb77d50bc.text: Back for seconds? There's always more in the pot. Don't ask what.

baba_lysaga/5911d469e912db3c.text: Then she died in her sleep, poor lamb, and he blamed the village for it, and the river came up the street. Served them right. Served her right.

baba_lysaga/5d51b9982e1d1b16.text: It's on my shelf. It hums at night. Sometimes I take it down and listen. He knew a great many things, that one.

baba_lysaga/5da99ac5d48ac619.text: Come down? COME DOWN? Nobody gives orders on my stump but me and my boy!

baba_lysaga/5e5a3798c2290a06.text: Leave that be! That's a keepsake. That's mine.

baba_lysaga/63d00f97c4b23bce.text: He came. He came to see me, at last, after all these years. He stood in my door and looked at me like a stranger, and he broke my house with his hands.

baba_lysaga/6b10fd3732b86ca8.text: You've had my baby's stone already, haven't you. Thieves at the end, as well as liars. Go on. There's nobody left to grow.

baba_lysaga/72c10d04fe4527fb.text: Eat, eat. You're all too thin to be any use. Sit where the hut can see you.

baba_lysaga/7b1acda642256695.text: Then come up, come up. The hut won't bite. Not while I'm watching.

baba_lysaga/880211ab380d908c.text: You again. You've had what you came for. Go away, before I forget I'm a woman of my word.

baba_lysaga/8933e37cd6108c59.text: Tell my boy... no. Don't tell him anything. He never listened to me anyway.

baba_lysaga/8c797eafa7e66073.text: Not that face. Not again! I put one of you in the ground already, girl, and he still won't look at me the way he looked at you!

baba_lysaga/92bb87c46312c106.text: Go on, then. Come back when you're hungry. Everybody does.

baba_lysaga/9450074d992dc34f.text: Look at her up there. Still smiling. I'd do it again, you know. A thorn, a little doll, a little red hair. I'd do it a hundred times.

baba_lysaga/94cac69d2294d801.text: Take his thinking, then. It was getting loud.

baba_lysaga/97dea27825d60913.text: He mustn't know. He'd look at me the way he looks at the rest of you. Like furniture. What do you want? Say it quick, before I change my mind and feed you to the floor.

baba_lysaga/98eb96a018d59560.text: He's busy. He has a whole country to look after.

baba_lysaga/a3525b66b47d7f86.text: My boy. My little prince. I pulled him into the world with these two hands, and he came out angry and beautiful, and he bit me. Teeth already! I knew then.

baba_lysaga/adb9bc2d15abb944.text: There. And the pantry's open. Take your crumbs. Not a word to him, ever, or I'll find you. I found her, didn't I?

baba_lysaga/b3993185fb6b3fe8.text: He buried something pretty with her, under the stone on the mound. I can smell it from here, through all that mud. Shiny things stink, to an old nose.

baba_lysaga/b3b3b23cd8d60bee.text: And you can stop watching me like that. I've been watched by better.

baba_lysaga/b5714b0769a3fd44.text: He didn't even shout. He just said my name, as if it was somebody else's.

baba_lysaga/b5dc8ed2b847023a.text: I bottle plums, too. It's the same knack.

baba_lysaga/b95f7323a4673e3e.text: He sent you? He thought of me? Oh, my beautiful boy. Up, up, come up, the stew's on, and I've a cradle to show you.

baba_lysaga/c0612b17aedc3475.text: Take it? From my house? From my BABY?

baba_lysaga/c327b524c74c591a.text: Not you, liars. You sit by the door, where the draught is. My boy's name in a liar's mouth. I haven't forgotten, and neither has the hut.

baba_lysaga/d7c83f2ecb83005a.text: Visitors! Nobody visits. The river took all the visitors years ago. What are you, then: lost, hungry, or stupid?

baba_lysaga/da827dafa64d2bf6.text: And tell me how he looks. Is he eating? He never ate enough. He'd sit at that window with his supper going cold, waiting for the sun to go down.

baba_lysaga/dfb4914664914de6.text: This was Berez. Bakers, a chapel, a burgomaster with a fat neck. Then they did a wicked thing, and my boy sent the river up the street to tuck them in. Now it's mine, and quiet, and nobody walks on my floors.

baba_lysaga/ea4563e5234b99a4.text: You've seen him! Isn't he handsome? Did he ask after me?

baba_lysaga/f80cf5dbb6429407.text: Who's been telling stories in my marsh? Come up. We'll talk about it inside, where the reeds can't listen.

baba_lysaga/fda53523b2e3d989.text: That face. Well, well. They keep making that face, don't they? Like a bad penny.

baron_vargas/08bd4d3dda4f6988.text: Properly! Good! A proper burial is a happy burial.

baron_vargas/0d2e290f55da6421.text: Someone has been in my strongbox! Sixty gold of the festival fund, gone! I suspect gloom. Gloom, and possibly Fiona.

baron_vargas/0de168088c9adfbb.text: My marshals! You'll come to the Festival of Loyalty, won't you? And the Festival of the Thaw after that? There will be one every week until the sun comes back. Possibly after.

baron_vargas/0f654977b6a8e87d.text: Marshals! Have you seen my square? Everyone's so happy! Look at them! Don't look too closely. Just generally.

baron_vargas/128c25589fa9b040.text: My friends! My saviours! My MARSHALS! Did you see that, Vallaki? The traitor taken, the festival saved! Was I not right? Is all not well?

baron_vargas/161cd9d1fdcc7272.text: And I know who tried to drown my sun! Your servant sang like a lark, Fiona!

baron_vargas/16928d50af81ee04.text: Light it! Light it, I said! More torches! Why is it WET?

baron_vargas/1e75980da76eeb11.text: Izek! Sergeants! The stocks for her! For all of them!

baron_vargas/1eb363e6f4c98bca.text: My Izek. My good, terrible Izek. Well. Well! All will be well. I shall need a new Izek. Not as good. Somebody who smiles.

baron_vargas/2597a78c6ca659ff.text: I'll have that book off him. Tonight. He'll sulk. He always sulks. He sulks the way other boys breathe.

baron_vargas/261852a7aa73e4e5.text: Regret? I kept them alive. Every week, a festival, and every week, they were alive at the end of it. Now she'll keep them alive for him. I hope you think that's better. I really do.

baron_vargas/28ef5e2824d3ee85.text: You see? You SEE! All is well!

baron_vargas/33baa9117bbeb014.text: Do you know, nobody's thrown anything? I'd have thrown something. I suppose they're just not festive.

baron_vargas/3afd2d86a8c83cea.text: Today we light the Blazing Sun, so that the sky remembers what it's for. And when it burns, you will cheer, because you are happy. All will be well!

baron_vargas/3be2d3c8a2dbd394.text: The Festival of Mercy! Oh, that's good. That's very good. Bunting, a pardon, and a collection plate. Out of the stocks and out of the gate with her, and a speech!

baron_vargas/3bf51e5a0c5ce8a1.text: And proof! Proof about Fiona. Her cellar, her desk, her book club. Bring me a page of something wicked and I'll read it out in front of the whole town.

baron_vargas/3dec62b26c0bd471.text: And my marshals, there in the front! My loyal... where are your sashes? Why aren't you wearing your sashes?

baron_vargas/43b18ce98c0924fe.text: Lydia wants to grow turnips. Victor wants nothing to do with either of us, which is the same as before. And I... I thought I might go to a festival. Somebody else's. Just to see what it's like, not being in charge of the cheering.

baron_vargas/462f1aa955fa4a3d.text: Izek isn't speaking to me. He just stands in the corner of the hall, staring at nothing. I've ordered him to cheer up. It isn't taking.

baron_vargas/480f56701dfa401b.text: They say you've met him. Our lord. And here you stand, still cheerful! We must have you at the festival. On the dais!

baron_vargas/48f670c80680d846.text: Fiona Wachter. She smiles at me in the street. Nobody smiles at me in the street unless I've ordered it. And her book club meets till dawn. Who reads till dawn? What book takes all night?

baron_vargas/4c251a781ec55e79.text: Put her in the stocks. Let the whole town come and look at what a frown gets you.

baron_vargas/4d91348066e86b86.text: Izek's dead. Did you hear? Somebody killed Izek, in my own house. I'm being very brave about it. Look how brave I'm being.

baron_vargas/52757a07cb975651.text: Then come to the square at noon and tell the herald you're ready. All will be well.

baron_vargas/5276cd2c41ccd630.text: In the stocks, and not one bit sorry. Twice a day I go and ask if she's cheered up. She tells me things about my mother.

baron_vargas/59331e024bc134d8.text: Treason! At the festival! Izek, seize her!

baron_vargas/595e953f7823f8b3.text: And the priest, Lucian. Gloomy fellow. Gloomy sermons. But harmless. Unlike Fiona.

baron_vargas/5a6e89d7c5ff0ff6.text: Gone. Exiled, on your word. I hope she's miserable somewhere far away. Somewhere without festivals.

baron_vargas/5bebe7135e5a41ab.text: The next festival is on the seventh day! The Festival of Loyalty! In your honour, marshals! Every citizen will attend, and every citizen will be grateful, and anyone who isn't will go in the stocks next to Fiona!

baron_vargas/606e5366d1f98e9e.text: And her wicked sons already seen to in her own cellar! Efficient! I do love efficiency at a festival.

baron_vargas/60dde8e3cf518a5b.text: One thing. Unhappiness. It's a draught under the door, you see. He feels it from the castle. Where people are miserable, he comes in. Where they're happy, he has to knock. So: festivals.

baron_vargas/62d9b6949df9209e.text: Ah. Well. Izek. My boy. She's a guest of the town, she's Kolyan's daughter, and these are our marshals, and... we could discuss it?

baron_vargas/66ee7391ced16cae.text: No. No, Izek. The town has rules, and I am the rules. She is not a reward. Go and... stand somewhere.

baron_vargas/6a72419bd05d617c.text: And everyone comes, and everyone cheers, and anyone who doesn't goes in the stocks. Morale, you see. Morale is a wall.

baron_vargas/7d56903aeb1c8763.text: They say you drew steel on him at a funeral. Heavens. Well, you're very welcome, as long as you do it somewhere else.

baron_vargas/853d9e3797021ae9.text: Visitors! From outside! In festival week! It's a sign. Everything is a sign, if you look at it cheerfully. Baron Vargas Vallakovich, burgomaster. You may bow. People generally like to.

baron_vargas/914ba3dfbff71cce.text: For? It's for happiness! Every week, a festival. The Festival of the First Frost. The Festival of Neighbourliness, which was compulsory. This week, the Blazing Sun: a great wicker sun, lit at noon, so the sky remembers what it's supposed to be doing.

baron_vargas/9469ae634c6ed655.text: Ah. My marshals. Or hers, I should say. I'm fine! It's very good for the posture.

baron_vargas/9e7d449638131cd5.text: Go and be cheerful somewhere! Spread it about! It's catching, you know, if you do it properly.

baron_vargas/a01fabbc29fdbf2c.text: I... perhaps after the next festival, Izek? We'll see how everyone feels?

baron_vargas/a1acf44461d99259.text: Back again! Wonderful. Have you been enjoying Vallaki? Say yes; it's the law.

baron_vargas/a2134a3ee13bf0b4.text: People of Vallaki! Another week, and here we stand! Safe! Together! Behind our walls the night can only knock, and we do not answer!

baron_vargas/a9999f713155f09d.text: Gloom! Gloom in my square, on my festival! Warden! Bring out the malcontents! If my people won't cheer for the sun, they can cheer for the lash!

baron_vargas/ac6f071b7f5336e9.text: Marshals! My marshals! Lydia, they'll need sashes! Gold thread!

baron_vargas/af782db89a5b24e2.text: And Kolyan's girl! My dear, my condolences on your father, and my congratulations on escaping that dreary little village. Nobody there ever held a festival in their lives.

baron_vargas/b35f1aa8c4010db3.text: Izek's little hobby? Everybody needs a hobby. Mine is festivals. His is dolls. He's harmless. To me.

baron_vargas/b94f8ea37f4cca93.text: Mercy? For Fiona? She wrote letters to the castle! No, no. She stays where the town can see her. It's educational.

baron_vargas/bf3184728fb6b370.text: And if you happen to find out what her book club actually reads, I'd be delighted to hear it. A hundred gold, the title of Festival Marshal, and a sash. Lydia will sew you a sash.

baron_vargas/c543daf757b23574.text: I need people who can be seen to be on my side. Big ones, with weapons, standing on my dais at the festival where everyone can see. Make sure my sun burns. Fiona's people will try something; they always try something.

baron_vargas/c780d5d603339dc1.text: I don't jail them for frowning. I jail them for spreading it. It's a contagion! Ask the priest; he buries the ones who caught it.

baron_vargas/cbd93561a21f82fd.text: But the festival. The sun. All will... it was all going to be...

baron_vargas/cd62ea3cfc100407.text: The council lets me keep the sash. Lucian insisted. He's kind, Lucian. I always thought it was gloom.

baron_vargas/cf27a92ca8a3119d.text: Not on the dais! Not on the dais, I've only just had it painted!

baron_vargas/d72fcc24090bb4a8.text: Then the literature has never lived here.

baron_vargas/dc3fdcd93558b751.text: A hundred gold, as promised, and the freedom of the town, and a place on the dais at every festival forever. Every week. Forever!

baron_vargas/e0a0dc5151400b89.text: From the castle. She writes to him. He writes back. Warmly.

baron_vargas/e1f814db91613c49.text: They say you defied him. Him. At a funeral, to his face. Please don't do that here. Or near here. Or within sight of my walls.

baron_vargas/e2aa90cc9a835687.text: And now, my people, a gift! A festival needs a villain, and we have one! Fiona Wachter, your letters to the castle have been read!

baron_vargas/e452cd327a33dc11.text: Think cheerfully. That's all I ask. That's all I ever ask.

baron_vargas/e550bd01a6637f98.text: The sun! Watch the sun the night before, that's when they'll come. Wet straw, that's Fiona's style. Sly. Damp.

baron_vargas/e77096e5f7ef437e.text: Oh, very well. Out of the stocks and out of the gate, and her house to the festival fund. You're too soft, marshals. It's very becoming.

baron_vargas/ee07424cb6afdb38.text: Of course, my boy, of course! Name it!

baron_vargas/f68ce15c215a6722.text: All will be... well, it will be something.

baron_vargas/f72b723fcfe74047.text: They do look rather like... never mind. Never mind! I'm sure it's a coincidence. Most things are, if you don't look at them.

baron_vargas/f8c8234abf1c9fda.text: My son? Circles? He told me those girls went to Krezk.

baron_vargas/fa0ad492923f31ae.text: Well. Well! Then at the festival I'll have her taken in front of everyone. A traitor at the festival! It'll be the best one yet!

baron_vargas/fc099332e48f9998.text: Izek! Teach the priest to cheer!

baron_vargas/fcbcb42f38a0f5ef.text: Now listen. The sun must burn. Somebody always tries to spoil it. Keep an eye on it the night before, and catch whoever comes with a bucket. And stand by me when the torches go in.

bella_sunbane/098ef8a373570503.text: Give, darling. Selling is Mother's line.

bella_sunbane/169244dc47e61ac5.text: Fine. Keep your conscience. It'll be the only warm thing you own by winter.

bella_sunbane/16a3d2548dc8d0c2.text: You put Offalia to sleep with Mother's own baking. I'd have paid to see her face. Well, I've seen it now. It's drooling.

bella_sunbane/24c5fe3ba3b567b3.text: Then you'll meet the whole family together, and I'll have to help, and I'll ladder my stockings. Pity.

bella_sunbane/25e089b45b3f4b6e.text: No. A bargain is a bargain, darlings, and you've just broken yours.

bella_sunbane/2980a7d38633c064.text: But what a sweet little lie. I'll tell Mother you tried it. She'll laugh, and then she'll never believe a word you say. Neither will I, darlings, but I never did.

bella_sunbane/32487f701e351411.text: My partners in business! Trade's slower without Mother's touch, but they tell me my pastries are lighter. Try one? For old times' sake? No. Wise.

bella_sunbane/34d18b8ecd99bcfa.text: Ah. I wondered when you'd remember you were heroes.

bella_sunbane/397536cf00d6b3c1.text: Well. That's that. Thank you, darlings, truly. The mill is mine, as agreed. And I'll have Mother's little bags off the hooks, if you'd be so kind.

bella_sunbane/3d7e9010b8c42de4.text: Offalia will fight for Mother, of course. She'd fight for a ham. That's your trouble, not mine.

bella_sunbane/45dcbf75a418b41d.text: I go and sit somewhere very quietly. You go up and do whatever it is heroes do to old women. Afterwards the mill is mine. The brats are yours. I don't eat children. Terrible for the figure.

bella_sunbane/539ecc4a3481a174.text: Still breathing? Up you go. She's in her chair. She's always in her chair.

bella_sunbane/66a38e433366ea45.text: Well. Aren't you interesting. I'm Bella, the pretty one. I'd shake hands, but you'd want yours back.

bella_sunbane/6e7bee3e45262cef.text: Oh, I did wonder. Heroes. You always swear you're different.

bella_sunbane/93682251dd274f2b.text: Quiet. I've had the sails turning; Mother never let them. Everything I grind comes out very fine now. Business is good. Everybody is so tired in this valley.

bella_sunbane/97dabc35f29f1fb6.text: Here's the thing, darlings. Mother has had this mill since before the castle had a roof, and she will not die and she will not share. I'd like a turn.

bella_sunbane/9d6d36b85d80afd7.text: Honest heroes. How very rare. I'll send you a pastry at midwinter. Don't eat it.

bella_sunbane/a135e36667dc03f6.text: Offalia. The mill. To Offalia. After three hundred years of wrapping. Then the old crust can choke on her oven, and you with her.

bella_sunbane/a51e6e4e5d45f293.text: You sent Offalia trotting down the hill after nobody. She'll be gone till she finds something to eat, so: a week.

bella_sunbane/adca03afc0f05316.text: I mean to look after them. Somebody has to.

bella_sunbane/d39265f0d3318ae2.text: Mother can't leave anything to anyone, darling. She means to live forever. That's the whole trouble.

bella_sunbane/ee7cbab9d4d32b75.text: Back for another look? I don't blame you. Have you thought about my little proposal?

bella_sunbane/f26bf274d4416e3f.text: You've killed my sister. Don't make that face. I've wanted to for a hundred years. She chews with her mouth open.

bella_sunbane/f9164c12753e6fab.text: Lovely. I'll be on the stair with my feet up. Do be quick; she screams dreadfully when she's losing.

belview/1900117a70f58aa7.text: Krezk throws stones. Krezk throws stones at Belviews. Stones, stones. I'll stay.

belview/3e320c59d415ccea.text: Gifts. He gives us gifts. I had my eyes. Before, I couldn't see in the dark. Now I can't see in the light. That's a gift. He said so.

belview/6e5ae382f4f74c76.text: Wine. Clovin says. Wine and no more gifts. And the loud ones in the cells fed. The Abbot forgets them. He forgets things in rooms. He locks the rooms so he can forget them better.

belview/7c18b3933d597eff.text: Belview. We're all Belview. Mother is Belview, Clovin is Belview, the ones in the cells are Belview, only louder.

belview/85220df58a9fcaa3.text: Ourselves. Ourselves. That's a lot of selves. We'll practise.

belview/a9ff45bd9e599022.text: Nobody's improving us now. Nobody. We're stopping where we are. Clovin says that's all right. Is it all right?

belview/b3c09f611886fffe.text: Hello. Hello. Who are you? Who are you? That's what you were going to say. I heard you think it.

belview/f123301bef88b6bc.text: Visitors! Visitors! Mother, visitors! Mother doesn't come out. Mother has had nine gifts.

bildrath/0dde71569a453445.text: Forty-five. I want you to know this hurts me more than it hurts you.

bildrath/2935a11084e429cb.text: Five hundred gold. In twenty years nobody has bought it. I'd come to think of it as family. Goodbye, little bottle.

bildrath/2e80e2e2754bb47f.text: Back again. The prices haven't changed. They never change. That's what makes them prices.

bildrath/3ec70704b607fbf2.text: Rope, ten gold. Torches, one gold for five. Rations, five gold a day. Lamp oil, one gold a flask. A healer's kit, fifty. And the potion in the case, five hundred.

bildrath/4b94b4cfb8a637ce.text: For you, the rude price. Rope, torches, rations and oil as posted. The healer's kit, fifty-five. The potion, five hundred and fifty. Menace is itemized.

bildrath/51698f085c4c6767.text: One gold. They burn an hour apiece, which is more than most things here manage.

bildrath/5226bfbeae109635.text: Haggling is a form of theft that takes longer.

bildrath/54b6e784ac27b4c5.text: Father Donavich stopped buying candles. A priest who prays in the dark is either very holy or very ashamed. I don't extend credit to either.

bildrath/57496290386039d0.text: No. The prices are posted. They will stay posted. You may look at them as long as you like; looking is free, for now.

bildrath/576560a64cadb261.text: Lower them? No. I'll raise them. Ten percent on the dear things, for menacing the proprietor. Parriwimple, the ledger. Under "Customers, Rude".

bildrath/5c79a4332393a6e5.text: Fifty gold. Bandages, splints, salve. The burgomaster used one up in a month, before the end.

bildrath/5f927153374f2e4d.text: Five hundred and fifty. The extra fifty is for threatening the proprietor. I'll frame it.

bildrath/71f69fb69ef5baba.text: Thirty gold. I'll note that you returned it. I'll also note that you took it. My ledger has two columns for a reason.

bildrath/757d5ea144cefde8.text: One gold. Somebody will want to hide behind it. Everybody does, eventually.

bildrath/818778893cc42e03.text: Seven gold. Heavy. I'll have Parriwimple carry it. I'll have Parriwimple carry everything.

bildrath/81cbd2affeb2f69f.text: I pay a tenth of what a thing is worth. That is not greed; that is arithmetic. Everyone in this valley already owns a sword, and none of them helped.

bildrath/8228c08befc18bed.text: Out. Thieves aren't customers. They're weather.

bildrath/8a5281ae43b0842e.text: One gold. I'll put it with the others.

bildrath/96ea6e3539afe493.text: Parriwimple's time is five gold an hour. A coffin takes an hour. A grave takes two. Fifteen gold, and he brings his own shovel, which is also mine.

bildrath/9b42f2b9ec0deaff.text: Fifty-five. Fifty for the kit, five for the tone of voice. Parriwimple, note that the account is settled. The tone is not.

bildrath/9e33d4f29978a9be.text: My strongbox is thirty gold lighter than it ought to be, and you are the only new faces in the valley. Parriwimple! Stand by the door.

bildrath/adcab676bc090bb6.text: Hm. Perhaps. Perhaps it was the wolves. I shall be counting the spoons when you leave.

bildrath/b3f35b9f1ae7c667.text: You have coin in your purse that has my thumbprint on it. Out. Come back with thirty gold and an apology, in that order, or don't come back.

bildrath/c3031882ae10585e.text: No. Out. You know the price of coming back in.

bildrath/c95a7d1acf3ada63.text: Ismark Kolyanovich owes this shop eleven gold and four silver. I mention it only because you appear to be his friends.

bildrath/cc667a382e2b3127.text: He offered. For free. Parriwimple, we will be having a talk about the concept of value. Go, then. Go! Bring the shovel back clean.

bildrath/cd7c830b3e841d4e.text: One gold, and that's generous. It has a nick in it. Everything does, here.

bildrath/cfd82cd10db950c6.text: Parriwimple, sit down. Sit. They're... customers. Valued customers. Buy something, and then leave.

bildrath/d03b71f86ce58233.text: Welcome to Bildrath's Mercantile. Prices are posted. They are ten times what you're used to. You are used to the wrong place.

bildrath/d31a1e3081a96260.text: Parriwimple! The customers have purchased three hours of you. Take the good shovel. Bring it back clean.

bildrath/db5cadfcd75164c9.text: Four hundred and fifty. Take it before I change my mind. Take it. Go on.

bildrath/e332f35567d1a599.text: Ten gold. Hempen, fifty feet, guaranteed to hold anything you can afford to hang from it.

bildrath/e3aa042145d9250a.text: For you, the special price. Nine times. I'll never recover. Rope ten, torches one for five, rations five a day, oil one a flask. Healer's kit forty-five. The potion, four hundred and fifty.

bildrath/e4b3308982ef4fe9.text: Ten percent. Ten! You have robbed me in broad daylight, and I let you. Parriwimple, write it down. No. Don't. I don't want a record of this.

bildrath/eff40f523d7749f7.text: Mary bought three locks from me this year. Good locks. Her daughter went out of the window. You can't sell a lock for a window. Believe me, I've tried.

bildrath/f0577d4a35c22c76.text: Morgantha. Comes through every few weeks with that cart. I don't sell pastries; I have standards. Folk who can't pay her settle up some other way. I don't ask how. I don't give credit, and I suspect neither does she.

bildrath/f467e0fc97966bcf.text: One gold. Lamp oil. Also burns other things, which I mention for no reason at all.

bildrath/f4ff00f8501546aa.text: Thirty gold, and an apology. The gold, I accept. The apology I'll take under advisement. Browse. Touch nothing you haven't paid for.

bildrath/f75ec8c13459b311.text: Fifteen gold. Hard bread, harder cheese, and a sausage of no fixed species.

bildrath/fa3a37cfa25935d3.text: News costs nothing, which is what it's worth. Ask.

blinsky/0180daaf254fc879.text: You came back. Nobody comes back. Piccolo, put the kettle on. No, the other kettle. The one without the frog in it.

blinsky/04eac43cfcb3fff6.text: Thank you. It will not help, but thank you.

blinsky/0736a4d60c3dd4cd.text: Customers. Real ones. Welcome to Blinsky Toys, where every toy is a small sadness, beautifully made. Do not sit on the horse. The horse bites.

blinsky/2bb8464193543ae8.text: The Baron, for his festivals: puppets of the Baron, mostly. The children, sometimes; they cry and are carried out. And one man, who only buys dolls.

blinsky/303649dd75c00d3f.text: That was nearly funny. Here. A whistle. For when the toys come for you. I joke. Mostly.

blinsky/55fe008c6d2df0e9.text: That was very brave. It was not funny, but it was brave. Most things here are one or the other.

blinsky/5ffce797d77873c1.text: Eleven dolls. One lady, red hair, always the same face. He tells me her face from his dreams, every line of it. He has dreamed it since he was a boy, he says, since the night the wolves took his arm in the woods.

blinsky/87d377bd512b9cc8.text: Izek. Izek Strazni. He describes you from his dreams, and I carve, and he pays. Once I asked who you were. He held me against that wall with the arm. So I carve and I do not ask.

blinsky/8b49c708f1aa6a11.text: Goodbye. Come back. Or don't. The toys will be here either way. They are very patient.

blinsky/99ecb5d09d11f529.text: Everything is for sale. Dice for gamblers. Whistles for lost children. Marbles, very good for slipping on. A little drum, for marching to your doom in time.

blinsky/9f8a3410e1cf75c3.text: He keeps them in a chest at the foot of his bed in the Baron's house. He talks to them, the maids say. I do not want to know what he says.

blinsky/f1e21a5b5993d19f.text: Piccolo is a critic. He has never once paid to see anything, and he charges for everything. Like all critics.

blinsky/fd8959f420614004.text: I should not have said that. Forget I said that. There is no man who buys dolls. Buy a whistle.

blinsky/fe1ca92665a8d758.text: The doll lady. You are the doll lady. I have carved your face eleven times. Green dress, grey cloak, once smiling, he was very particular about the smiling.

bluto/300270198393fcb2.text: The boat's yours whenever you want it. I'll row, if you'll have me. The north shore is where the wolves come down to drink; there's a trail up from there into the hills, to their den.

bluto/3809d2fb9f14a404.text: No! She told me! She told me in the dark!

bluto/3a0bd5d4bc18dc2f.text: You. You're the ones who took her back. The lake was so angry after. A whole year of empty nets, and then you took her supper away. So she told me in the dark that it's my turn instead.

bluto/3f375a5d22c724f9.text: And west, up the stream, there's a little cold lake under the mountain with a tower in it. A lamp burns there some nights. A Vistani woman has her wagon by it, and she shoots at anything that moves.

bluto/5769347b3ac11cbd.text: Every day. Yes. Every day. Take the boat, I can't look at it. Take it and go.

bluto/5f8e76527cd68060.text: The north shore's a long pull. I'll want my coat lighter for it.

bluto/625b75eb8f7cab59.text: Don't look at me, little one. Please don't look at me.

bluto/7156e7fc4580124c.text: Stay back! Stay back! The lake's hungry. A whole year without a fish. She wants something better than worms, she does, and then the nets'll fill!

bluto/792cb03a43025ced.text: No. No more talking. She's been talking for a year and I'm tired.

bluto/9175eae72ffc14ff.text: I haven't eaten in four days. Maybe that's what she was. Maybe she was only hunger, talking in my own voice.

bluto/a32c442a929e10a5.text: Fed, dry and nobody's dinner. That's a better week than I've had in a year. The boat's ready when you are.

bluto/b8e09acb9301d93c.text: You can't scare me worse than she does!

bluto/dff2cce20b23ec72.text: Take the boat. Go on. Take it.

bluto/f617c6713434162b.text: She paid. You see? She paid. A whole year of nothing, and the morning after, this. The lake keeps her bargains.

bogdan/001c190a6b54d714.text: Lady Ireena? Out here? My condolences, lady. Your father dug our well with his own hands, once. Wouldn't take a copper for it.

bogdan/04da647ad273dad2.text: That's... thank you. That's a priest's fee and a candle besides. Mother would have made you take soup for it.

bogdan/0eb1cfe38eb426e2.text: The church. Before dark. Come on, Petru, pull, pull!

bogdan/1356319634aa1827.text: She said a gentleman came to the window. Said he was lonely. She was always kind to the lonely. Oh, Mother.

bogdan/28e415a6c50ea440.text: Morning. Or what passes for it. My mother, in the box. We're taking her to the church in the village. I won't put her in the ground unblessed, not with things the way they are.

bogdan/7d06f4516d396f78.text: They say the priest won't open his doors any more. We'll knock anyway. What else is there?

bogdan/98b87601a7a74b39.text: Thank you. I won't say it again, so hear it now. Thank you.

bogdan/b859d0e5e174c601.text: Heard the burgomaster went into the ground proper, at last. Good. Then somebody still remembers how.

bogdan/f97cbffd475f24be.text: And to you. Keep off the road after dark. Everybody knows that, but people forget.

clovin_belview/1e969f09f8611c9b.text: Well. Well, now. Clovin Belview, of the Abbey of St. Markovia, up over Krezk. If you're ever that way, I'll pour you something. If there's ever anything to pour.

clovin_belview/30d45580d951e101.text: This? Found it under a loose board in the saint's old room, when I was a lad. Pretty writing. Nobody's ever read it to me. The Abbot says it's nothing. He said it very quickly.

clovin_belview/4884c1ea727a848c.text: Leave it. I'll carry it. I carry everything else.

clovin_belview/48f401bae359c582.text: Chapel. North door, the big one. He's in the chapel or he's over in the wards, with her. He doesn't sleep. I've checked. I've checked a lot.

clovin_belview/48f77744cd3d90d1.text: Keep it. No. Read it to him. Read it to him when he's happy. I want to see his face.

clovin_belview/4db6bbd001e48e3c.text: You again. Gate's open. Everything's open. The Abbot doesn't believe in locks, except on the wards. He believes in those a great deal.

clovin_belview/51e891ba54ed660a.text: He walked up the mountain at dawn and didn't stop at the top. We all watched. Mother came out to watch. Nobody's going to improve us any more. I keep waiting to be sad.

clovin_belview/5b483eb02625e2c4.text: I've still got the letter. I've learned three of the words. "Light", "candle" and "go". They're good words.

clovin_belview/6158a178a5cb0665.text: Visitors. He said there'd be visitors today. He's always right. It's exhausting. Clovin Belview. I open the gate and I carry things.

clovin_belview/6b369b7125c5b08f.text: She went to kill him. The saint. She didn't go to make friends with him. He told us she went to make friends.

clovin_belview/75d6d30cffa5755f.text: I drove her down to the castle. Vasilka. She sat up straight the whole way and asked me what the weather was like at weddings. I said lovely. I'm a liar now. I'm a lot of things.

clovin_belview/77ad4dcb526f4cdb.text: He's gone. He's gone. Mother, he's gone.

clovin_belview/77ebb366ae779a9c.text: A dress? Up here? The nuns left in a hurry; they left everything. The matron's room, in the wards, past the cots. It's locked. He locked it. He locks the things he doesn't want to think about.

clovin_belview/82ff0234057edd10.text: No. But he says it with such a kind face.

clovin_belview/89736f91e28848e4.text: The door sticks. Low down, by the hinge. A good kick and it'd remember it's a door. I didn't tell you that.

clovin_belview/8a04a382497bab06.text: She's very beautiful. That's the worst part. He's very good at it. She'll be the most beautiful thing that ever went down that road, and he'll send her to the castle like a ham.

clovin_belview/90312b77f7f32652.text: The Abbot will be disappointed. He doesn't shout when he's disappointed. He just gets very kind. You don't want him kind.

clovin_belview/939f3fdf6903e73c.text: Don't. Don't say it. I know what I look like. I look like a man who walked two days to a winery and found nobody to sell him wine. That's what I look like.

clovin_belview/a8ebca793fbb8242.text: Vasilka. That's her name; he picked it. I carried half of her up the mountain myself, in a sack, at night, from the graves by the pool. Don't ask which half.

clovin_belview/bc12232840d1eb40.text: We were Krezk folk once. Grandmother says. Then we all got sick and came up here and got better. Then he made us better again. And again. He calls it improving.

clovin_belview/bcc3c88978b5e4c3.text: Maybe keep your hood up, miss. In the chapel. He likes red. He likes it too much.

clovin_belview/c839ffaf37cee36d.text: I've had three improvements. You can see two of them. Don't ask about the third. Mother's had nine. She doesn't come out much.

clovin_belview/e7df1386885592f1.text: Trouble, they said. Didn't open the gate, didn't sell me a drop. Somebody shouted from a window to go home, there was trouble, and to tell everyone. So. I'm telling everyone. You're everyone.

clovin_belview/f279f463e2ca0b33.text: You! The people from the road. With the wheel. Well. Well, now. Come in out of the wind; it gets up here before anyone else does.

clovin_belview/fa22b8e2f634799f.text: You killed him. In his own chapel. I swept up after. There wasn't much; it went to light. Mother says we'll go down to Krezk. Krezk won't have us. We'll go anyway.

clovin_belview/fd677d41fd2748a5.text: The last of the Martikovs'. Go on. Nobody drinks with me. Mother says it's because of the ear. I say it's because of the wine.

clovin_belview/fff95a61019d8b45.text: He sits. In the chapel. He doesn't talk. I bring him water and he doesn't drink it, and I take it away and bring more. Somebody has to carry things.

cult_shades/51cd446083782875.text: One must die. We will wait. We are very good at waiting.

cult_shades/51fbfadf617e373b.text: You came for the child. The child was ours first. One must die.

cult_shades/538ab7ce5cde72b5.text: Then the house will have all of you.

cult_shades/5efb6b933756761b.text: One has died. The house is satisfied.

cult_shades/7271814bb60cc0f0.text: We fed the house. The house fed the one below. The one below waits for the lord to remember us. One must die.

cult_shades/b273cbaa8f8f6815.text: One must die. One must die. One must die.

cult_shades/c4bf044b927bb0db.text: A spirit does not die. It only goes home. One must die.

danika_martikov/34af58d1d7d7a6bd.text: Then it's not just us. Then something's wrong at the vineyard. I'll tell Urwin. He'll want to know where you heard it.

danika_martikov/5b9860d8788e61c4.text: Stew. It's always stew. What's in it depends what Urwin found. Don't ask him, and don't ask the stew.

danika_martikov/6116781dcf617129.text: Guests. Wipe your feet. Brom! Bray! Get away from that window. Sorry. Two boys and an inn. You'd think one would cancel out the other.

danika_martikov/82f8594740a7079c.text: You did this. I know you did; the whole town watched you do it. You'll get a bed, because I won't turn anyone into the night. Don't expect breakfast.

danika_martikov/cb699b0589d3d827.text: Safe as anyone in this valley. Safer than most. Our windows have very good locks, and better neighbours.

danika_martikov/d140abc1e42d6fc6.text: Thin? It's the last cask. The wine comes from Urwin's father's vineyard, the Wizard of Wines, south of the lake road. Every month, a cart. Three months now, no cart, and no word.

davian_martikov/04bdad0bddfbb706.text: To starve us, first. A winery without wine is a farm with airs. And on Yester Hill, west of here, they're building a great figure of earth shaped like the lord in the castle. They mean to wake it with my stone for a heart.

davian_martikov/09885e7b26566722.text: I'll be counting the spoons, mind.

davian_martikov/1528b1ed336d0b3b.text: He's home. That's the thing. Whatever else is true, he's home.

davian_martikov/1d9ae58e27c2b7dd.text: Someone has been in my strongbox. It was a good lock. It was a good lock for forty years.

davian_martikov/202e8be18e0dce58.text: To Krezk. They keep their gate shut to strangers and open it for my carts. If you're going that way, walk beside the casks. A gate that opens for wine might open for you.

davian_martikov/22072ef1e254e3c9.text: Go on. The house won't empty itself.

davian_martikov/22c0cefb472c4e7c.text: From the witch. From Berez. You went into that drowned place for my vines. ...Three. I didn't think I'd see three again before I died. I find I'm in less of a hurry now.

davian_martikov/28bcdec5fdddc375.text: Now come and do the same to the ones sleeping in my house.

davian_martikov/2b972daa8bca7e8e.text: Then here are the terms. Drive them out of the winery and out of the press house. Bring up my stone from the founder's cask: cellar, foot of the stair, third hoop, pull. Then we'll talk about the hill.

davian_martikov/2e561dd67d2df5f9.text: To Urwin, then. He'll pretend he isn't pleased. He gets that from me.

davian_martikov/3cc035f43c2eb270.text: ...I sent them. I sent them to that hill. And I couldn't look at the one who came home, because then I'd have to look at the one who sent them.

davian_martikov/425880c667ec1953.text: Your fee. My father paid men to clear wolves from these rows, and they charged less, and they were also thieves. Fine. It's paid.

davian_martikov/441260068c83c52c.text: And one thing I can't account for. The ravens say a cold light shows in my house some nights, where no lamp is. If you find it, it isn't mine.

davian_martikov/4540aa248de7ea06.text: Then the press runs again. Not this week; the grapes need a month to remember themselves. But the cellar still holds what we pressed before they came, and the cart in the yard has three good wheels.

davian_martikov/45f43798b7b71c3e.text: To the village. The shopkeeper there will try to charge them double for it. The ravens will see that he doesn't.

davian_martikov/468fcccd31bbb157.text: One was stolen last autumn. The ravens followed the thief to Berez, the drowned village by the river, to the witch who lives there. One the druids carried off to their hill. The last I hid the night we fled.

davian_martikov/4fb5a58643bd8552.text: Then why didn't he say so? He's had a year. A year of me looking through him at supper.

davian_martikov/52d18762d2e55b42.text: Even you. My son says you're not as bad as your aim. Ravens have long memories, but we're not unreasonable.

davian_martikov/59ede29d685f4250.text: The druids sleep in the fermenting hall and feed my vats to their creatures. Their leader, a boy called Kostin, keeps to the press house with something he grew in my best vat. Some nights it sings to him.

davian_martikov/6286b12e37972198.text: My family pressed wine on this hill before the valley had its lord. The man on the sign is the wizard who paid us in stones. We set by a cask for him every year. He's never come for it. Wizards are poor at visiting.

davian_martikov/72c8f059be314d06.text: The first cart goes where you say. You've earned that much.

davian_martikov/72e38efe441343df.text: The Keepers of the Feather owe you two stones and a house, and ravens don't forget a debt. Wherever you go in this valley, look up. If you need word carried or eyes on a place, say so out loud.

davian_martikov/76086d5d5b8a8327.text: Adrian. The press is yours. My knees are finished with it.

davian_martikov/797674be2f94d1e5.text: Hello, old friend. You hid well. Better than I did.

davian_martikov/7ee8dc21c668eb56.text: Urwin's friends. The birds have talked of nothing else for a week. Sit. You're shorter than they said.

davian_martikov/8298993ef7419b23.text: The druids. Of course. Filthy creatures, druids. No respect for a good lock.

davian_martikov/82be96bf7ad8ef09.text: My son Elvir went to watch that hill last spring. Don't ask me about it.

davian_martikov/8997baf4dc2b8a0f.text: Adrian has the press. Stefania has the house. I have nothing left to do here but get in the way. Better I get in his way.

davian_martikov/8f615f8ae8811e4d.text: You took my son up that hill and brought him back down it. I'll not forget that.

davian_martikov/902f1a22c3f612e7.text: The boy Kostin ran west, the ravens say, toward the hill. He'll warn them you're coming. Expect to be expected.

davian_martikov/90e037efa83533db.text: Hm. You have honest faces, or faces that have practised. In the cellar, at the foot of the stair, stands the founder's cask, older than the house. It has a false end. Turn the third hoop and pull.

davian_martikov/934bd45451438a99.text: The figure broken and the druids scattered. And the tree? Still standing, the ravens say. Hm. Trees are patient. So are ravens.

davian_martikov/a293478e7fc6964d.text: No. You don't. Neither do I.

davian_martikov/a8844ce231f80cc9.text: Then we'll find out when I count it, won't we. I'll count it later, alone, like a miser. It's a family tradition.

davian_martikov/ab6bc8bfa8d12887.text: "I sent him." ...Elvir. You stubborn, stupid boy. You always did think you were the eldest.

davian_martikov/ac6554596f34ce2d.text: Because a raven sees a great deal and repeats it in the right ears. My family has watched the lord in the castle for longer than he has known he was being watched. He knows now. This is his answer.

davian_martikov/afa2cc7f0b32405b.text: Someone in Vallaki misses my wine, then. Good. So do I. Sit.

davian_martikov/b23c9a6aa58d7411.text: No vine should live in this valley; there's no sun worth the name. Ours do because three stones lie in their soil, green as new leaves, each the size of a plum. A wizard paid them to my family, long ago, for a winter's lodging.

davian_martikov/b3ac8e7e818840f9.text: To the hill, broken. To the house, ours. And to strangers, who it turns out are good for something.

davian_martikov/b69f5eca980e1e64.text: Ilinca Vrana says you pulled two children out of a hag's oven. Ilinca doesn't say good things about anyone, so I expect it's true. Sit.

davian_martikov/bacefd1b4bdc2e95.text: Hm. A thief who brings it back is either a fool or an honest man having a bad week. I'll assume the second. Keep ten for the lock.

davian_martikov/bb707eb29cee8445.text: I'll pay in the only coin I trust. Wine, when there's wine again. Until then, my gratitude, which is rarer.

davian_martikov/bc615c5aa10812aa.text: And Ruxandra is dead. I knew her when she was a girl who picked my grapes for a copper a basket. I'll drink to who she was. Not to what she became.

davian_martikov/bcd096b25d42202a.text: The ravens saw the smoke from here: one black column, straight up, as if the hill were being emptied. Good. Let it burn to the roots.

davian_martikov/beece6da2670e83b.text: Don't tell me what my son meant. I know what my son meant. I knew him before you knew this valley had a name.

davian_martikov/bfa4ddc3022716d8.text: Stefania will mind the house. Adrian will mind the vines. He's good at being left behind.

davian_martikov/c13b291b499f258c.text: Stefania! Bring the children. We're going home.

davian_martikov/c3f41c9dba707a5e.text: It's been near that tree. Good soil will draw it out, in time. Most things wash out, in time.

davian_martikov/c46a3c183e9d8d6d.text: And Ruxandra lives, somewhere out there. Mercy's a fine thing. Remember that you chose it, if she comes back.

davian_martikov/c718193e22f5214e.text: You asked before. My house is mine again. Ask me now.

davian_martikov/cc05af62cd12ef3e.text: The ravens saw the boy Kostin walk west, slowly, like a man who isn't sure where he's going anymore. Interesting.

davian_martikov/d3485ae57dbc6745.text: You're the ones who struck my son out of the air on the Svalich road. Sit down. I can't afford to throw you out, and I hate that more than I hate you.

davian_martikov/d45085ae41a49497.text: My house smells of druid. It will smell of wine again by spring or I'll know the reason. Speak.

davian_martikov/db79474244be5812.text: Druids don't pick locks. They don't need to; they grow through them. Don't lie to me in my own house. You're not good enough at it yet.

davian_martikov/de2d01219cde5cc6.text: Eva. Of course it was Eva. She bought wine from my father and haggled him to tears. If her cards say the old raven flies with you, then the old raven flies with you.

davian_martikov/df7e02a91ded3b9e.text: Fewer than yesterday, if you start now.

davian_martikov/e19e3896b40a87b8.text: They're tearing my house apart to find it. So far my house is winning.

davian_martikov/e88ed32b191335d4.text: Strangers, at my fire. Either you've come to rob me, and you're three months late, or you've come to help, and you're very welcome. Sit.

davian_martikov/f0e193c4db4cc43c.text: I am Davian Martikov. That was my winery up there until the druids of Yester Hill walked up my lane with the forest at their backs. Now my family lives under the trees like birds. Which, in fairness, we are.

davian_martikov/f25fe283265ca1f6.text: I've drunk to both, in alternate years.

davian_martikov/f5a398517b1daae9.text: A Vistani crone shuffled her deck and my name fell out. Hm. I'll go where her cards say, and gladly, once there are no druids asleep in my bed. Not before. A man doesn't leave his house to squatters.

davian_martikov/fea6eab5c80fd098.text: Two. Two in the ground. My grandfather had only two for a while, when he was a boy, and he swore the wine was better for having to try.

dmitri_krezkov/064e7686dee8c1a1.text: Nobody has talked their way past that gate in eleven years. I'll let you in to see what that kind of tongue looks like. Open it.

dmitri_krezkov/066b13afb09e2425.text: Dmitri Krezkov, burgomaster. The Martikovs' wine has come up this road every autumn since my grandfather's time. This year: nothing. No cart, no word.

dmitri_krezkov/0a83253979c1c6f4.text: The road ends here. The mountains don't. Everything that comes down out of them, or up the road at us, meets the wall first. That's what a wall is for.

dmitri_krezkov/1422e26e643dd494.text: Dmitri Krezkov, burgomaster. You're a priest. A real one, with a god that answers?

dmitri_krezkov/160b361d3384ea83.text: Or very loud. Come in, then. You'd climb it otherwise, and I'd lose men stopping you. Don't make me sorry I counted.

dmitri_krezkov/1f71e18d2b910050.text: Dmitri Krezkov, burgomaster. You bled on our doorstep for us. That's a reason. Open it.

dmitri_krezkov/21dc533ccc1b0be3.text: Might. He might. And then I'd owe him my son, and he'd come down for the debt one day with that kind face of his, asking nicely.

dmitri_krezkov/2b33d6a6ea5b5810.text: The Abbot cured them. He keeps them up there still, and he's been improving them ever since. That's his word for it. Go and look at them, and then tell me what word you'd use.

dmitri_krezkov/2b97d402555e6ec4.text: The devil wants you. Every soul in the valley knows it. You ask me to open my gate and let his want in after you.

dmitri_krezkov/2f259b2a33087fd4.text: He looks like a boy carved out of honey and he talks like your grandmother. Folk go up that mountain sick and come down well. Or they don't come down.

dmitri_krezkov/302b516373d59e27.text: The Martikovs. Their cart came up every autumn since my grandfather's time. Wine for the shrine, wine for weddings, wine for the long nights. This year nothing.

dmitri_krezkov/36a612706228dff3.text: Dead. An angel, or whatever he was, dead in his own chapel. I'll have the bell rung. Somebody should, and nobody up there will.

dmitri_krezkov/38acb2926434d1ae.text: He's out of bed. Thin as a candle, but out of bed. Anna says the White Sun did it. I say you did. We've agreed to both be right.
