dmitri_krezkov/3c425ff957a29b03.text: You came to my gate with threats, and now you want me to take in the one woman in the valley he'd burn a village to reach? No. Find her another wall.

dmitri_krezkov/4965ea1543af43bf.text: Dmitri Krezkov. Burgomaster. My watchman tells me you're very persuasive.

dmitri_krezkov/59a7aab62b1f5a5b.text: A village that can't drink can still pray, but it does it with less conviction. Come in. Drink our water. Tell me what you know.

dmitri_krezkov/5a598402f396f04d.text: Five of our children are in the churchyard by the pool. I can walk to their stones with my eyes shut. I am not going to learn the way to a sixth.

dmitri_krezkov/612e7751c91ac03e.text: Inside. Quickly. We don't hold it open for weather. My house is the big one past the well, if you've business with Krezk.

dmitri_krezkov/62d86336f10f5e68.text: That's more than mine does. My son is sick. My last son. If your god answers you in my house, you can have anything Krezk owns. Open it.

dmitri_krezkov/78fa5c2941ac8e2e.text: If you pass that way, find out what's become of them. Krezk would owe you, and Krezk pays in things you can't buy anywhere else. Goat cheese, mostly. And honesty.

dmitri_krezkov/8070d6130682800c.text: Ireena Kolyana. I knew your father. I am Dmitri Krezkov, and Krezk is mine to keep.

dmitri_krezkov/8498c8a389d54235.text: Our healer died two winters back. Anna sits with him. She sings. When she stops singing, I go up and check he's breathing.

dmitri_krezkov/853b4e9b595337f3.text: He's never once raised his voice, or a hand, to anyone in Krezk. That frightens me more than if he had.

dmitri_krezkov/8b72b93cb9d04565.text: Back again. Sit, if you like. The chairs are older than the both of us and they've held worse.

dmitri_krezkov/8d209f282b1cd354.text: My son is well, and the thing on the mountain is dead, and I didn't have to choose which I wanted more. You did that. Krezk keeps its debts.

dmitri_krezkov/90f7c95fb7f48697.text: The little room off the hall. It was my eldest's. It's had nobody in it for six years, and it'll be glad of the company. Lock the shutters. Krezk does.

dmitri_krezkov/9380ab0a2d32ecc5.text: If he says you're harmless, you're harmless or you're his. Either way, he'd find another road for you. Open it.

dmitri_krezkov/94d1b9ff94a54ccc.text: The Belviews were a Krezk family. Farmers, two doors from here. A sickness took the whole house, and they went up to the abbey for the cure.

dmitri_krezkov/a36d24971ea7bf71.text: Your father sent us salt, the winter the passes closed and we had none. Krezk doesn't forget salt. Open it.

dmitri_krezkov/b21af8c0cbe042aa.text: The Abbot came down at dawn and put his hand on the boy's head, and walked back up without a word. I owe him. I hate owing him. Both of those are true.

dmitri_krezkov/b37fcbe836083619.text: One thing. Word came up from Vallaki that Fiona Wachter sits in the burgomaster's chair now, and that strangers put her there. If that was you, keep it to yourselves inside my wall.

dmitri_krezkov/b40bf8522bee23af.text: The Belviews say he walked up the mountain and didn't stop at the top. I've hated him for twenty years. I find I'm not sure who to hate now. It's restful.

dmitri_krezkov/b4e23f3514246c34.text: And she wants me to go up the mountain and ask the Abbot. On my knees, I expect, the way the Belviews asked.

dmitri_krezkov/b578123498ced975.text: If he comes to my door on his own, I won't bar it. That's as far as I can bend. Don't ask me to bend further. I'll break, and Anna needs one of us whole.

dmitri_krezkov/b86ac6e36a3f4e92.text: Word came from Vallaki that the town threw out its Baron and put a priest and an innkeeper in charge. If you had a hand in it, I'd shake it. Once.

dmitri_krezkov/bff4743d94643dab.text: In Anna's dress. I haven't told her yet what it was for. I don't know if I will.

dmitri_krezkov/c0c37e4a36a5e616.text: I'm Dmitri Krezkov, burgomaster. You've been up the mountain. And he sent you down to me with his blessing.

dmitri_krezkov/c7327af817520444.text: I made nothing of him while he lived, because I was afraid. Now he's dead and I find I'm still afraid. Perhaps that was never about him.

dmitri_krezkov/cbe8e76b41c2eb67.text: You gave him his bride. A dead girl sewn out of our dead girls, sent down the road to the castle in a wedding dress. Krezk will pray about that for a long time.

dmitri_krezkov/cded5316c9518776.text: Our wall, our roof, our bread. It's not much and he'll know where it is within a week. But it's yours, Ireena Kolyana. Your father sent us salt once.

dmitri_krezkov/ce7f0215d34e7280.text: He's out at the well, shouting at goats. My son. I keep going to the window to check it's true.

dmitri_krezkov/dd80bf03df15c41a.text: Every stranger who knocked in my lifetime wanted something. Twice, it was him, wearing a stranger's face, asking nicely. So now we ask for a reason, and we decide what a reason is.

dmitri_krezkov/e31270f96ab95cb3.text: And you're the ones who offered to test my wall. My bowman remembers your faces. So will I. Behave inside it.

dmitri_krezkov/e55916f319bc899f.text: Dmitri Krezkov. This is my house, and that's my table, and you're welcome at both while you mind the wall's rules.

dmitri_krezkov/f2f26a8aa67397ac.text: You. The ones who threatened my watchman. Say your business and don't get comfortable.

dmitri_krezkov/f4c3c703e80b40a4.text: My son Ilya. Eight years old. A fever came up the road in the autumn with the last carter, and it found him. It's been burning a month.

dmitri_krezkov/f5ea8dda7ec2c3d1.text: He sits in his chapel, the Belviews say, and won't speak. A thing like that, broken. I thought I'd be glad. I'm only tired.

dmitri_krezkov/f68dc12f06131757.text: You were. Don't spend it all at once.

dmitri_krezkov/fa9def900ca6af90.text: Sent by who? No. Don't answer that. I'd rather not have to pray to whoever it was.

dmitri_krezkov/fce93394c15894e9.text: Upstairs. Anna won't let go of his hand, so you'll have to work around her.

donavich/053e692327b64cbc.text: It's still quiet below. I keep waking to listen for him. Habit, I suppose. Grief is mostly habit.

donavich/09c8fd642f507493.text: There's nothing to tell. Nothing. Please.

donavich/14ff4b0c7dd936df.text: Please. Whatever you are, don't hurt him. There may be a way back. There must be.

donavich/1a3f7c948a5ad59e.text: The rest is in the vestry, for the burial of the dead. Ask me again when I know you better.

donavich/2290855b8c982567.text: You've been below. You've seen him. Then there's no use lying, is there.

donavich/273ba3923b9e1b1a.text: And Morninglord forgive me, the moment he was gone I slept, the first time in weeks. What kind of father sleeps?

donavich/35f027b0a2824b70.text: If anyone alive knows where it lies, it's the old Vistani seer at Tser Pool. Or him. He keeps what frightens him.

donavich/36b98c50e734102b.text: You still feel Him? Here? I haven't, not for a year. I say "Dawn will come" every night, to keep my mouth from saying other things.

donavich/38d77e067fd1f8b3.text: Get out of my church. Bury your burgomaster yourselves. I have a son to bury, and no one to say the words over him either.

donavich/3e2f13bfacd0d52c.text: Ah, but you've found the vestry chest already. Keep what you took. It does no good in a box.

donavich/3e39a663631605b4.text: There's nothing for you here. Not anymore. Go.

donavich/3e3c9c15c8463e35.text: My own hand. Yes. I've held it every night for months, from this side. First let me pray. An hour. Forgive me; I need the hour more than he does.

donavich/44a392f65e32d166.text: It's quiet. For the first time in weeks, it's quiet below. Thank you. I think. Ask me again in a year.

donavich/46b9eebcc87f0201.text: The Durst children. Rose and Thorn. Folk saw them in the road for years. If they are at rest now, then you've done more for this village in a night than I have in a year.

donavich/4d4f70818680fba5.text: The Holy Symbol of Ravenkind. Older than this church. A giant raven brought it to a paladin of the dawn, the stories say, and it was turned against the devil once, and lost after. Lost, mind. Not destroyed.

donavich/4fcb1d49ec7cd93d.text: Then he's farther from the castle than any of us. Go. Bury your dead. I'll bury mine.

donavich/510a40441a61dce2.text: Months later Doru came home, at night, wearing his own face. I lured him below and barred the door. I pray. He screams. Neither of us has stopped since.

donavich/539ab017640b6d79.text: You've come back. He's still below. You left him to me, and I'm grateful, and some nights I wish you hadn't. Both of those are prayers, I think.

donavich/53a0c144b2542ccf.text: You've come back. He hasn't. I leave the side door unbarred at night now. I don't know if that's faith or foolishness.

donavich/6233819e2ad9964c.text: The bell rang by itself when that house at the end of the lane began to groan. You were inside it, weren't you, children? And you came out. The Morninglord keeps odd company these days.

donavich/67cc6f3665fd04fe.text: No. I'm sorry. I can't. If he gets past you, he gets past me, and then the village. The bar stays.

donavich/70b16faca21bb9a9.text: Do it, then. Gently, if there's any gentle way. I've lifted the bar. I can't watch. I'm sorry, my boy. I'm so sorry.

donavich/72bcc122dabeb539.text: No. No! He's my son. You'll not touch him. The bar stays where it is, and you'll stay away from it.

donavich/795a613178f81655.text: You went down there. You killed my boy. I begged you. I begged you.

donavich/7a9a52b918dc86cd.text: You've come back, children. Forgive me if I don't rise; my knees have taken the shape of the floor.

donavich/7ac52eedc1a77796.text: Talk? Oh, he'll talk. He'll talk you all the way to the door and through it. He was always good at talking.

donavich/7add3eb5f9df0e72.text: Forgive me. Pay it no mind, children, please. It's nothing that concerns you.

donavich/7bfe148e14559072.text: You ask me that? After what you did below? No.

donavich/7f0522b8de65b2cf.text: I'll keep him fed on prayer until you come back. It's all I have to feed him on.

donavich/7f11e8a1fc10b9f5.text: My son. Doru. He went with the other young men to storm the castle and kill the devil in his bed. They had torches and a song. The devil gave them dinner.

donavich/8f7e7efc60d1c245.text: Need? Food. Sleep. My son back. You can't give me those, children. Holy water is all I have left to give, and precious little of that.

donavich/9cafebe75706fe58.text: Forgive me. Forgive... I've lost the words.

donavich/a9484897955c9eb3.text: We give Kolyan Indirovich to the earth he kept, in the light he trusted. Morninglord, you who come back every morning though no one thanks you for it, come back for him.

donavich/a9ea6c32240cdfc7.text: Forgive me, children. You've been in the house at the end of the lane; there's a smell on you I know from funerals that went wrong. That house wanted an offering. I won't ask what you gave it. The Morninglord already knows.

donavich/b07d60b1ecd1b344.text: End it. You mean kill him. Kill my boy.

donavich/bfd171e410046db3.text: Take these. Holy water. It will burn him. I blessed it for him weeks ago, and could never throw it.

donavich/d392551f4c51d7e0.text: Here. Two flasks. Throw them hard; the dead don't flinch the way the living do.

donavich/ddc46aed171f2bb8.text: The bar is up. The undercroft is empty. You let him out. He'll go to the castle. He'll go to him.

donavich/e6a09acb84391b4e.text: Rest, Kolyan. Nobody will call you up again. Not while I have breath to forbid it.

donavich/e89ff3d79983fbd3.text: Your word. In Barovia that's a strange coin. Very well; the bar is up. Don't open your hand to him. Don't let him see your throat.

donavich/ec0ac84afa5e05f9.text: I've given you all I had. The well's dry, and so am I.

donavich/f186972a6db0642d.text: A madman. A poor soul I shelter, out of charity. He's loud. Please, don't go near the undercroft door.

donavich/f4f880796e6cc8d4.text: You would? There are old stories. Saints' bones that turn the dead. Relics of the Morninglord. The sun itself, once. If anything in this valley could bring him back, it's one of those.

donavich/f59eab40f9247a58.text: Forgive me. You've sat through it now. There's no use lying to people who've sat through it.

donavich/f706681d48fd2b91.text: Who... forgive me. Visitors. We have so few. The doors are open; I can't remember why I stopped barring them. Perhaps I hoped someone would come.

donavich/f75ea70729aa651f.text: Kolyan. He came every holy day until there were no holy days left. Yes. Yes, I'll say the words over him. It's the one thing I still know how to do.

donavich/ff607d5632fe1e5c.text: Bring him to the grave behind the church; I'll meet you there. And if my boy cries out during the rites, keep singing. Please. Keep singing.

doru/2633bf933b768a92.text: He fed us. He let us talk about killing him all through the meal, smiling. Then the candles went out. I was dessert, he said. The others weren't so lucky. Or they were.

doru/36dbfbc447f3b194.text: You would? Oh, you would. I'll go far away. To the castle; the master will take me in. I'll never trouble Father again. I swear it on the Morninglord. On my mother. On anything.

doru/4909a05251994079.text: Doru. The priest's son. I rang the bell on holy days, before. I was going to be a hero. Everyone was going to sing about it.

doru/54c9badd83f8545f.text: He sent you. Didn't he. He finally said yes. Tell him I'm sorry about the cake on his name day. Tell him... quickly. Before I stop being sorry.

doru/9ee2ed3865d2b96f.text: Stop. Stop it, it burns. No, keep going. Father used to... stop! Stop!

doru/b2fe66ea26a527b0.text: We went up the road with torches, singing. The gates were open. He met us in the hall in a beautiful coat and said we must be hungry after such a climb.

doru/d39fe9e90b2ddf4e.text: Then come up here and do it.

doru/da2cda4de1875412.text: Don't stop. I like funerals now. My master sends his regrets; he's dining elsewhere tonight. He says Ireena should leave her window open. It's stuffy, waiting.

doru/db8f3a4228a846ed.text: Father? No. You smell like outside. Like rain and roads. I'd forgotten roads. Come closer; I can't see you properly.

doru/df08d4ec011540ff.text: Is he. Is he still. Tell him... no. Tell him nothing. Tell him I was never here.

doru/ed3216072f30a7cc.text: I'll tell him. He'll be delighted; he loves being told no. He sent a gift, in case you said it.

doru/eede6669c4ff8b7b.text: Go, then! Go! I'll be here. I'm always here. Tell Father I'm hungry. Tell him every night!

durst_nursemaid/3f688642df16de11.text: Liars. You're with them. You're wearing their faces!

durst_nursemaid/475a41be2343b6f3.text: He's under the house. He's been under the house so long. If you go down, sing it to him. Someone should.

durst_nursemaid/6f63aaf020b50c00.text: Gone. Yes. I knew. I knew when they stopped him crying. They stopped me too, at the bottom of the stairs.

durst_nursemaid/7a60fba2052cd40d.text: He was mine. The master's and mine. The mistress gave him to the robed ones the night he was born, and they carried him down, and I followed them.

durst_nursemaid/f06fdd0abb77cc7c.text: Have you brought him? Have you brought my Walter back up?

elisabeth_durst/114280b8a69c12e9.text: One must die, so the rest may live forever. We only got the second half wrong.

elisabeth_durst/3401308dfbde8e12.text: Upstairs. Safe. We locked them in so they wouldn't see.

elisabeth_durst/5daba77263063c8b.text: That one was never mine. He was the first gift. The finest gift we had.

elisabeth_durst/ed9e599aae00c894.text: They came down the children's way. Didn't you, dears.

emil_toranescu/16c9f6a5130098d7.text: The Vistani grandmother and her cards. She told me once I'd die in chains. Funny, how close she came.

emil_toranescu/19af3d13928d64b3.text: You freed me to kill me? Zuleika said you were honest. She was right. You're honest butchers.

emil_toranescu/2bbb4e5b8e044aa8.text: I'll be here. The jewellery makes sure of it.

emil_toranescu/2e40a729202e2ebd.text: Zuleika has one; Kiril trusted her with it so she could watch. Kiril keeps the other on a peg in his lair, north of the great cave, because he likes to look at it.

emil_toranescu/2e7641ddbdf175d1.text: It's done. By the old law the pack is mine again. Kiril's favourites are dead or running down the Krezk road with their tails tucked. The rest are listening.

emil_toranescu/3386e728dd21b226.text: I know it. That's why I'm the one in chains.

emil_toranescu/3396ba1fa8e695d5.text: He's not far. He never was, from his supper. Wait for him in the great cave, where he can see us.

emil_toranescu/3df98278ec1ca216.text: Hear me, then. We hunt deer. We keep to the high hills. We don't come when the castle whistles. And the children go home.

emil_toranescu/4632d4881a479bc3.text: The Vistani grandmother's cards. She told me once I'd die in chains, and she was nearly right. Now they say I'm to walk with you to the old man's door.

emil_toranescu/4d0626087f781649.text: Thank you. Now I have to do something you won't like. A chained wolf who walks free without howling his challenge is a thief, and anyone may kill a thief.

emil_toranescu/5615c80d7e7e2f11.text: Emil Toranescu. I led this pack nineteen winters. We hunted deer and the odd careless shepherd, kept to the high hills, and left the villages alone. The castle left us alone in return. Then Kiril came home.

emil_toranescu/5c401a16c13bd2ce.text: Get me out of these, and let's see what else she got wrong.

emil_toranescu/66177b81b06c4a8a.text: But if it ever comes to the end with the old man on the hill, and you need teeth at his gates, send word up this hill.

emil_toranescu/73bf612faee3a92e.text: Not mine. I wasn't leader then. But I was in those woods that night, and so were wolves that weren't ours: the castle's, big and silent.

emil_toranescu/833538e3db13b101.text: Kiril will hear it. He'll come. When he does, you'll want to be standing next to me.

emil_toranescu/8911897212e1778d.text: You smell of Zuleika's herbs. She sent you. That woman. I told her not to.

emil_toranescu/8a7f672c50eb9b79.text: Visitors. Kiril's? No. Kiril's visitors don't look at the chains like that.

emil_toranescu/8b8127f092beb4af.text: The pack is quieter without Kiril. Hungrier, too. Deer it is, for a while.

emil_toranescu/9a57b5f0ce4437e0.text: I know. I told you not to.

emil_toranescu/9bfa58a62c87504a.text: And the huntress. You killed two of Kiril's on the Krezk road. Good shooting. I'd have done it myself, with my hands free.

emil_toranescu/9d131a9030519fe8.text: You've given me back my pack. I can't follow you to the castle; they'd be at each other's throats in a week without me, and at Zuleika's in two.

emil_toranescu/9f7165706077f504.text: The ones who loved Kiril are dead or gone down the Krezk road. The rest are tired and glad to be. Zuleika has them mending things. Wolves hate mending things.

emil_toranescu/a0b0399868178833.text: She means she never needed me.

emil_toranescu/a59ea0516707b3a4.text: Then stand close, and don't let them get behind you.

emil_toranescu/a5d875f61384023d.text: Go well. Keep to the trail; my wolves know your smell now.

emil_toranescu/a860dea8819a3662.text: I misjudged you. That's my fault, not yours. I always was too quick to like people.

emil_toranescu/ac7b481977bf8cd0.text: And be hunted through the hills by a pack that knows every stone, with five children who can't run? No. We do it the old way, here, with rock at our backs.

emil_toranescu/bdfc834112dbd6b5.text: Watch, then, huntress. From a respectful distance.

emil_toranescu/c131c78eac2038b5.text: I told him the old law: we don't take pups that aren't ours. He said the old law was dead. Then his favourites held me down.

emil_toranescu/d78fcc34cf16889d.text: There was a boy screaming and a girl with red hair, and a rider in black at the treeline. We ran. I've been ashamed of running for twenty years.

emil_toranescu/d9771e68eda034d7.text: Not come. Let the old man on the hill whistle for his dogs. If it ever comes to the end with him, and you need teeth at his gates, send word up the hill.

emil_toranescu/db1482a64381ce5b.text: The key would be kinder. To both of us.

emil_toranescu/e35afea0ed4afaba.text: Still here. Still chained. Neither of us is enjoying it.

emil_toranescu/e7677a143b700f6c.text: I howled the challenge, Kiril. By the old law, you answer it.

emil_toranescu/eb6d5a7315c95cd2.text: I always mind the bite. That was the whole argument.

emil_toranescu/ef556c51dc16fde1.text: You found Kiril's chest. Good. Half of it came off the Krezk road; if you pass anyone who looks robbed, you know what to do.

emil_toranescu/f188ca634dc58544.text: Kiril went up to the castle and came back with a new law. The master wants an army that runs on four legs. And where do new wolves come from? He came back from the Krezk road with a sack of children.

exethanter/055dd0501cc44a2f.text: Not so loud! Someone might hear, and then they'd know where it isn't.

exethanter/0888e9573f2ddcc4.text: Please. I'd like to forget this again now. Would you mind very much if I did?

exethanter/0cf77f9d0b804d6f.text: How thoughtful! I'll read it every time I see you. If I remember to read it. I generally do read my sleeve.

exethanter/16e619a29eab21cd.text: Oh, no. Oh, my dears. We had one rule. One. We carved it over the door so we wouldn't forget, and even I...

exethanter/1a6eaec0d78d37ee.text: I took him down to the one with no name. I told myself the rule was for wardens, and he wasn't one. The jackal was there, I think. I think he was smiling.

exethanter/1c0f95cc87825869.text: We gathered up the vestiges, you see: the last scraps of dead gods and worse, things the world was right to forget. Amber holds them. Nothing else does. And then we sat down to guard them forever.

exethanter/22995ceb480c89a5.text: This? The Amber Temple. We built it. Well. They built it, and I helped, and then they all died and I didn't, which I gather is the usual arrangement with liches.

exethanter/23f4f75b52175424.text: Need? Oh, there is something, now you mention it. I've lost a... thing. Small. It has a lid, I'm nearly sure. A box, or a jar. Something with a lid.

exethanter/31a02403206ecb05.text: Ah. Well. You live a few centuries, things slip. Names. Faces. Most of my spells. I used to know one that made a sort of wall out of... no. It's gone. It had a lovely name.

exethanter/3ad1ca803d5fd080.text: Goodbye! Do come again. I'll be delighted to meet you.

exethanter/3b39ae87a28c1a61.text: One by one. They were very persuasive scraps. I believe I listened too. I can't remember to which.

exethanter/3baac9570d68b5ae.text: Goodbye, friends! It says friends. Mind the duck.

exethanter/3ef1405d6e17d4fc.text: The jackal's gone. I felt him go, like a draught shutting off. I've been cold for three hundred years and never noticed.

exethanter/3f74c60a3d4f0548.text: Here! I wrote it down. Clever me. You say it like a door closing. There. Now you know it, and I've already half forgotten I told you, so we're both quite safe.

exethanter/44ed5b7a58f17fbd.text: The word! Yes. The wardens' word. It quiets the colossus and it opens the honey doors, and it's... it's...

exethanter/4fbfb0a6c972b3fc.text: Where else would I keep it? In my head? Have you met my head?

exethanter/6724f56ee3e7e871.text: Vosk? Is that his name this time? Pleasant fellow. Reads a great deal. He's been in my library for... I want to say a week. I said that last time too. It may have been a century.

exethanter/68c8f97a27da9a67.text: I'm sorting. Deciding what to forget on purpose, for once. It's quite pleasant. Did you want something?

exethanter/68ff43e4dbf5d0f5.text: NOT THE... oh, that's good. That's very clever. Nobody would ever look there. I didn't, for a hundred and twelve years.

exethanter/69925a40f1ff48a2.text: ...Yes. All right. A warden's whole job is to remember. I'll write it on the back of my hand, where I'll see it every time I reach for something.

exethanter/6c6cc6df2404d99e.text: It's in here somewhere. I'd look harder if I weren't so distracted. I've lost something, you see. Something with a lid.

exethanter/7662d589362f0a67.text: The word for the doors, at least, you shall have, written out large. And there's a note about the jackal somewhere. Ask me about him; I'll find it now. I feel much less distracted.

exethanter/7665abf90a0ef477.text: Thank you. ...Thank you for what? Never mind. I'm sure it was kind.

exethanter/77fe8d294cd66f06.text: Visitors! How unusual. We almost never get visitors. Have we met? You have the look of people I've met. Everyone does, lately.

exethanter/8394884a3ee1d039.text: "These are friends. Do not freeze them." Friends! Of course. I knew that. Sit, sit. What can I fail to remember for you today?

exethanter/89dfed95d05b6b32.text: Norganas? I don't... oh dear. Oh, dear. The eraser.

exethanter/8b5d1541108894a3.text: I think I've been waiting for that for a very long time. Thank you. I think. Would you go away now, please? Gently.

exethanter/8ce883556cb81fcf.text: Visitors! I feel as though I ought to be grateful to you for something. I am, whatever it was. Hello!

exethanter/8d5d74d116d5856f.text: Have you got it? Might I... could I have it back?

exethanter/8f18deb53f8d23f5.text: I write things down. That's what the notes are for. The difficulty is remembering to read them, and which ones are still true. One just says DUCK, underlined, and I have no idea at all.

exethanter/950bb7e23fe540f5.text: That's my hand. That's... yes. That's my hand.

exethanter/98aeb1df5b6e94ba.text: And the colossus won't let you out with it, you know. It was built for nothing else. Say the word to it on your way out, if you have the word.

exethanter/9cff5c27cc6f3052.text: There. Done. I think I'll sit down now. I think I'll sit down for a very long time.

exethanter/9db7cea31bb56661.text: It was very kind about it. It kept on taking. It's still taking. That's why everything goes, isn't it? It isn't age at all. It's interest.

exethanter/a0c11dba24eb2dc4.text: If the jackal is in my temple, he's waiting at the bottom, where it happened. And when he's gone, there's a rite. The last one we had. Find me after.

exethanter/a36c2917ea50392e.text: Yes. I remember remembering. The voices were so loud, those first years. I asked it to take the whispering out of my head. Only the whispering.

exethanter/a36eccbe075805bb.text: Oh, must we? I was enjoying the company. I can't remember the last time I enjoyed company.

exethanter/b2821931acac4286.text: Then this is the third time, and the third time is when one finally gets to know a person. Splendid.

exethanter/b416906da016c3bd.text: Do they? I'll write that down. I'll write it down this minute and pin it somewhere I'll see it.

exethanter/bc2240267692d782.text: The jackal's gone, and he left smiling. He's never left smiling before. What did you give him?

exethanter/bdbbfd8f331f1e0c.text: Oh! Living people. Hello! Don't be alarmed, I'm a lich. Was a lich. Am a lich; one doesn't really stop. Exethanter, Warden of the Amber, at your service, if I can remember what the service involves.

exethanter/bed5895133e2c113.text: Well. It's done; it never comes undone. Don't take another. They're like stairs: each one is only a small step down.

exethanter/c22bd5cefc9216d7.text: It's on the back of my hand, see? "He showed the prince the way down." I've read it nine times since you left. It doesn't get easier. It isn't supposed to.

exethanter/c477725ab8bb2a66.text: Here. Take the note. I won't be needing it.

exethanter/c5b8598334b79841.text: He was so polite. Young, angry, grieving something he hadn't lost yet. He wanted time. He said he had a war to finish, a woman to win, and a brother who would always be younger than him.

exethanter/c68565214c9c72a0.text: Still here? So am I. It's what I do.

exethanter/d3c156a0123d6c5b.text: Of course. Practical. We said that too, the first year. I'll just... sweep.

exethanter/d7c7bd2b69f77fff.text: It wants a warden, which I am, and a reason, which I think you've given me. Shall I?

exethanter/ddbb2a3dc30fec75.text: It's rather important. If anything happened to this body, the thing with the lid is how I'd come back. And I hid it so cleverly that now I can't find it.

exethanter/de708f57f1cfff1f.text: Was there a fight? There's always a fight down here, sooner or later. I come down afterward to sweep. Oh. Is that... was that a jackal?

exethanter/e044652ec648d9a0.text: The thing with the lid! You remembered. Did you find it? No? It'll be somewhere sensible. I'm a very sensible person. That's what worries me.

exethanter/e047e19625620b6d.text: Very well. I'll be... cooperative. That's the word, isn't it? You'll have the doors' word, and anything else I can find.

exethanter/e1a0da1362d1414f.text: Ask away! I'll answer the ones I recall. It won't take long.

exethanter/e612ad276a865279.text: I don't like him. I can't remember why. There's a note somewhere.

exethanter/e66fd829a0ee31c5.text: Thank you. Truly. I'd give you something, if I could remember what I own.

exethanter/eb093a453e6e3fde.text: There's a rite. The wardens' last one, the one we were meant to use if it ever came to this. It seals every sarcophagus at once. Nobody would ever hear them again. Nobody could ever bargain here again.

exethanter/f235cc05236ed7a1.text: Jackal? I don't recall a jackal. But I recall that I don't trust him, and that will have to do.

exethanter/fb0560f147812ea3.text: The trouble with forever is that the things you're guarding can talk.

exethanter/fc0d652f1e40c5ad.text: Ah. Yes. I see. I've held a few things over people myself, in my time. I just can't remember how it turned out for them.

ezmerelda/005d978c5ff939fa.text: Somebody has been in my wagon. Don't. Don't say anything. I know who's been up and down this shore this week, and it's a very short list.

ezmerelda/034d813733368223.text: And the children are going home. Good. That's a better day than this valley usually allows.

ezmerelda/0545627be7ab614b.text: Eva. Of course it's Eva. That old woman has been dealing me into other people's games since I was six.

ezmerelda/05f0a9ffbac3f1be.text: Four. The fourth is his handwriting.

ezmerelda/078ec7a045f3c2dd.text: Everyone does, at first. Ask Rudolph.

ezmerelda/0928fe3d145c3574.text: That's no monk. Look at his feet. He's standing a finger's breadth off the floor.

ezmerelda/0980f5cae2115f15.text: Kiril. Big, black, laughs with his mouth open?

ezmerelda/09fbced0f2f576c3.text: Feathers? Tell me there are feathers. No, don't. I'll see for myself. I'm leaving tonight.

ezmerelda/0c17a9dde2b25d5c.text: I've been taking them back two at a time ever since. Lately they've been carrying children up there, from the farms under Krezk. I'd go in after them, if Rudolph would let me into his armoury.

ezmerelda/0f1d986cc90c285b.text: The abbey. The locals call the man in charge an angel. Angels don't stitch, and somebody up there stitches a great deal. I've seen a sack carried in at night that was shaped like a woman.

ezmerelda/12fb2b58cfcfa3db.text: That sounded like you meant it, and nothing came off you in smoke. Good enough.

ezmerelda/151472af42bd7b94.text: In a taproom, pretending to be loud. I trained under that man for six years and never once heard him raise his voice. Did he do the lute? Please say he did the lute.

ezmerelda/173f4db7f71eec28.text: Kiril. Big, black, laughs with his mouth open? You left that one on top? With the children?

ezmerelda/18106db41217be4e.text: "If you are reading this, I am dead, or you are more stubborn than I hoped." I am more stubborn. I am always more stubborn. He knows that. He wrote it anyway.

ezmerelda/1b1cb32a7e3e4156.text: Stop there. Say something a vampire wouldn't say.

ezmerelda/25f5c13fb5193318.text: Back again. Has the tower spoken to you yet? It won't speak to me.

ezmerelda/2730342751aa7168.text: Then I'll tell him I wrung it out of you. He'll believe it. He knows me.

ezmerelda/2761dcaf96d0a6cd.text: He's in there. He came home. He's been in there the whole time, listening to me shout.

ezmerelda/2f6b2d7e9e7b70e3.text: A vampire would have said something about my eyes. Fine. Sit down before you fall in the lake.

ezmerelda/30db28a2aebd4cc9.text: A pack that leaves people alone. I'll believe it when I've watched it for a year.

ezmerelda/3653db5af7e8dd21.text: It won't know you. Go in for me. Find out where he's gone, and bring me anything with his handwriting on it.

ezmerelda/382d7df69e575f0c.text: Says someone who still has both feet.

ezmerelda/38a1dbb8e528e984.text: You're stitching a corpse a wedding for Strahd. I've hunted a lot of madmen. You're the calmest.

ezmerelda/390d69a7f25f7639.text: Rictavio. Rudolph is calling himself Rictavio. In a taproom.

ezmerelda/3d00f83234a550de.text: Ha. All right. A vampire would have said something charming. That was the least charming thing I've heard all month.

ezmerelda/3f14aee6bd0b0bdb.text: A werewolf in the hills above the lake, when I was young and quick and stupid. I kept the rest of me. Fair trade. The brace was Rudolph's work; it kicks harder than the old one did.

ezmerelda/3f9a6b0c775dd787.text: Then you should have stayed alive near me, so you could keep an eye on me. That was always the deal.

ezmerelda/45588df5ad8d1c63.text: Go carefully. If anything in these hills hums, growls or compliments you, shoot it.

ezmerelda/4795d83d09ae3cb0.text: You'd have done the same. You taught me.

ezmerelda/4904794cce3aad39.text: Ezmerelda d'Avenir. Of the Vistani, when they'll have me. I hunt the things that hunt people. I'm very good at it, as you can tell from all the bits of me that are left.

ezmerelda/4e1ffff193850cd4.text: Keep what you took. You'll need it. And then stay out of my way.

ezmerelda/508bc9c788225f28.text: He was always thorough about the wrong things.

ezmerelda/516ff1a8f3ec4c8f.text: A pack that leaves children alone. I'll believe it when I've watched it for a year.

ezmerelda/59055ddbddfab085.text: Peace. From him. I've heard monsters plan a great many things. That's the first time one's planned a honeymoon.

ezmerelda/5a849a10edf551c9.text: Wait. If he'd left Vallaki, where would he go to lick his wounds? Where would he go that I couldn't follow?

ezmerelda/5ccb31286cd7d955.text: Now go away. I have a wagon to hitch and an old man to shout at.

ezmerelda/652541fe80c5d360.text: Back. Good. I've counted the Belviews twice more and got two different numbers. Are we going in, or are you going to make me admire the view?

ezmerelda/656e5375ec9871b5.text: Nobody with fangs has ever asked to buy silver. Not twice, anyway. Sit.

ezmerelda/686aacd960666b3b.text: Then keep it. From everyone but me. I'm not everyone; I'm the reason he needs a secret.

ezmerelda/687eabe75e71df71.text: You're a terrible liar. He made you promise, didn't he. He always makes people promise.

ezmerelda/6b20f19af2c7698f.text: She would. Tell her I ate a whole sausage last week. Don't tell her it was the only thing I ate. Fine. Fine, you've got honest faces, and she sent you.

ezmerelda/6e1c969898073421.text: The cards said I'd find friends on this road. I told Eva the cards had never met me. Fine. I'll come. I go first through doors, I take the silver, and nobody calls me "girl".

ezmerelda/75ca530b83bcee6e.text: I hunt alone. Usually. But you've done more for me in a week than the whole valley has in a year. All right. Until it's done.

ezmerelda/76de3227db45cce7.text: He's making tea. He's terrible at tea. Don't tell him; he thinks it's the only thing he's good at besides killing.

ezmerelda/7ccbc137ce55c437.text: Eva's cards, I suppose. They've been dealing me into other people's games since I was six. Fine.

ezmerelda/824b39ba4a3920e6.text: ...Fine. Keep his secret. You're the first people in this valley who've kept anything. I'll keep looking. I'm good at looking.

ezmerelda/94341c516677c5de.text: I'm going to pretend I didn't watch that. I'm a very good pretender.

ezmerelda/98c25c3c1d89bd83.text: Then I'll keep waiting. I'm good at waiting. No, I'm not. I'm terrible at it.

ezmerelda/9c1e33ccad81a535.text: Two of Kiril's. Tell me I chose badly.

ezmerelda/9da1397c7c7d181d.text: Remind me to kill him. After I've hugged him.

ezmerelda/9e10bd1e2297dd18.text: That's the one who took my leg. Thank you. I wanted to do it myself. I find I don't mind that much, now.

ezmerelda/9e9954cc8d77e1fc.text: The ward. It knows my name; it also knows my temper. We had words. It won.

ezmerelda/9f055c96b4244552.text: I could go in on my own. I've decided I'm not that brave. Which, for me, is new.

ezmerelda/a5f5ea5d5dedfbc0.text: You let that happen. I'll remember who let that happen.

ezmerelda/a7de8a63d8bc7620.text: Whatever he's left lying about that isn't his notes. He'll be appalled. That's a reward in itself.

ezmerelda/a90f32d3aa31d0a3.text: That's done, then. I thought it would feel like more.

ezmerelda/ab0a88c7b6b50092.text: A pack dens two hours east along the ridge, in a cave above Lake Zarovich. One of them took my leg below the knee, years ago, when I was young and quick and stupid. Big, black, and laughing while it did it.

ezmerelda/ac8ff90a61ce558d.text: Ezmerelda d'Avenir. Vistani, when the wagons will have me. I hunt the things that hunt people. Right now I'm hunting one stubborn old man who taught me how, and who has locked me out of his house.

ezmerelda/b11d4fe5ad05701a.text: Save them for the walk. It's a long walk, and he wrote very long books.

ezmerelda/b3d382a77a4c0c2e.text: I came up here to kill you. I'm still not sure I shouldn't.

ezmerelda/b6261334bc43f3c7.text: I hunt alone. Usually. But this valley's too big for one pair of eyes, and too dark. All right. Until it's done.

ezmerelda/bde7766e517e6bc3.text: Did she say anything else? About me?

ezmerelda/bfe743087d832f03.text: Here. You've earned better than thanks. Silver-headed bolts, holy water and my last good potion. Don't waste them on anything that doesn't deserve them.

ezmerelda/c38e4b18966f6f9c.text: I go first through doors, I take the silver, and nobody calls me "girl".

ezmerelda/c8f1c5e95047c8d4.text: He's agreed. He just doesn't know it yet.

ezmerelda/c994115c9f7013d4.text: He made you promise. Of course he did. He's very good at making people promise things that keep them away from him.

ezmerelda/cb9a9f43bd6e8cdb.text: It's a terrible costume. You look like a chicken that's been to a wedding. You keyed your ward to me.

ezmerelda/ccf3991adf711fdb.text: If you see a man who looks too tired for the face he's wearing, tell me before you tell him.

ezmerelda/d199657c944d659c.text: Then I'll come and fetch it, dog.

ezmerelda/d9575e7830c3796b.text: Stopping's the one thing I'm bad at.

ezmerelda/dc1f752ddf5e8b09.text: An old man with burned hands and a head full of monsters. Rudolph van Richten. He taught me everything, then went off into the mists to die heroically without me. I'd like a word with him first.

ezmerelda/dd860914ad8bd38a.text: Yes, yes. I know. I love you too.

ezmerelda/e253dbe176179a95.text: You got the children out, at least. I'll give you that. I'll give you that and nothing else.

ezmerelda/e6abbeb081029ab1.text: He'll have got my good side wrong.

ezmerelda/e6f1bf3b7be9a48c.text: Then Rudolph's own ward threw me twenty feet into the lake. He wove my name into it. Mine. Nobody else's. Months of work, to keep out one person.

ezmerelda/e75d4b51dae5107a.text: Good. Say the name, mind your feet, and don't touch anything that hums. He likes things that hum.

ezmerelda/f0861d3aa596faa1.text: Of course I trapped it. There's a werewolf pack two hours up the ridge, and a castle that reads over everyone's shoulder. You found it. Good eyes. Most people find it with their faces.

ezmerelda/f3680ef16e2120ff.text: It's Rudolph's. Rudolph van Richten. An archmage built it centuries ago, and the old lock still opens to that wizard's name. I found the name under the moss in an hour: KHAZAN.

ezmerelda/f5269b9946f345d9.text: And he's left Vallaki already. Of course he has. He never stays where people might start to depend on him. It's his only real flaw, and he has it in bulk.

ezmerelda/febaa65324ff0e11.text: And there's a strongbox in his lantern room he never let me near. He called what was in it "the thing the cards keep moving". Eva would know what that means. So, I suspect, do you.

father_lucian/047836bf58b37326.text: The town should hear this, from my mouth, in the square. Not as a weapon. As a warning.

father_lucian/07ebd4816303a3a4.text: And Fiona will try to step into his shoes the moment they're empty. If there's proof of what she is, the town should hear it.

father_lucian/0a0047bc4cc8a4c8.text: Vargas has asked me to preach on gratitude at the next festival. I'm going to preach on mercy instead. We'll see whether he notices.

father_lucian/103f8f9617241e0f.text: Tonight, or any night now. If whoever took the saint means the church harm, they'll come after dark, when the doors are shut and I'm alone with a few candles. Come back at dusk, if you're willing, and keep the vigil with me.

father_lucian/10e6ba471659c478.text: You know your saints. Andral stood in a doorway here against the dead, the old stories say, until they stopped coming. Whatever was in him stayed in his bones. While they rest under the altar, this whole building is a doorway he's still standing in.

father_lucian/12c6f25c09169f58.text: Never mind. I can see in your faces it isn't a happy answer.

father_lucian/15d9f460376c71e8.text: Councillor work. I have spent the whole morning settling a dispute about a goat. It was wonderful. Nobody was put in the stocks.

father_lucian/1c3672d01ab5497b.text: Three nights ago, someone opened the saint's sarcophagus in the crypt and took his bones. St. Andral has lain under this altar for two hundred years. While he did, nothing dead could set foot in this church.

father_lucian/208003e5e38035b1.text: Then God bless you, and God help us. Urwin Martikov feels the same, and he's quieter about it than I am, which is wiser.

father_lucian/20b21256fba048fd.text: Nobody seize anybody! Please! These are your neighbours!

father_lucian/284a0a5fcb3c35d6.text: And Milivoj. I'll speak to him. Hunger is a sin, they tell me, but I don't think it was his.

father_lucian/28c774c0ed92aa5a.text: Take these, and my blessing with them. It's not much, but it's what the church has.

father_lucian/2be0603b9bada453.text: Doru, destroyed, and against his father's wishes. I understand why. I'll pray that Donavich comes to, one day.

father_lucian/325e5425925b4312.text: You let Doru out? Then Donavich has lost him twice. And something hungry is walking the roads with a priest's son's face.

father_lucian/44309e0ad5ac08a9.text: Welcome back to St. Andral's. It feels like a church again. I keep stopping in the doorway just to feel it.

father_lucian/4bb971e2edc08f27.text: Welcome to St. Andral's. Forgive the bare altar; we've had a loss. I'm Father Lucian. Are you hurt, or hungry, or in trouble? Those are the three reasons people come here now.

father_lucian/4f25adf455a9a75c.text: He let his son go. That's the hardest prayer there is. Thank you for being there to say amen.

father_lucian/5bd060b9ac3ad10d.text: Only two people knew where the bones lay and how the lid comes away: myself, and my gravedigger, Milivoj. I haven't accused him. I would very much like never to have to.

father_lucian/5f42736f3cfe6cb7.text: Not yet. Without the saint this is only a big wooden room, and he knows where it is. Try the Blue Water Inn. The Martikovs keep a very good door, and Urwin sleeps less than any man I know.

father_lucian/5fb7435c68e871ed.text: It was, my dear. Until three nights ago. I'd take you in tonight if I could promise you anything. I can't. Not until the saint is home.

father_lucian/67cac5fa0961f659.text: The poor souls in the lockup, too. Every festival he drags them out to make an example. I'd sleep better if there were nobody in there to drag.

father_lucian/692158fe10a48b15.text: Only stories. That it was carried against the castle once, and didn't come back. Stories are what we have instead of relics, these days.

father_lucian/791c57b31e5e9dbf.text: Fiona. I baptised her children. She sat in the third pew every holy day for twenty years. And she was writing to him the whole time.

father_lucian/7cfe918543b6283c.text: Whatever happens, they don't reach the altar. Not while I'm breathing.

father_lucian/9070b6e184bb8b01.text: Vargas. It's over. Go home to Lydia. Nobody is going to hurt you.

father_lucian/90ef9c68f3dd95c4.text: Someone who wants this church to be ordinary ground again. And there's only one creature in this valley who'd want that, and he has many hands.

father_lucian/92a2a1ee87b21163.text: Welcome home. Welcome home, old man.

father_lucian/adc24e3c82584bd4.text: No. No, Vargas. Not today, and not again.

father_lucian/ade4aa512ac73712.text: Take her to the lockup. Gently. Lock it well.

father_lucian/b5a5eb18d488f6be.text: Then go with God, my dear. The door is open if you ever need it.

father_lucian/bc3b336d09c34438.text: My dear, this is holy ground again. You may stay as long as you like. Nothing dead comes through those doors now, and nothing living will while I'm here.

father_lucian/c6cc9c30d58a0655.text: Stay near me, if you would. When Vargas is frightened, he shouts. When he shouts, Izek moves. I would like someone between Izek and the crowd.

father_lucian/c8bc7d9f1ce0d22f.text: You held. All night, you held. I've lit a candle for each of you, and one for the windows, which did not.

father_lucian/cb5228f48dba4d2b.text: Vargas loses his temper when the sun won't burn. It rains, it always rains. When he does, he'll want someone punished, and Izek will want to do it. Stand near me. If someone has to be between Izek and the crowd, I'd rather it were people who can hit back.

father_lucian/d5bbdee6c7b26c54.text: You've come from the village of Barovia? Then you've met Donavich. We were novices together. How is he?

father_lucian/d94258eceee88b19.text: I won't ask who took them. I find I don't want to know. I've decided that's a mercy, and not cowardice.

father_lucian/d9489a1e34dc2a96.text: Thank you. I mean it more than I can say without sounding like a sermon. Start with Milivoj, if you must. He digs in the churchyard most days. Be gentle with him. He has three young ones at home and no parents for them.

father_lucian/dc10d4663cb183da.text: Go with God, and come back to us. People keep forgetting that second part.

father_lucian/e153a81dabf22c43.text: You've come to church. Good. I've been preaching to Lydia and Victor and a great many empty pews. Lady Wachter's men sit at the back and take notes.

father_lucian/e22c1815631e903c.text: And you, my friends, if you'll stay a while. There's a bed at the church and a seat on any bench in this town.

father_lucian/e8ac433a31433c86.text: He was a holy man, and he died here, and his bones kept the dead away. That's all most of us know. It was always enough.

father_lucian/e938e65444f20298.text: Blessed this morning. Throw it, don't drink it, and don't miss.

father_lucian/f5bf8b78908b57ab.text: Still locked under the church, still screaming. And Donavich still feeding him. God help them both.

father_lucian/f650fff6e21d2107.text: No. It's a hope. I'm a priest in Barovia; hope is the only tool they let me keep.

father_lucian/fab8f5eb2da5c6b2.text: Vargas is a frightened child with a whip. Fiona is a patient woman with a much worse master. If you're asking me to choose between them, I won't. I'll choose the people in the pews.

grigor/18b1dd4dbcc4d675.text: The wolves took my brother off this road a month back. We've been taking them back since, one pelt at a time.

grigor/23ea9ac1c217c8da.text: Kolyan's girl? Out here? Then the world's ended and nobody told me.

grigor/519c7fe7fab05ecd.text: And the big wolves, the ones that walk on two legs when it suits them, den in the hills above the lake. They pray to some mother of theirs. Keep clear.

grigor/56f697794f8e3aad.text: That's close enough. Strangers on this road, this near dark, are mostly his. Give me a reason to think you're not.

grigor/80ccc1256b4709cd.text: Fine. Go on, then. And may the wolves find you before you find us again.

grigor/b1bc060a8daceb19.text: That's what his things say too. Walk past, slow, hands where I can see them.

grigor/ef1af5c9d1bd9788.text: Two things, for free. There's an old windmill on a crag on the way to Vallaki. Don't knock. Crows on the sails, and some nights a child crying inside, and nobody in this valley has a child to spare.

gunther_arasek/04368764494c3045.text: Back for more? Good. Steel doesn't sell itself. It mostly sits there being heavy.

gunther_arasek/3a8ced6be3153d1f.text: Pleasure. Bring it back dented and I'll buy it for half. Bring it back bloody and I'll buy it for less.

gunther_arasek/45b900b23f11530e.text: Twice what you'd pay over the mountains. Every cart that reaches us loses a horse or a driver on the way, some months both. My sister Yelena keeps the books, and the books say twice.

gunther_arasek/49477ea56252a10f.text: You came over the pass and the wolves let you by? Huh. They don't let my carts by.

gunther_arasek/67d952cf4166f7de.text: West road to Krezk: wolves, and worse past the river. The lake road: fishermen who've stopped catching anything and gone strange with it. East road, the way you came: an old windmill nobody sane stops at.

gunther_arasek/7c7653a9bbd89810.text: Then you heard right. My carters won't water their horses within sight of it. Horses go in. Horses don't come out.

gunther_arasek/9abb08590b7cea83.text: Arasek Stockyard. Steel, leather, rope, grain. Everything that comes into Vallaki on a cart comes past me first, and the wolves get a look at it on the way.

gunther_arasek/a9ac349bb96ec112.text: You've come from the village, eh? Bildrath's prices? Ten times. And I hear somebody helped themselves to his strongbox. Not that I'd ever think it of you.

gunther_arasek/ed66e7615c3901ba.text: You can ask Yelena. I'd sell you a helmet first.

gustav_durst/12790cc4ae672d87.text: Go down and see. The altar will ask you too. Everyone gets asked.

gustav_durst/6b6ca485c84ae6be.text: We wanted what he has. Forever. So we fed the house, and the house fed the thing below, and we waited for him to notice.

gustav_durst/6d88cdcdbb741d80.text: And the gift was refused. He wanted nothing from us. Not even that.

gustav_durst/708375940383990b.text: We meant to go back up for them. And then we were so very hungry.

gustav_durst/ecad08f5bea780ea.text: Gustav Durst, and my wife, Elisabeth. This is our house, you understand. All of it. Even the parts that never appeared on the plans.

gustav_durst/f3b4df070b5b9791.text: Guests. Elisabeth, guests. Do sit. We so rarely have anyone down.

hedda_ironvow/005bb1d583daeb1a.text: That's the first prayer in this valley that didn't feel like shouting down a well.

hedda_ironvow/01c56590ac879805.text: You can pray for anything. That's rather the point of it.

hedda_ironvow/045c987aafee7637.text: You want the last light out. I carry one. We have nothing to discuss.

hedda_ironvow/065e4c9ea15a1722.text: Then let's be late. Rudely, unforgivably late.

hedda_ironvow/0871d631f8fe387e.text: Or we bring the dawn to all of it at once. Dawn comes.

hedda_ironvow/09bdc187b6e71cad.text: And you? What do you think happened?

hedda_ironvow/0b2b60822a72b1e3.text: "To whoever keeps this house after me. Tomorrow I take the bell-ringers, the gravediggers and the two old soldiers who still remember how, and we go up the road to his door."

hedda_ironvow/0d1ccdc119bf5753.text: Listen. Nothing. For the first time since the stair, nothing at all.

hedda_ironvow/0e340e4ae214dd32.text: Mm. Not a sunrise. But it's facing the right way.

hedda_ironvow/12b1c2bddcc9fb22.text: She thanked us. In his name. I can still hear it.

hedda_ironvow/12c8281370df8cdb.text: I've ground a lot of things in my time. Ore. Grudges. Never that.

hedda_ironvow/132903772db2e1ea.text: Whoever kept this crib made never stopped hoping. That's the saddest kind of housekeeping.

hedda_ironvow/1391c3c184f0fea1.text: Mm. Nobody should wait that long to be told they can stop.

hedda_ironvow/13c2d3f0389c18f1.text: We put a man in the ground without a word said over him. That's not a burial. That's tidying.

hedda_ironvow/14b455c645dda240.text: You broke a bad oath to keep a better one. The stone in that chapel is older than his table.

hedda_ironvow/158780b3f04bfcda.text: It was never going to. It just did. There's a difference, and I'll keep insisting on it.

hedda_ironvow/17a00c30662db447.text: Don't. Whatever this buys us, we'll be paying for it forever.

hedda_ironvow/194cfc61fa813820.text: Divide them, then. It feels like cheating.

hedda_ironvow/19bf52acd6bef21b.text: There. Mm. There it goes. Out you go, you miserable thing. This boy has goats to shout at.

hedda_ironvow/1a497876b1f8e599.text: We pointed the devil at a witch. I'll not pretend I'm sorry for her. I'll not pretend it was clean, either.

hedda_ironvow/1e077b5e68b361b4.text: We've sworn ourselves to a man who jails widows for laughing. I'd like that noted somewhere.

hedda_ironvow/1e14fb995627e827.text: "Cared for." I've read that phrase on too many graves.

hedda_ironvow/1eafe6d668666ca9.text: He's celestial. An angel, or the next thing to one. And something in him has turned, the way milk turns.

hedda_ironvow/1ef4d2e15e644c8e.text: He'd filled his pockets with stones. A man doesn't do that in a hurry. He'd been thinking about it for days.

hedda_ironvow/1fc0e71bd0bfaf44.text: For her son. She knew what she was doing. That's what makes it hard to carry.

hedda_ironvow/210ee7200afae068.text: The raven and the sun. I have dreamed that symbol every night for a year. Mm. Then it's real, and it's here.

hedda_ironvow/212d5d04fba1d975.text: There was no blood. Only light. I don't know what we killed, exactly. I know it needed killing. Mm. I'll pray for it anyway.

hedda_ironvow/226e9d73394b6645.text: The old man grieves like stone weathers. Slowly, from the outside in, and he calls it standing firm.

hedda_ironvow/2273825068b77321.text: There's no shame in a wound you didn't choose.

hedda_ironvow/235cb466d45d37e8.text: A dead man for an ally. Calling a soul back is no small mercy, and no cheap one.

hedda_ironvow/23f0e307fe040ea9.text: The locket. I'm good, but I'm not that good. Nobody leaves a coach that easy to rob. I think somebody put it where my hand would find it, so I'd carry it here.

hedda_ironvow/250418619cd19143.text: Brother Kesten came up this hill alone with a cudgel and a prayer. I'll wear his symbol a while, so that someone finishes the walk.

hedda_ironvow/26ae0a88d2b205bd.text: Stanimir thinks one of his own boys took his gold. Somebody is going to be shouted at for that, and it won't be us.

hedda_ironvow/2798d5c862e21128.text: We took the old man's strongbox in a war he was losing. I'd like that remembered when we're being proud of ourselves.

hedda_ironvow/27e859764aa4dbec.text: Someone who wants a church to be just a room. Which tells you who.

hedda_ironvow/287265aa11e6d6ea.text: That's a hard sum. I won't pretend it isn't.

hedda_ironvow/290c2b8336cb2ac0.text: Mm. I prayed my whole life to meet something sent from above. I didn't think it would be lighting candles with its thumb and sewing corpses.

hedda_ironvow/2a4212dedc518140.text: She isn't. You know she isn't. That's why you're cross.

hedda_ironvow/2c706656d2bf3fde.text: Don't. I don't want it to make sense.

hedda_ironvow/2de50cbeb03c32b8.text: He walked out of the square like a man going to bury someone. I suppose he was. Himself, the one he'd been.

hedda_ironvow/2e5bd69004c27cfd.text: Dawn comes, little one. Even here. Even to arms.

hedda_ironvow/2f3c1ff808a3c61c.text: Earth to earth, and the dark to the dawn. Rest, Kolyan Indirovich. Let no voice call you up again.

hedda_ironvow/3110e4b812d66a8d.text: Holy ground again. You can feel it in your teeth.

hedda_ironvow/315030aede5da1ec.text: A shrine to a lord, not a god. They knelt to the wrong one.

hedda_ironvow/33c7ab885f8ff131.text: That isn't a tree. That's a grave that learned to stand up.

hedda_ironvow/355bf457d3b439d4.text: They're not lying. That's the worst of it. Every one of them tells you the price.

hedda_ironvow/358ead387511d47c.text: Go gently. Nobody will lock that door again.

hedda_ironvow/36fc9b2f4cdbc9ee.text: Stone remembers what's sworn over it. I'd hoped to forget this one.

hedda_ironvow/3770c0f3c0d28ffd.text: Wolves don't keep ranks. Not on their own.

hedda_ironvow/37bb70fc60bf01ed.text: Mm. And would they have thanked you for it, sergeant?

hedda_ironvow/37f2d0c2b26d6143.text: We'll keep her behind us, always. Always.

hedda_ironvow/38c5bd305da8d8fb.text: There's a law older than both of yours about children.

hedda_ironvow/38c60f245803977b.text: Stone remembers, my folk say. Stone doesn't love. There's a reason we always say both.

hedda_ironvow/3c25ba91e37d73df.text: That is not a choice I will carry for her. Remember that I said so.

hedda_ironvow/3d117712126b90e8.text: Then we treat them like a family from Krezk. Whatever they look like now.

hedda_ironvow/3d51aa5bab12b9c3.text: The White Sun's people. Krezk's not far, then.

hedda_ironvow/3d5a94fd55999798.text: I know which I'd rather have nowhere near a child. They're the same answer, which is a mercy.

hedda_ironvow/40289af21fb98690.text: A sunburst on the altar. The Morninglord, this far into the dark. Mm. Someone kept faith here.

hedda_ironvow/4063073f24bd3ac4.text: Easy, sister. Easy. We're not the ones who took him.

hedda_ironvow/4076ad42c2419935.text: Fire's a kind of dawn. The small kind. It'll do.

hedda_ironvow/416cfbde2a0fa3da.text: I have stood on hills to watch the sun come up. I have not felt this before about putting one out.

hedda_ironvow/421ecc27a5f2ffbe.text: Dawn keep you, stranger, and the dark keep its distance.

hedda_ironvow/42bea5e1713f5ad5.text: It feels like dawn in my hands. I haven't felt that since the mists.

hedda_ironvow/46e2e71ca33a79cd.text: He can't come like this. Not with half of him still in a bottle somewhere.

hedda_ironvow/4aa98ff158ae0e21.text: Night hags. Fiends who ride sleepers' dreams and keep the souls they steal in little bags. I'd hoped those were stories for novices.

hedda_ironvow/4b55ccd64aec9909.text: Forgive me, sir knight. You're dead.

hedda_ironvow/4b617450330aab50.text: One of us lay down in the devil's own coffin. I want us to say that out loud, once, so none of us can pretend later.

hedda_ironvow/4c52e91fa120b9f8.text: Report. Kestrel Company marched into the fog without me. I had a fever. It wasn't bad enough to keep me back. I was tired of the work. That's all.

hedda_ironvow/4c86341ba6be616f.text: Then we keep looking. Or we keep our word another way.

hedda_ironvow/4f75ea7922bd88a7.text: That was necessary. I'll pray about whether it was right.

hedda_ironvow/4fcfb1713e367875.text: We'll see him buried right. You have my word on it.

hedda_ironvow/53fd68d0408954ff.text: Mm. Words help. So does a straight grave.

hedda_ironvow/540c592cb1f0b7b4.text: I haven't. Give me time; I'll learn, I suppose. I'd rather not.

hedda_ironvow/54622bed5129c701.text: Rest. You kept it long enough.

hedda_ironvow/5571970129a9327c.text: Two bites, and she still keeps her own counsel. Most would be raving by now.

hedda_ironvow/56506cbc9482b0f0.text: Then we spend it well. Every day of it.

hedda_ironvow/56b807f3c0f8db12.text: Dawn comes, little ones. Go on ahead. We'll be along. Not soon, I hope.

hedda_ironvow/57939516ed74b81e.text: That's a no. My knees have gone to water, but that is a very firm no.

hedda_ironvow/58b472adf6032fb9.text: Mm. They remember what dawn is. Good.

hedda_ironvow/593746aa6b32ea3f.text: I'm going to pretend I didn't see that, and then I'm going to pray about it anyway.

hedda_ironvow/593c91817ceb8968.text: We took a reading by force from an old woman. I would like it written down somewhere that I was against it.

hedda_ironvow/5a173abccbaf6825.text: Lycanthropes who worship nothing but keeping watch. I was taught they were all cursed. She seems more tired than cursed.

hedda_ironvow/5a9b31fe7608a1e1.text: Go with the dawn, old dragon.

hedda_ironvow/5b27cc50d5697100.text: Then we look until we know, sergeant. Dawn comes.

hedda_ironvow/5c5b6b8083245115.text: That isn't justice. That's a feud you've married.

hedda_ironvow/5db7655f24c4e467.text: The tavern calls him the Lesser, I hear. Mm. Villages name their sons the way masons name stones: by what cracked.

hedda_ironvow/5de1f81bb7ba4686.text: Mm. Bring coin. Seers always want coin. So do scholars.

hedda_ironvow/5ef4474454be083c.text: Whatever holds them is still in that house. Nobody has let them go.

hedda_ironvow/5f299574b9b453d9.text: Whatever brought us here went to some trouble. That's worth remembering.

hedda_ironvow/626781f7e5bbb839.text: Mind the bite, and we'll get along.

hedda_ironvow/627e106c14ac8d71.text: That is how they get you.

hedda_ironvow/62d6dce96698d190.text: Mm. She poured my tea before I asked how I took it. Some people learn your habits because they like you. Some learn them the way a butcher learns the weight of a pig.

hedda_ironvow/64310df69087a446.text: Mm. That is exactly what it was.

hedda_ironvow/64d52b7304ae73b0.text: That wasn't justice. That was only the end of something.

hedda_ironvow/66a0c22d74a6252e.text: That is not an answer. It is very nearly an answer. Thank you.

hedda_ironvow/66cc431d02d3682e.text: Whoever did this was angry, and then very, very calm. I'll pray for her twice.

hedda_ironvow/66f1b780c453770f.text: Dawn comes, but it never arrives. I've been chewing on that for a mile. It's the worst sermon I've ever heard, and the truest.

hedda_ironvow/69c9646766467d25.text: If it can do that to a flask, it might do something for a fevered boy.

hedda_ironvow/6aae39c901745167.text: Behind me, Father. You've done your part.

hedda_ironvow/6ac23380e7024de6.text: Bones don't walk off on their own. Not a saint's, anyway.

hedda_ironvow/6adf9336641ea3dd.text: Mm. That's the part I'll be praying about tonight.

hedda_ironvow/6ba4c83d5415d3e8.text: We let it happen. A bride in a cart, waving at nobody.

hedda_ironvow/6baee4874026989e.text: Whatever he made of them, they were people first. They should have a sky over them.

hedda_ironvow/6c160cc686e35b57.text: Good stonework, all of it. Somebody with a real chisel cut these crypts. Pity about the tenants.

hedda_ironvow/6c2d5ee043baaa77.text: Go to whatever's waiting, mother. I hope it's kinder than your god.

hedda_ironvow/6e64621c455cbf45.text: Yes. That much, at least, we can do properly.

hedda_ironvow/6ec48496e56b2529.text: Mm. We were never going to be alone. There are four of us.

hedda_ironvow/7291dcca6c338e50.text: Sixteen years old. We could have broken that circle with our boots.

hedda_ironvow/73d077d344ff5f47.text: That isn't a pastry. That's a sleeping draught with a crust on it.

hedda_ironvow/75a462899691500c.text: There. Feel that? That's it leaving.

hedda_ironvow/75d6ef032b21b378.text: Some doors are shut for a reason.

hedda_ironvow/777825ee07021146.text: Dawn comes, my lady. Even here. I'll sit with you until it does.

hedda_ironvow/7aff4acb201c40a0.text: Eleven wolf heads on that wall, and wolves waiting for us on the road. I don't think that's a coincidence.

hedda_ironvow/7b3027bb3dbf5827.text: That bite on the girl's arm. Somebody in Krezk had better know what it means before the moon does.

hedda_ironvow/7b775f7fc660c730.text: Lost, not destroyed. Mm. Then it can be found.

hedda_ironvow/7be1e31bfda99db9.text: She's offering to sell us her own mother.

hedda_ironvow/7c0e9295188279b2.text: There's a word for this in every temple I know, my lady.

hedda_ironvow/7c8a79037839b1c0.text: They starved in that room waiting for you. I want you to know that, whatever you are now.

hedda_ironvow/7d81026868cdec68.text: You're a night hag. You ride sleepers' dreams and steal what's left of them.

hedda_ironvow/7e9a47e4b1634978.text: Those bags hold souls. People. She means to keep them.

ireena/6b8df6c0d391f760.text: Ismark said you'd come. He also said you were "probably not monsters". From him, that's a glowing reference. I'm Ireena.

ireena/6cd3d8725db19f58.text: My father and my brother never said it either. Not once, before the end. I'm glad somebody did.

ireena/6ebfceca4ad487af.text: And I know your voice. You're the one who told my door to open. Now. Keep that voice down in this house.

ireena/72634da58edeb691.text: I see. No, I do. It's a long road, and he's very patient. Go on, then.

ireena/72b3ea523036b645.text: It's only water now. I keep checking. I'd hoped it would hurt less, choosing. It doesn't hurt less. It hurts properly, which is different.

ireena/72d001c23b1a7683.text: You'd do that? Then listen: the parlor window is the weakest, the front door the most stubborn. If he comes himself, he won't break in. He'll ask. Whatever you do, don't answer.

ireena/75900f7dc9ee162e.text: Then I'll stay. For now. Don't get yourselves killed while I'm safe; I'd never forgive you, and I'd say so at every one of your funerals.

ireena/75bf9d5dffbf9239.text: Changed your minds? Or just checking the shutters for us?

ireena/7bf4c8fc76308b18.text: Vallaki first, then Krezk. Farther than anyone in my family has ever walked.

ireena/810cecbe64eb77ca.text: I'm sorry. I loved you. She loved you. I can't be her and still be anyone at all.

ireena/84c7b13d5e14f525.text: Let him write. I've had his letters before. I burn them.

ireena/84de9f4d452cf200.text: The Vistani women say there's a seer at Tser Pool, on the way. If anyone can tell me what he wants with me, perhaps she can.

ireena/854210746c7d7079.text: My eyes are up here. So is my sword.

ireena/862e587fcce80a89.text: I know this. Not this place. A height, and white cloth, and somebody shouting a name that isn't mine, and then I stepped...

ireena/871bab8545eda7d4.text: The Martikovs are kind. Urwin sits up all night watching the windows. I've never met a man so interested in birds.

ireena/877da13d891f70bb.text: Someone has been in my father's strongbox. If it was you, I'd rather you had asked. He would have given it to you. That was the sort of fool he was.

ireena/87aa0cb53c40704f.text: I'd sooner sleep in the lake.

ireena/88cae0b691269aff.text: No. I've heard sweeter voices than yours at this door, and they had claws. Find Ismark at the tavern.

ireena/8c411815bda7efcb.text: Kolyan Indirovich. Burgomaster for twenty years. Loud, stubborn, and kind to everyone, even the people he was shouting at. He found me on a road when I was a girl and never once made me feel found.

ireena/8d231dfbbf864fdf.text: I'm not asking you to fight him. I'm asking for a roof he hasn't been under.

ireena/8dc72b5f3c852e08.text: If I go now, he waits. A hundred years, two hundred, for the next one of me, in some village, with my face. Some girl who doesn't know what's coming to her window.

ireena/8e83fdef5b2ec052.text: I'm fine. I'm not made of glass. I just wasn't sure, for a moment, that I'm not.

ireena/909d44fb7643aa02.text: A wall that's never let him in. A burgomaster who remembers my father. I came all this way for something like that.

ireena/9110bf694eada617.text: Izek comes to the church door at dusk. He doesn't come in. He can't, or he won't. He just stands there.

ireena/93b8a00104790220.text: He keeps finding us. Doesn't he. Over and over, he keeps finding us, and it never ends well for the girl.

ireena/99f9ad5bd1bcf45a.text: Then I'll go on. Walls never kept him out of my father's house. I'd rather be moving.

ireena/9c99f1b147d6454d.text: Where did you get this? I've never sat for a painter. I've never owned a dress like that. Who is she?

ireena/9cb1fc29c0e69664.text: Then you know it's a cage.

ireena/9f592b40e4c1f51b.text: And you went for him with steel. He laughed, but you did it. I've wanted to do that for a month.

ireena/9fb080b569894928.text: I don't remember anything before Kolyan's house. Only trees, and being cold, and a boy shouting a name. I always thought the name was mine.

ireena/a145cbf093c9d4f6.text: I've been offered rides by strangers before. I walked.

ireena/a275f017368ca46a.text: I'm not visiting. I'm hiding. Tell him that, if you have to tell him anything.

ireena/a27cf3394d5802ea.text: Good. I was going mad sitting still. Walls didn't keep him out of my father's house; I'd rather take my chances with you.

ireena/a2e31ca9c5e8ad05.text: I don't know what he means. I don't. Don't look at me like that.

ireena/a3cdb5ad99d23005.text: Vallaki. Where we were going anyway. At least the cards are economical.

ireena/a4d0dae7c5eb2dc5.text: I've never been here. I know I've never been here. So why do I know there are nine steps under that plinth?

ireena/a55d3d03557de0da.text: A wall, very high, and a gorge under it. A wedding. No: after a wedding. I was running from someone who said he loved me. Isn't that a stupid thing to be afraid of?

ireena/abcc4b7701e0fc3a.text: Ismark says you'll help with Father. Then he needs a priest. Father Donavich, at the church on the hill. He hasn't left it in weeks, but he owes Father that much.

ireena/abdc1d0f9f5ac34d.text: Before Kolyan? Nothing. Trees. Being cold. A boy shouting a name through the trees, over and over. I always thought the name must have been mine.

ireena/ad43242d4878fc7b.text: And that was Donavich's boy on the wall. You let him out. You'll have to live with that, and so will the rest of us.

ireena/af227a8982f72046.text: Father used to ride out and cut them down himself. He said a crossroads is no place to be left; the dead get confused about which road leads home.

ireena/b25905477d903713.text: I don't remember you. I'm sorry. I don't remember anything from before.

ireena/b27b4c2f4368ab33.text: Not a priest's words. Honest ones. He'd have taken honest over pretty, most days.

ireena/b33b5dfa18e603ee.text: I dream about falling. Every time I close my eyes near a window.

ireena/b346998ac3eed71c.text: Krezk, then. I've never seen it. For once I'd like to go somewhere I've never been, on purpose. Through Vallaki, and on.

ireena/b4164aeabef61641.text: Ireena Kolyana. This is my father's house. It's still his, until he's in the ground.

ireena/b4774f5014bf51bb.text: Then I'll fetch my sword and my good boots. I'm not made of glass; I'll walk, I'll fight, and I'll take a watch. Don't argue about the watch.

ireena/b706c3c6f4417252.text: Stay in Krezk? Beside the pool. Beside him. I'd sit by that water every morning and every morning I'd want to walk in.

ireena/b7ba9652abe7bebe.text: Good. I've made forty cheeses. That's enough cheese for a lifetime, and I'm not sure how long mine is.

ireena/ba893d1ecbbad855.text: No. When he's dead, I'll come back. I swear it on my father. Wait for me a little longer, Sergei. You're good at it.

ireena/bb0e390f24ab432d.text: I know the end of that story. I've dreamed it. The wall, and the wind, and somebody calling a name that isn't mine.

ireena/bb605e44cf728db9.text: Father said there was nothing past the crossroads but more Barovia. He was right. It's the same mud. I still want to see it.

ireena/c0af52bd1d26cb87.text: Ismark would want me to stay. Father would have. And I'm very tired of sleeping with a sword in the bed.

ireena/c0ce4775e7b8ca1d.text: Don't. Whatever you're about to say. Later. By a fire.

ireena/c4023de052e46bf9.text: No. Not yet. I made a promise, and I can only keep it if the devil's dead. That means I go where you go.

ireena/c464b1151ee4c61b.text: Donavich won't come. Then he'll go into the ground without the church's words. I hope one of you knows some others.

ireena/c91bfbae2238f482.text: My brother sent me to you. He said this church was the one place in the valley the devil can't walk into.

ireena/ce8cf1676ecda5b1.text: Ireena. Yes. That's me. That's who I am.

ireena/cecdabd6a01f3089.text: No. Yes. Later. Ask me again when we're somewhere with a fire and no water anywhere.

ireena/cfe4968cbd34ea0b.text: Thank you. That's the kindest wrong thing anyone's said to me in a month.

ireena/cfed50b18e8264b1.text: Anna's teaching me to make cheese. I'm terrible at it. Dmitri says it builds character. I have character. I'd like a sword drill.

ireena/d19c5ba3df650ef4.text: There's no such custom. I lived in that village all my life.

ireena/d204b5e4824f34f4.text: He was buried properly. With words said over him. That's all he'd have wanted.

ireena/d2a8baeedf722f52.text: Then tell him I said no. He's heard it before.

ireena/d40321fb7b5a9403.text: You're the ones who came out of the house at the end of the lane. People don't come out of that house. Come in, quickly, before the dark notices the door is open.

ireena/d4dd0ef8fab36c78.text: Thank you. Then he needs a priest. Father Donavich, at the church on the hill. Ask him to say the words. Then we carry Father over together, before dark.

ireena/d6d7438001334751.text: Your god didn't know him. Your god does now. Thank you for that.

ireena/d70e4e2717020846.text: You put our dead back where they belong, too. Buried twice. Father always said this village did nothing by halves.

ireena/da1556d5b0b4ff00.text: He's in the ground. No words, no prayer. I'll go, because staying is worse. But I won't pretend I liked how.

ireena/dad1aa2098b40ee6.text: Krezk, then. It's farther, and it has an abbey, and nobody in it has ever served him tea. Take me there, or I'll walk it alone.

ireena/dc34e3292e314934.text: Ireena. I'm Ireena Kolyana. Kolyan found me in the woods and taught me to hold a sword, and I'd like to find out what I do next.

ireena/de56bfbf4b514d0e.text: Say it again if I ever forget.

ireena/df7dc4986e2ea5ba.text: Wolves, most nights. Dead things on others: neighbors we buried, back to scratch at the boards. And once, him. He doesn't scratch. He knocks, and asks, very politely, to be let in.

ireena/e1c447d5578479fe.text: Last night you stood in my father's house, and nobody ran. I've watched a lot of people run. I won't forget it.

ireena/e57774004dda9288.text: I'm not made of glass. But I'm not a fool either. I'll be by the well. Shout if you need a sword.

ireena/e7015008560f4a18.text: Donavich said the words. Father would have corrected his grammar. He'd have been pleased, though. He liked things done properly.

ireena/eb4bfd5443179abc.text: I am standing right here, and I am not a sack of flour to be handed over a counter.

ireena/ec13e4eee1a5901b.text: Bring him back in one piece. He's the only brother I have.

ireena/ec262933970b9bb8.text: Back again. Good. The house is quieter with more swords in it.

ireena/ed268219258f9602.text: She had my hair. Didn't she. Whoever she was.

ireena/f18221a21b34732a.text: I could have told you that for free.

ireena/f39271a4a02421e6.text: Why are you all looking at me like that?

ireena/f4eb4a29af125655.text: Krezk. All that road, and it's a wall with a man in front of it.

ireena/f60f433325f0fbc3.text: He's still down there. I can feel it, like a door left open somewhere in the house. When this is over, I'm coming back here. Don't let me forget I said it.

ireena/f6a4140195454a3f.text: He dreams about me. A man I've never met dreams about me, and pays for dolls.

ireena/f6ecc73a01a92191.text: Fine. Come in. Slowly, and with your hands where I can see them. I've opened this door to worse than you, and I'm still standing.

ireena/f85499811a1ee145.text: Thank you. He'd have liked you. He'd have argued with you about everything, and liked you.

ireena/f88a9813292e6cef.text: I've never been here in my life.

ireena/f8a1614c8b69ce91.text: I don't remember him. I don't remember anything. And he's dreamed of me every night since he was nine.

ireena/f8c49b65da6347a3.text: Tser Pool first, then. If this Madam Eva reads cards for strangers, she can read a few for me.

ireena/fec5c736bcda575f.text: I remember you. I remember a chapel full of white flowers, and being happy for one whole morning. And then the wall. And your brother at the top of the stair.

ismark/01f21b9723fdb4e7.text: Do you know, I'd never been to Tser Pool? Twenty years, half a day's walk. Father always said the Vistani would steal my boots.

ismark/073ecb13cffc9f64.text: The house. Of course. Somebody has to argue with the wolves. Get her there. I'll walk you to the west road and wave like a fool.

ismark/08b31cc7e8eb2b18.text: And I'll go and sit by a different door. I'm getting very good at doors.

ismark/0daaf664e938d165.text: The house with the iron fence, north-west of the square. Follow the claw marks. I'll go ahead and tell Ireena not to stab you.

ismark/109393cee928305f.text: She's packed. She's been packed since the funeral. Every hour she sits by that window is an hour I don't sleep.

ismark/166d5068266f2d4b.text: Where she goes, I go. I'd rather argue with wolves than drink to his health.

ismark/1bf420b41b55a619.text: We'll manage. We always do. Badly, mostly, but we manage.

ismark/1c3ba6cf552b9695.text: Ismark the Lesser, off to see the world. Someone tell the tavern. Actually, don't; they'll only throw a party.

ismark/1d26f1d644c04181.text: Strangers. In Barovia. And you came out of the house at the end of the lane; you've still got its dust on you. Sit. I'm buying. It won't help, but I'm buying.

ismark/21c6db89c76af6c6.text: Then I'll sit by the door and glare at it. I'm good at that. Ask any door in Barovia.

ismark/25ef38cbee395558.text: Then he invited you. You're his guests, or his game. Let's make you the third thing: his problem.

ismark/265225d5d64efcf4.text: You're the ones my sister let in. She doesn't let anyone in. Sit down, before I decide that's suspicious.

ismark/26ca23d01a36f8d1.text: Me? The cards want me? Somebody tell the tavern. No, don't. They'll only laugh, and then they'll stop, and that will be worse.

ismark/283795b41a5e4723.text: Where she goes, I go. Don't make me say anything sentimental about it.

ismark/28a70e0b80fb2e21.text: Donavich isn't coming. After what happened under his church, I can't say I blame him.

ismark/2e5ede49fcd07254.text: This is as far as I go. Get her there. Bring her back one day, if there's anything to bring her back to.

ismark/3089b0261ae2e0c1.text: Strahd von Zarovich. Our lord. Our landlord. The thing in the castle on the cliff. He collects his rent at night, and the coin he likes best is us.

ismark/39e91ec7e63841eb.text: Changed your minds. Good. I'd stopped hoping, which in Barovia is usually when things happen. Talk to Ireena; she has opinions about how it's done.

ismark/3d459ebc23bb87e5.text: Wolves, most nights, big ones. Some nights, the dead: people we buried, back to scratch at the boards. Once, the devil himself, knocking politely. Father answered with a lamp in his face. That was the last good night.

ismark/3f6c90c404be1651.text: Of course I'll stay. There's a wall. I'll stand next to it. It's the one thing in Barovia I'm reliably good at.

ismark/45413dc141122928.text: No. Of course not. Why would you. If you change your minds, I'll be at the house, waiting for something to come through the door. It may as well be you.

ismark/4d13a4f93594b954.text: Fine. I'll sit in the taproom and drink Urwin's wine and glare at the door. It's a sacrifice, but I'm prepared to make it.

ismark/531fa67a33f2ccb8.text: Ireena. Father took her in when she was a girl; she's my sister in every way that counts. The devil has been at her window. Twice. You'll see the marks on her neck, and she'll hate you for looking.

ismark/54af7cbb9b2f59a8.text: Strangers. In Barovia. Either a miracle or a mistake, and I've stopped believing in miracles. Sit. I'm buying. It won't help, but I'm buying.

ismark/55e0629ddd0f21ac.text: About time. She's safe here, and I'm going soft. Lead on.
