narrator/4655b89bcb3c43ff.text: The east rows, where the grapes still hang: small, hard and purple-black, like a fist of bruises. A few of the leaves are green, stubbornly.

narrator/466939b771cf0de1.text: Two children stand in the road where the cottages begin: a girl of ten with her chin up, and a small boy holding a stuffed wolf by one ear. Neither is dressed for the cold, and neither seems to feel it.

narrator/4682a1d2b2b698d1.text: Everything, sooner or later. Tonight, the town. Tomorrow, whatever he asks for next. She knows it, and she has decided it is a fair price, because she has decided she will never be the one who pays it.

narrator/46989a3229b72d61.text: A young monk in a plain brown habit is lighting the candles along the altar rail. He doesn't use a taper. He touches each wick with a fingertip, and each one lights.

narrator/46ab9a0329d47f17.text: A long nave under a sunburst window, every candle lit, the altar dressed in white. The air in here is warmer than outside, and it isn't the candles.

narrator/46d62b63674dbe57.text: It's a spell, not weather: a great one, cast once and left running, like a clock somebody wound and forgot. Whoever told the sky to strike here every evening never told it to stop, and the work is so good it hasn't faltered once.

narrator/46f195f5e2c2c601.text: The vault ceiling is cracked amber, hanging in shards as long as knives. One good shake would bring it down.

narrator/472e2569e8422e96.text: A cobbled yard between the house, the winery and the press house, with a well in the middle and a wine cart sitting on its axle by the gate. The winery door hangs open. Something inside is humming.

narrator/4733ebd44cd5cc4a.text: The hut turns its door away from you, the way a cat turns its back. There is no ladder, and the stump is slick as a fish.

narrator/473d22f847b98058.text: On the jetty he coughs up half the lake and lies there laughing and crying at once, which seems fair.

narrator/478388f75675b417.text: The floorboards ahead sag, grey and spongy. Something has been chewing them from below.

narrator/47963a6ef0b1c2ce.text: Ireena wipes her face with the heel of her hand and stands up, and is herself again, mostly.

narrator/47af10dd80ed1937.text: The rocking slows. For the first time since you came in, she looks at you and not past you.

narrator/47d53f9ee2357a3b.text: A dollhouse taller than a child, painted in the same colors as the house around you.

narrator/47f5674bc9b1e528.text: Where the commander last stood, laid across a pair of empty gauntlets as carefully as an offering, is the thing he kept so that nobody would end the lord of the castle with it.

narrator/48055acde5971309.text: Alcoves cut into the walls, each with its relic: a goblin's hand, a knife of human bone, a rat's skull, a frog on a stick, a hag's finger. None of it is worth anything. All of it was precious to someone.

narrator/481b7c850aadf782.text: A watch brazier on a tripod, full of grey ash. It burns, though nobody feeds it, with a pale flame that gives light and no heat at all.

narrator/4827c2313b4c7a5b.text: Rose folds her hands at once, the way she was taught, and Thorn copies her a beat late. Halfway through, they both look up, puzzled, as if they have forgotten the words.

narrator/483742325cc788ce.text: At the foot of the stair stands a cask bigger than the rest, black with age, its hoops brown with rust. The druids' axes have been at every cask in sight but this one.

narrator/4844b06bb1ea8030.text: Every hearth on the floor exhales at once.

narrator/488e2b45771fd780.text: You rest among the flour sacks. Overhead, the rocking chair creaks and creaks, and never once stops.

narrator/48aee68b158e97d5.text: What's left of the Order's banners, rotted to grey lace on the house front. The device is still just visible: a silver dragon holding a lamp.

narrator/48b8747b90a33649.text: She doesn't write it down. She doesn't need to; you watch her remember it.

narrator/48d6f8c3c3ea5133.text: She snatches a jar from the shelf and shoves it at you. Something silver turns over inside it, slow as a fish.

narrator/48ffcb7b01b0cdd6.text: Ireena looks at the doll on the offering stone for a long time, and doesn't touch it.

narrator/4922c2427b181f7c.text: Low rafters, warm air rising through the floor from the oven, and overhead the great gear of the sails, locked still. It smells of straw and sugar and something kept too long.

narrator/4925818ebf092b00.text: He doesn't answer. He screams, high and thin, like a kettle left on the fire, and behind the storeroom door something heavy shifts inside a crate.

narrator/49471c32739c01fe.text: He pats his robe. He unpins a note, reads it, pins it back. He unpins another.

narrator/494e4d52a24b1b46.text: A wooden peg driven into the rock, and on it an iron key, its bow wrapped in rag. Kiril keeps it where he can see it from his bed.

narrator/49965c1b53ed0334.text: Wolves come down the lane from both ends at once, in no hurry, because there's nowhere for you to go.

narrator/49c1a539c3d612bd.text: A chamber hung with skeletons in rusty shackles. In an alcove at the far end stands a painted statue of a pale man in a black cloak, and the soot on the walls behind the skeletons is shaped like people.

narrator/49c2c159ebbcca25.text: For one breath the sweetness drains out of her face, and what's under it is older than the village.

narrator/49c71278acf4cc11.text: Inside the gate the bar leans against the wall, as thick as a man's thigh. The watch fire is kept high. Everyone who passes it puts out their hands to it, the way you'd touch a doorpost for luck.

narrator/49cb01657d89dd57.text: He rides on. Long after the hoofbeats fade, nobody wants to be the first to speak.

narrator/49e40e5e23593fd4.text: Three green moss agates wrapped in a handkerchief, worth about thirty gold to the right buyer.

narrator/49f1c99b24bd3011.text: Dire wolves, five of them, big as ponies, fanning out across the slope ahead. Behind them a man steps out from the trees, smiling, and starts to change.

narrator/49f6aa8c4fafdebd.text: He steps back from the bier. He doesn't look at you. He looks at her.

narrator/4a578dd6c70dded1.text: Shapes stand in the square, swaying like washing on a line. They turn toward you all at once.

narrator/4a663ecbe445448a.text: An old man sits on an upturned cask by the fire with a blanket over his knees: white beard, black eyes, and the bearing of a king who has mislaid his kingdom and expects it returned by supper.

narrator/4a7e42097374f8e1.text: The press house is empty and smells of rot and lamp oil. The great press stands where it always has, waiting for a harvest worth crushing.

narrator/4a89abb90a63dce4.text: A long gallery of statues and portraits of knights. At the far end a narrow door leads into the tower, and the floorboards in front of it are worn pale, from people stopping there and not going through.

narrator/4aa2a3093897534a.text: A cot made up neatly, a lump of charcoal on the pillow, and the blanket worn through at the place where a big man sits every night to read a wall.

narrator/4aa4b5f2c0b30309.text: The head turns back toward the valley. Whatever it was waiting for, it wasn't you.

narrator/4aa8203bb31ee990.text: The chant has become a howl, and under it something heavy is dragging itself toward the stairs.

narrator/4abe48db6a1859f5.text: Five soldiers in old mail stand at their posts around the guardroom, grey as the stone behind them and a little blurred at the edges, like breath on a cold window. One of them steps out into the middle of the floor. He has sergeant's knots on his shoulder and no colour in him anywhere.

narrator/4b01b31a4ec0edb5.text: The chandelier lets go of the ceiling with a sound like a carriage-load of glasses hitting the floor.

narrator/4b275284c2bfd4fa.text: Plain pews, worn smooth. Somebody has carved small names into the back of each, generations of them, so the dead can still sit with their families.

narrator/4b3aa5890740a2ef.text: The man behind the bar has black hair, black eyes and the stillness of somebody who has been listening to the room since before you came into it.

narrator/4b640d9192060409.text: Wolf blood dries on your boots. Ahead, two headless stone knights keep a gate that seems to be expecting you.

narrator/4b6842285036afee.text: A kitchen with a cauldron big enough to bathe in, and two small boys underfoot who vanish the moment you look straight at them.

narrator/4b7e2d9902804659.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Tarakamedes, the dragon in the grave. Its faithful went down into the earth to serve it. None came back up."

narrator/4b8b1d8827562831.text: Bricks fill the doorway where the front door used to be, and the tall window you came out of is half bricked over already. The house is mending itself, slowly, like a scab.

narrator/4b94c8e0ed06e64c.text: A narrow passage, two shoulders wide. The flagstones are worn smooth down the middle by a great many robed feet.

narrator/4ba303794d1ff8f0.text: An old cask, and a great one. If it's hiding anything, it's better at hiding than you are at finding.

narrator/4bb743bf43e84ef1.text: The lump of grey clay beside the dollhouse altar. It was never clay.

narrator/4bcb118167caca76.text: The vat's hoops go off like pistol shots, one, two, three.

narrator/4bda2c4726da538a.text: The undergrowth at the roadside stands up and walks. Behind it, two figures in bark-dyed robes are chanting, and the trees are listening.

narrator/4bf6d9164f928597.text: You bar the door and wait while the fire burns down to embers. Then, all at once, every board on every window begins to creak.

narrator/4bfef629b8e8af0d.text: An old well with a rope, a pulley and a bucket on a hook. Something down there is breathing in time with you.

narrator/4c125f9521d763a8.text: A thick ledger lies open on the table, a pen laid across the page.

narrator/4c485228df6b74c1.text: You make the archway as the heap rises behind you, wet and enormous, its tendrils closing on the place where you stood a moment ago.

narrator/4c4854d32e72ca80.text: Grey light pours through the broken gate: men-at-arms, translucent, shields up, charging a line that broke four hundred years ago. You are standing where the line was.

narrator/4c6c7eaa8f27f949.text: The vault is long enough for a church, and it needs to be. Along the middle, on a raised stone bier, lies a skeleton with folded wings, as long as a ship, its neck ending in nothing.

narrator/4c6f43d633401fb6.text: A dais of new planks, painted yellow, with a carpet nailed down at the front where the Baron stands. The carpet is worn through in one spot, from turning to face the crowd.

narrator/4c7293f5e0a5c8e3.text: A letter on the desk, in a big, generous hand that goes small and shaky by the last lines. It was never sent, and never finished.

narrator/4c780bc4ecf59399.text: A rotten jetty with half its planks gone. At the end, a mooring post, and a fresh rope tied to it with nothing on the other end.

narrator/4ccb05e1772e5764.text: She puts the crossbow down, which she hasn't done since you arrived.

narrator/4cd403bd45d9e1ae.text: The bottom drops away under you and you go in over your head. You come up spluttering, with the bow rope somehow in your fist, and tow her in while she watches with polite interest.

narrator/4ced36044a5d030d.text: The town square is swept, garlanded and full of people pretending to be in no hurry. In the middle stands a wooden dais, a pair of stocks, and a great wicker sun on a pole, as tall as a house and painted a desperate yellow.

narrator/4d012816fd2b23f8.text: A drum of black chain and a crank as long as a spear, and through the murder holes in the floor, the top of the portcullis, waiting.

narrator/4d114a52b29148b3.text: Grey stone, fitted without mortar by people long dead, three men high. Here and there are marks scored deep into the stones from outside, at about the height of a big dog standing on its hind legs.

narrator/4d193a23b404e9e4.text: You sleep by a fire that someone has lit with far too much magic. Your host stays up all night writing, and swears at his own handwriting.

narrator/4d208998d1805bd1.text: When the candles below it gutter, a thin line of light shows round its edge from behind, as if there were a second sun back there, smaller and closer.

narrator/4d728b8fa414580b.text: The house is silent in a new way: not the hush of something listening, but the hush after a long day's work is done.

narrator/4d7556af3fcb8cbc.text: A long nave of pews under a sunburst window, an altar on its step, a vestry and a narrow stair down to the crypt where St. Andral's sarcophagus waits.

narrator/4d8458d2c25c782e.text: In the ditch beside the road lies a peddler's pack with its straps torn through. No peddler. A long smear in the mud leads off into the trees, and stops.

narrator/4d8c194f72eacbcb.text: She says her own name under her breath, the way she did at the falls. Ireena. Then again, louder.

narrator/4d9f3007a2334d74.text: Davian takes the stone in both hands. Green light comes up between his fingers, the way sun comes through a leaf.

narrator/4de04d32d0bd7aee.text: Inside the ring the ground is warm, like the flank of a sleeping animal, and every step you take is answered from somewhere deep under your feet.

narrator/4de1ad5626ad349a.text: The shutters are barred, but a candle burns behind them. When you look closer, it goes out.

narrator/4df035d7d63f0e77.text: The road at night: open fields, low walls, and a sky without a single star. Anything could cross those fields, and something is.

narrator/4df8f7beac537d6a.text: The buckets go down. The servants go back the way they came, a good deal faster. The sun sleeps dry.

narrator/4e206610104fb170.text: Every eye in the square that isn't on the Baron is on you: the armed strangers. Whatever you do now, Vallaki will remember it.

narrator/4e22711e04f33867.text: The blow lands like a verdict.

narrator/4e2ed638f9e6452c.text: Four roads meet here, and none of them looks as if it wants you on it.

narrator/4e8ce49d1ee002b6.text: A wide stone hearth, cold and swept clean. Set into its back wall, where a cookpot ought to hang, is a rod of green copper as thick as a thumb, running straight up into the chimney.

narrator/4e923189ded9d6bb.text: Three druids stand among heaps of dead brush that were blights until the tree on the hill burned. They have had a bad week, and they mean to share it.

narrator/4ea95a2e86f94264.text: The house is emptier without the coffin in it. Somehow the boards on the windows look less sure of themselves.

narrator/4eeb24fcd23813a0.text: A wall of trophies: a shepherd's crook, a hunter's cap, a Vistani boot with a fine buckle, a child's bonnet. The boot has a knife slash across the ankle and a dark stain down to the heel.

narrator/4f06fef17c2362a7.text: He is not there any more. Out in the east, a long way off, something made of timber begins to scream.

narrator/4f1bfc6f987f069c.text: The pool lies still as glass. Ireena has stopped walking. She hasn't noticed she's stopped.

narrator/4f492a363b52882d.text: A landing at the head of the great stair. North, the dragon's study, its shelves half burned; west, a dormitory of beds nobody sleeps in; east, a long gallery of statues ending at the tower door. Two smaller rooms south: one bare, one covered in writing.

narrator/4f683f28f3b42a8d.text: Somewhere ahead, under the black water, a bell rings. Once, then again, slow, the way a chapel bell rings for a burial. There is no wind. There is no chapel.

narrator/4fa13955385ddf18.text: A knight in dented plate waits on the broken front steps with his helmet under his arm. His face is grey and quite plainly dead, and he is doing his best to smile with it.

narrator/4fc1ccad6475d756.text: A spinning wheel, turning. The thread's coming on again, fine and even.

narrator/4fed16f4ba8b8522.text: The quiet lasts a breath; then the hasty grave shifts, and every old grave around it answers. Unblessed earth, it seems, is an open door.

narrator/50672f83980e2a02.text: You break a seal stamped with a pointed hat. Somewhere, you hope, a wizard is not keeping count.

narrator/507f854e27b1bc40.text: Low beams, a smoking hearth, a dozen tables and four drinkers. At the corner table, three women in bright skirts are laughing, which in this village is practically a crime.

narrator/5086a0e8e664d556.text: You sleep in turns on the dry end of the causeway. The marsh is full of small noises, and for once none of them are about you.

narrator/50c559062ee02ff6.text: Under the velvet he's sweating. He believes every word, and the belief is the only thing holding him upright. He is not a cruel man by nature; he is a frightened one, and he has found that cruelty is quicker.

narrator/50e84b02602528df.text: Soot on the plinth, old and greasy, in a long black smear like a lick from a tongue. The dark up here came in after the light went out, and made itself at home.

narrator/50ea768be7610c44.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Savnok, the locked mouth. Its keepers never told us what it wanted. They couldn't."

narrator/5107e81e9024d6b1.text: "Petitioner: Strahd, son of Barov, a prince of the western wars. He asks to stay young for as long as he wants anything, and to keep whatever he has taken. Brought before the one whose name we do not write."

narrator/5114a26cd0c0afd3.text: A deep well with a wooden lid. Someone has scratched a word into the lid, over and over, in a child's hand: HOME.

narrator/516aee12be1811ac.text: Brick. Where the front door stood, there is only brick, still warm, still settling.

narrator/517b6692dc1eb072.text: Inside a ring of standing stones stands a tree with bark like a burnt hand. Beside it lies a man of earth and timber forty feet long, cloaked, with a face you have seen before.

narrator/520ad1dbd58d1450.text: Izek lies at the foot of the dais. The fire in his arm goes out last.

narrator/52114cef993c0fcc.text: The shelf of snow before the temple doors is littered with amber, broken into pieces the size of shields. Neither colossus is watching now.

narrator/523dfed120249bbc.text: It takes the crust, considers it, and then, quite unmistakably, nods. It flies off west toward the vineyards beyond Vallaki, and circles back twice to make sure you saw which way.

narrator/524072115262469a.text: The floor gives way to the knee.

narrator/5247bdef26f86f03.text: The pole gate at the back of the den creaks open. A girl of about ten comes out first, holding a much smaller girl's hand, and three more children behind her in a line.

narrator/524b3ae9bc1c31bb.text: A narrow bedroom with a crucifix nailed over the bed and another nailed over the door, facing the storeroom.

narrator/525f255b95b0e434.text: A woman in a patched wool coat straightens up from a patch of purple flowers by the cave mouth, a knife in one hand and a fistful of stalks in the other. Her eyes catch what little light there is, the way a dog's do.

narrator/5268322f387fef10.text: Kneading tables, cooling racks, and an oven big enough to walk into. There are no small shoes by the door. You check.

narrator/5277973ef0bbbc9a.text: And it is still tied to this place, by a thread as fine as hair that runs out of the mountain and down into the valley.

narrator/527f2ea6c325aa92.text: A plain iron strongbox, unlocked. The man who owns it trusts the room more than any lock.

narrator/5298c551900c2cd7.text: An elegant hall lit by oil lamps: a hearth with the family portrait over the mantel, and two suits of wolf-helmed armor standing guard by the library door, spears grounded.

narrator/52b7ef8fcb1fc492.text: The Abbot isn't looking at his bride. He's looking past her. At Ireena.

narrator/52cb2b058dd8bc96.text: The altar is dressed in white again, and candles burn along its step in a row as neat as teeth.

narrator/532329786bcad382.text: The hearth looks like a hearth. If anyone hid anything in it, they did it well, and they did it a long time ago.

narrator/532d6759ee6df59a.text: Hot skin, a racing pulse, a cough that rattles. You've seen fevers break, and you've seen them not. You can't tell which this is.

narrator/53563f8cadb45661.text: The hut lies broken across its own roots, door open, shutters gone. It smells of cold soup and rot, and for the first time it isn't breathing.

narrator/53683852c36ac95a.text: Ireena has gone very still. Her hand has found her own sleeve and is gripping it hard.

narrator/536ceb68fbc5d4f7.text: An old woman in a flour-dusted shawl leans on a handcart heaped with glazed pastries under a cloth. Her smile arrives well before she does.

narrator/536fabfe71b7b18e.text: The cellar stair goes down into the right kind of cold, the kind that smells of oak and old wine. From somewhere at the far end comes a sound of scraping.

narrator/5373f274f9ededdf.text: A ring of good chairs, facing inward. The cushions are worn, but there isn't a book on any of them, and the candle stubs on the side tables are black ones.

narrator/538aa1dfd23d447d.text: You knock. The tower considers the question and declines to answer.

narrator/5390b594a2d6de51.text: The end sounds wrong when you knock: higher, emptier, a door rather than a wall. The third hoop down turns a quarter-inch further than any hoop should.

narrator/53a5146745ce54cb.text: Little cots with names scratched on the frames: Ana, Tomas, the twins, Little Bird. On one, under the name, a smaller hand has added: I WAS HERE.

narrator/53a79dbb88e6834c.text: The vat bursts its hoops. What rises out of it is the winery's last harvest: skins, stems and rot, heaped into something the height of a man and still growing.

narrator/53afcc01adb17211.text: The cabinet glass is clean enough to show your face. The crossbows inside are oiled, as if the hunt is tomorrow.

narrator/53cd6950ddd86143.text: The last wine cart, loaded and never sent, sitting on its broken axle by the gate. The casks have been stove in. The druids made very sure nobody in the valley got a drink.

narrator/53ebe61f4cdf92f1.text: The frost on the window holds the shape of a long, patient head. When you look straight at it, it is only frost.

narrator/53fa43a0fb4218ea.text: A spinning wheel with the wool still on it, stopped halfway through a thread a month ago.

narrator/541ee25f1a946b52.text: Not scratches: letters, cut with a fingernail or a tooth, over and over until they were deep enough to last. I SENT HIM. I TOLD HIM FLY. TELL FATHER. E.

narrator/543154c5c0b96afa.text: A hall of portraits and boarded windows, a staircase climbing into the dark. Somebody has nailed a plank across the front door from inside, and another, and another.

narrator/547fa6d0291629bf.text: She sets the bowl down very carefully, and pushes it away with one finger.

narrator/54c0cd478e1e86cf.text: The palisade's south-east corner: a watch fire, a squat log lockup with one barred window, and a walkway where the watch can look out over the dark and see nothing at all.

narrator/550f9e74e7c82617.text: Nobody sleeps. Somebody keeps humming, very quietly, and nobody admits to it.

narrator/552ff003b304e947.text: The stair is worn hollow in the middle by three hundred years of the same feet. Or so it feels. The creaking above you stops while you climb, and starts again when you stop.

narrator/553a3e5dfb8d0d41.text: You read him Markovia's letter, kneeling there, every word. He listens with his eyes shut.

narrator/554b1181672e9437.text: The burgomaster's grave is the only neat thing in the churchyard. Somebody has already left a candle on it.

narrator/55590faf2ffba83b.text: The little red-haired doll turns slowly on its thread in the heat from the hearth.

narrator/555c29b52baf3527.text: He gets up. He's an old man, and it takes a while. He goes to where his son is working, and they stand there, two men with the same black eyes, and neither of them is any good at this.

narrator/557e766009c5936e.text: Only clean flagstones now, as if the frost was waiting for a reason to leave.

narrator/558f60ad156b7366.text: The hedge on both sides of the road stands up and walks toward you, rustling.

narrator/55b191e409c7b08b.text: Little houses on wheels, carved and painted and hung with bells. Every door is shut. Every window has someone behind it.

narrator/55b68893ff43d0c3.text: Upstairs, the rocking stops for a moment, then starts again.

narrator/5619c62c20150401.text: You sleep in shifts, and whoever has the watch keeps one eye on Ireena's window. Twice in the night something taps on the glass, and nobody answers.

narrator/563345b36109f9e7.text: You say what you can about a man you never met: that he held his door every night until his heart gave out. It's short, and Ismark nods as if it were the right length.

narrator/56369477aa0afe22.text: Rays. A sun. Gilt. If it means more, it's keeping the meaning to itself.

narrator/5651bac258f4c17b.text: Out in the east, a shutter bangs. A scream comes across the reeds, thin and rising, the scream of someone who has seen a light where no light should be.

narrator/566a46f76160cc07.text: For a moment you think he won't answer. Then he looks at the stair, as if he can see through it.

narrator/567d91e4f370263c.text: He bounces off a will like a bird off a window and sits down hard, wailing. Rose holds him and glares at you over his head.

narrator/568d592c7801f70a.text: A row of narrow shops with painted signs. In the toymaker's window, a hundred wooden faces watch the street with perfect patience.

narrator/56bb079503853379.text: A full-length mirror in a carved frame. Cold air breathes along one edge of it, and the room behind you in the glass is a little darker than the room you're in.

narrator/56bbed44435e24fe.text: The weapons in the hall hang crooked on their hooks, trembling. The paneling creaks like something drawing breath to shout.

narrator/56d21fe4d7aebc74.text: Silver light comes down the stair from above, lying on every step like snow.

narrator/56e019003bf9420b.text: Ireena stands at the foot of the bier and doesn't move. The girl on it has her face, too.

narrator/56e1d793153ff9f6.text: The ring groans and holds. The chain rattles loud enough to wake the whole hill, and somewhere in the dark, something stirs in its straw and settles again.

narrator/56ea385c404ec7f7.text: Alabaster dancers stand along the mantel, caught mid-turn, every one of them facing the harpsichord.

narrator/5708f05c0f85ec94.text: Offalia is still snoring on the bakery floor. Whatever you mean to do about her, do it first.

narrator/570d0c42c822ffa8.text: Somebody starts pulling down the bunting. Somebody else starts taking the stocks apart, slat by slat, for firewood. Nobody tells anybody to smile.

narrator/5726bebe272e5ddf.text: Vladimir is down on one knee among the scattered chairs. The wounds you gave him are already closing, slowly, with a sound like ice forming on a pond. He does not get up.

narrator/572ad463bb2bdd3b.text: St. Andral's stands on its rise at the north-east corner of the town, its bell tower leaning very slightly toward the castle, as if listening. Gravestones crowd its yard, and a fresh grave is being dug beside them.

narrator/5738943940b4b918.text: The wall of Krezk is a darker dark against the mountain. There are lamps on the wall-walk, and every one of them is turned outward, toward you.

narrator/574091a3f814bc27.text: Scratches in rows of five on the inside of a cage bar, made with a fingernail. Two full rows and one more. Under them, smaller, a single scratch on its own, scratched out.

narrator/574c9c67f93aa8b9.text: Steel rings off amber. The colossus considers the scratch, and then it considers you.

narrator/5777a4aa4c0b9779.text: The lock gives. Inside, someone small says: Mother?

narrator/57857f5c8e31b3b7.text: Two cages hang from the rafters on chains, each big enough for a child to sit in if the child doesn't stretch. There are scratches on one of the bars, in neat rows.

narrator/579155e14797465f.text: Ireena's face changes. Not fear. Something worse, and softer: recognition, coming up through her like a drowned thing finding the surface.

narrator/57957e14ae690bd0.text: You tell her. She listens without moving, and when you're done she lets out a long breath, as if she has been holding it for twelve years.

narrator/5796e0852a6e48b5.text: He steps back into the wall and is gone, and the doorway is only a doorway.

narrator/57b2f7882a142a27.text: The fermenting hall is quiet. The mash in the vats has gone still and grey, like porridge nobody wanted.

narrator/57d257a862c4136a.text: Rations, torches, four gold pieces knotted in a sock. And a letter, half written, that begins: the road is safer than they say, my love, and stops there.

narrator/5822195a6337f430.text: For a moment the pretty face forgets to be pretty. Then it remembers, and smiles, and that is worse.

narrator/582e99ae26ce4cbd.text: Quiet, again. The house is already thinking about what to try next.

narrator/58386217d34a3616.text: A yard of dead hedges and churned mud inside an iron fence. The mud holds paw prints the size of dinner plates, all of them pointed at the house.

narrator/5850eed2bcbdcfac.text: The vault is quiet now. Somewhere in the stone, very faintly, a sentry is still saying the challenge to nobody.

narrator/586d4e6f4ea722f1.text: A small square door with a brass button beside it. Behind it, ropes run up and down a shaft from the kitchen to the master's bedroom.

narrator/58743d89b382a3d5.text: No wound, no bruise, no poison's colour in the lips. Only, above her heart, a single red scratch, fine as a bramble's, that has never healed in all this time.

narrator/587d609fdc442afd.text: The upper floor creaks under your weight, a long low complaint that travels ahead of you down the hall.

narrator/589aeecf75e5f89b.text: The glass holds one heartbeat too long. Behind you, the dining room's silver lifts off the sideboard with a sound like a breath let out.

narrator/58a058078b1db4a1.text: In the mud, the marks of a man's boots going down to the water, and between them a long smear where something was dragged, small and kicking.

narrator/58dddfd056704eae.text: Kasimir has stopped walking. He stands in the archway with his hands at his sides, as if he has forgotten what they are for.

narrator/58f0607f9b42aeaa.text: Things that were people once come scuttling from behind the sarcophagi, each with one great eye where a face should be. Two of the wardens' dead drift up through the floor behind them.

narrator/58fd132c86d97ed4.text: A reading table stacked with books on contracts, oaths and wagers, each one bristling with neat paper markers. The cup beside them is still steaming, though nobody has touched it.

narrator/591ce0003712b098.text: Her hands are shaking too badly to hold a spell. She is not going to fight anybody. She is going to sit in the mud until it rises.

narrator/59206de75af0ce9f.text: Inside lies a heavy book bound in black leather, clasped in tarnished silver. Nobody wants to be the first to touch it.

narrator/5936a4f295326852.text: At the words "sent to keep", something old moves in his face, like a sleeper hearing his name in another room.

narrator/594052143dd02629.text: You say the words. When you look back from the next bend, the snow has covered them over gently, like a sheet drawn up by someone who loved them.

narrator/5949c8b8ed7e283d.text: The biggest house in Berez, and the only one with stone walls, which only means it took longer to fall. The burgomaster's chair is still at the head of a table under two feet of silt.

narrator/595a54119d026c87.text: Coins, teeth, a child's shoe, candle stubs. The wolves bring her what they value, and some of it is very strange.

narrator/595e75bbeb35fc1a.text: The gallery floor gives way with a long tearing groan, and the dark underneath comes up to meet you.

narrator/59633b1549e39ac5.text: Under the pines at night the road is a pale stripe in the black. Your lantern makes a small room of light, and the forest leans in to look.

narrator/5976b6e9cdce0c21.text: A handcart comes squeaking round the bend, heaped high under a white cloth, and behind it, pushing, a little old woman in a flour-dusted shawl.

narrator/599cc26f59566346.text: The stand is empty, and this time it will stay that way.

narrator/59aa6116c6ee6a5b.text: You knock on it. It answers hollow, like a door with nobody home, and the bung comes away in your hand.

narrator/59aa8b0d89fc5d5f.text: The lockup warden spreads his hands. The lockup's empty, he calls, and somehow does not sound sorry.

narrator/59b4ad5e20f8df9d.text: The chest is empty now, except for a wooden horse with one ear and a faint smell of lavender.

narrator/59c0453dc3efad37.text: Shapes uncurl from the straw along the walls, and the cave is suddenly full of yellow eyes. Nobody told them you were coming. They are taking it personally.

narrator/59c7bff8786197e2.text: At the shrine, a woman in a patched coat is relighting candles that your fight has blown out. She does not turn round.

narrator/59d892d78c0f738d.text: Three grey wolves cross the trail ahead of you at a lope. The last one stops, looks at you for a long moment, and dips its head before it goes on. Emil's wolves know your smell.

narrator/59e376e5027b829f.text: The tent is as you left it. The five cards are back in the deck; the table remembers where they lay.

narrator/59f815da068b9601.text: A dead knight sits on the front step with his back to the doorpost and his helmet in his lap, facing the light, the way a man sits at the end of a long watch.

narrator/5a21fbaafc0f4d77.text: A traveller sits against the inside of the doors, wrapped in a good cloak, chin on chest. They got past the colossi and in out of the wind, and then the cold finished what the climb had started.

narrator/5a54882c61143a21.text: The causeway ends where Berez begins: broken walls standing up out of black water, reeds taller than a man, and the smell of a river that came indoors and stayed. Far off in the west a white statue stands on a dry mound. In the east, on a stump wider than a house, a hut is breathing.

narrator/5a777deeffce11f9.text: A fire pit of blackened stones, a spit across it, and something on the spit you decide very firmly is a deer.

narrator/5a818f79f9107c25.text: Old Barovian letters, from before the castle was built. Not a blessing or a warning: a single name, cut by someone who wanted it remembered. KHAZAN.

narrator/5a8beb43b4b4ed00.text: A priest kneels before an altar stripped of its cloth, as though the church were in mourning. He rises when he hears you, and his face rearranges itself into something welcoming, with effort.

narrator/5a98338792b29f5a.text: Tser Pool is black and perfectly still, though a stream pours into it from the north. The reflections in it are a beat behind the things they reflect.

narrator/5ac10e5e205a792c.text: For a moment the sparks in his sockets burn white. Then, very quietly, he begins to remember.

narrator/5ad6c00fffc5d7ae.text: He looks back at you with the flat patience of a man who hurts people for a living. Whatever he wants, it isn't to talk to you.

narrator/5ae0554ebe2907c0.text: The lullaby is still in your head. It will be for a while.

narrator/5ae95be2bf7989d5.text: You lay a hand on the coffin and begin the words. Cold comes up through the wood into your palm. Then you see the marks.

narrator/5b03eabccc780ae6.text: He doesn't move until Ireena turns away. Then he watches her go, and goes on watching the place where she was.

narrator/5b1418d2ecb6cf4a.text: The inscription has been gnawed. By teeth. Small ones, patient ones.

narrator/5b1611b8abd2c86b.text: Dmitri looks at Ireena for a long while. Something in his face gives way, slowly, like ice on a thawing pond.

narrator/5b1d03f49d7eb497.text: A rented room turned into a travelling showman's dressing room: costumes, a lute, a stage moustache on the washstand. Under the bed, the corner of an iron-bound sea chest.

narrator/5b20d3868f98f2cc.text: The captain's room. The strongbox chained to the wall is the only thing in the tower that seems to want your attention, and wants it very much.

narrator/5b5bd87ed2ef159b.text: In the cradle, the root that was shaped like a baby has withered to a twist of brown, like a thing left too long in a cellar. The blanket is still tucked around it, very neatly.

narrator/5b5f8ec3fbf28e69.text: You dream of brick, climbing over your mouth course by course, and wake swallowing.

narrator/5b73dcdf79791878.text: The goat track comes up from the south through switchbacks of pine. The hut stands in a yard to the east; the summit, with its cairn, rises to the north-west; a lookout to the west shows the lake below.

narrator/5b8987bbfa5e50ce.text: Your light won't settle on the lid. It slides off the letters as if the stone were wet with ink.

narrator/5b8b656b0186ffc0.text: Izek sits on his cot in the dark with a doll in his ordinary hand, turning it so the candlelight moves across its painted face. He doesn't get up.

narrator/5b9a03bc0869c963.text: The road leaves the village between two leaning posts and runs west toward the crossroads. Ireena stops at the last post and looks back once.

narrator/5bc8a949baf1fc5c.text: The hooded figure's hands are folded over its box, and the box is silent. It has nothing more to say to you. It has already said it.

narrator/5bd0f30d85224e6b.text: Elisabeth is already over the table.

narrator/5bd5d0da1cbd7a4f.text: The rope parts at the first cut. You lay him on the road, then dig beside it where the earth is soft, with blades and hands and whatever else will move dirt.

narrator/5c10f95f3035d8c1.text: Coffins in every size, all well made. On the smallest, someone has carved a little sun, and then a little moon over it, as if unsure which would be kinder.

narrator/5c1231743e2de01e.text: The humming stops. In the silence, somebody at the back of the church begins, very quietly, to cry.

narrator/5c14e0f8174b677c.text: A howl from up the ridge, answered from below the road, and answered again much closer. The two at the front run on two legs.

narrator/5c209267190e24ed.text: A hearth with a green fire, a rocking chair worn pale on the arms, a table laid for more guests than she ever has.

narrator/5c28f57ac8b05321.text: The jar is warm, and it hums against your palm the way a cat does. Somewhere inside it, faintly, someone is arguing with himself about the correct way to open a door.

narrator/5c2a3d4e4b023609.text: A huge hearth with a black pot over a low fire. Something in the pot is bubbling. You decide, as a group, not to look.

narrator/5c524a792dfd0f67.text: She looks at each of your faces in turn, slowly, the way a cook reads a list of what's in the larder.

narrator/5c5be704e55f716f.text: The camp under the trees is struck, the tents folded, the fire cold. Only the cairn of river stones stays, and the ravens.

narrator/5c625cf4f2f44b41.text: He takes the dress the way a priest takes a relic, in both hands, and holds it up to the candles. For a moment his face is so happy that it's hard to look at.

narrator/5c7fdcfe1f6b85c6.text: There is nothing frightened in her at all, which is rare in Barovia. What's there instead is patience, and faith, and a quiet appetite for the Baron's chair that she isn't troubling to hide.

narrator/5cb8d2be912b019c.text: The grey light makes every letter look the same. You give up before your eyes start to ache.

narrator/5ce2689186338c24.text: Drawings pinned to the wall: a house, a sun, two children holding hands. Under every house, in the cellar, a black scribble with a great many legs.

narrator/5d10c84bccac4bd0.text: Wedged in the reeds, a waterlogged satchel: some fisher's knife, wrapped in oilcloth by someone who meant to come back for it.

narrator/5d4977774af5a714.text: Kiril's hoard: the purses, rings and good coats of everyone who ever walked the Krezk road at the wrong time.

narrator/5d4f69ea7b47baf5.text: A raven drops out of the dead oak and lands badly, the way old birds do. By the time it has straightened up, it is an old woman in a black shawl, brushing feathers off her sleeves like crumbs.

narrator/5d5e20033cf6cf59.text: You sleep inside Van Richten's wards, on his floor, under his maps. For the first time in Barovia nothing scratches at the door all night. It turns out to be very hard to sleep without it.

narrator/5d8e027dd465d78d.text: You tell him what was scratched into the post of the last cage. Davian listens without moving, the way old men listen to weather coming.

narrator/5da021db6d7da674.text: A wooden trapdoor in the ceiling, bolted from this side. The bolts slide, and still it won't lift: something heavy is sitting on it, the way the house sits on everything down here.

narrator/5da0dd570f346949.text: He steps off the end of the jetty, and the stones take him straight down.

narrator/5db4341cf6070b70.text: Steel comes out. Morgantha smiles at it the way a grandmother smiles at a child's wooden sword.

narrator/5dbedd0f3a4c815e.text: You find a way that keeps to the shadow: thorn, shale, a loose stone caught before it can fall. Take it, and nobody on the crown will know you're coming until you're there.

narrator/5dc0847fdee7080a.text: Ireena walks to the very lip and stands there, too still, the spray beading in her hair.

narrator/5dd2e1ccbf0b3e4c.text: Piccolo applauds, slowly, then reaches into the nearest purse and takes a coin. Admission, apparently.

narrator/5df51a7534f4f284.text: Inside the palisade, Vallaki is all steep roofs, swept streets and festival bunting in a yellow that nobody here would choose for themselves. Every face you pass is smiling. None of the smiles reach the eyes, and several of them are watching you.

narrator/5e0580f85bb9a713.text: The frost has gone from the great window. The glass dragon curls around its lamp, and the lamp in the picture seems brighter than glass can be.

narrator/5e069166413fa6c9.text: She presses a small iron key into your hand. It is warm from her pocket, and the bow is wrapped in rag where it would touch the silver.

narrator/5e0fed181101bc7c.text: A howl from the pines ends in a word. Something tall comes down the lane on two legs, and the pack comes with it.

narrator/5e134558c6c97934.text: Under the dolls and the wooden horse lie two small bundles wrapped in faded blankets, tied shut with a child's careful knot.

narrator/5e2a196fbc310b56.text: You lower the flame. Vladimir watches it all the way down, then turns and goes back down the stair without a word, and his knights go with him.

narrator/5e2fc35abd7833e7.text: Old graves, tidy and close-set. The newest have little bells tied to them on strings that run down into the earth, just in case.

narrator/5e331a0ea76b5078.text: Offalia drops the berries. Her hands are already longer than they were.

narrator/5e62f0165f88a826.text: You work the earring free. It is a little silver horse's head, warm from nothing at all.

narrator/5e840f4a76f110f1.text: Wintersplinter lies across the crown in splinters long as spears. In the split heartwood, where a heart would be, sits a green stone the size of a plum, pulsing faintly, like something trying to get its breath back.

narrator/5e8dedb3b115e286.text: The shuffling stops. Madam Eva looks past you at Ireena for a long moment, the way you might look at a house you lived in as a child.

narrator/5e9584c2b6ab5b89.text: The lid is set square again, and the stone under your hand is faintly, stubbornly warm.

narrator/5e99708cc333c20f.text: A broad man in a leather apron stands behind a stall of blades, mail and coils of rope, with a ledger chained to the counter so nobody can walk off with the prices.

narrator/5e9dd40b38297af4.text: Frost has softened the lid's letters to dimples. You make out the name, and the word "crowd", and nothing kind.

narrator/5ebf66fbe770c35f.text: The bridge, two strides wide over the cloud. The sky above it is empty now, and you find you can cross it without looking up.

narrator/5ece3898083da479.text: Godfrey says the oath. Half the table says it with him. Vladimir does not.

narrator/5eeba1e1a21056d6.text: The earth goes in fast and badly, and nobody speaks. Somewhere beyond the wall, something laughs, softly.

narrator/5efb76a1d7c2753d.text: The glyphs are a sentence, and each waits for the next to be spoken. You find the grammar, and speak them all backward. The doors swing open, and nothing in the alcove beside them stirs.

narrator/5f1a7a7ed2024116.text: From the crest you can see the vineyards to the east, Lake Zarovich like a dropped mirror, and beyond everything, the castle on its rock. It looks back. It always does.

narrator/5f2d1967dfc8e99c.text: A thin man in a threadbare vestment kneels at the altar, praying in a voice worn down to gravel. Beneath the floor, something answers him: a long, hungry cry.

narrator/5f4de43515b66dd6.text: The record of what he paid is here somewhere. The copper book on the lectern hasn't been opened in a very long time.

narrator/5f5b9e7d33620067.text: She catches your glance before it lands and tugs the scarf higher. Whatever is under it, she isn't sharing.

narrator/5f70d017903cf033.text: At "patience is how he feeds", the Abbot sits down on the altar step, as if someone has cut a string.

narrator/5f990d9565a92f5e.text: A palisade of sharpened logs rings the town. The Old Svalich Road comes in at the east gate and leaves by the west, past a Vistani camp outside the walls. The burgomaster's mansion, Wachterhaus and St. Andral's Church face the square from the north; the Blue Water Inn, the coffin maker and the lockup stand to the south.

narrator/5fa08aeaeda91871.text: Half an hour of scraping silt and pulling reeds bares a slab at the foot of the plinth with an iron ring in it. Under the slab, a stair goes down into the mound, perfectly dry, and somewhere below it a candle is burning.

narrator/5fd3d0bd448254b8.text: Horse bones in the stalls, still in their rotted harness, each under its own name: Briar, Thunder, Old Meg. The stablehands didn't leave them. The stablehands didn't leave either.

narrator/606b004123e8a0a0.text: Rows of narrow beds, all made with the blankets folded square at the foot. Nobody has slept in any of them. Somebody makes them every morning anyway.

narrator/607021d387a91846.text: Three locks on the inside of the door, a bolt, a bar and a padlock, all new and all locked the night Gertruda left. None of them was the one that mattered.

narrator/60ba2b097cb27af7.text: A crypt cut with the name Gustav Durst and the year of his birth, its slab set ready and never closed. Nobody ever got around to dying properly.

narrator/610141688cacbf30.text: The lake lies black and flat to the far shore, reeds rattling at its edge. The jetty has rotted halfway out, and there are footprints in the mud going down to the water and none coming back.

narrator/6142fe4a7956444b.text: Flint, wicks, a tinderbox, and lamp oil in stoppered flasks, all laid out ready for a night that has been four hundred years coming.

narrator/615412b742b53e97.text: You leave it for whoever comes looking. You suspect nobody will.

narrator/617fc4419a7b9058.text: Reeds as tall as a man rattle against each other at the water's edge, though there is no wind.

narrator/618376b258b78344.text: A young woman with a horse brush in her fist looks up from the pen, sees that you are not who she hoped, and goes back to brushing harder than the horse needs.

narrator/6197f160ee1a56f5.text: Four wicker cages hang from a frame of poles, each big enough for a man to crouch in. Three are open and empty. The fourth has had its door torn off, and its post is scored all over.

narrator/61a91a2e9b49fdb6.text: A soldier stands in the inner doorway: a man-at-arms made of grey light and old mail, his spear held crosswise across the arch. Through him you can see the long dark of the vault.

narrator/61f4cccf679edf48.text: The camp is waiting for you outside the tent: no music, no fire-talk, only knives and drawn bows.

narrator/6200a8bee388309c.text: The door shuts behind you with a soft, satisfied click. Inside, the house smells of beeswax and old smoke, as if the family stepped out a minute ago and has been gone for years.

narrator/62255552c8c3f001.text: The Baron climbs onto the dais in a sash and a gold chain, Lady Lydia beside him in a dress she certainly sewed herself. Behind them the wicker sun stands on its pole: straw, willow and hope.

narrator/6226cfde6f9911d7.text: Two empty cages, swinging a little. Someone has left the doors wide open, on purpose, so nobody can ever shut them again.

narrator/622cd3766478fada.text: The ash in the cradle stirs with no wind to stir it. The dark that settled into the dead lamp gathers itself into shapes, and the shapes have been waiting a long time for someone to bring a light up here.

narrator/625cb86ba1eae7f7.text: Silver in felt-lined drawers, every fork counted and in its place. The house will notice what's missing.

narrator/628ccc9afc957104.text: The door stands open on its silent hinges. Warm air comes out of the dark inside, smelling of lamp oil and old paper.

narrator/62a4ada6ce7b4008.text: You pray aloud for a girl you have never met. Mary doesn't close her eyes; she watches your lips, as if checking the words.

narrator/62a6c4fc4728bb37.text: The tower's one lit window throws a long yellow line across the black water, all the way to your feet, like an invitation nobody actually sent.

narrator/62b8715e19f3aa9a.text: The lanterns drop into the mud, still burning. The mourners come on without them.

narrator/62d3737c22a0a2ee.text: The window's shutter hangs open on one hinge. The sill is clean, the latch unbroken.

narrator/62e4dd5bd502b39e.text: The doors don't give, and the glyphs under your feet brighten, offended. In the dark alcove beside the doors, something tall turns its head.

narrator/63339f9926354657.text: The straw is dark with water to the heart. It will not burn at noon, whatever the Baron shouts at it.

narrator/6380ed4b7fcb2e53.text: The crypt was full of something, and now the passage is.

narrator/638e5c91413505d4.text: A stern man with black eyes and a white beard, holding a bunch of grapes the way other men in portraits hold swords. The resemblance to Davian is so strong it's almost rude.

narrator/63900046cc023261.text: Twenty riders go past in a column, grey as fog, lances up, every face turned toward the ridge. Not one of them looks at you.

narrator/63b96b66168879d3.text: Charred spars, all that's left of the sails. One still turns, a little, when the wind gusts.

narrator/63c97c796d5a732d.text: Her smile doesn't move when she talks, and she isn't looking at your faces at all. She's weighing you, one at a time, like flour.

narrator/63c9c37879379aa2.text: Exethanter comes shuffling into the sanctum with a broom in one hand and a lantern in the other, and stops at the edge of the light.

narrator/63d15b8c7e4af967.text: The kill is still here, still uneaten. The wolves that left it are still somewhere ahead.

narrator/63dd0b12f37f8d84.text: The dais has a trestle table on it now, with a jug, some cups and a ledger, and the stocks are half gone for kindling.

narrator/6405787d8390c1df.text: The hut is cold now. The drawings have started to curl off the walls, as if they don't see the point any more.

narrator/64096251f5b0e160.text: You step around her. She smacks her lips in her sleep and murmurs something about marrow.

narrator/641e6ced2b536167.text: Something spidery is folded in on itself in the amber, legs over legs, crowned with a ring of small black eyes. Every eye turns to you at once.

narrator/644bfff1ba58ec2f.text: A lean man in a black coat and a silver-buttoned waistcoat rises from the steps of a painted wagon, unhurried, as though he'd been expecting you since before you set out.

narrator/644c62d6ce57dc25.text: The house is quiet and well-fed. A curtain twitches in an upstairs window, as if to say: come back any time.

narrator/6483a3ad731f95a0.text: A raven drops onto the road a few paces ahead and walks beside you, the way a dog would, for the better part of a mile. When you stop, it stops. When you look at it, it looks back.

narrator/64a8fa83ef96ca5a.text: You sleep on the warm bakery floor. In the morning the oven is cold for the first time in living memory.

narrator/64a98f0615bfb925.text: The causeway again. The tower's door stands open at the far end, which somehow makes it less welcoming rather than more.

narrator/64abb2bf17fa5731.text: A long black scorch across the stones at the foot of the door, as though something was thrown backwards very hard. A few long dark hairs are fused into the soot.

narrator/64c5b52bb1d1f356.text: A young knight with his helmet under his arm, grinning. It takes you a moment to recognise the commander, and the moment is not a comfortable one.

narrator/64e2712225cc6165.text: Izek hasn't been dreaming of a woman all these years. He's been remembering a child.

narrator/6501c04db599cb05.text: Reliefs of robed figures carrying small bundles to an altar, and a great shape rising from a heap to receive them. The sculptor took care over the bundles.

narrator/65067d5ec2adf186.text: The Luna slides past to the north, wide and brown and in no hurry, as if it never did anything to anybody.

narrator/651fb6b9e7c2e7d2.text: The light of your faith hits them like a wind. They set the empty coffin down in the middle of the road, turn together, and walk off into the fields toward wherever they were buried.

narrator/652b01aa3757658a.text: The wick takes at once, as if it had been waiting. A small, steady yellow light stands on the mound in the middle of the black marsh, where everything can see it.

narrator/654b26d3fd4a9dc1.text: The gelding steps squarely on a boot. Luminita does not hide her smile very well.

narrator/655a311ae8c2314f.text: The cells stand open and empty. Straw, a tin cup, scratches on the wall in long rows, counting something.

narrator/656fd9a4f3c5b462.text: Baba Lysaga sits in the reeds by her broken hut, singing something without a tune to nobody. She doesn't look up.

narrator/65961825719890fb.text: Black water, weed and cold, and nothing in your hands. When you come up for the third time, the surface has closed and gone flat.

narrator/65bead2c40cf138d.text: It isn't a lock. It's a net, and it faces inward. Whatever this temple hands out, the colossus was made to stop it walking away.

narrator/65c12af9df15a9e1.text: A peat fire burning low and steady. The mantel holds a row of small things in no order: a wooden horse, a hair ribbon, a sling, a doll with no face. Five of them. Room for a sixth.

narrator/65eb766536a72000.text: It's a pastry: flaky, golden, and smelling better than anything you've eaten since the mists closed behind you.

narrator/65f8e7c2d01e6135.text: He's charming, and calm, and impossible to read. That may be the whole of him. It may not.

narrator/663842bb93da1846.text: Over the door, five little wooden suns in a row, and a sixth, new, still pale, hammered on crooked by someone who couldn't wait for the glue.

narrator/6663a4e9c7bc597a.text: A taproom with a long bar and a fire that is actually lit. Through the kitchen, the guest rooms; through the back door, the stable yard and a painted wagon.

narrator/6681d6348b7a415e.text: She slams the shutter. The stump heaves under the hut, and the hut stands up.

narrator/6687ba2e6791b2d5.text: Pilgrims, by their coats: people who set out for the abbey's healing a long time ago, and are still walking.

narrator/668af057316509e3.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Seriach, master of the burning hounds. Its hunts did not end when the quarry died."

narrator/668c171349fa4e27.text: The colossus steps down off its plinth, and the whole ledge shakes.

narrator/66bbc326ce58be30.text: A black leather eye-patch set with a carnelian, worth about fifty gold.

narrator/66ceb8beda0db034.text: The pack let you pass, and the woods have gone very quiet about it. Ahead, a wall of stone and a gate of iron.

narrator/66d9055cb5a7788d.text: The nest is pine trunks woven like straw, lined with fleece and bones and what the roc couldn't eat: a purse, a sword, a coat of rings.

narrator/66f54dee5976ccb4.text: Pews for sixty. There have not been sixty people in here at once for a very long time.

narrator/674bb1585ee84005.text: The pastry cart comes round the bend again, but the woman pushing it is young and lovely, with a red ribbon in her hair and a new shawl.

narrator/674d3a949a9ccba7.text: A pair of tall iron gates bars the road, kept by two stone knights who have lost their heads but not their posts. The gates are shut, and the road goes through them anyway.

narrator/6752306377a1ebd3.text: Izek Strazni walks down off the dais and out of the square, and nobody, not even the Baron, tells him to come back.

narrator/67921c62a9a67580.text: Pines, ferns, and a pack lying in the bracken where somebody put it down and didn't come back for it.

narrator/67b8f381853ab84c.text: The third floor is colder than the rest, and quieter, with the hush of rooms where a family slept.

narrator/67cd727ac6b64db0.text: Whatever is left of her goes into the grey between worlds, and it won't come back whole. Under the floor, the oven ticks as it cools.

narrator/67cd97eb4142377b.text: The ritual fire goes into the roots by the armful. For a long moment the tree won't catch. Then it does, all at once, and it makes a sound as it burns, high and thin, like a kettle, or like something that isn't one.

narrator/67e9dce92859daac.text: The doors stand quiet under the snow. Whatever used to murmur behind them has stopped, and the silence up here is very large.

narrator/67eb5ecee935ec40.text: The iron-bound chest stands open and empty. Madam Eva has not bothered to close it; whatever it was waiting for has come and gone.

narrator/67efa76213d7a7f8.text: You open the Tome beside the copper book. His own pages tell the same night from the other side: a long climb, a courteous old warden, a voice in the dark that understood him at last.

narrator/681b85046138fd96.text: A dead oak full of ravens. They watch you the way a jury watches a defendant who has already been mentioned in evidence.

narrator/681e8a2a3dad44b3.text: An iron-bound chest behind Madam Eva's chair, with a lock that is older than any key you have seen.

narrator/682e5d63926cc7de.text: A dry ticking, close behind the stone. It could be anything. It could be a great many anythings.

narrator/683cac602b410a05.text: The church front: a pointed arch, a carved sunburst over the doors with its gilt rubbed away, and the doors themselves, very old and very clean.

narrator/6860c22263afa343.text: The hill rises bald out of the moor, as if the grass knew better. Smoke goes up from a camp on its shoulder, and from the crown comes a sound like a great many people humming one long note.

narrator/6880461cb16e3960.text: A swollen, motherly shape fills the clouded amber, ringed with tiny bubbles like a rash. The air near the lid tastes of sickrooms and boiled linen.

narrator/68a96ead145d6368.text: He says "his light" the way a man touches a bad tooth with his tongue. Whatever keeps that beacon dark, it isn't strategy. It's something he did, or didn't do, a long time ago.

narrator/68a9f192928e48df.text: The cart goes away toward the village at a speed no coffin was built for.

narrator/68b442a705dce14c.text: Walter slept here, for a little while.

narrator/68c3d66ccd588c42.text: It stops. This time, it stays stopped.

narrator/68d382542a0999c5.text: Steps on the stair: Sir Godfrey, climbing slowly, one hand on the wall. The light falls on his face, and he shuts his eyes in it.

narrator/690875158d425893.text: The keys are silent, and they stay that way.

narrator/69148041df4b9c46.text: The council has taken the half-burnt sun down and split it for kindling. Three families will be warm tonight on the Baron's festival, which is more than any festival did before.

narrator/6950016b21596af5.text: Three bolts slide back, one after another. The door opens on a tall red-haired woman with a drawn sword and very tired eyes.

narrator/696a49f1388ac110.text: A neat little chamber hung with drying herbs, with a swept floor and a real bed. Somebody in this den still lives like a person.

narrator/697993b6d9f7dbdd.text: He opens his mouth to argue, and finds he's thinking about it instead, which is plainly a new experience.

narrator/697a66b872e51067.text: Low beams, thick dust, the smell of mice and old cedar. The roof ticks overhead as it cools.

narrator/69c67e0f422d4707.text: A mild man, a little lonely, too fond of the sound of his own sentences. If there's anything else to him, it's well hidden.

narrator/69c71e0ac605ba10.text: The Baron's enforcer stands in the square with his arms folded, the scaled one under the ordinary one, watching the town the way a dog watches sheep.

narrator/69d05c540cf24239.text: The attic hall. The humming stops as you come in, like children caught out of bed.

narrator/69d7af6df6950ffa.text: The shades unravel into the dark, and the heap sighs and settles deeper into its sleep. Far above you, every lock in the house turns over, one after another, like a man cracking his knuckles.

narrator/69dab3386e520c9d.text: Grey shapes keep pace with you along the ridge above the road, and then, all at once, they don't.

narrator/69e1e18655f40c72.text: Jars and bottles in neat rows, each labelled in a small hand: wolfsbane, garlic oil, grave dirt (three cemeteries), holy water (blessed twice), and one simply marked DO NOT.

narrator/69e2125c0b7994c9.text: You take their potions, their purse and their ropes, and you tell them, out loud, that you'll put it all to good use. It seems only polite.

narrator/6a0b0c0fc0e29493.text: Lake Baratok is small, cold and very still, held in the lap of the mountain like water in a cupped hand. In the middle of it, on a knuckle of rock, stands a round black tower with one window lit.

narrator/6a0eddfc5114986a.text: The Luna, slow and wide and the colour of strong tea. Downstream, half a church roof sticks up out of the water like the back of a whale.

narrator/6a16472f98febe12.text: The dining room, still laid for guests who never arrive.

narrator/6a3b05a39a3a3318.text: A long stone house with a turf roof and a door with three bolts on the inside. Over the door, five little wooden suns are nailed in a row, and a sixth nail with nothing on it.

narrator/6a752fc4f02bc23b.text: The words go down into the grave with him. Behind the gallows, one of the old mounds settles, like a sleeper turning over.

narrator/6a7e4a0463904951.text: Her currant eyes find Ireena and stop there. For a moment the old woman doesn't breathe at all.

narrator/6a9d30b3a76c7d6b.text: The track climbs out of the trees onto bare rock. The windmill stands at the top with its sails locked in a cross; smoke leaks from a pipe in its side, and the whole hill smells of baking.

narrator/6abb974f666ef2f6.text: You put the folded dress back in her lap. She runs her thumb along the lace, at the place where it was mended.

narrator/6ac34587561e5d54.text: You sleep on the shingle with your backs to an empty hut. All night the lake laps at the jetty, patient and steady, like something counting.

narrator/6ac6e08a6090ae76.text: The candles all lean toward her, every one, the flames lying almost flat. Vasilka, forgotten on her bier, turns her head to see what everyone is looking at.

narrator/6aecbcb1ee7c6374.text: She unlocks the iron-bound chest behind her with a key she keeps on a cord round her neck, lifts out a bundle of oilcloth, and sets it on the table between the cards.

narrator/6b1d0b297a4cc270.text: They don't know; they are still waiting for a door to open, the way you wait for morning. Telling them will hurt, and not telling them will hurt longer.

narrator/6b2d746f2d2b12ec.text: A stair under the plinth comes down into one square room cut from the rock. The marsh is all around it and not a drop has got in.

narrator/6b4ccacfe00d472b.text: Behind the mill, out of sight of the road, a heap of bones is half sunk into the nettles. Sheep, mostly. Mostly.

narrator/6b519332dc384e30.text: Over the hearth, on a black thread, hangs a little doll of rag and straw with a head of real red hair. A tiny M is stitched on its breast. Through the M goes a long black thorn, pushed in and drawn out so many times the cloth around it has worn to lace.

narrator/6b5504cfcae3e20d.text: A handsome townhouse, freshly painted, its windows dark. It has the look of a house expecting guests, and looking forward to them.

narrator/6b691905728bb7fa.text: The smallest crypt in the row says Walter, and nothing else: no family name, no dates. It has never been opened.

narrator/6b7027f990924e81.text: Two children stand in the road where the cottages begin, as if they have never moved. The girl lifts her chin; the boy holds his wolf by one ear.

narrator/6b9d41328a31290f.text: He looks at Ireena for a long time. She looks back and doesn't help him.

narrator/6bb3be55e862a0a2.text: One board by the gear sits a fingernail higher than the rest, with no nail in it. Under it is the chute to the millstone.

narrator/6bcd1766ca7084f5.text: It tumbles into the ditch, struggles up and flies away low and lopsided, shrieking. From the trees on both sides of the road, a great many ravens shriek back.

narrator/6bf23be937b1af22.text: Beside the cradle, the lamp-keeper's iron locker is bolted to the stones. When you nudge it with a boot, something heavier than lamp oil shifts inside.

narrator/6bf9194f55163b59.text: The board tips, and so do you, down the chute and onto the millstone with a sound the whole mill hears.

narrator/6c01149b1bc6283c.text: You dream of a long table laid with pastries, and everyone you have ever lost sitting round it, eating, too busy to look up.

narrator/6c1163d4c01ebd08.text: Ireena slows at the crossroads and reads every arm of the signpost twice, as if it might have changed its mind about where things are.

narrator/6c161bec65686c45.text: Bluto looks back once, as if he'd expected someone to argue. Then he walks off the end of the jetty, and the stones take him straight down.

narrator/6c1c1687e0004ad0.text: St. Andral's stands on its rise, and the bell rings for the evening office as you come into the yard. It rings clean.

narrator/6c1eb5b5013686c7.text: Smoke, sour wine, and the low talk of people who have learned to talk low. Every head turns when the door opens, and then, one by one, turns back.

narrator/6c3858c0a7489954.text: The water comes up to your chest and the cold drives the breath out of you, but you get a hand on the bow and walk the boat back to the jetty like a reluctant horse.

narrator/6c55fa8b7d413a5f.text: Kiril's lair: a bed of good furs, a wolf-skin rug, an iron chest, and a wall of trophies. The trophies are not wolves.

narrator/6c6f2109ed335b04.text: Patrina is at her desk again, turning pages that crumble at her touch and re-form, and crumble.

narrator/6c82f55cc0b03bf5.text: Good horses, well kept, every one of them facing the lake with its ears back.

narrator/6c86838bc4c0ad25.text: Read together, they say what neither says alone. He didn't bargain to live forever. He bargained to stop growing older than her. Everything after was the price.

narrator/6c9dd40b5a4ee375.text: Ireena's hand goes to the scarf at her throat before she can stop it. He sees, and his smile widens.

narrator/6cac7b105b17848c.text: A cradle on rockers beside a copper tub. A mobile of little bones turns above the cradle, though there's no draught.

narrator/6cdf0be29fe622a1.text: Forty beds, blankets folded square, pillows plumped. Somebody makes them every morning for men who never come up to sleep.

narrator/6d117b287a378292.text: Cold stone and the smell of old candle wax. The floor of the vestibule is worn into two shallow hollows, side by side, where people knelt for a very long time.

narrator/6d4a78859aa9966e.text: Rot is spread across the floor in a great slick. Lorghoth the Decayer has finally decayed.

narrator/6d4d71e8c837cdc1.text: His eyes go to your faces, one by one, and stop. Whatever the road has written on them, he reads part of it.

narrator/6d511c8f9ab7a4ed.text: The frost on the parapet melts all at once and runs down the stones like rain.

narrator/6d58549f436947ac.text: He tries to hold your stare and can't. With a sound halfway between a curse and a sob he kicks the hoops off the vat and bolts out of the back door, west.

narrator/6d6defff1b7bd44e.text: A flat-bottomed rowboat, tarred and sound: the only boat on the landing that isn't rotting. Somebody still cares for it. Somebody who hasn't been home in days.

narrator/6d785f7f7b754117.text: Bones, bells, little mirrors, a dried bird's foot, a child's tooth on a thread. Each one is turning, very slowly, to face you.

narrator/6d7a7d5bcb58e2ac.text: The flame touches the old ash, and the beacon takes it like a long-held breath let go.

narrator/6d97536203d0beca.text: Nobody moves to fetch a book. You suspect nobody has for a very long time.

narrator/6da9c58a97c647bf.text: The balcony again, where one of the doors is breathing. You are fairly sure it's the nursery.

narrator/6daa6cd1f004a173.text: The attic again. The dust shows your footprints, and some smaller ones that aren't yours.

narrator/6de23905a806a481.text: Bones gnawed clean and stacked, with a kind of tidiness. The tidiness is the worst part.

narrator/6de48418e8dc742a.text: Her eyes rest on Ireena a moment too long, the way a jeweller's rest on a stone.

narrator/6e1bc24e3ee75526.text: Lady Wachter receives you in a parlour set with a ring of chairs, though only she is in it. She pours tea for each of you without asking how you take it, and gets every cup right.

narrator/6e1c4e0f47de4613.text: A hard man with a bow, and friends in the trees. That much was already clear.

narrator/6e2eeb5d3fee1cdb.text: The blanket is stretched so tight you could bounce a coin on it. It has been made every night for four hundred years, and never once unmade.

narrator/6e54a67ab872662b.text: Among the roots, half drawn into the earth, lie the bones of a young man in the rags of a black coat. At the throat is a wooden clasp carved like a raven, the twin of the one Davian wears.

narrator/6e7b5c9492742bbf.text: Past midnight the boards over the windows begin to creak, then to split. Wolves throw themselves at the front door, and in the parlor and the wake room grey hands come through the gaps.

narrator/6e8270956dc884c6.text: You hang the sunburst back on its hooks. It settles with a sigh.

narrator/6e84ff21b0ae8d96.text: The spare bedroom. The rocking chair has moved.

narrator/6e9b59ee64026e83.text: The fiddle stops mid-note. Every knife in the camp comes out at once.

narrator/6ea99f3a3623aa67.text: The den is silent. The fire pit is ash, and the straw beds along the walls are empty, and they will stay that way.

narrator/6eae7e3f2956217e.text: Up to his thighs in the black water, a gaunt man in a sodden coat is wading out from the shore with a sack over his shoulder. The sack is kicking.

narrator/6eb17c0bc63a7eb1.text: Rope coiled to the same diameter, candles in rows of ten, lamp oil with every label facing out. The shelves are fuller than the village has any use for.

narrator/6ed2a5108e29a203.text: The faceless god looks down on the hall with nothing. You find yourself not standing directly in front of it.

narrator/6eebeafe2608610b.text: Grey shapes come down the scree above the road at a lope, spreading out as they come.

narrator/6ef23e5d3ad865ce.text: An arrow thumps into the road a hand's breadth from your boots. Up on the wall-walk, somebody you hadn't noticed is already nocking another.

narrator/6ef6bdec509e0a9e.text: Grave mounds, very old, sunk and grassed over. Something has burrowed into one of them recently, and not to get out.

narrator/6f1dd4d259a056f9.text: The armor on the landing steps down off its stand.

narrator/6f200941cc701f3b.text: The altar is clean. The grooves are not.

narrator/6f2b2b90cce99b47.text: The tasting room: a long bar, a few tables, and a row of cups hung on hooks, every one of them clean. The druids haven't touched the cups. They don't drink, apparently. It explains a great deal.

narrator/6f38a6ab433d132b.text: A foyer with a boot scraper, a coat stand and a sign in a round, hopeful hand: SMILE, YOU ARE A GUEST.

narrator/6f716294eb209f91.text: Emil gets up the way old men and old wolves do, in stages, and stands rubbing the black rings on his wrists.

narrator/6fba81b68df38314.text: At the far end of the jetty stands Bluto, in the same sodden coat. His pockets hang heavy and lopsided. He has filled them with stones.

narrator/6fd5fbbe5859c2ea.text: A cloaked woman with no face. Whatever she is, she is very old, and very patient, and she was here long before the wolves.

narrator/6fd749ea3014ae74.text: Holes, dozens of them, knee-deep and ragged, clawed rather than dug. In one of them something has given up and left its claws behind.

narrator/6fdc25babfc620d4.text: The pines empty of bats all at once, and the dark comes down the lane like a flood.

narrator/6fea3f9952551fb8.text: The burial register: names, dates and causes in a careful hand. The careful hand gets less careful as the pages go on.

narrator/6fef9daff580e20a.text: The bunting is gone. Black ribbons hang from the watch's spears now, and the town is very quiet, the way a house goes quiet when someone important is asleep upstairs.

narrator/6ff4494b309f740a.text: The shutter stops swinging. The old woman goes so still that the hut, beneath her, goes still too.

narrator/700b7c08c07ab50a.text: A windowless room behind the shelves, crammed with black-bound books on summoning and the dead. A heavy chest stands on clawed iron feet, and beside it lies a skeleton in leather armor that found this room first.

narrator/7024ceb6fe6a43fd.text: Every window is boarded from inside, and the boards are scored with claw marks on the outside of the wood. The house smells of candle wax, wet dog and grief.

narrator/70299f64f1b5da8b.text: Outside: the end of the road, the shut gate and its watchman, and a switchback track climbing toward the abbey. Inside: the burgomaster's house, the well and the square, goat pens, cottages, and the lane north to the shrine of the White Sun.

narrator/702d1ad115189387.text: Two centuries of Wachters, each in the fashion of their day, each with a small silver S somewhere in the painting: on a ring, a brooch, the clasp of a book.

narrator/702e58d4445536d1.text: The stair winds up inside the wall, every step worn into a hollow by four hundred years of boots that only ever went up to look at a dark lamp.

narrator/70446a55ebe7bcd5.text: The camp is empty. The fire has burned to a red eye in the ashes, and the wagons stand with their doors open. Only the great tent still glows.

narrator/704cf939138c68f2.text: The scholar takes off his spectacles, and his face goes with them: a jackal's head, black-lipped and smiling. The cold braziers light themselves with green fire.

narrator/705acaee3b0c9e2d.text: The road west runs on into the mist. You have already said your goodbyes to this village; it didn't say any back.

narrator/705bc920b700d884.text: A painted sign over the gate: a wizard in a starry hat pouring wine into a cup held up by a raven. The paint is fresh on the raven and peeling everywhere else.

narrator/7071150e1ab1d742.text: A very small crypt at the end of the row.

narrator/7076246d38828cbf.text: A handcart lies tipped in the ditch with one wheel off. Beside it, sitting on an empty wine cask, is a stooped figure in a monk's cast-off habit, with one ear like a hound's and a hand that is mostly feathers.

narrator/7088b69c2186fb51.text: The inscription is there, and you read it, and a moment later you can't recall a word of it. You read it again. The same thing happens.

narrator/708f45b1fad3788e.text: You uncork the oil, and stop. Nobody has raked through the ashes at the back of that oven yet, and something about that oven nags at you.

narrator/7094e9084d9418b3.text: His eyes go to the dark line of the hills above the trees, once, before his smile comes back.

narrator/70e66ef952993601.text: Candles, benches, and a dozen people in their good clothes kneeling before a black-draped shrine, chanting softly. The chanting stops.

narrator/70ed8b11812c21c5.text: The chair stands still. It looks smaller than it did when someone was sitting in it.

narrator/7106e2e8dea13951.text: The bar is polished dark by hands and elbows. Behind it, a row of casks, and above them, three black feathers pinned to the beam in a row.

narrator/7116c89c6788b01e.text: She says it the way any other cook would say "not the rind".

narrator/712571fbbb9415cc.text: The road runs on between its ditches, open fields on both sides and stone walls tumbled into the grass. Plenty of room to see what's coming. Plenty of room for it to come.

narrator/7131fed96a88ea0d.text: Small graves, kept tidy. Someone has put a candle stub on each one, and lit none of them.

narrator/7151802fb03573d7.text: A doll with red hair, a green dress and a painted face carved with unusual care. A card reads NOT FOR SALE in a gloomy hand.

narrator/716ded291e969f79.text: Lines, arcs and glyphs, very neatly done. They mean something. They are quite certain of it, even if you aren't.

narrator/7189f0c51b4a2a8c.text: A square of mud around a dry well, and in the middle of it all a pastry cart, the only cheerful thing in the village. That should worry you more than it does.

narrator/71cbbf30574bc88a.text: A low vestibule, its floor worn by kneeling. One narrow doorway leads on into a long vault where a skeleton far too big for any tomb lies along a raised stone bier, wings folded, neck ending in nothing.

narrator/721c0568c30fbe8e.text: You find the joists under the rot and lay a path along them, and the old floor lets you pass.

narrator/7223c44f13494d82.text: The scarecrows lie where they fell, face down, poles snapped. Nothing is watching you from the reeds.

narrator/722c2524b2a541e9.text: The nuns' graves, small and neat, each with a sunburst cut into the headstone and a name: Sister this, Sister that. The last stone has no name, only the date the abbey emptied.

narrator/733d4c885afa1543.text: The track crests a rise, and there it is on its ridge to the north: the beacon of Argynvostholt, burning silver, laying a pale road of light across the treetops toward the castle.

narrator/73411567f60269cb.text: Kiril is dead. The wolves that are left go out of the cave mouth in a grey stream and don't stop running. Somewhere down the hill one of them howls, and none of the others answer.

narrator/73466e7085c1bad6.text: You find the place where the ward turns back on itself and pull. The colossus freezes mid-turn, head cocked, and stays that way.

narrator/735e1dc951c3d00e.text: A squat bell tower with no rope. The bell is still up there. On still nights, Krezk says, it rings anyway.

narrator/7363ae091f9063e4.text: Recipes, lists, warnings, a careful sketch of a duck. If the useful notes are here, they're under the useless ones, which are under the confusing ones.

narrator/73730eb6fb2f88e0.text: He says a word under his breath, and the door swings open. Then he lays his palm flat on the frame and murmurs again, and somewhere high in the tower something goes quiet, like a held breath let out.

narrator/738cec3c08d2fd91.text: A big grey wolf with an old arrow scar on its flank, set by the wall like a dog waiting to be let out.

narrator/739daa2069610f7f.text: The hut has been waiting for her. When you come instead, it stands up on its roots and screams through its door.

narrator/73eb641e4b0e6cdd.text: Another guardroom, and this one is not empty. Figures stand at their posts, coated in frost, perfectly still.
