narrator/73f823705eaa1fa8.text: The inscription has been scratched over with tiny star charts. Someone sat here a long time, copying what the vestige told them.

narrator/740b28974a193f3d.text: Main street runs straight through town from gate to gate, its mud raked smooth. Bunting hangs between the eaves on both sides, so low you have to duck the sodden ends.

narrator/74127b0dc0b475eb.text: The press house is all height and shadow, built round the great wine press like a church round its altar. The air is thick with the smell of crushed fruit going bad on purpose.

narrator/7429f6229057bb9d.text: A walled garden under frost. The poles along the north wall stand empty, and the snow beneath them is black with ash.

narrator/7459ce00d47a41bc.text: Black water to the far shore and the wolf hills above it. The fishers left a year ago when the nets stopped filling; only Bluto stayed. His rowboat is tied at the jetty's foot.

narrator/745e4c9041bcdb84.text: Low mounds ring the foot of the hill, old graves without stones. The track threads between them. Your boots, you notice, choose not to step on any.

narrator/746b9e94c2f366d6.text: A great round stone, white with dust. You run a finger through the dust and it isn't all flour: there's grit in it, and the grit is the wrong colour.

narrator/746d5f088284169f.text: You have two dresses: the one from the matron's trunk, and the one you brought up the mountain.

narrator/746f96ee339f2168.text: Stained glass of singers with their mouths open. In this light they could be singing, or screaming.

narrator/7480b9793675c17c.text: The captain's strongbox opens with a sound like a held breath let go.

narrator/74854425b7b1aa98.text: The black, sodden sun still stands on its pole. Lady Wachter has ordered it left where it is, as a reminder of what the Baron's light was worth.

narrator/748a4baec218215e.text: The road ends at a wall of fitted grey stone three men high, older than the trees around it, with one gate of iron-banded black oak. A watchman stands before it with a spear and the look of a man paid to say one word.

narrator/74929a707f26dbeb.text: The bridge is two strides wide over a gorge full of cloud. You remember the shadow on the ridge road, and find yourself looking up.

narrator/749bf970bf4936fd.text: The voice in the armour stops, and the wounds stop closing, and the armour is only armour.

narrator/74d7b5bd9336d7a1.text: The man at the table by the hearth has a sword across his knees and a cup he isn't drinking. He watches you cross the room the way a sentry watches a road.

narrator/74dc4a54444cad61.text: You can, now that you listen. Creak. Creak. Creak.

narrator/74f0fb074fec0ad7.text: The doll goes very still in his hand. He's been in enough fights to count yours before they start, and he doesn't like the total.

narrator/7777692ea9c25d7f.text: The first pin comes out, and the whole row erupts. Starved things are not grateful. Starved things are fast.

narrator/777a1403b17bacbe.text: You sit with your backs to the wall. The wall, to its credit, stays a wall.

narrator/77a64cacdd25822e.text: A ledger ruled in red ink, every line squared off with a straightedge. Bildrath has not made a mistake in it in twenty years, and has corrected other people's mistakes in the margins.

narrator/77bd858685a95ce5.text: The colossus watches the valley below. When you come close, the light in its eyes brightens a little, the way a sleeper's breathing changes.

narrator/77d758080027e78f.text: Bones in the corner, cracked for the marrow. You count four skulls before you stop counting.

narrator/783d2b45dcc4d1b9.text: Under the house again, and the chanting hasn't stopped. It doesn't need to breathe.

narrator/78528d2a9c91950d.text: Somewhere far below, the thing you killed is already rotting back into its heap. The house will grow another; it can wait.

narrator/78a34fa2523675ce.text: The Blue Water Inn sits at the bottom of the town with its lamps lit and its door open, which in Barovia is the bravest thing a building can do.

narrator/78b9ae2e1a8ff6b3.text: Bella climbs the stair humming, steps over what is left of her mother without looking down, and settles into the rocking chair as if it had been made for her.

narrator/78c1adb38221c4c8.text: A fresh grave, very deep and very square, its spoil heap so tidy it looks measured. It was.

narrator/78cf5fdbc9d69515.text: A nail squeals slowly out of a lid. Then another.

narrator/78ef89dc97d8a282.text: Near the head of it something pale moves and goes still: a druid on a rock, watching the gully. Somebody warned them.

narrator/79072a4d24a03440.text: He says it exactly the same way as last time. You suspect he has said it exactly the same way for centuries.

narrator/7914a04aa7b2d5d6.text: An emaciated shape in the amber, its ribs opened like a cage door with nothing inside. Its jaw works all the time, chewing nothing.

narrator/793c72952a08581d.text: The chalk lines flare white under your boots. For an instant you are everywhere and nowhere, and then you are back, and it hurts.

narrator/793d844124c97ca0.text: Equations in chalk cover the wall from floor to ceiling, beautiful and fluent, and every one of them stops halfway, at the same point, where the writer forgot what he was solving for.

narrator/794ced451d7262c2.text: Kiril lies on the floor of his own den, and as he cools he forgets how to be a wolf: the fur goes, the snout goes, and what is left is a big, ordinary dead man.

narrator/795169d91bfe2a5b.text: The road east runs back toward the gates, and the mist lies across it like a held breath. Nobody has come in from that direction in a long time, except you.

narrator/7969c6464dc914c9.text: Above the archway, a carved crest: a wolf's head over a closed door. The Dursts were proud of this house.

narrator/796a436938e7a1f6.text: The gorge falls away into cloud. A stone kicked over the edge never makes a sound.

narrator/79702d708e450eb9.text: His knuckles whiten on the spear. Behind the gate, someone shouts a question; he shouts back an answer you don't catch, and it isn't brave.

narrator/797870ac6a14696e.text: Under your feet the hill's slow heartbeat stops, and then begins again, fast.

narrator/798ced941e03d3cc.text: The dead come out of the trees on both sides of the road, slow and sure, still wearing the clothes they were buried in.

narrator/79965358d7e8903c.text: A scarecrow taller than the others, in a monk's old habit, with a sacking face and a mouth sewn shut with neat black stitches. Its arms are folded tight across its chest, as if it were holding something it was told to keep.

narrator/799a90b498888cb0.text: You don't argue. You tell him what you would want if it were your child, and what you would want if it were you down there, and he listens with his eyes closed.

narrator/79a03477395b9f8f.text: Under a recipe for ink and a list of the names of his own fingers, you find the wardens' word, written out in capitals with DO NOT FORGET beside it.

narrator/79cf02edcce70502.text: The men round the fire are big, bearded and painted green to the eyebrows. They see you, grin, and reach for their axes with something like relief.

narrator/79f39ff2268d789c.text: He looks at you for a long moment, and then at the two young men behind him, and you can see him deciding which of them to shout at later.

narrator/7a0f0d36898909b3.text: Two cages hang from the rafters like birdcages for very large birds. In one, a thin girl with a set jaw and scraped knuckles. In the other, a small boy asleep against the bars, with crumbs on his chin.

narrator/7a15561c0edbb711.text: Bones under the black water, laid out in a neat row, as if someone tidied them.

narrator/7a2405326c9f844c.text: Down in the great hall, at the head of the table, a commander sits back in a winged chair and lets his sword lie.

narrator/7a27ef6bdafc7dd4.text: Three locks on the door, boards on every window, and a cold stove in the middle of it all. The weeping fills the house the way water fills a jar.

narrator/7a305faf32b8a2ed.text: The cobbler shakes your hand on the way past, very hard, without a word.

narrator/7a59a9ddf5286151.text: The undercroft smells of old stone, old bones and something fresher. The dark here is very thick, and very attentive.

narrator/7a6201f411f6c315.text: A sparrow, a jay and a crow, hanging in the air at head height, wings out, frozen in mid-flight so perfectly you can count their feathers. They have been there a long time. Nothing has disturbed them.

narrator/7a7923fbd17bbeec.text: A parlour drowned in yellow cloth. Half-sewn suns, swallows and sashes cover every chair. It's the happiest room in Vallaki, and the most frantic.

narrator/7a80435b7c46cca8.text: The floor round the press is stained to the knee with what's left of the Mash.

narrator/7a89adcd14db0608.text: He turns his back and starts redrawing a line that didn't need redrawing, pressing so hard the chalk snaps.

narrator/7aa3830cd66d004c.text: The roar arrives before the view does. Then the trees open on a gorge, and the River Ivlis goes over the edge in one long white fall.

narrator/7aefc712ffc6bfc2.text: A raven drops onto a post at the side of the track and looks at you with one eye, then the other, as if checking its arithmetic.

narrator/7af1532d65cb1d38.text: Doors open a crack as Ireena passes and close again, and nobody calls out to her. A few people touch their foreheads, as if at a funeral.

narrator/7b1733bbc52da23d.text: A pine as thick as a barrel lies along the edge of the road, felled long ago. Its upper side has been worn smooth by people sitting on it to rest, and by claws.

narrator/7b1a275594cb247e.text: A brick oven as big as a cottage hearth. Far at the back, through the glow of the coals, something catches the light in a way that ash and bone never do.

narrator/7b4a6497b54e1b55.text: A bed that hasn't been slept in, and a chair pulled up to the wall that adjoins her daughter's room. The plaster is worn smooth at the height of an ear.

narrator/7b6bce48857f46c2.text: Hedda tells him the dream: the sun going out, the silver raven, the sunburst in its claws. Donavich's hands stop shaking.

narrator/7b81f772cece87d1.text: The air around the cairn claps shut like two great hands, and the summit rings like a struck bell.

narrator/7b983bebd2ea32c9.text: The drive climbs between dead trees to a house that burned a long time ago and never quite finished falling down. Above it a square tower stands against the sky, with no light at the top of it at all.

narrator/7bd845e671a965e0.text: Rusty shackles at wrist height, and on the hooks between them, black robes stiff with old wax. One is small enough for a child.

narrator/7bdbc4f154e46cab.text: Five small stones in a row, each with a little sun carved on it and a name below: Pyotr, Mila, Sofia, Anya, Lev. The snow has been brushed off all five this morning.

narrator/7bfd51172c982223.text: A smaller wolf, crouched as if to spring. Its glass eyes are on the door, not on you. You check.

narrator/7c027a25c78ec71a.text: The watch takes him at dawn. The sun sleeps dry.

narrator/7c151ed63c9cdb74.text: Students' desks, each with a book still open. The pages are frozen together. On one, someone has written the same line over and over until the ink ran out: I WILL NOT ANSWER.

narrator/7c1b426538056c1e.text: Above the library hearth hangs a painting of a windmill perched on a rocky crag, its sails stopped. The frame is the only thing in the room without dust.

narrator/7c216e59bf384221.text: She draws a breath she doesn't need, and the frost on the desks begins to sing with it.

narrator/7c248f5a554c6bc9.text: Crates, sacks, barrels and, in the far corner, a small iron strongbox that sits on the floor like a toad.

narrator/7c2c72b1b8111df4.text: The burgomaster's mansion takes up the whole north side of the square: three storeys of timber and plaster with a portrait of the Baron painted over the door, smiling down at everyone who knocks.

narrator/7c81138cb7ca2bc2.text: Skeletons hang in rusty shackles around the walls, and the soot on the stones behind them is shaped like people.

narrator/7c817c42b13f2bd5.text: The rock at the lip is slick with spray and very cold. Beyond it, nothing but white water and a long way down.

narrator/7c938e27b2441690.text: Shelves of books and a wall covered in chalk, and in the corner a stack of slates, each with one word written on it and rubbed out.

narrator/7ca1635e5d863ea4.text: And one of you carries a little of the same Thirst now. You can feel it, if you hold still: a thread as fine as hair, running out of the mountain and down to a castle on a hill.

narrator/7cd2431c0201caba.text: She digs in her apron and throws something at your feet without looking: the green stone from the cradle, muddy and still warm.

narrator/7fd696ff4742bf0c.text: Straw and sacking smoulder in the reeds. On the stump, a shutter bangs open.

narrator/81243114b6c3487d.text: Thorn hears the word and doesn't understand it. Then he does.

narrator/81ac6a94d23e7e85.text: He weeps and guts, weeps and guts. Mad, right, or both: his face won't say, and neither will the lake.

narrator/81ddd8f6c073e4ca.text: A brick oven as big as a cottage hearth, its door black with soot. The heat coming off it makes your eyes water, and the smell makes something worse happen.

narrator/81ebb3aea67f5456.text: A squat iron stove, long cold, its door rusted half open.

narrator/81ed02c33ec2b32e.text: He lifts one hand, and the churchyard earth begins to split.

narrator/81fcb2dd5713cd2f.text: He unpins a scrap from inside his cuff, holds it up to his sparks, and hands it over without a word.

narrator/8273054df79046d7.text: Near the middle, under the water, something catches a light that isn't there to be caught.

narrator/8277df5ec1504778.text: The wheel goes back on its axle with a clunk, and the little cart rights itself. Clovin looks at it, and at you, as if nobody has ever done anything for him on purpose.

narrator/82932875e41039cd.text: A big black bird with a big black beak, and opinions. Beyond that it keeps its own counsel.

narrator/829f335c16ce27d5.text: The winery smells of vinegar, lye and scrubbing. The floorboards are back down, most of them, with new nails shining in the old wood.

narrator/82a1cb5a34f7b285.text: The vaults are dark and still. The amber in the walls has stopped glowing, and you find you miss it, which is worse.

narrator/82a47774f030c1b6.text: A little later, through the window, you hear the shouting start on the shore. It goes on for a long time. Then it stops, and there is only the sound of two people sitting by a fire.

narrator/82acebe39cd8df0a.text: Mother Night. The old Barovian almanacs give her the dark half of the year and the Morninglord the light, and say the two were never on speaking terms. Farmers lock their doors on her feast nights. Wolves, it seems, open theirs.

narrator/82b758b99b26e098.text: A black wagon with silver trim, very neat, very quiet. A black horse is tethered beside it, saddled, as if for a journey at short notice.

narrator/82d355adaa0a93e4.text: Cold, still water; a half-drowned stone causeway out to the island; a round tower with one lit window and no handle on its door. On the shore, a painted wagon and a campfire.

narrator/82e83b660b3781a6.text: He hammers on the gate and calls a name. After a while the wicket opens and a broad, grey-bearded man in a sheepskin steps out, the way a man steps out into hail.

narrator/82e8d14185697515.text: In the great cave behind you, somebody laughs: a big, delighted laugh that turns into a howl halfway through.

narrator/82f4767a182f657b.text: A rocking chair worn smooth on the arms, with a cushion embroidered MY BOY in red thread. It rocks a little when nobody is near it.

narrator/830c8623a6665069.text: Someone keeps the silver earring back from the grave. His people will want it.

narrator/83173e3e96d5e7f7.text: Vosk's shape slips like a badly hung coat. Under it: a jackal's head, a scholar's robe, and claws that shake.

narrator/8324d6f888810830.text: She lies down on the altar step and smooths her dress and closes her eyes, and does not open them again.

narrator/833965941616ba52.text: Tall, close-set houses with their shutters open exactly the width the law requires. Behind one of them, a child is practising a festival song, and keeps stopping at the same note.

narrator/834b528278953577.text: The path is worn deep by many feet, all going one way and coming back again. People come to the falls to leave things.

narrator/8350814565b55f7b.text: A new ribbon hangs on the ribbon tree, knotted around a lock of black hair. It is the brightest red on the tree.

narrator/837355a2ef2b3a82.text: You bend to read the lid, and feel the eye on the back of your neck the whole time. You read nothing. You straighten up quickly.

narrator/837c09c60db43d4a.text: It's heavier than clay ought to be, and colder. Something inside shifts when you tilt it, like a stone having second thoughts.

narrator/838a56963779cc57.text: Little bags of greasy leather hang from hooks in the beam, each tied with a hair ribbon. When the chair stops rocking for a moment, you could swear you hear them whispering.

narrator/8392a02ddddc3b45.text: Cold, and the right kind of cold: the cellar air holds the smell of oak and a hundred years of wine. Somewhere at the far end, something is digging.

narrator/91685aec1255689b.text: The antechamber stinks of the heap. It is coming.

narrator/9206bb19b0e7cfda.text: His hand is flat on the table, pressing, as if the table might get up and leave.

narrator/92283de0f2c7f06f.text: The lane runs straight up between the rows. On both sides the dead vines rustle, though the air is perfectly still.

narrator/9228dcd44b941ba1.text: The dragon lies along the bier with his wings folded like a cloak, every bone in its place, except at the end of the long neck, where there is nothing at all. Frost furs the ribs and doesn't melt.

narrator/9229302cfccb3198.text: You reach in among the roots, and your fingers close on something that is not a root, not cold, and not yours.

narrator/9241d98f2a9d02f6.text: A cart with a broken axle, half in the ditch, picked clean. The harness was cut, not broken. Whoever drove it left in a hurry, and on foot.

narrator/925174a8d2b71d1a.text: A real fire, banked high, with a kettle on the hook. It's the first fire in Barovia you've seen that someone made for comfort rather than defence.

narrator/925cbfd386c314ea.text: A crowded little shop: puppets, dolls, music boxes and wind-up creatures on every shelf, every one of them looking at the door. A curtained doorway leads back to the workshop.

narrator/9279970ec80c4ec6.text: The parapet is old work, every stone fitted dry. Long scratches run across its top, in fours, as if something very large once landed here to see what it had caught.

narrator/92a66c41bd97e4d8.text: The last entry is a single name, Walter. Where the others say given, it says first.

narrator/92a69da30b28cb1e.text: It wants the dragon's fire, and you aren't carrying it. That waits in the mausoleum, in the frost on his bones.

narrator/92b7d587c671ec62.text: A net hung from a hook, sagging with meat gone green. Venison, you hope.

narrator/92b7fb73b3a21349.text: Steps cut into the ice by hands that have been dead for centuries, worn into shallow bowls by the feet of everyone who climbed up after them.

narrator/92dd25ac3a2f2b76.text: Below, the woods and the far grey lake, and here and there a farmhouse with no light in it. Every one of them could see this tower once.

narrator/92fc1b4234b6a201.text: The east wing is a ring of sarcophagi, each one a block of amber taller than a man, and each one has something in it. Something in all six of them is talking, softly, at once.

narrator/930e6f163a0fe505.text: The fermenting hall: eight great vats in two rows under the beams. The vats are full, and what's in them is breathing.

narrator/932e21e05f354b34.text: A stag's head over the hearth, antlers dusted, glass eyes fixed on the door. The only thing in the den that isn't a wolf.

narrator/9343fcc9cafbca42.text: A trough frozen solid, with a goat's beard frozen into the top of it. The goat seems to have got away. Mostly.

narrator/93629bf095a18d00.text: You speak the old words for the dead, the ones every faith in the valley shares: rest, and be remembered, and let the living go.

narrator/9366fe20d895b162.text: The letter is read aloud in the middle of the square, every courteous word of it, down to the single initial at the bottom. When it's finished, nobody is looking at Lady Wachter. Everyone is looking at the castle on its cliff, and then at her.

narrator/936e42e03f2f26b3.text: She takes a child by each hand and goes down the stair with them, slowly, talking about soup the whole way.

narrator/939e7b21cce82a91.text: A long cell with rusty shackles on every wall and stiff black robes on hooks between them. One prisoner never left: a skeleton in a tattered robe, a gold ring still on its finger.

narrator/93b3112ef9943ed0.text: The trail is worn smooth and wide, the way paths get when a great many feet use them. Some of the prints in the mud are boots. Most of them aren't.

narrator/93ecb402759a1ecb.text: Lucian bars the doors and lights every candle he owns. You take your places in the nave. For hours there is nothing but the wax burning down and the priest's voice saying the long prayers under his breath.

narrator/93f1de9474d531e4.text: She stands between you and the cave mouth, but her eyes keep sliding past you, down the slope, west toward the Krezk road. She is listening for something coming home, and dreading it.

narrator/940e1ccbd37ed5be.text: The family in the portrait over the hearth keeps its eyes on the stairs. On you, specifically.

narrator/9413ad6a41c2e6cc.text: Morgantha unhooks a ring of iron keys from her apron and opens both cages, humming. The children don't move until she has sat back down.

narrator/942252e9e57760e4.text: Soot is creeping out of the hearths along the floor, black and low, pooling in the middle of the hall.

narrator/942396b68326dcda.text: Her face gives you nothing but its scars. Whatever she feels about the castle, she has had a long time to bury it.

narrator/94391e3c18c9f21b.text: A milestone with the village's name chiselled off and a single word scratched in its place: TURN BACK. Under it, in a different hand: WHERE TO?

narrator/94a60997f029ef39.text: The vines rise up off their trellises on both sides of the lane, and the vineyard comes for you row by row.

narrator/94dbeda1b872353f.text: The inside of the wagon is a hunter's armoury squeezed into a Vistani caravan: stakes, mirrors, bundles of herbs, and a neat little bed nobody seems to sleep in.

narrator/94e3448106486fc1.text: The boy is gone between one breath and the next. What drops from the ceiling is only hunger.

narrator/94fa6b038d49763d.text: Two leaning posts mark where the village ends and the road west begins. Stop at them before you go.

narrator/95168178cc42dbd0.text: The amber drinks. You feel it, a tug at the wrist like a child pulling your hand, and then the doors are open and your hand is white and cold. In the alcove beside them, something tall wakes up hungry.

narrator/951bd03ac4e660af.text: The stove is cold and the pot on it is full of soup that set days ago. Two bowls wait beside it.

narrator/9536f25c4b02639a.text: Two small punctures at her throat, under the collar, as neat as a seamstress's work. She did not die of age. She died of visits.

narrator/95401eea8a2934dd.text: The oven roars as if somebody had thrown open its door.

narrator/955f9681150e8cd3.text: You look up into the blank face, and for one long moment it looks back with every face you have ever feared.

narrator/956c33de204eae46.text: Blades, mail shirts, rope, lamp oil and grain sacks, each with a price chalked on a slate in a hand that has clearly done this for years and has stopped apologising.

narrator/9572399fb89dde74.text: The heap in the corner is a crater now, a wet hollow the shape of something very large that has gotten up.

narrator/957a49bd2bc5c5f1.text: A drum of black chain as tall as a man, a crank as long as a spear, and a ratchet that has been oiled by nobody for a very long time.

narrator/95817c4706e0ca3d.text: The jaw in the amber has stopped chewing. It is listening, hungrily, to whoever carries its gift.

narrator/959ad729801b1f84.text: The family's floor is silent. Even the cold has gone out of it.

narrator/95af419bc03771a9.text: Hooves on the road behind you, a great many of them, coming fast. You get off the track just in time.

narrator/95bda2ca79555b1a.text: The last window in the house that isn't brick, and it is closing.

narrator/95ea40288ba2355f.text: You drag your boots through the chalk. The glow sputters along the lines and goes out, like a fuse that has been stamped on.

narrator/95f4c5fd24d3f425.text: She steps back from the edge, one pace and then another, and lets out a breath she seems to have been holding for a very long time.

narrator/95f97887093def77.text: Lady Wachter sits in the Baron's great hall, in the Baron's chair, with her own tea service on his table. The festival portraits are stacked face to the wall.

narrator/9613c7b95e857e44.text: Tin birds turn on their threads above the crib, though there isn't a breath of draft.

narrator/961b1071f4ff45cd.text: The hut is down, its roots twitching. The old woman lies at the foot of the stump in its shadow, breathing in little sips.

narrator/963f9e3bd8b323e9.text: He's kind to her. Kind to everyone. If there's anything else in it, it's buried too deep for you to see.

narrator/9648fde0c6190f0e.text: The silver earring is still there, a little horse's head. You work it free.

narrator/9649aa2eb8f9139b.text: The shades will not let you leave so easily.

narrator/9660d0a5d6fefbd3.text: Berez is quiet now in a way it wasn't before. The frogs have the marsh to themselves, and on the stump in the east nothing breathes at all.

narrator/968d1f34a121e270.text: He believes every word. As for the fish: a shoal like this comes in when the water turns cold all at once. It could be the season. It could be anything. The lake isn't telling.

narrator/96ba85b50764fa03.text: The hut is warmer. Somebody has lit the hearth for the first time, badly, with far too much magic, and the books on the shelves have writing in them now.

narrator/96c402e6ed29787c.text: The attic is lit by candles and by the chalk circle on the floor, which glows faintly on its own. A thin boy of sixteen or so looks up from a book far too big for him, and is instantly furious.

narrator/96c521c45f31c00d.text: A low round table, a deck of cards, a chair, and an old woman who looks as if she has been sitting in it since before the tent was put up around her.

narrator/96cf224d7c6fc9af.text: Under the thyme, faint and bitter: almonds. Ireena sets her spoon down without a sound.

narrator/971ac669689f218a.text: The colossus steps down off its plinth, and the ledge shakes. High on the facade, two stone shapes unfold their wings.

narrator/9757041a199c904e.text: The sacristy: vestments on pegs, a chest, the smell of old incense. One white surplice hangs apart from the others, freshly pressed, as if for an occasion.

narrator/975fe49f3ea7b9a3.text: A fire in an iron basket, fed with something that burns green at the edges. The smoke goes straight up into the dark and doesn't drift, as if it were being drawn.

narrator/979b415f357cc2b3.text: The cart has a new wheel and a load of casks lashed under canvas, ready to roll. Someone has tied a black feather to the shaft for luck.

narrator/97d367df78b76925.text: A reading room of lecterns, each with a book left open on it, as if the readers had stepped out for a moment three centuries ago.

narrator/97e71da9fe183bec.text: He lowers the bow. In the trees, the other bows lower too, one by one.

narrator/97eaf31d449e5c1e.text: The top of the tower: windows on every side and a strongbox under the sill. The floor is studded with copper nails in a careful spiral, and the air tastes of a storm that hasn't arrived yet.

narrator/97f9191b37a8f320.text: Straw pallets on the floor, black robes on pegs, a duty roster scratched into the wall. The cult's newest members slept here, close to the stairs.

narrator/97fd8b8b31c35e20.text: The nursery door opens on the smell of milk and lavender, both long gone sour.

narrator/984c50b277276d4f.text: The niche is empty except for a stub of white candle and a few grains of incense, gone to dust. Someone used to pray back here, out of sight, where only the sun could see them.

narrator/9856077ec4edac45.text: Skeletons hang in rusty shackles along the wall, wrists over their heads. Behind each one, the soot on the stone is the shape of a person.

narrator/9856375c86a692ae.text: For a moment the scaled hand flexes, and you hear the claws click. Then he looks at your weapons, and at the crowd watching, and steps back one pace.

narrator/985a8d7ab1ea6131.text: A roof beam swings down like a door slammed in your face.

narrator/9867ea8ce900259d.text: A single potion in a locked glass case, red as a cherry and dusty as a tomb. The tag reads 500 GOLD, and the tag is dusty too.

narrator/986b3d47019a2fb6.text: A stair spirals up inside thick walls, its steps worn into hollows by boots. At the top, a round platform open to the sky behind a low parapet, and in its middle, on a stone plinth, a great iron cradle full of old ash.

narrator/98a57ec3d6368d77.text: Anna lifts out a dress of heavy cream wool and old lace, folded in lavender. It has been mended in two places by a careful hand, and never worn since.

narrator/98b1107cb63da882.text: A painted toy chest at the foot of a little bed, its lid shut.

narrator/98b4e74c9b79cebf.text: The bone-strewn passage. The bones stay down now.

narrator/98df82dc9d919acd.text: Maps, notes and books cover every surface, weighted down with candle stubs and skulls. Small skulls. Not human. Mostly.

narrator/98f6e58e8546c649.text: The knights sit along the table with their heads bowed, quite still. It looks less like death than like the end of a long grace before a meal.

narrator/99213082ebfd4aac.text: Pews for a hundred, polished smooth by generations. Only the front one is worn recently, in one spot, by one pair of knees.

narrator/993fd4f06fcab798.text: The stairs deliver you into a house that has stopped pretending, its walls sweating. The front of the house is very, very quiet.

narrator/994a9e6bd0514151.text: The bakery is warm and quiet except for the snoring. Offalia lies where she sat down, smiling at the rafters.

narrator/994adb662475f597.text: The undercroft is empty. On the ceiling, the scratches lead to the stair and up it, and stop.

narrator/99769fedea5b9270.text: Sir Godfrey has gone very still beside you, his face turned up to the light like a man in the first sun after a long winter.

narrator/997700b28b21798a.text: A spark, a puff of colored light, a floating flour-dust star. Parriwimple watches it with his whole face.

narrator/99a08ee7bd79e34e.text: Red hair. An M. A thorn through the heart, and the cloth worn soft from being handled, the way a rosary goes soft. You don't need to read witch-knots to read that.

narrator/99b6bb70a36e8291.text: A carved warning, repeated in nine scripts and a set of pictures for those who couldn't read: a hand reaching toward a box, and the same hand without its fingers.

narrator/99bd57f355c5700a.text: A narrow entrance hall: a coat stand, an umbrella with nothing to keep off, and an archway into a grand hall beyond.

narrator/99c0fdacb297190e.text: Vosk's nose lifts, very slightly, like a dog's at a kitchen door.

narrator/99c22d11253e3fbc.text: A cramped room with an iron winch and a chain that runs up into the wall.

narrator/99d34c03c0e5cf54.text: The mist thickens at the gate, and he is gone.

narrator/9a78c8cc4385f775.text: Parriwimple writes it down very slowly, so you can watch him do it.

narrator/9a7de53d0a365854.text: The hidden stair: up, and up, and out. The steps are slick, as if the house is sweating.

narrator/9ad5e0b2630ae51e.text: Izek's eyes stop on Ireena and stay there, through the whole of the cheer and after it.

narrator/9ad747c4e18220e4.text: A book of poems with the pages turned down at the funny ones, and a few coins wrapped in a handkerchief embroidered with a goose.

narrator/9ae6e1d26fd4def9.text: The wardens' fire has burned down to coals. The cages creak on their poles in a wind you can't feel.

narrator/9af15dcc7c0f7d79.text: A farm cart lies on its side in the ditch, one wheel still turning slowly in the wind. No horse. No driver. In the bed of the cart, a child's coat, and a long smear leading up the slope into the trees.

narrator/9b038c3dd4c736de.text: He listens. He doesn't want to, but he listens, and somewhere in the middle of it he sits down on the planks and starts taking the stones out of his pockets, one at a time, and dropping them in the water.

narrator/9b04441ede8310e0.text: The hut leans with her. Every jar on the shelf is humming the same note.

narrator/9b08e6e4a4a59d25.text: On the only dry ground in Berez stands a young woman in white stone, her hands folded, her face turned toward the castle. Someone has scrubbed the moss from her. At her feet lie fresh black roses, and an iron grave-lamp, unlit.

narrator/9b1c67ebf3f7f6df.text: The road south climbs between dead pines toward the castle. It is the best-kept road in the valley. Somebody wants it used.

narrator/9b1cde0a1aed5616.text: You are through the antechamber before the thing in the heap has finished standing up. Behind you it says its own name in a voice like a drain: Lorghoth, Lorghoth.

narrator/9b5db8b47fdb7264.text: Polished floors, good candles, and the hush of a house where servants are trained not to hear things.

narrator/9b78326e627c2b2d.text: You sit. He mends. The camp's fire burns down and is built up again, and nobody says anything for a long while, which seems to be the point.

narrator/9b8569b31a9263c6.text: The dig is abandoned now: holes, spoil heaps, a lantern guttering on a stone, and nothing at all found.

narrator/9b9d970459781fba.text: A man and a woman sit at a laid supper table by the light of one candle, their fine clothes hanging off them. Their fingers are long and grey, and the plates in front of them are not empty.

narrator/9b9fa586dc42a4e4.text: A stone dragon's head lies in the dry basin of the fountain, its body somewhere else. Someone has set it upright, carefully, facing the house.

narrator/9baf93e578c05a64.text: The fiddle is playing something fast tonight, and somebody is dancing to it: a small girl with black hair, solemn as a judge, on her father's feet.

narrator/9bd655dba609971e.text: The south row backs onto the wall, and beyond the wall there's nothing: the shelf of the mountain ends in a drop into cloud. Children here learn very young not to climb.

narrator/9bdfd518cc8cfc27.text: At the water's edge the air is warmer, very slightly, the way a room is warmer when someone's just left it.

narrator/9bf0c3f02d6af811.text: A narrow camp cot with the blanket folded square and tucked tight. Under the pillow, a stake. Under the stake, a little bag of lavender.

narrator/9c2c51b4c6f7cfce.text: Rows of empty pews face an altar under a grey sunburst. The floor is cold enough to feel through your boots, and it isn't only cold that comes up through it.

narrator/9c34c071fcfa0cbb.text: A map of the whole valley painted on the tabletop, villages and roads and farms, and from the tower on its ridge thin lines of silver paint run out to every one of them.

narrator/9c547f461d14c2d9.text: She comes up out of the mud with her nails out, shrieking, and the reeds shriek with her.

narrator/9c636afb1a05ca06.text: The fiddle goes down on the log beside him, very carefully, as if it might break.

narrator/9c7f4214af06c090.text: A raven carved over the door, wings half open, done with real skill. Its eye is a polished black stone that catches the firelight from wherever you stand.

narrator/9c9e632a30dd36e5.text: That night the Martikovs broach a cask from before the druids came, and the whole family drinks in the yard under a sky with no stars in it, and for an hour nobody looks up.

narrator/9ccf654158766883.text: The captain's room: a narrow bed, a desk with the watch log on it, and an iron strongbox chained to the wall.

narrator/9cd9d75e1454a312.text: His hand closes over the earring and stays closed.

narrator/9d0b8d277e43cbe9.text: Black water is rising in the well, and something in it is singing along with the chant.

narrator/9d1e877777b35a0e.text: He strikes the table once with a gauntlet. All down its length, dead heads lift and turn toward you, slowly, like flowers that have forgotten the sun.

narrator/9d1fd8897f6da650.text: The bell rings. The pencil stops.

narrator/9d2e8e2d8375725c.text: Whoever carries a gift still feels it, warm under the skin. The seal keeps the vestiges in. It can't take back what they have already given.

narrator/9d6f2183c2d45667.text: A burned entry hall with a cracked stair going up on one side and, in the middle, the stump of a statue that used to be something rearing up.

narrator/9d80f88cd0ae7df8.text: The roof has fallen in, and a young pine is growing up through the floor. The lake path's wildlife has moved in and doesn't care for visitors.

narrator/9d82078968920980.text: The colossus stands with its head bowed and its eyes dim, a guard who has been told to stand easy and has decided to believe it.

narrator/9da698f3f30c1d46.text: Deeds and titles tied with string: this house, a vineyard plot long since sold, and a windmill on the Old Svalich Road, its sails sketched in the margin by a bored clerk.

narrator/9de1281467aee2cc.text: A great round window of yellow glass, grey with soot, that would fill the nave with light if there were ever any light to fill it with.

narrator/9de68e0bfb8891ef.text: Strings of onions, strings of mushrooms, strings of things that aren't either. Jars on every shelf, and some of the jars are humming.

narrator/9e0d8ea63b03d907.text: The tavern is as you left it. The hearth table is empty without Ismark at it; the wine is no better without him.

narrator/9e46aa40305b2416.text: Every time the floor creaks, his eyes go to the storeroom door. There are fresh scratches on the inside of the frame, at about the height of a hand. Something has been coming and going through that door at night, and Henrik has been letting it.

narrator/9e4a4a080c6c33c4.text: Inside the gate, a stooped figure in a cast-off monk's habit is sweeping snow into a heap with no particular plan. One of his ears is a hound's. One of his hands is mostly feathers. He looks up and sighs.

narrator/9e4bb56bd67f0f7a.text: The scarecrows in the reeds turn their sacking heads all at once, and climb down off their poles.

narrator/9e61d4e8c143ee80.text: The Baron's sergeants shove into the crowd with clubs. The rest of the watch looks at the priest, and stays where it is.

narrator/9e8458d547ef76bf.text: Bella's laugh comes out of a mouth that is suddenly far too wide. The rocking chair goes over.

narrator/9eb0122d430340de.text: The air is thin enough to make the head swim. Below, the whole valley lies under its lid of cloud.

narrator/9edc6c36bf429324.text: "Bracken. A root through my leg. Adrian wouldn't go, so I gave him the order in Father's voice. Tell Father it was mine. Tell him I was good at it."

narrator/9f197bdf8e1e27b8.text: "Terms, as the Thirst set them: one life he loves, given by his own hand on the day he most wants to be happy."

narrator/9f36d5ba2f2d23d4.text: He never got a surname. He never got a birthday either.

narrator/9f45366fca31c6f2.text: A thread of black runs through the green, fine as a hair: the same black as the tree's bark.

narrator/9f53081aa0519e16.text: Wooden soldiers with hollow eyes. Rag dolls with button smiles. A carved wolf that, when you press its back, opens its mouth and keeps it open.

narrator/9f649d03b26f79c7.text: The wax comes away. Something silver pours up out of the jar like smoke going the wrong way, hangs in the cold air between you, and then goes into him through the eyes.

narrator/9f68fb7fcd23159f.text: A small woman sits in a nest of yellow cloth, sewing so fast the needle blurs. She leaps up when she sees you and drops three bobbins and a thimble.

narrator/9fa089599047e4ad.text: A wolf-pelt rug with the head still on, its glass eyes watching the door instead of you. Small mercies.

narrator/9fa9c186d12a4c48.text: A bronze plaque, green with age: FOR MARKOVIA, WHO WENT UP THE ROAD, AND THE TWELVE WHO WENT WITH HER. Someone has scratched a thirteenth line under it and then scratched it out.

narrator/9fda34b2da05b878.text: The tree stands over the broken effigy as if nothing happened. Its roots have moved since the fight. You're nearly sure of that.

narrator/a005ed8a0c7e3a0e.text: The sealed letter goes down on the table between the cups. Ismark looks at the ornate S, and the colour leaves his face.

narrator/a01319cd62e4b2d8.text: The house on the ridge is black against a blacker sky, and in the courtyard something grey moves in ranks, back and forth, the way a tide does.

narrator/a0206ddb1d5153aa.text: The mountain is still cold, but it's an honest cold now, and the storm over the summit has gone.

narrator/a06fff0614e84485.text: Whole rows of floorboards levered up and thrown aside, the joists scraped, the earth beneath dug into. Somebody wanted something under this floor very badly, and didn't find it.

narrator/a0710646fc6cb982.text: Cairn to cairn, roped hand to hand, you find the path. When the snow lifts, you are further on than you'd have dared to hope.

narrator/a079e929fe4db446.text: At the end of the old surgery, on a long table under a clean linen sheet, lies a young woman. The sheet is turned down to her collarbone, neatly, the way you'd tuck in a child.

narrator/a08e6c0a8149c2c1.text: The cave mouth is dark and nothing breathes out of it. Crows have found the bone heap, and nobody is chasing them off.

narrator/a092529175d9ec96.text: A narrow stair winds down into the dark under the altar. The steps are worn into hollows by two centuries of priests going down to pray.

narrator/a099a0904b5ad80b.text: Black water to the brim, still as glass. Your reflection in it moves a moment after you do.

narrator/a0ad233401a28cbd.text: The Old Svalich Road runs past the camp under the pines. A track turns off it toward the firelight and the music.

narrator/a0cefa36ee57800e.text: Nine dry steps down into a vault of white stone. Tall candles burn at the head of a bier without burning down. The marsh is all around this room, and not a drop has got in.

narrator/a0d99cdc68f005da.text: Steel clears leather. The black horse doesn't flinch. Your blow passes through the place where he was and closes on cold fog that smells of old roses.

narrator/a0de3df9afff8d87.text: He gives you nothing but a tired man's face. It is a very good tired man's face; he has had practice.

narrator/a0ec6514fde5a504.text: Lady Lydia sits in a pew with a half-sewn sash across her knees. She hasn't put a stitch in it for hours, and she doesn't look up when you come near.

narrator/a322bdce9db7e651.text: Behind you, below, something vast is dragging itself up the steps. Do not wait to see how fast.

narrator/a33474a147c48a8b.text: Behind the heavy coats, on a peg of its own, hangs a hooded lantern with oil still in it. Someone meant to take it with them.

narrator/a335ef4d85ce9646.text: An empty hut, its hearth cold for a year. A child's chalk drawing of a big fish is still on the wall, smiling.

narrator/a3368b345fa2898c.text: The passage is narrower than it was. You are certain of it.

narrator/a347d676b192510f.text: A long gallery of sarcophagi, ten of them, all talking. Not to each other. To you.

narrator/a38ee57cc8a0ec30.text: The chancel, two steps up. The altar is spotless. So is the floor around it, scrubbed pale, the way you'd scrub a floor after something that needed scrubbing.

narrator/a39644a3966c9aba.text: Lamp oil, kindling, and a mill that has dried in its own oven's heat for longer than anyone in the valley remembers. It would go up like paper.

narrator/a3b0c0dae566c283.text: The words are still there. They'll be there a long while.

narrator/a3ff48aadaed5df1.text: Nikolai and Karl Wachter draw at their mother's side, and all through the crowd men who were cheering a moment ago are drawing too.

narrator/a40e834b14841cf5.text: The statue's hand is empty now.

narrator/a425b810b487a5d8.text: An empty plinth at the centre of the gallery. The plate on it says only OUR LORD, and the dust on top is undisturbed in the shape of nothing at all.

narrator/a4269410aff5531b.text: A side chamber off the great cave, cold after the fire. Something in the dark rattles softly: a chain, moving because someone at the end of it has looked up.

narrator/a43456d98b5aefcf.text: She lies on a bier of white stone under a veil of lace, a girl of perhaps nineteen, with red hair braided over one shoulder. She looks asleep. She has looked asleep for a very long time. There is no smell at all.

narrator/a467cb87e37ab8f3.text: Dire wolves come down the shore at a lope, heads low, spreading out to cut you off from the water.

narrator/a4715154d0b1871b.text: A large woman in a floury apron sits in the ditch with her legs stuck out, stripping a bramble of its berries with both hands and crying with her mouth full.

narrator/a47f91036168f247.text: The jewel box plays three notes of a lullaby and stops. Inside lie three gold rings and a thin platinum necklace with a topaz as big as a thumbnail. The music box is broken, and both facts feel important.

narrator/a48c925551e8c26c.text: A long passage ankle-deep in black water. Things float in it that you decide not to look at closely.

narrator/a499ee1fb8688ded.text: The coffin inside is empty and its lining eaten to lace. Nothing ticks now.

narrator/a4aba09026150b73.text: On the gallows the hanged man lifts his head. Behind him, all across the field, the mounds begin to split.

narrator/a4c79f0641fc240d.text: Pine shavings, varnish and fear, in that order. Coffins stand on trestles all through the workshop, and most of them are small.

narrator/a4d098932106d175.text: Feathers come down out of the cloud for a long time afterwards.

narrator/a53f9fca9ed58472.text: A painted wooden statue of a gaunt, pale man in a black cloak, one hand resting on the head of a wolf at his side. The other holds out an orb of smoky crystal, as if offering it to whoever kneels here.

narrator/a541fc105a3c08c8.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Dahlver-Nar, the mouth of borrowed teeth. It cannot make anything. It only keeps."

narrator/a55f728ef170a759.text: A pair of small white slippers set side by side at the foot of the table, with the toes turned toward the door.

narrator/a592ce2781b64b67.text: Vasilka comes down off the bier like a dancer finishing a bow, and the Belviews come after her with cleavers and pruning hooks, humming.

narrator/a59b4535a89b1442.text: The path above the Tsolenka Pass climbs in switchbacks along a shelf of rock and snow, with the mountain on one side and nothing at all on the other.

narrator/a5a14eb5a11cf6e0.text: Three ogres sit on the road ahead around a dead goat, arguing about who caught it. They stop arguing when they see you.

narrator/a5a23aa9e1f653d3.text: The young face on the ceiling looks at the holy water in your hands, then at the open door above, and understands.

narrator/a5a9472eb523f231.text: Neither of them says anything for a while. Then she hits him on the arm, hard, and he lets her.

narrator/a5c395903639c228.text: The crowd cheers on cue. The watch walks among them, listening for anyone cheering too quietly.

narrator/a5cd8d5ab78d83c6.text: Zuleika comes out of the dark at a run, and stops just short of Emil, and then doesn't.

narrator/a5f4a87c36008945.text: He looks at you, and then at nothing, for a very long time. The scaled hand opens and closes. When he speaks again his voice has gone quiet, the way a struck bell goes quiet.

narrator/a5f976eb26f730a9.text: From inside, the front door is a mess of patches, braces and bent nails. Every repair has a later repair over it.

narrator/a604342876968fd8.text: He's counting your throats. Every plea comes with a glance at the stair behind you, measuring the distance.

narrator/a60ac6ce53a58bb9.text: A broad, grey-bearded man sits at the long table with a ledger he isn't reading. He stands when you come in, because a burgomaster stands.

narrator/a60e376841824567.text: Warm, floury and close. Everything is dusted white: the tables, the sacks, the floor, the great millstone in the middle. The oven on the far wall breathes like something asleep.

narrator/a62f64a2f2d354aa.text: Burial niches along the wall, most of them sealed. Three have been opened from the inside.

narrator/a63a6d19941fc887.text: A brazier of coals where the watch warms its hands. Somebody has written CHEER UP on the wall above it in charcoal, and somebody else has drawn a face beside it that isn't cheering.

narrator/a67bed8abaddb497.text: The door from the road opens into a vestibule and the guardroom. The gatehouse with its winch is to the west, the barracks in the middle, the captain's room to the east behind its own door.

narrator/a68696529f51e7ec.text: The old notice still hangs by the gate, its warning addressed to nobody. Behind it, the portcullis stands up in its slot, and the road goes on into the cloud.

narrator/a69cea8a6219463f.text: Nobody comes down the stair all night. You can hear her up there, rocking, and once, very softly, laughing.

narrator/a69f331b6751fad0.text: A handcart tipped over in the lane, one wheel missing, its load gone. A child's shoe lies in the mud beside it; the other is nowhere.

narrator/a6a073b658761659.text: The gates swing open before anyone touches them, slow and silent on hinges that should be screaming with rust.

narrator/a6b9cfbf5bd53a71.text: White, cold and patient. The road you came in on is somewhere inside it, and the mist would rather you didn't go looking.

narrator/a6c198278dfa76b0.text: The stair ends in rock, cold and sweating. Somewhere ahead and below, many voices are saying the same thing, over and over.

narrator/a7050c4a9847f9b4.text: The hill rises out of the moor with almost nothing growing on it, as if the grass knew better. Low mounds ring its foot, old graves with no stones. Smoke rises from a camp on its shoulder, and from the crown comes a sound like many people humming one long note.

narrator/a7231e93c9650a72.text: One great lidless eye fills the amber, its pupil as wide as a cartwheel. It isn't looking at you. It's looking at something just behind you, and it has been for a very long time.

narrator/a72c335f07d4cc1e.text: A walled garden under frost: raised beds of black stalks, a tool shed, a few small graves in the corner. Along the north wall, a row of scarecrows hangs on poles, their sacking faces all turned toward the gate you came in by.

narrator/a77001a5e5501f76.text: It is quick, and it is quiet, and afterward none of you can remember who held the knife.

narrator/a77715e47dab38b0.text: You sleep in the lee of the crag. The ravens keep watch in the oak above you, and twice in the night they all shout at once, at something you never see.

narrator/a79ff67a4660527d.text: Up close the vines aren't dead, quite. They're waiting, like a man holding his breath under water. The grapes on them are small, hard and sour.

narrator/a7a5642fd85bfeb9.text: Webs as fine as breath cover the lid. Under them the letters are there, but the webs move when you try to read.

narrator/a7e881d3f4740d20.text: Exethanter's sparks drop to whoever among you carries a gift, as if he could smell it on them.

narrator/a8153a9dec2f54a6.text: Gauzy drapes, upholstered chairs, stained glass of singers along one wall, little alabaster dancers on the mantel, and a harpsichord with its lid raised, as if someone has just stood up from it.

narrator/a81de9e1e60328a2.text: She tucks the arm inside her coat and turns her shoulder to you, and that's the end of that.

narrator/a84e2f28d989f1ff.text: It is very quiet, and very cold, and the books smell of ice instead of dust.

narrator/a85304beade3e5bc.text: The lock gives. Inside, coin and a scroll, packed square, and nothing personal at all. Not one letter, not one keepsake.

narrator/a85911f4b637a339.text: A chalk board of what each regular owes the house. Most columns are short, but one, headed ISMARK, runs to the bottom of the board and carries on along the wall.

narrator/a8a19ce07cdd9539.text: The workshop smells of pine and varnish and nothing else. Henrik is whistling. Badly, but whistling.

narrator/a8c7ea721afb9f74.text: A fresh grave beside a headstone that reads only "Beloved". The earth is piled neatly, ready to go back in.

narrator/a8f6d782be051802.text: They step aside, one to each verge, and let you pass. When you look back, the road is empty.

narrator/a8fd7f994c1971d4.text: You dream of sails turning in fire, and wake with the smell of smoke in your hair.

narrator/a90c8de33d58e02b.text: A music box with a dancer who turns, and turns, and slowly comes to face you, though the tune has stopped.

narrator/a92a8a15bd07f1b5.text: You sleep in shifts on the hillside. All night the mill's one window glows, and the smell of baking drifts down the slope.

narrator/a93af930d5c09134.text: Stone stairs wind up inside the wall. Every room is tidy in the way of a man who expects to leave in a hurry.

narrator/a94b7e83bdeb00f8.text: Dead knights stand at the broken gate now, faces turned toward the castle. They step aside for you without a word, the way sentries step aside for officers.

narrator/a9782313c984794a.text: A dragonchess board, three tiers of it, with a game in progress. Every piece on every side is carved from black stone.

narrator/a979bc1ccdf375f0.text: A scratch that never heals, over the heart, and no hand laid on her: that is the mark a doll leaves when a thorn goes through it. Somebody in this marsh knows how to make that kind of doll, and lives on a stump.

narrator/a98c5a96632681a5.text: Purple hooded flowers, planted in rows and weeded. Wolfsbane, a whole garden of it, at a werewolf's front door. Either somebody here has a sense of humour, or a plan.

narrator/a9e5a5ebe0e2819e.text: The guardroom, empty. The table still has dice on it, mid-game.

narrator/a9f888d546aa5ca6.text: The attic stair shudders under you like a ladder someone is trying to shake loose.

narrator/aa22710562bf9a49.text: Blades slide out of the paneling like teeth, and the house bites.

narrator/aadb25fdfd2e5c67.text: A lovely figure lies curled in the clear amber as if asleep in a warm bed, one hand cupped as though holding out something sweet. When you look closer, the smile has a few too many teeth.

narrator/ab02b3d8cdec156f.text: A dead oak leans out over the slope, and every branch of it is full of ravens. None of them make a sound. All of them are watching you.

narrator/ab2add4f7578ce34.text: A neat black wagon with silver trim and a small locked strongbox under the step. The window has a black curtain drawn tight.

narrator/abacefb8e7600d2f.text: Over the dress, his eyes go to Ireena, and stay there a heartbeat too long.

narrator/abae572e46c13e1d.text: A doorway with no house left behind it, and a horseshoe still nailed over it, points up for luck. It held, in its way: the doorway is the only part standing.

narrator/abe20f80174ac322.text: The pews are fuller than they were. People have started coming to church in Vallaki, now that it's the only place nobody bows to the castle.

narrator/ac6d98a537a75830.text: Yellow bunting by the furlong, every pennant hemmed by hand. On the back of one, very small, someone has embroidered: please.

narrator/acc2b143f344b02f.text: An armor stand with nothing on it, its pegs bent, as if something stepped off in a hurry.

narrator/acce8e1b2625f1de.text: At the bottom is a room with a tiny stone table, and beside it a lump of grey clay, shaped like a sleeping heap.

narrator/ad2c7f55dee4a8a6.text: The snow near the edge has the wrong sheen: an overhang, not ground. Your boot finds the difference before your weight does.

narrator/ad70b650d8480d1f.text: The vats boil over, and what climbs out of the mash has opinions about guests.

narrator/adc0252296a59ae0.text: Under the weeping she is perfectly clear-headed. She isn't mad; she's guilty, and grief is the only thing loud enough to drown it out.

narrator/adc1edc2ef341e00.text: You sleep in turns on the dry end of the causeway. All night, out on the stump, a hut shifts its weight from root to root, and something hums a lullaby.

narrator/adead48561fb07ee.text: The footlocker opens on someone else's luggage: a mail shirt, a lantern, a coffer of red potions, a yellow-bound spellbook, a folded cloak. The cult kept whatever its guests brought.

narrator/adf6085845f1b3db.text: At the head, in a chair carved with a dragon's folded wings, sits the only one who turns his head.

narrator/ae2e0fd87b6a3337.text: A long table runs the length of the hall under banners rotted to lace, and at it sit armoured figures, both sides, all the way down. Every one of them is facing the head of the table.

narrator/ae30e568b70f1320.text: The door gives with a dry crack, low down by the hinge. Lavender dust comes out to meet you.

narrator/ae632bad47124012.text: Morgantha's keys hang on a ring at what was her apron. The cages open at the second try, and the children climb out as stiff as old men.

narrator/ae7ca459db0e6061.text: The tower holds up its light like an arm held up in a crowd: here, over here.

narrator/ae824118478904dd.text: Candlelight under the door, and the small clink of cutlery.

narrator/aed63682016ef118.text: Izek lies at the foot of the dais. The fire in his arm goes out last, ember by ember, like a lamp being turned down.

narrator/aeff53adc5561ed8.text: The split colossus wears a warden's robe and hood carved in amber. Through the crack you can see right into it: hollow, and packed with old snow. Whatever moved it once has gone.

narrator/af05b3cf4d27017f.text: A workbench covered in wooden heads waiting for faces. One of them already has a face, and it's a red-haired woman's.

narrator/af1081b722061fab.text: The grave-lamp still burns at the statue's feet, small and steady, in the middle of all that black water.

narrator/af18a1098d920952.text: The sparks in his sockets keep drifting toward the stair down to the vaults and away again, the way a man's eyes keep finding a door he has locked. Whatever he's forgotten, part of him is glad of it.

narrator/af20d2b40f86c31e.text: The light around him bends toward him the way water bends toward a drain. He is no man: something sent from far above, of the kind that stands behind the saints in old paintings. Something that has stood here far too long.

narrator/af2962cf5c46f4b3.text: A bell rings as the door opens, and somewhere a pencil starts moving. Every shelf is dusted, every label straight, every price outrageous.

narrator/af64e4553d7f082b.text: You lay the two small bundles in their two small crypts and slide the slabs home. The sound is final and, for once in this house, kind.

narrator/af6e5a7ff4f13be0.text: Crates of stock stacked to the beams, each one stenciled with its contents and its price. One is marked FOR THE BURGOMASTER, PAID, and has never been collected.

narrator/af81cef4dfe094ca.text: The tower is empty now, and just a building. Someone has left the guardroom swept.

narrator/af875bb73de59667.text: A doll in a lacy yellow dress, propped in the window box as if to watch the street. Someone small loved it, and then left it here.

narrator/afb513aec1247c9c.text: The small crate by the back wall is empty now. The altar cloth that was in it smelled faintly of incense, even down here.

narrator/afb973a97788a53d.text: Silt and reeds have buried the foot of the plinth. Something under your boots rings hollow.

narrator/afcb34a9eb01b19b.text: A row of soldiers' faces carved into the tower, each one different, each one stern. Under them, a line of letters: THEY KEPT THE ROAD.

narrator/aff308c54065a129.text: A copper tub full of something dark that has gone stiff at the edges. It isn't water. She is very old, and she does not look it.

narrator/affb294001628a4b.text: The dressing table in the corner stands empty. Morgantha glances at it once, and goes on smiling, and goes on shelling.

narrator/b02a18a913f84bc1.text: The burgomaster's diary said the candlemaker's girl died with a scratch over her heart, like a bramble's. It was never a bramble.

narrator/b038639d8d623f38.text: Green firelight leaks round the shutters, and the whole hut is humming to itself, like an old woman over washing.

narrator/b03b274a23e664c8.text: A square tower above the east wing, with an open lantern room at its top. Even from down here you can see the soot that climbs the parapet like a black tongue.

narrator/b0420b4d3071b00f.text: A rocking chair by the stove. It is perfectly still whenever you look at it.

narrator/b067995e290bc4e8.text: The chained books have titles like instructions. Some of the instructions are for things that should never be done twice.

narrator/b077625bdf9e0960.text: He takes the jar in both hands, carefully, the way you'd hold a bird. Then he looks around for somewhere to put it, opens his mouth, shuts it again, and tucks the jar inside his robe.

narrator/b0b194724a8938f2.text: The smile is real, and it's held in place with both hands. Under it she's been afraid for so long that she's stopped noticing. She is the only person in this house who isn't afraid of the Baron, and the only one who's afraid for him.

narrator/b0be5e8286790cea.text: Off the path, half buried, a ring of tents has been crushed flat by old snow. Inside, a party of climbers sits where the cold found them, still holding their cups.

narrator/b0da6694bffef77e.text: Furniture under dust sheets, an iron stove, two trunks, and in the corner a bare nook where the plaster is warm to the touch.

narrator/b1042148c608d713.text: Someone has to go in after it. The water is black and cold enough to stop a heart.

narrator/b128aa7afd5a2962.text: The desk faces the bookcase squarely, the way a guard faces a door. Now you know why.

narrator/b135afedc10e8e85.text: The prayer is long, and it costs. Warmth goes out of the caster and into the old man, and for a moment the frost on the chessboard melts and runs. Somewhere inside him, a lock that a witch closed decades ago turns over.

narrator/b1592753b8ac8920.text: A long table laid for twenty with the best plate, every chair empty. It has been laid with great care for guests who are not coming.

narrator/b194ce1214e47791.text: The way out is open, and nothing in this house will stop you leaving now. Nothing in it needs to.

narrator/b197f4777527f67b.text: The top of the tower: windows on every side, a strongbox under the sill, a spiral of copper nails in the floor, now dull and quiet.

narrator/b19e941e9cf93d88.text: A long, low hall under the roof. Somewhere along it, a child is humming.

narrator/b1b86bca15649509.text: The chandelier over the hall is swaying gently, though there is no wind at all.

narrator/b1db16a3b9121364.text: Gustav and Elisabeth in oils, younger, dressed for a ball. The dust on the canvas has settled thickest on her face.

narrator/b1e83d30d7f6b9a1.text: You speak the word. The glyphs on the floor go dark one after another, like a row of lamps blown out, and the doors swing inward without a sound.

narrator/b1edbe4142d0782e.text: The figure in the clear amber has turned over in its sleep, toward whoever carries its gift, and its smile has grown a little wider.

narrator/b1fb5a7aa4f63571.text: Torches go to the straw. You kept it dry through the night, and it shows: the wicker catches with a roar, and for a few heartbeats there is a sun in Vallaki, gold and enormous, and the faces in the square are lit with something very close to joy.

narrator/b1fda388150f7010.text: She steps sideways into nothing, cart and all, and the lane is empty. The smell of honey hangs in the air for a long while.

narrator/b2335a8e7bba459b.text: A carnival wagon in red and gold, with RICTAVIO'S WONDERS painted along the side and a padlock the size of a fist. From inside comes the slow, heavy breathing of something very large.

narrator/b2444a223b12c294.text: The mist thickens at the gate, and then he isn't there.

narrator/b250c422232fdfef.text: For a heartbeat something old and very cold looks out of her eyes. Then she laughs, a dry sound like a deck being cut.

narrator/b295c1b995b48718.text: A hut of fitted stones without a speck of mortar, raised by somebody who knew exactly how and has since forgotten. The door is shut. Something inside is talking to itself.

narrator/b2ab9555a4fab9dd.text: Grigor spits, nocks, and shouts a name. Arrows answer from three sides.

narrator/b2b2d9a3506ddde0.text: A well rope, tied tighter than a well rope needs to be. It's taut, as if something heavier than a bucket is hanging at the other end.

narrator/b2cf96d3762c044f.text: She turns a page. It crumbles. She turns it again.

narrator/b2f33db5f5faa98b.text: Old headstones, their names worn to dimples. Several have been dug around recently, as if the earth was checking on them.

narrator/b2f707b679d6966a.text: The mouth cave is full of straw and the smell of animals, and every heap of straw could be a wolf, or a sleeping man, or both.

narrator/b328144acdf60de0.text: They go on toward the village, the cart creaking, the boy pulling. The old woman's hands are folded very neatly. Nobody in this valley would think to look at her throat.

narrator/b35e3fdba4ed338d.text: A camp on the hill's shoulder: hide tents, a fire, a frame of poles hung with wicker cages. Bones are piled by the fire, picked and sorted, the way a careful cook sorts them.

narrator/b369662c051f3935.text: Behind the pole gate at the back of the den, a girl's voice says something you don't quite catch, and then nothing.

narrator/b3825eadf119a630.text: Krezk inside its wall: low stone cottages with turf on the roofs, smoke going straight up, and people who stop what they're doing to watch you pass and don't start again until you've gone.

narrator/b3edebe36bfee106.text: She breaks the seal with her thumb and reads it twice, and then folds it very small and puts it inside her coat, against her chest.

narrator/b3fe4355fbdb4fb7.text: For a moment he's only a young man on a wall. Then he isn't there at all.

narrator/b4044ec95b0583d8.text: The road climbs south through dead pines toward the castle on its cliff. Every sensible part of you says: not yet, and not like this.

narrator/b4382fc1b565f139.text: She heaves herself out of the ditch and sets off up the lane toward the mill, humming. You may come to regret that.

narrator/b43a07f11dbd3fdd.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Fekre, the mother of fevers. She emptied a city by loving it. Wash your hands after."

narrator/b4437d8a311a251a.text: Charred poles and wet ash where the scarecrows stood. A sacking face lies in the mud, still smiling.

narrator/b4640ce966e85b77.text: The gallows rope hangs empty now, and the mound beside the road has settled. Crossroads are patient; this one will have another guest soon enough.

narrator/b47d5907f2f9fbef.text: Frost has had three hundred winters at the deep cuts. You make out a list of things the temple refuses to be, and no word at all.

narrator/b483dd0bbc2324a3.text: Two figures in green-dyed sacking step into the road ahead, and the brush behind them steps out too.

narrator/b4bc0346e0a5a168.text: Vladimir stands. Down the long table the dead knights stand with him, and the sound of their armour is like a house settling. He lays his sword flat on the table, and one by one, so do they.

narrator/b4c4c112abba6682.text: Warm, floury and close. Everything is dusted white: the tables, the sacks, the floor, the millstone. The oven on the far wall breathes like something asleep.

narrator/b4e23356182242e9.text: The boards in front of the tower door sag a finger's breadth when you lean on the one before them. Rotten through, and only the carpet holding them.

narrator/b55857762bd0591e.text: He frowns at the lock for a long while afterwards, and then lets it be.

narrator/b5a1e01d55c16a29.text: The silver light runs out from the tower across the trees to the castle on its rock. Up there, a single window that was lit goes dark.

narrator/b5aacf7cf78c4980.text: The words echo strangely in the low cave. The candles at her feet don't gutter; nothing answers. But nothing objects, either, and the air feels a little less close when you are done.

narrator/b5b0adab14d27d63.text: The altar is clean. That is the worst thing about it.

narrator/b5bbd9df7cbc918f.text: Two people are sitting by the fire on the shore, not quite looking at each other, passing a cup back and forth. The tower's window is dark for once.

narrator/b5c6e433ed39c619.text: They bury Elvir at the end of the last green row, under the cairn they raised for him when there was nothing to put beneath it. Stefania sings. Davian doesn't. Adrian digs, and won't let anyone else hold the spade.

narrator/b5e0ff45aebcaaec.text: The wicker sun towers over the crowd on its pole, waiting for its torch.

narrator/b5e6dfdd14e6a01e.text: A mound of rot and old rushes, taller than a man, steaming faintly in the cold. It rises and falls, very slowly, like something asleep.

narrator/b5f30bd9722f56c3.text: A well with its rope rotted away. When you drop a pebble, it takes a long time to land, and then something below says the word "thank you" very quietly.

narrator/b6082106a0df6314.text: The door of the hut slams itself. The fire in the hearth stands up tall and green, and the jars on the shelf begin to hum.

narrator/b60ce641bf9d954c.text: It smells of straw and something big and alive. A shape breathes under a tarpaulin at the far end of the wagon, slow and deep, and doesn't wake. Yet.

narrator/b620450816f12127.text: A plain room with a cot and a chest, and every inch of one wall covered in charcoal writing, floor to as high as a big man can reach.

narrator/b687a41167bfb43d.text: You kneel by the bed and lay a hand on the boy's chest and pray. For a moment nothing. Then the warmth under your palm changes: not the fever's heat, but a cleaner one, like sun through a shutter.

narrator/b69e0ec9bfc0b193.text: Wooden heads waiting for faces, in rows. Blinsky carves the mouths last, he'd tell you, so the toys can't complain about the rest.

narrator/b6f0f6fe6d1c7f3e.text: A handsome family in oils above the mantel: a broad, smiling man cradling a swaddled baby, a narrow woman looking at that baby the way you'd look at a stain, a girl of ten with her chin up, and a small boy holding a stuffed wolf by one ear.

narrator/b72a528aaa71822d.text: Whatever you carry out of Berez, you carry it on your backs for a long time. You find you are stronger for the weight.

narrator/b77f30b25b8d0b3b.text: Under the smell of oak there's something else down here: a cold that isn't the cellar's, pooling in the vaults like water.

narrator/b78269090b561bab.text: Inside the chest, wrapped in cloth, lie eleven dolls with red hair: one in a green dress, one in a grey cloak, one smiling. Every face is the same face, carved with terrible love.

narrator/b78a7ad15a8d4d78.text: Each of you came looking for something. None of you came looking for this.

narrator/b7b85f56df9ae20b.text: The grey gelding stops sidling and leans its whole weight on you, the way horses do when they've decided you are furniture.

narrator/b7c41611090233d5.text: The cold hits like a fist. You find him by touch, three fathoms down, already still, and you tear the coat off him and the stones go on down without him.

narrator/b7df212e2e4d2ba5.text: He's past you before the words are finished, a rush of cold air up the stair. Somewhere above, a door bangs, and the bell rope thrums once, as if something brushed it going over the wall.

narrator/b7e2fe9088f4f4c8.text: The winery smells of old wine gone to vinegar and of something else under it, green and wet, like a pond in summer. The floorboards have been pried up in rows, as if someone were looking for something.

narrator/b82434fdf4405c6f.text: A high, cold antechamber before a carved archway. Through the arch: braziers, an altar, and figures in robes who are not quite there.

narrator/b824a6e82046f12c.text: The ward is still there, coiled in its ring of frost, but now you know where its edges are, and so does it.

narrator/b875a47484280ae1.text: You sleep in shifts, and nobody sleeps much. The voices in the amber don't shout. They say your names, kindly, all night.

narrator/b87ccd9f3d528bd4.text: Kiril throws back his head and laughs, and the laugh turns into a howl halfway through, and his loyal wolves come pouring up the passage behind him.

narrator/b88874cff77f5a1c.text: He takes off his spectacles, and his face comes away with them.

narrator/b8a67fc4c28dd511.text: Strong, glossy horses with plaited manes. One of them, a grey gelding, watches the road east and won't stop.

narrator/b8b7886f3b1ce8fd.text: You tell him about the pool, the young man in the water, and what Ireena remembered: the bride his lord truly wants ran from him once to her death, and given a second life, chose a dead man over him again.

narrator/b8c94713002b4ffb.text: From the crest you can see a green smudge on the hills to the east where the Martikov vines are. It's the only green in the whole grey valley, and it looks like defiance.

narrator/b8f351440be5839a.text: He takes the book as if it might be a trick. Then he opens it, and reads the flyleaf, and his lips move.

narrator/b8f439a29e8ba01c.text: The sparks in Exethanter's eyes go from candle to forge. Somewhere in the shelves, two skulls catch fire.

narrator/b916a098d5769ad6.text: The racks by Bluto's shack are heavy with fish nobody has salted, and the gulls have found them, and so has the smell.

narrator/b9257429865cdaf7.text: The warden's spear comes down, and the walls of the vault answer: grey men-at-arms step out of the stone on either side, shields locked, between you and the bones.

narrator/b92ed72d88576da6.text: In the cradle by the tub, under a crocheted blanket, lies a root dug out of the marsh and trimmed into the shape of a swaddled infant. Tucked under its chin like a rattle is a green gem the size of a hen's egg, glowing softly.

narrator/b9407626648fcac0.text: A good silver mirror turned to face the wall. On its back, in chalk: DON'T.

narrator/b94ed3b5cea66135.text: Elisabeth Durst's crypt, the finest carving in the row, its slab still shut.

narrator/b966e2b2c5991415.text: The pale figures on the shore move all at once, faster than anything dead has a right to.

narrator/b967cf876251d874.text: The boards split, and a leg goes through to the ceiling of the room below.

narrator/b995ae3671836e2c.text: Small bones, a great many of them: rats, mostly. They've been cracked open and sucked clean, and then arranged, neatly, by size.

narrator/b996d6a0de377719.text: Dead knights sit along both sides of a long table under rotted banners, armoured and unmoving, as if a feast was called four centuries ago and nobody has been dismissed.

narrator/b9aec08ba189b4b8.text: Every bench in the refectory has turned to face the stairs, as if waiting for you to be served.

narrator/b9b580029dfd6777.text: She stops sweeping. She looks at Ireena for a long moment, and then, very slowly, makes the sign of the sun over her own heart.

narrator/b9d00a476bcc9550.text: Lysaga fills one more bowl, from a second, smaller pot at the back of the hearth, and puts it in front of Ireena with both hands, very kindly.

narrator/b9f57b57cf6095b6.text: You walk past slowly. The arrows follow you all the way to the bend in the road.

narrator/b9fe2474b08f4469.text: Pews worn smooth along the backs by armoured shoulders. In front of every one, the stone floor is dented where knees went down in plate.

narrator/ba05855727390082.text: Silver light lies over the whole ridge from the top of the tower, steady as a held note. The house under it is still a ruin. It looks like a ruin that has been forgiven.

narrator/ba1d311212e0ad1b.text: She doesn't want revenge; she wants to hear him once more. She would know his song anywhere.

narrator/ba27a38cd9f869ec.text: In a small room downstairs, under a wall of charcoal names, a big knight in dented plate sits down on his cot and is still.

narrator/ba2bcf209e4bcdc5.text: The marks go up and up, north toward the rock face above the lake, and the prints beside them change, halfway, from boots to paws.

narrator/ba33dce111ff062d.text: At the very bottom of the temple, in a chamber of cold braziers, lies the largest sarcophagus of all, and it is empty.

narrator/ba4933da600d504a.text: A plain iron strongbox, unlocked, and under the holy water a bundle in oilcloth that the old man clearly didn't want to carry and couldn't bring himself to leave.

narrator/bac641f9346d7e16.text: The bones in the passage stand up, and some of them still have meat on.

narrator/bac7a7598ee905a9.text: Ismark takes the head of the coffin and Ireena walks in front with the lamp. The burgomaster is heavier than he looks, as grief usually is.

narrator/bb171fe96f6290d0.text: Four cages of woven willow, each big enough for a crouching man. The willow is still green. The druids grew them that shape, which is somehow worse than weaving.

narrator/bb2538ff47a95f85.text: Two figures in black plate stand in the middle of the track ahead with drawn swords, quite still, as if they have been standing there since before the trees. Their faces are grey. Neither of them is breathing.

narrator/bb45b47b77aab80c.text: A girl's bedroom with the bed pushed against the wall and scratches on the inside of the door, low down, at about the height of a cat.

narrator/bb463802f13cd809.text: A courtyard of worn flags round a well and a statue. Footprints in the snow go in every direction, and some of them aren't any shape that has a name.

narrator/bba0957ae5680cb6.text: A rag doll, face down in the mud: a little stitched woman with a wool scarf and one button eye. Somebody small has loved it nearly to pieces, and then dropped it here.

narrator/bbc9bfd536bd09b0.text: A great chair at the head of the table, carved with a dragon's folded wings. The arms are worn bright where gauntleted hands have gripped them, night after night, for centuries.

narrator/bc07d3c4cd8f0955.text: A good sword, well oiled, leaning where a hand can find it without looking. It has been used, recently.

narrator/bc14465461cc6758.text: Under the last stone, wrapped in oilcloth gone stiff with cold, lies a fat spellbook bound in grey leather, and tucked inside its cover two loose scrolls, written fast. The hand is strong and impatient. The capital letters all have a little hook.

narrator/bc43349d6caa0c1f.text: You say it aloud. The colossus lowers its head like a hound told to lie down, and the light behind its amber eyes sinks to an ember.

narrator/bc455a33d9eb7877.text: She smiles. She rocks. She shells. Whatever is under that smile has had a very long time to practise staying there.

narrator/bc66a1ced2c8187e.text: A cold bedroom hearth, the ash swept, a poker leaning at exactly the angle someone left it.

narrator/bc833f76906023d1.text: The stone comes free with a small wet sound. It is warm, and it smells, impossibly, of grapes in the sun. In the cradle the root sighs and begins, very slowly, to wither.
