narrator/bc89a65f20745c27.text: The foot of the stairs, its walls cut with little alcoves, each holding something strange: a dried hand, a bone knife, a hag's finger. Down here the chant is clear: they are praising the land, and the ancient one who is the land.

narrator/bcdb12ffeb1d6c3c.text: The mist lets you in, holds you a moment like a host taking your coat, and hands you back to the road, facing west.

narrator/bced191433223d9f.text: The boards split, and a leg goes through to the ceiling below.

narrator/bcff5e94ba5c699e.text: He watches the windows more than the door. Each time a bird lands on the sill, he glances at it the way a man glances at a friend, and once you'd swear it nodded back.

narrator/bd6347321eee478a.text: A painted statue of a gaunt man in a black cloak, holding out an orb of smoky crystal.

narrator/bdc52e904bd826e8.text: Stanimir is not smiling. Two younger Vistani stand behind him with their thumbs hooked in their belts, close to their knives.

narrator/bdd1ccecd131c1b6.text: He goes into one of you like breath into a cold mirror; for a moment two sets of eyes look out of the same face, then only one. Somewhere inside, a small boy stops crying.

narrator/bdd68dc0984a180d.text: Scarecrows step off the poles along the track, one after another, as if somebody had called them in for supper.

narrator/bdf7b1a5182c0c0f.text: Cold candles, cracked windows and a sunburst over the altar gone grey with soot. Under your boots, faint through the floorboards, someone is weeping and someone is praying, and you can't tell which is which.

narrator/be13b2f0356aa9e4.text: One room with a sleeping corner and a study divided off by a half wall. The hearth has never been lit; the cold doesn't seem to bother him.

narrator/be30c2e30a708cac.text: The colossus steps down off its plinth, slow and stiff with ice.

narrator/be39a71dc42d5416.text: The track to the abbey goes up the mountainside in switchbacks, cut into the rock, so steep in places that someone has driven iron pegs into the stone to hold on by. Far above, a bell tower stands against the clouds.

narrator/be3e0233c3874b4c.text: The Baron reads the letter twice, moving his lips. On the second reading, the colour drains out of him from the forehead down.

narrator/be4aff61ca373aa0.text: Shut for the night. A slate on the door reads, in a neat hand: OPEN AT DAWN. BRING COIN.

narrator/be6c9d7114b34c26.text: The hidden stair lets you out into a little rock-cut room with an iron gate. The walls are warm here too, warm as skin.

narrator/be7d76678bf674d1.text: Exethanter looks up, blinks, and reads the paper pinned to his sleeve, his jaw moving with the words.

narrator/be8b894e9ecbbf06.text: The iron gate swings open with a long, thin screech: the only sound down here that isn't chanting.

narrator/be9a10ff0540851c.text: Lamplight, maps, the smell of cold tea. Someone has been working at the table very late, every night, for a week.

narrator/be9a392635ed83dd.text: The burgomaster's strongbox opens on dry velvet: he paid a good smith. Whatever he was saving for, he never got to spend it.

narrator/bea18572648d73a7.text: The village looks the same as it did, which is to say exhausted. A few more shutters stand open a finger's width than before.

narrator/bec6c0356b594566.text: Horses stamp on their line and the road runs back east to the gate. Somebody at the fire has noticed you, and gone to tell somebody else.

narrator/bedbca263f7b1594.text: A row of narrow cells with iron bars across their doors. Behind them, in the straw, shapes move: Belviews whose gifts didn't take, all elbows and fur and wrong-jointed legs, thin as winter. They watch you through the bars without blinking.

narrator/bede8d5d07e675ed.text: The portcullis is up, and the way is open. Ahead, candlelight and voices.

narrator/bf0ee40164f4e6f6.text: You sleep at the edge of the pines, and grey shapes keep watch on the slope above you all night. For once, they're watching for you, not at you.

narrator/bf1e6448defa9b36.text: A young woman in the horse pen looks up, and you know before she speaks that Stanimir has told her.

narrator/bf1eeb675dc2ca0a.text: The great press fills the middle of the floor, its screw as thick as a man's waist. Beside it stands a vat full to the brim, and the surface of the mash is moving.

narrator/bf4ae9c5caf5947b.text: You can see the whole Svalich road from here, and the village, and the lane to the mill. Anyone sitting up here would know who was coming long before they knocked.

narrator/bf67d3be9ef04880.text: As Ezmerelda comes near, a thread of blue light runs round the door frame and crackles, like a dog lifting its lip.

narrator/bf87ab20283ee412.text: The door is oak, iron-bound and scored to splinters around the latch. Somebody has nailed a horseshoe over it upside down, and somebody else, or something, has bent it.

narrator/bf889722e1d72327.text: The bottom room was a wizard's hall once: you can see where the carvings were chiselled off the walls. Now it's a hunter's storeroom: crates of holy water, bundles of stakes, a camp cot made with military corners.

narrator/bfb3bfeb2744d04f.text: You rest with your backs to a wall that has seen worse. Somewhere a dog barks once and thinks better of it.

narrator/bfba04ff261c916d.text: He looks at you for a long moment before he speaks, the way you'd look at someone you have already heard about, and not kindly.

narrator/bfc3c00b168775ba.text: Davian doesn't take the third stone at once. He looks at it in your hand, then at you, and his face does something it hasn't done since you met him.

narrator/bfcd52f323ba57df.text: Eyes in the dark on both sides of the road, low to the ground, and more of them every time you look.

narrator/bfd2182ccc7781c9.text: Below you, the house goes quiet in a new way. Along the long table in the hall, armoured heads lift toward the windows and then bow, and the knights are only men sitting very still.

narrator/bff1cafde4721f7a.text: The amber is dark and cold. Whatever is inside is still there, but the wardens' seal holds, and for once it has nothing to say.

narrator/bffc58403f70cfeb.text: The key turns stiffly. The cuffs open with a sound like a held breath let out.

narrator/c00138314d43ab34.text: The niches hold offerings: silver buttons, a ring, a child's carved dragon, candle stubs. The squires left what they had.

narrator/c01058074af190e7.text: A big, generous fire built by people who don't have to worry about firewood or who sees it. Its smoke goes straight up, which in this valley counts as a miracle.

narrator/c014097fb0f8dfef.text: Figures are wading up out of the reeds, streaming lake water, with weed in their hair and their eyes gone white. The lake is giving back what it took, and it wants something in exchange.

narrator/c02c3c8e4b854bc8.text: At the back of the nook, behind the dust, a thin seam in the plaster, square as a doorframe.

narrator/c030994575e2cae7.text: Wedged under a root, a traveller's pouch, the leather gone black, with a stoppered vial inside that the water never reached.

narrator/c03339cf0ff48e92.text: The cairn has a grave beneath it now, the earth still dark. Someone has pushed a vine cutting into the soil at its head, and the cutting has put out a single green leaf.

narrator/c044230f1a116ab5.text: A tall, handsome house behind a rusted fence, its windows dark, its porch swept. It is the best-kept house in the village, and nobody will walk past it.

narrator/c08e86c3baedc2a3.text: At the statue's feet, among the offerings, something catches your light and holds it a moment longer than the rest.

narrator/c0910b759093a59c.text: The lid is so cold that your breath freezes on it, and the frost fills the letters before you can read them.

narrator/c0a228e5d90032ce.text: A hunting tapestry on an iron rod: hounds and riders in full cry after a single grey wolf. Look closer and every rider is smiling.

narrator/c0b02351b5315243.text: A shack of grey boards with a sail for a door and a lamp in the window. The kind of place where one man has been very lonely for a very long time.

narrator/c0bc0f03bb363d7a.text: A bundle of legal papers, tied with string and heavy with seals.

narrator/c0c0dc514e6d7e34.text: A cold spare bedroom: a slender bed, a little iron stove, a writing desk and stool, a rocking chair, and in the window box a doll in a yellow dress.

narrator/c0e0b5871fbd39d1.text: She lowers the spyglass at last and looks you over properly, the way a horse trader looks at a horse.

narrator/c0e174fa5cc9607d.text: A narrow boy's bed, made tight. Under the pillow, when you lift it, there's a stone with a hole in it, the kind children think lets you see fairies.

narrator/c0ecb3ef68fa46f9.text: The water goes into the flasks bright and stays bright, faintly, like the last of a sunset in a window.

narrator/c107dd6a91c3b7fc.text: Just a house now, and a sad one. Whatever waited inside it has stopped waiting.

narrator/c118a5c8d9e75b61.text: Hoofbeats, unhurried, out of the fog ahead. A black horse with eyes like banked coals comes down the road at a walk, and the man riding it does not need to be introduced.

narrator/c124e9dc4b589352.text: The track comes out of the pines onto bare rock, and there it is: a windmill on the crag, its sails lashed still, its chimney smoking. The whole hill smells of fresh bread, and under the bread, of something else.

narrator/c13d0fd1b1ad6a54.text: Armour on the stair, coming fast.

narrator/c13d59e2462c8a0d.text: You have come farther into this house than most guests, and it has noticed. So have you.

narrator/c156a718742783bd.text: The hearth is cold. The green copper rod at its back has been drawn out of its socket, and the air in the tower no longer tastes of thunder.

narrator/c18174aae46813af.text: Iron jaws snap shut on a boot. Somewhere in the fog, a wolf yips, almost like laughter.

narrator/c18b49213dea7b93.text: You huddle in the lee of a boulder while the mountain screams over your heads. It passes, eventually. Everything up here passes, except the cold.

narrator/c1b6183aff36e2dc.text: The grey soldier at his post doesn't look at you. His eyes are on the door to the road, exactly where they have been for centuries.

narrator/c1f51c7d6b3bd358.text: The shingle shore of Lake Baratok. A stone causeway runs out from it toward the island, broad and solid until halfway, where the lake starts to win.

narrator/c1fd03b47cd1d273.text: He sees it coming and doesn't run. It is quick. Afterwards the fish go on flapping on the shingle for a long time, and then they stop.

narrator/c2013bea7102f17b.text: The slope is quiet. A grey wolf lies in the sun on the watch rock, sees you, and puts its head back down on its paws.

narrator/c2077779ba0691ab.text: The road runs west into darker trees, toward Tser Pool and, a long day beyond it, the walls of Vallaki.

narrator/c207bb5bacaa7ebc.text: You've been through them once already. They look no more organised for it.

narrator/c2159e0dc2feede6.text: He sees it coming, and for once he doesn't smile.

narrator/c2258392eb691e66.text: The skull and coiled spine of a dragon fill the amber, packed so tight the bones have cracked. The amber is the dark red of old blood, and it is cold even to look at.

narrator/c22f7bd9c2dc1b5d.text: A woman with flour to the elbows looks up from a cauldron, takes in your boots and your weapons, and decides you can stay.

narrator/c23ff7a994761b97.text: A cot of bare planks. There's no hollow in the wood where a body would lie. It has never been slept on.

narrator/c258e182a7606482.text: The frost on the ribs glows faintly where you took the light, like a coal remembering it was once a fire.

narrator/c2a47d401cd4ddbd.text: She rocks, and hums, and scrapes the pot. If she is hiding anything, she has had a very long time to practise.

narrator/c2bcd4d7b9a50e8e.text: The mansion is a festival that never ends: bunting on every banister, ribbons on every lamp, and on every wall a portrait of the Baron, beaming, in a different hat.

narrator/c2c31aa6ecf553fb.text: For the first time since the stair, you sleep. The temple is cold and silent and, for one night, only a building.

narrator/c2d5398e8c4d39ad.text: Her hands never stop working, stripping leaves from stalks, and her face gives you exactly as much as her hands do.

narrator/c2df7cb6b617e2d8.text: The rocking chair has worn two grooves in the floorboards from rocking in the same spot, day and night, for days.

narrator/c2e27497108c7672.text: It smells of wax and cold stone and, very faintly, of roses. Whoever keeps this room keeps it the way you keep a promise.

narrator/c30543f8801c73b5.text: His eyes go to Ireena and stay there, politely, the way a merchant's eyes stay on a price.

narrator/c30635a79d9ec087.text: The candle you lit is still burning, though there's no wind-shield on it and the snow comes in sideways.

narrator/c34045c46ce33b8e.text: Adrian reads it once. Then he lays his hand over the words, as if to keep them warm.

narrator/c3653bd7378e589b.text: Lights bob up out of the flooded houses, pale and friendly, and drift toward you at the speed of a walk. They are humming.

narrator/c3665139464dd737.text: You say it: the watch, the sleeper and the stranger, the fallen, the gift, the light. The spear doesn't move until the last word. Then it lifts.

narrator/c36694a7a9fb582c.text: Off the end of the jetty, a little boat has slipped its rope and is turning slowly in the mist, a few yards out. In it, sitting very straight with her hands folded in her lap, is Arabelle.

narrator/c396631aa96beaf4.text: Inside, the tower is grey and orderly, swept and squared away, the kind of tidy only soldiers manage. A pale light hangs in the air with nothing to give it off.

narrator/c3968f331436a4f5.text: A shadow the size of a barn roof slides across the bridge. Then the wind comes, and the scream, and the talons.

narrator/c39c3f2aabd1d606.text: A low passage, the rock polished at shoulder height by bodies brushing past. Two kinds of shoulder: one at a man's height, one at a wolf's.

narrator/c39c50ac3fa4f9dd.text: Jars on every shelf, and some of them humming. Under the humming, from somewhere in the pantry, comes a quieter sound, steady and patient, like something that knows it's been found.

narrator/c42cabe8943547a8.text: A crest over the captain's bed: a sun over mountains, the arms of a crown that ruled this valley before the castle did.

narrator/c43912cd8ef092d1.text: Above the mansion door, the Baron's painted face beams at the square with his arms spread wide, as if about to embrace the whole town, whether or not it wants to be embraced.

narrator/c43f5a4074707c90.text: A long bar, a crackling hearth and a dozen tables, most of them occupied by people who stop talking for exactly as long as it takes to look at you.

narrator/c4415b422d3c8104.text: The field is cold, colder than the night, and the mounds look less like mounds than like people lying very still with blankets pulled up.

narrator/c45877768e7251e1.text: She takes one step toward you and the next step into nothing, and she's gone. Far down the hill, a little later, something shrieks, and every raven in the oak goes up at once.

narrator/c49b7b13a6ec0d67.text: A wall of trophies. Ezmerelda stops in front of a Vistani boot with a fine buckle and stares at it for a long time, and says nothing at all.

narrator/c4a4503674d0d3b2.text: A map of the whole valley, closely annotated. A cave in the hills above Lake Zarovich is ringed in red ink with one word: WOLVES. Beside Vallaki, in smaller letters: R. The Blue Water.

narrator/c4b2e41022ffa986.text: The goat track climbs through dark pines into cold that comes too early for the season. Somewhere above, a small storm is waiting over the summit like a dog outside a door.

narrator/c4ce92e2697c578e.text: Elisabeth's fork stops halfway to her mouth. For one moment the hunger leaves both their faces, and what's left is worse: two parents who have just remembered.

narrator/c5117b9c648c7956.text: The lane north narrows between cottages and climbs toward a gap in the wall, and the snow on it is swept, every flake, by somebody very old and very determined.

narrator/c52d98b4ed5bfc50.text: A dark marble hearth, laid and never lit. Whoever hung the family over it wanted them kept warm.

narrator/c53670e71cb4ecb7.text: The lock holds. Somewhere in the walls, something that might be laughter.

narrator/c54816e5a9bb728a.text: The wind off the wings nearly takes you over the parapet.

narrator/c559db207d90249c.text: The abbey is quiet in a new way. The window that was always lit is dark, and the Belviews are out in the courtyard in the daylight, blinking at it.

narrator/c5665b8a3d5f4fdd.text: The lane runs straight up between the rows, and the vines stay vines. You notice yourself noticing that.

narrator/c5788f7b07485daf.text: Blankets and old sailcloth stretched between the trees. Inside one, a row of children's boots; inside another, an old man's wine-stained coat folded with great care.

narrator/c589650fcb0177a5.text: A burgomaster's study: ledgers, maps of the valley, a desk buried in papers. On top of the pile, one letter is written in a hand that grows shakier toward the end.

narrator/c5d6875a1e586c6f.text: The ceiling sheds a curtain of amber, every shard as sharp as glass.

narrator/c6090068ca1c9dec.text: A rocking chair worn smooth, a bowl, a basket of knitting, and a footstool placed exactly where a child in a cage could see it.

narrator/c62070106411a0cf.text: The house gives something up. It doesn't like doing it.

narrator/c64ce958ae649e23.text: The flagstone tips, and the dark beneath it is ten feet deep and full of spikes.

narrator/c6b22a11c2caf294.text: A footpath climbs north through the pines to the lip of a gorge. The river goes over the edge in one long white rope of water, and the roar fills everything.

narrator/c6e0f2fa6b2ccb35.text: The roof beams groan as if the house is flexing its shoulders.

narrator/c6f802bf689d7ae9.text: In the alcove a big, grey-bearded man sits against the rock with his arms spread wide, chained by both wrists to iron rings. The chains are bright. Where they touch him, the skin has blistered black.

narrator/c743512909bc7a4e.text: A short letter in an elegant, unhurried hand. It notes Gustav Durst's devotion and declines it, mocks the cult's candles, and promises nothing.

narrator/c7845c859c0c0a02.text: A deep well with a stone lip worn smooth by buckets. When you drop a pebble, it takes a long time to hit the water, and the water, when it answers, sounds warm.

narrator/c78b1c61fe548122.text: A lane climbs between rows of vines the colour of a paper bag left out in the rain. At the top stand a house, a winery and a tall barn, all shut, with ravens on every roof.

narrator/c791c2d7d88a7ded.text: Wachterhaus is dark, except for a grate low in its wall, where candlelight flickers from somewhere under the ground.

narrator/c79fe30d1061b2d4.text: Offalia wipes her hands on her apron, and keeps wiping them as they lengthen into something with knuckles like walnuts and nails like a baker's peel.

narrator/c7ac8820a5f73e73.text: The mausoleum stands apart from the house, as if out of respect. Its door is shut and its stones are white with a frost that the sun doesn't touch.

narrator/c7aeaf4112a4568b.text: The wainscot has thin dark slits in it at ankle height, knee height, throat height.

narrator/c7bb813ee9aa2b68.text: A shop window full of toys. A jack-in-the-box. A wooden wolf on wheels. A doll with red hair, in pride of place, with a little card that says NOT FOR SALE.

narrator/c7bde819dc9fe239.text: Letters from Gustav Durst to the household's nursemaid, tied in blue ribbon. They begin politely and stop being polite.

narrator/c7c1999ced2a25ed.text: Floury old hands on a cart's handles. She catches you looking and wiggles her fingers at you.

narrator/c7cb94d2b3020974.text: Cut into the lintel, in letters taller than your hand: HE KEPT THE WATCH. Below it, smaller and newer and much less tidy: WE KEEP IT NOW.

narrator/c80a52d32a5b1e7c.text: The silence afterward is yours. Keep it as long as you can.

narrator/c81870f1391d1579.text: The fog hums very faintly, like a held note. Whatever made it is still making it.

narrator/c82391d15d9f8aa5.text: His face is a dead man's face. Whatever it's hiding, it has had four hundred years of practice.

narrator/c82c4434b7055209.text: Scarecrows stand all through the reeds around the stump, on poles, in sacking smocks, with sewn-on faces that all look the same way: at you.

narrator/c85c544da8d6144e.text: You wait, and the wolves wait longer. When you finally look up, every one of them is still looking at you.

narrator/c89a04b168e9c677.text: Izek comes down off the dais, and his strange arm is already smoking at the knuckles.

narrator/c8bc446e2bfa7855.text: Izek Strazni stands at the Baron's shoulder with his scaled arm folded under the ordinary one, watching the crowd the way a dog watches sheep.

narrator/c8ca37a124f2b81f.text: Something heavy scrapes across the floor on the other side and thumps against the door. A wardrobe, by the sound of it.

narrator/c90b31063ce05c7b.text: Incense, candle smoke and old canvas. Behind a low table sits a woman so old she seems made of the same leather as her chair, shuffling a deck of cards without looking at it.

narrator/c90bc2991817d443.text: Before you reach the door, the weeping starts again, exactly where it left off.

narrator/c90ddfa2539161a3.text: A wayside shrine with a sun carved on it, and offerings frozen to its shelf: a loaf like stone, a wooden horse, a lock of hair. Nobody has left anything new in a very long time.

narrator/c93bff3a22a0ea61.text: Glass bursts inward along both walls of the nave. Pale shapes come through the windows head first, like swimmers, and the candles gutter as they pass.

narrator/c96404083ecd1a67.text: A bare room: a cot, a basin, a sword on a peg, and a chest at the foot of the bed. It smells of oil and smoke, and faintly of a hot stove, though there isn't one.

narrator/c982ab7e92666981.text: Two narrow beds made with tight corners, two footlockers, uniforms pressed and hanging, and a small door in the wall with a brass call button beside it.

narrator/c98438d81ba43f83.text: In the middle, where the reflected sun lingers longest, your fingers close on something in the silt that has no business being warm.

narrator/c985cac07fff9e80.text: She looks up at you, and something of the old fury comes back into her face, because it is easier than the other thing.

narrator/c996544de0444ca3.text: It takes him a long time. When it comes it's barely a whisper, and it is the whole truth.

narrator/c99d0c4f855642e9.text: A silver dragon in coloured glass, curled around a lamp. The glass is cold enough to fog your breath, and the frost on it has a grain, like the lines of a face.

narrator/c9bef03c64eb1d8b.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Sykane, the hollow belly. Its priests ate first. Then they ate each other."

narrator/c9db7e856d64c469.text: She snatches her arm away and tucks it into her coat, and looks at you the way she looked at the wolves.

narrator/c9dfa29e886b2828.text: Weeds, rubble and fog. The gate keeps its own counsel.

narrator/c9e39c1a150507e6.text: Offalia snores on the bakery floor with crumbs on her chin, smiling at whatever she's dreaming. Now and then her fingers twitch, kneading.

narrator/c9e765f6ce99e9f9.text: For the first time in years the chant falters. Knowing a story is a kind of power over it.

narrator/c9f56ff377cefed6.text: A puppet theatre with a little castle at the back and a little village at the front. All the villagers are on strings. So is the castle.

narrator/c9ff9b73464fdac9.text: The bar comes up with a groan. The gate opens a body's width, no more, and waits for you to fit yourselves through it.

narrator/ca29294e4a420f26.text: A shuttered window with a candle burning behind the slats. The weeping comes from just inside, and it doesn't stop when you stop to listen.

narrator/ca41cbe07f779662.text: A bare room: a cot with a blanket stretched tight enough to bounce a coin, a lectern, a strongbox. Nothing on the walls. Nothing on the floor. A room kept by someone who has stopped living in it.

narrator/ca50f48fbb8d4ad0.text: The coin clicks into the niche beside the candle. The flame doesn't move, but for a mile after, the wind seems to be at your backs.

narrator/ca5dc4a3bb8b707b.text: The cairn stones lie where you set them down. The frost ring around them is melting, now there's nothing left to guard.

narrator/ca898c708f791232.text: The reading hall is only cold now. The frost on the desks is thinner than it was, and nobody is weeping.

narrator/ca914e5cb2c592e8.text: The top of the watch rock is polished smooth by a great many patient bellies. There's a good view, and a fine collection of fleas.

narrator/cab192f865aa89a7.text: A dead knight in the courtyard is going through the motions of saddling a horse that isn't there, buckle by buckle, very carefully.

narrator/cad359f59ab37e23.text: Nobody moves for a long moment. Then a knight halfway down the table, whose name nobody has said for centuries, stands up. Then another.

narrator/cadd798f1156023a.text: The camp smells of horses, plums and pipe smoke. Every wagon is painted in colours the valley has forgotten: red, gold, a green like summer.

narrator/cb16a464af071b52.text: The bow comes down. A whistle, and three young men drop out of the trees, all with the same nose.

narrator/cb1b28e83d76e9a1.text: He rides on through the middle of you. The black horse never breaks its walk, and you find you have stepped aside without meaning to.

narrator/cb326601040ab373.text: A square of mud around a dry well. Two shops face it, one tavern and one mercantile, and both look as if they're waiting for customers who stopped coming years ago.

narrator/cb6cdd606c63d7f3.text: The former Baron of Vallaki sits in his own stocks with his wrists through the holes and his gold chain gone. Somebody has hung his sash over the board, upside down.

narrator/cb92f62721910fc8.text: Downstairs, something heavy stops chewing. In the corner, a stool scrapes back. Three voices begin humming the same tune, and the loft is suddenly much smaller.

narrator/cbd4b75ec6105124.text: His face is a shut door with good locks. Whatever is behind it, you won't have it today, and perhaps neither will he.

narrator/cbed3ded0bd6a9db.text: There. The house hid it well, but not well enough.

narrator/cc27e8a2f3545f6a.text: Jars of pickled things in cloudy brine, labeled in a neat hand. One label just says: for later.

narrator/cc29a5d20498d7f3.text: Each cask is chalked with a year. The oldest years are in a hand you saw in the office ledger, then a heavier hand, then Davian's. The newest chalk on the rack says only: next year.

narrator/cc464e355f316880.text: Raised beds of frozen stalks: cabbages gone to black lace, beans that never ripened. Someone still weeds them.

narrator/cc49c3ef08d46016.text: Racks of empty bottles to the ceiling, waiting, with the terrible patience of glass.

narrator/cc4b6ae7a96accad.text: He looks past you, at Ireena, the whole time he's speaking. Then, once, at you, the way a man marks a tree he means to come back and cut.

narrator/cc5afcc5d8a2b17e.text: A child's book of tales, read until the spine gave up. One page falls open by itself.

narrator/cc76bd9b1c5656b8.text: You sleep in the lee of the rock with a watch set. In the night, from the tower above, someone calls the hour, and gets it right.

narrator/cc810944b8baa84f.text: He's handsome, and calm, and very still. If there's more to it than that, the chapel isn't telling you.

narrator/cc8c8d48d3162efb.text: Graves, close-set, each with a small stone sun on it instead of a name. The ones by the pavilion are very small, and there are five of them.

narrator/cc9bf93728d725b6.text: Lights rise out of the reeds, pale and friendly, and drift toward the track. The nearest one is humming.

narrator/ccbab2154514a086.text: The vines on both sides of the lane shiver, though there's no wind. Then, row by row, they stand up.

narrator/ccc49875b0550a6c.text: Elisabeth Durst's crypt, the slab still in place. The carving is the finest in the row, and something behind it is ticking, very faintly, like a great many small clocks.

narrator/ccc77e06e33b7ea7.text: The oven door is barely open when a floury hand slams it shut again. Offalia isn't smiling now. Nobody touches Mother's oven.

narrator/ccc809ec76aa4725.text: Where the front door stood there is only brick, still warm and settling, mortar oozing between the courses like sap.

narrator/cd0993941ce1ee95.text: He tips his head back and howls. It starts as a man's voice and finishes as something else, and it goes on long after it should have run out of breath. The whole hill takes it up.

narrator/cd0bf40478d6a588.text: Days later, the Belviews will say he went down the mountain once, at dawn, laid a hand on the burgomaster's boy, and climbed back up without a word. You'll never know if anyone asked him to.

narrator/cd0d91445c090337.text: Burned books, mostly; a few spines still readable. Histories, songs, a very old cookbook with a great many notes in the margins about mutton.

narrator/cd12b6d16924a06b.text: Torches go to the straw. A drizzle has been falling since dawn; the sun catches at one edge, smokes, goes out, catches, goes out. Somebody in the crowd laughs, and then very badly wishes they hadn't.

narrator/cd5d6587359054f9.text: A dead oak with a raven on every branch. When you look up, every one of them looks down. When you look away, you can feel them going back to their conversation.

narrator/cd6fb9927a8bbe50.text: You reach in among the roots. They're warm. One of them, you'd swear, flexes against your wrist.

narrator/cd7e6af729aabece.text: An old woman, grey and peaceful, with her hands folded on a sprig of dry thyme. Whatever took her, it left her looking asleep.

narrator/cd80f2992684ef09.text: She wants to step into the water so badly her hands shake on the stones. And under that, stubborn as a root, she wants to see what she'd have been if nobody had ever loved her this much. Both. She wants both.

narrator/cdb28b754823036e.text: Two tiers of bunks, blankets folded square. One has a name scratched into the frame and, under it, a tally of days that stops at a number nobody should have to count to.

narrator/cdda905316a4c022.text: The words reach her slowly, like warmth into frozen hands. Her cupped hands open, and there is nothing in them, and she looks at the nothing for a long time.

narrator/ce0688d32b6eb02f.text: The room keeps its secrets. It has had a great deal of practice.

narrator/ce118e9c44bcdd20.text: The words come out in the wrong order. You say them anyway. It is the meaning that counts, or so you have to hope.

narrator/ce2615c575cb5da5.text: For the barest instant something flickers behind his courtesy: not fear, but attention. He looks at you as if you have just become interesting.

narrator/ce2d2e58e616de0f.text: The door is barred from inside. The wood around the latch has been clawed to splinters, and it is not old damage.

narrator/ce44bc3e24b05cd6.text: A ribbon of Vistani silk, red and gold, knotted round the jetty's last post. It's damp, but it hasn't been here long. Someone tied it where the water is deepest.

narrator/ce49e79a14142b22.text: Kiril weighs the purse in one big hand, then tosses it to the nearest of his wolves without looking.

narrator/ce4d99a02ebcf539.text: Candle stubs in rows, a hundred years of them, and the stone floor worn into two hollows where the same knees went down every night.

narrator/ce7a2b09e9baec61.text: The wild men come over the fire with a roar, as happy as anyone you've ever seen.

narrator/ce99922b28e13fd0.text: The words go out over the water, and the bell rings straight through them, as if it has heard a great many prayers and none of them helped.

narrator/ce9d5aa0786e57c9.text: A road stone with the distance cut on it, to a place whose name has been chiselled off by someone very thorough.

narrator/cea8ffd0105c12ff.text: Rose's finger touches a panel in the corner of the toy storage room. It swings open on a staircase winding down inside the walls.

narrator/cea98f48e17ed4c5.text: A small white crib, freshly made.

narrator/cf0056375b972cbc.text: The altar is scrubbed bare. Wax has run down its sides in long pale ropes, from candles that burned all night, every night, for a long time.

narrator/cf311c2137b3092a.text: In the dark the falls are only a roar and a pale ribbon. Something on the far side of the gorge is howling, and the water is not quite loud enough to cover it.

narrator/cf4aeae003304ca8.text: The lead wolf's lips peel back from its teeth. Behind you, in the trees, something answers it.

narrator/cf4cd98a3d281d4e.text: Through the glass of the shutting door you glimpse the road outside, empty. No children, and no footprints where they stood.

narrator/cf56c45401aff035.text: No handle, no keyhole. The door is warm, and it is waiting for a word.

narrator/cf7c75afef248b94.text: You rest by the cooling oven. Upstairs, nothing creaks at all, which takes some getting used to.

narrator/cf7fe1afe4ce767d.text: She fades from the doorway like a word you meant to say and didn't.

narrator/d00e05eb07219ed7.text: A long corridor of cells, each just big enough for a cot and a prayer. The wardens lived here, a few steps from what they guarded. It must have been very hard to sleep.

narrator/d0218dc1005834d2.text: Under the loose riser, wrapped in a handkerchief, are a purse and two little bottles. Mother's emergency: Rose was right.

narrator/d045763b23d437f6.text: Bats pour out of the canopy like smoke, and under them the wolves come running.

narrator/d049b89066c5acb3.text: On a stone by the track at the foot of the hill sits Kostin, the druid from the press house. He has no staff now, and he's torn strips from his robe to bind his feet.

narrator/d0541d152844f633.text: There's smoke from Bluto's chimney and a smell of frying, the first cheerful smell this shore has produced in a year.

narrator/d07917c0f83024bc.text: A plain altar of grey stone with a lamp carved on its front instead of a sun. On top, a hundred stubs of candle, every one burned all the way down.

narrator/d07aaee76eb3a5a9.text: The prayer comes out in the wrong order, and the last verse leaves you entirely. Ireena finishes it, quietly, without looking up.

narrator/d07ed4b3fac92184.text: Pale skin, a careful hand with a needle somewhere in her past. She could be sleeping. You'd prefer she was sleeping.

narrator/d081795428aed23f.text: The oven door swings open on a gust of heat. At the very back, untouched by the coals, lies something no hag would ever have baked.

narrator/d0990a6e373856e6.text: For a moment the showman's smile stays exactly where it is, and everything behind it goes very still.

narrator/d0ba1f319adc4487.text: The hut folds its root legs and kneels in the mud, and a ladder of living roots unrolls from its door to your feet. It is warm to the touch.

narrator/d0dabdf41b85c1a7.text: Dust sifts down from beams that are shifting in their sockets.

narrator/d10aed3a529619e6.text: The candles are out. In the grey light from the door, a figure sits on the altar step and doesn't look up.

narrator/d1679684a2d3e669.text: A plinth with no sarcophagus on it. Scrapes on the floor lead away toward the stair, as though something very heavy was carried off by people who were in a great hurry.

narrator/d1834f6ae13c0046.text: Inside the sack is a small girl, soaked, furious and very much alive, with black hair plastered over a solemn face. Bluto has gone, somewhere in the reeds.

narrator/d190ada6fdbcf206.text: A cupboard of a room with vestments on pegs and a chest under the window. Everything here has been folded with great care by someone whose hands were shaking.

narrator/d1c0e932b4f5a8a5.text: There, under the leaves: the iron teeth of a wolf trap, set right in the road.

narrator/d1c313afc23d3210.text: The old causeway is logs laid edge to edge, rotted soft, with water standing in the gaps. Somebody has been mending it, recently, with bones.

narrator/d1c3a78b324849e3.text: The gallows rope hangs empty, cut short above the knot. Beside the road, a mound of turned earth, marked with a board laid face down.

narrator/d1d185034062f680.text: Lady Wachter steps up onto the dais the moment he steps down, smoothing her gloves, as if she had been waiting in the wings.

narrator/d1d69af0bbe8c537.text: Every time she says "Mother", her eyes flick upward, toward something in the loft. Whatever she wants, it isn't the mill. It's up there, and she wants it badly enough to lie about it.

narrator/d1d90f586b14a9e0.text: The Belviews' humming doesn't stop when the fighting starts. It gets louder.

narrator/d1e0771cb0c06db8.text: Berez, and the witch still in it. A shutter on the stump bangs shut as you come in off the causeway, hard, like a door slammed on a family argument.

narrator/d1e9f9fa3c48b084.text: Plaster, dust and a warm wall. Nothing more, not yet.

narrator/d21d9053e4caf313.text: A gallery of crypts cut into the rock, names and dates carved over every niche. Generations of Dursts, filed neatly away.

narrator/d2334fab4c4664eb.text: A long nave under a sunburst window, cold candles and a bare altar. The church feels like a room that has been holding its breath for days.

narrator/d2735179f4d11f9d.text: Charcoal drawings of a boy: a baby with a full head of dark hair, a child on a pony, a sullen youth, a young man in armour. The last few are of an older man in a high collar, drawn from memory, a little wrong each time.

narrator/d28f8c7c7dca40e6.text: A kitchen that has been feeding three people on rations for a month. A cleaver lies on the table, not for cooking.

narrator/d28fe068cbe3457b.text: Four long sails, their canvas grey with flour and age, lashed to a stop in a cross. Whatever this mill grinds now, it isn't grain, and it isn't the wind that turns the stone.

narrator/d2caff81a875b9ca.text: A boy in the woods by the lake. Wolves. A little sister who was never found, and an arm that was never found either. Izek's story fits Ireena's like a key in a lock.

narrator/d2e324274498ab91.text: A young knight with his helmet under his arm, grinning as if he has been told to look solemn and can't. The brass plate on the frame says HORNGAARD.

narrator/d343cc803f46184c.text: They don't know you, and they never will. The house is fishing again.

narrator/d345dc6986169b3b.text: Two colossi of amber flank the doors, each three times a man's height, robed and hooded like the wardens who carved them. The left one has split from crown to knee, and snow has packed the crack.

narrator/d372882e92e54879.text: Behind the iron gate, the books are chained twice. Some of the chains are on the inside of the covers.

narrator/d3ab6728890170c4.text: A lady's writing desk: good paper, a silver inkstand, a drawer with a lock. The blotter has been used so often that the backwards words on it have run into each other.

narrator/d3b3e7ac4d366072.text: The yard has thawed. The birds that hung over the hut lie on the ground in a neat row, and someone has given them a small, respectful cairn.

narrator/d3bb3041ecf1412d.text: A narrow storeroom: shelves of folded sheets and blankets, bars of old soap, and a broom leaning in the corner with the air of a servant pretending not to listen.

narrator/d40489b157536455.text: His hound's ear goes flat as he looks at Ireena. He looks away, and then back, and then away.

narrator/d446a4f2100c029f.text: Shelves of good books, bound in leather, every page blank. On some, a capital M is written at the top of the first page, with a little hook, and nothing after it.

narrator/d44982e45b05050a.text: The candles lean, all together, as if someone has opened a door. Nobody has.

narrator/d45f382e01a2734c.text: The sculptor finished the robe down to the stitching, and the hands down to the knuckles, and then left the face perfectly smooth. Whether that was a choice or a refusal, the stone isn't saying.

narrator/d470b382baf0c140.text: Godfrey says the oath. He stumbles once and finds the word. When he reaches "be the light", half the table is saying it with him.

narrator/d4887a1d954bb4e4.text: Sheets, blankets, soap gone hard as stone. Everything folded, nothing used.

narrator/d48e91c1b0384f6d.text: You sleep on the shore with the tower at your backs. Twice in the night, out on the ridge, eyes catch the firelight and then think better of it.

narrator/d49c56ebf926d2c6.text: The great eye isn't looking past you any more. It's looking at whoever carries its gift, and they're looking back.

narrator/d4b6e5dda84ad577.text: Bogdan sends the boy to sit by the cart with his back turned. It is quick. It is not easy. Afterwards he closes the lid himself and stands with his hand on it.

narrator/d4da24b1eefe59c5.text: He's loud, cheerful and slightly drunk on his own voice. Either that's all he is, or he's very good at being it.

narrator/d510272c4814f215.text: A great iron cradle on a stone plinth, full of ash so old it has set like mortar. Soot climbs the parapet behind it in a long black tongue.

narrator/d5186ae4466f4f3c.text: You sleep in the cart shed with a watch at the door. All night, something walks the cloister in slow, even steps, and every hour it stops outside and listens, and goes on.

narrator/d5383bbc7da94213.text: A tall, mournful man in a patched jester's cap rises from behind the counter. On his shoulder sits a small monkey in a waistcoat, who looks at you with the same expression.

narrator/d54462d0168832d1.text: You rest. The village is a little quieter than it was; or you've grown used to it, which is worse.

narrator/d5645c7ce730be68.text: She weighs it, and you, and decides a mill in the hand is worth more than a fight she might lose. The bags split under the knife like ripe plums, and something goes out past you, many somethings, all in a hurry to be elsewhere.

narrator/d56a098ed1738c56.text: Two iron rings set deep in the rock, and two lengths of bright silver chain hanging from them, with cuffs at the ends. The silver is blackened on the inside of each cuff, where it has been burning someone for a month.

narrator/d56fe8e361805ec3.text: The door with the carved hand swings open, and the chanting doubles.

narrator/d5755eb5e149400d.text: A pillared chamber around a stone altar, braziers burning on either side, and robed shadows turning toward you as one. In the corner, a heap of refuse breathes, very slowly, like something asleep.

narrator/d587fdd31352f977.text: A row of narrow cells behind iron bars. It's dark in there, and the dark is breathing, quick and shallow, from more chests than you can count.

narrator/d5ab605484524612.text: She turns, slowly, and looks out across the water at the tower with the one lit window.

narrator/d5af349c28ca4ac9.text: The book on the desk is closed now. It hasn't crumbled.

narrator/d5d12025fb1aa84c.text: Two small crypts, side by side.

narrator/d60376a9d4d971f1.text: The shades boil up out of the floor between you and the stairs, hooded and hungry. They mean to hold you here until the heap can stand.

narrator/d60d90d1af46da11.text: A cook-fire, a black pot, a ladle, and a heap of carefully split wood. The Martikovs have been camping for three months and have made it look like a habit.

narrator/d61d24dd4ba0d8fd.text: She rocks, and weeps, and rocks. Whatever is under it, the weeping keeps covered.

narrator/d631557ff608b4e7.text: A broad stone hearth, the only warm thing in the village. Someone has carved initials into the mantel: a heart, two names, a date fifty years old.

narrator/d6627db08e226ebe.text: Heaps of dead brush lie in the vine rows where the blights fell when the tree burned, like scarecrows somebody forgot to finish.

narrator/d6635ac3152c1a02.text: You say so. The fight goes out of him all at once.

narrator/d6799c733e37fb7a.text: The bunting is gone, and the portraits are stacked face to the wall. The house smells of someone else's tea.

narrator/d6aa939eaf70d64d.text: From under the floor a young man's voice cries out, hoarse and eager: Father, who's there? I can smell them!

narrator/d6be21e2c64659e3.text: You take the watch in turns beside the pole. Past midnight two figures cross the square with buckets, hoods up, livery buttons catching the lamplight. Wachterhaus livery.

narrator/d71165cf10cffb0f.text: Izek comes off the cot in one movement, and the arm that isn't his starts to glow like a coal someone has blown on.

narrator/d72f01e8b2601119.text: The east guardroom, its watch relieved at last. Shards of frost and mail lie where they fell.

narrator/d7330f7e21ceb15f.text: The square is packed shoulder to shoulder. The watch walks through the crowd with clubs, listening.

narrator/d781d21855ef90f2.text: Doru drops from the ceiling without a sound. Whatever was left of the priest's son is gone behind his eyes.

narrator/d79e205d6521475f.text: She gets up the way the very old do, in stages, and goes down the far side of the hill without once looking round.

narrator/d7a539ef9c87b4ff.text: Thigh-deep in the cold, your boots find the bell where it fell: on its side in the silt, green with weed, its clapper still swinging. Wedged in the mouth of it, somebody's offerings from a long time ago, coins gone black.

narrator/d7f45f5ec025711a.text: Green-painted figures step out of the hedgerow on both sides of the road, and at their head walks an old woman you last saw among the roots of a black tree. The tree called her back, as she said it would. You let it keep calling.

narrator/d81c81ad56213833.text: The wardens' inscription, in our own plain words: "Zantras, who crowned beggars. Every king it made was pulled apart by the crowd that loved him. Do not look at it for long."

narrator/d836535755276b75.text: A slab of black stone, its grooved edges running to a drain. The drain is not dry.

narrator/d83eeedc7e01db8e.text: The family crypts, where the dead keep their own counsel. Most of them.

narrator/d85783053cb02d38.text: You raise the silver flame toward the cradle, and behind you, slow and heavy on the stair, comes armour.

narrator/d85fb37dfa14083b.text: For a long moment Izek's arm smokes at the knuckles. Then he turns his back on all of you and goes to stand somewhere.

narrator/d867567b8de44554.text: Warm, close and dark. Straw and furs, gnawed bones, the smell of animals that are sometimes people, and somewhere deeper in, small voices whispering.

narrator/d86bb575465ce86b.text: The road ends here, in a trampled half-circle of snow before the gate, as if it had walked all this way and lost its nerve.

narrator/d8b6b2968748df8d.text: Davian whistles two notes. Ravens come down out of the trees, off the eaves, off the roof of the press house, until the yard is black with them and every one is looking at you.

narrator/d8db8148afafd6a5.text: The churchyard earth heaves. Old graves split along their seams, and the village's dead climb out to finish the funeral their own way.

narrator/d928564dca821626.text: The trail climbs through pines and tumbled boulders. Through the trees, far below, the lake glints like a dropped knife.

narrator/d92cd73b5e3f6a5c.text: A cleft runs up the hill's west flank, choked with thorn and loose shale, out of sight of the camp on the shoulder.

narrator/d930c53210b6d2ac.text: The bunting sags. Somebody has turned half the Baron's portraits to the wall and then, out of kindness, turned a few of them back.

narrator/d959aaa7b813d238.text: The blights lie where they fell, dead brush in heaps around their holes. Only the druid with the lantern is still digging, and he has a spade now, and opinions about who should use it.

narrator/d95d4b27b0d0866d.text: The racks are hung with fish now, rows and rows of them, silver going grey. Nobody is going to eat them.

narrator/d9905004accfc2db.text: The headman's wagon: painted horses gallop round the sides. Inside, a child's bed, empty, its blanket thrown back.

narrator/d9a36cd29469f308.text: He closes his eyes, or the sparks dim, and when they brighten again he is smiling at you pleasantly.

narrator/d9b6c52ac25ac3c3.text: Ink, staves, a smudge that might be a tear. The notes refuse to become a tune, and the stand tips the music face down as if embarrassed for you.

narrator/d9b95e194ddb22bf.text: Stairs to the rooms upstairs. On the bottom step, a sign in Arik's square hand: ROOMS. LOCKS WORK.

narrator/d9c512721d22aa88.text: His eyes flick to Ireena, and back to you, and his smile goes stiff at the corners.

narrator/d9e7ec2b751b92a3.text: Empty crates, lids pried off, bottoms lined with grave earth. Somebody should burn them. Somebody will.

narrator/da359707965ffdbb.text: His eyes keep going back to her. Her hair, her hands, the line of her throat. Not hunger. Worse: the look of a collector at the one piece missing from a set he has spent his whole life completing.

narrator/da9879970e7b7c89.text: The frost around the cairn lies in a perfect ring, and the snow that falls on the ring doesn't settle. Something here is waiting to clap.

narrator/da9e858b824a2896.text: Two burned-out candles and two empty trestles. The room still feels like it's holding its breath.

narrator/dadb80929a8918f2.text: The great hall again. The lamp has not burned any lower.

narrator/db116b65224bd4c7.text: A long gallery of fallen frames and torn canvas. Somebody has turned the few portraits still hanging to face the wall.

narrator/db4b90c25c75cc16.text: The cliff road is a ledge cut into the mountain's side, with the drop on your right getting steadily more interested in you.

narrator/db5065f9a9457c3a.text: He chatters on, pleasant and vague. If something lies underneath, he has hidden it from himself too well for you to find.

narrator/db5128298963606a.text: Swords come off the table and go back into scabbards that have not felt them in centuries. Somewhere in the house a door bangs open, and the cold that comes through it smells of horses that aren't there.

narrator/db555c980f202fa3.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Shami-Amourae, the honeyed hand. Its lovers died smiling. All of them."

narrator/db5c0b0bbdf5fbf8.text: A sweet old woman with flour on her sleeves. You find nothing else, and she watches you look.

narrator/db6459d54a65fde6.text: A great bowl of yellow bone by the door, with a pole for steering. It is the top of a skull, and the skull was the size of a cart.

narrator/dba6b0e264778cce.text: Needle blights are scraping at the earth floor with their claws, and a druid with a lantern is telling them where.

narrator/dbc657f62f09bede.text: The lantern swings toward the ditch and stops. The lead mourner says three words, in a voice like a door that has not been opened in years: room for one.

narrator/dbe226af07b8ae86.text: All through the temple, the voices in the sarcophagi fall silent for a moment, as if a door had shut somewhere in a house they live in.

narrator/dbea4a18342c0329.text: Your voice catches his and carries it. He finds the next line, and the next, and the howling below fades under the two of you.

narrator/dc183daa56b4bae9.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Yrrga, the eye that opened outside. Its priests put out their own eyes. It was a mercy, and they knew it."

narrator/dc26207e97616f7b.text: The room drops cold enough to hurt, and the boy flings himself at the nearest of you.

narrator/dc4a2b4a313e7eba.text: He watches you reach for your weapons, and for the first time something crosses his face that isn't kindness. It looks very like grief.

narrator/dc67bb3bde191d4d.text: A tidy study: a desk, an inkstand, a bookcase of very old and very unread books. One of the shelves has no dust at its edge.

narrator/dc6d7df985ed015b.text: Pale lights bob out over the reeds, three of them, and drift toward you, swaying, the way a lantern sways in the hand of someone walking. Nobody is holding them.

narrator/dc760fe6cb67544e.text: He doesn't answer at once. The frogs stop. The wind stops. The flame in the grave-lamp, if it is lit, lies down flat.

narrator/dc8277d5f989ade7.text: The crest. The humming is very loud up here, and under it there's another sound: slow, deep, irregular, like something enormous learning how to have a pulse.

narrator/dc8ab1e4218c9baf.text: She is not afraid, and she is not resigned. She is waiting for nightfall, and for a visitor, with the calm of someone who has never once been let down by him.

narrator/dca6c9c517274a2e.text: The stair turns down into the dark. The bar has left fresh gouges in its brackets, and the bottom edge of the door is scored with marks like fingernails, from the other side.

narrator/dca7870ac751425d.text: At the bottom of the temple, beside a great hollow sarcophagus, a stooped scholar in spectacles is waiting, a book open in his hands as if he'd been reading by the amber's glow.

narrator/dcaf394fd46cfef9.text: Then she is gone, and Berez is empty at last, and the marsh goes on making its small wet sounds as if nothing has happened.

narrator/dcbf93ea1751387a.text: Painted wagons stand in a ring around a fire between the road and the black water of Lake Zarovich. Somebody is playing a fiddle very well, and nobody is dancing.

narrator/dcd01c531cb98574.text: The sails turn in the wind, creaking at every pass. A mill doing a mill's honest work, for once, even if there is nothing in it to grind.

narrator/dcddba734bfffcbb.text: Sausages, cheese, a sack of flour, and a smell of cloves. It's an ordinary pantry. That's the worst thing in the hut.

narrator/dce0a2850ea5242f.text: Figures stand in the lane ahead and behind, in the clothes of farmers and carters. One of them still has a pastry in its hand.

narrator/dd1d28d0de22ffae.text: The crypt is low and cold, lined with burial niches. In the middle, on a stone plinth, stands the sarcophagus of St. Andral, its lid pushed a hand's breadth crooked.

narrator/dd7ac4652c347e78.text: The crowd cheers. It's the first cheer of the day that nobody had to be prodded into, and the Baron very nearly weeps.

narrator/dd9ec0092cec3c2a.text: At the graveside Davian keeps looking at Adrian, like a man who has something to say and has forgotten the language it's in.

narrator/ddb572b25255b8f6.text: Ireena pushes through the crowd to you with her sword already belted on and her bag over her shoulder.

narrator/de04244186a61c8d.text: Every frog in the marsh goes silent at once.

narrator/de08fe7fdd6c42c5.text: He looks at you a long while. Then he sits down on the edge of the grave and puts the spade across his knees.

narrator/de15c0eabfbff0e8.text: The air turns cold enough to fog your breath. At the lych-gate, where nobody stood a moment ago, a tall man in a fine black coat waits, hat in hand, like a mourner who came late.

narrator/de508fd4840e52b2.text: You kneel beside him and pray aloud. For a few breaths the voice under the floor stops, as if it's listening too.

narrator/de5650ca3a86625c.text: The bridge is older than the road on either side of it, and the river under it is the colour of strong tea. Something white turns over once in the current and is gone.

narrator/de9b8e2937ff9613.text: You draw the sheet up over her face. It is the first thing in this house that has felt like a funeral.

narrator/ded75e3b016f9aa2.text: A heap of bones in a hollow, out of sight of the trail. Deer, mostly. Sheep. Further down, newer, the long bones of something that walked on two legs, cracked for the marrow.

narrator/ded82534aaee4533.text: The mountain exhales through a crack in the floor, and the breath is cold enough to stop yours.

narrator/dee5eb8b2f8548e6.text: He's off the wall before your weapons clear, laughing, and the laughter comes from the dark between the graves, where the earth has started to move.

narrator/deee71f1bc11ab98.text: A long low kitchen gone feral: straw beds, a hearth with a black pot, bones in a pile, and a dozen Belviews of all sizes who stop what they're doing and repeat your footsteps back to you on the flagstones.

narrator/df058b9cdc250bd0.text: Racks of weapons gone to rust, and a row of armour stands wearing nothing. Someone took the armour, and then someone else went on wearing it for four hundred years.

narrator/df1eeddea8d4e239.text: A young man in a robe of green-dyed sacking stands by the great press with one hand on the rim of a vat, as if he were comforting it. The mash inside shifts under his palm, and he doesn't flinch.

narrator/df2f1a9c6a42a2bf.text: A board of prices in neat black letters, each number roughly ten times what it should be. Underneath, smaller: "Browsing: free, for now."

narrator/df492ca2eeefa22b.text: She rocks the empty air one last time and is gone, the way breath goes from a window.

narrator/df815c52ec05f50e.text: It is colder in the hut than outside. Frost furs the chessboard, the shelves and the old man's beard, and none of it seems to trouble him in the least.

narrator/df8502061481721f.text: The tune is simple and sad, the kind you sing over a crib at two in the morning. As the last note fades, a second pair of hands nobody can see plays it again, softly, from the beginning.

narrator/df85a433f7bf8f21.text: A board is nailed up beside the portcullis, its letters cut deep and filled with lead so the weather couldn't take them: BY ORDER OF THE CROWN. THE ROAD ABOVE IS CLOSED. NOTHING COMES DOWN. NO ONE GOES UP. APPLY TO THE WATCH.

narrator/dfadaef52042938d.text: Long stacks furred with frost, books chained to their shelves, and a smell of ice instead of dust. Somewhere among the shelves, someone is humming a song they can't remember the end of.

narrator/dfadbf55973c8609.text: A raven drops out of the dead vines onto the lane ahead of you, hops twice, and unfolds into a lean, black-eyed man who brushes feathers off his sleeves as if they were crumbs.

narrator/dfbca9462290d8cc.text: A dead wolf hangs by one leg from a bent sapling, the snare bitten deep: silvered wire, tied with a neat, showy Vistani knot. More snares run off west, toward the little cold lake under the mountain.

narrator/dfc1cacf5bdb4021.text: A doll with red hair, a green dress and Ireena's face, exactly. Ireena looks at it for a long moment and says nothing at all.

narrator/e009bfeeb0a45a9e.text: A crow sits on a rain barrel and watches you with professional interest.

narrator/e04d529803aa3ab3.text: Far off in the house behind you, a chair scrapes back from a long table.

narrator/e05113f392fa04df.text: As they come close, the one at the front lifts his lantern to your faces, one after another, as if measuring.

narrator/e05d6606a69d405c.text: A ledge road with rock on one hand and a long drop on the other. The wind up here has opinions.

narrator/e0666914370f8dbb.text: Out of the house, into the open air, which turns out to be only slightly larger. Behind every shutter, someone is pretending not to watch you.

narrator/e07d6e92573df7e1.text: You read him the bottom of his wall. At "laughed like a goose" he laughs, and the sound is so alive that everyone flinches.

narrator/e0b2b6463d541028.text: The abbey's bell is ringing, slowly, though there's nobody in the tower. Somebody inside is still celebrating.

narrator/e0b8381af4b5a215.text: You tell her. She listens all the way through, holding the boy's hand, and her face does nothing at all.

narrator/e0babc40a0fe87c0.text: You leave it standing. The roots don't move. Walking away, you have the strong impression that they will once you've gone.

narrator/e0c7ad637d5a383d.text: A post carved with names, one under another: Osric, Melchior, Bertram, Magnus, Marvellous. Each one has been crossed out, firmly, by the same hand that carved it.

narrator/e0d4016db9b2b87c.text: Something has been through Berez since you were last here. The scarecrows lie face down in the reeds, and out on the stump the hut is lying on its side.

narrator/e0dba60de30ae5f6.text: The broom against the wall has opinions about visitors.

narrator/e0dba67c9951e639.text: The bunting is fresher than ever and the smiles are wider. In the square, a woman sits in the stocks with her back very straight, and the townsfolk walk wide around her.

narrator/e0dea8ada9a53c6d.text: Bluto stands among his drying racks up to the elbows in a net so full it has split, and silver fish flap all round his feet on the shingle. He is gutting them as fast as he can, and weeping while he does it.

narrator/e0e0c36914b1aa43.text: When it is over, the den is very quiet. Kiril, Emil, Zuleika and the last of the pack lie where they fell, and in death every one of them is only a man or a woman, and older than you thought.

narrator/e0f18967be6b0a1d.text: For a long moment he says nothing. Then he looks down at his hands as if they belonged to someone else.

narrator/e10d88f9b64745a1.text: She doesn't look up. She lifts a small loaded crossbow off her knee instead and points it at you.

narrator/e116a653b20fbdd6.text: The snow underfoot was never ground at all, only an overhang. It gives, and you slide toward the drop before your fingers find rock.

narrator/e117f2a8e14946f0.text: For a heartbeat the hunger leaves his face, and a scared boy looks down at you. Then it comes back.

narrator/e16fe5c43be3df1c.text: Five deep gouges in the bark, higher than a tall man can reach, still weeping sap. Fresh. Something stood up tall here to sharpen its claws, and wanted you to see.

narrator/e18aeb36daf466e6.text: Her whole face changes. It goes soft and pink and dreadful, like a girl's.

narrator/e1994c1526e1c22c.text: A round window of colored glass, a rising sun in reds and golds. It's the brightest thing in the church, and it is the color of dusk.

narrator/e1c2f052c44dcdc3.text: A thin boy in a too-big coat is leaning over the well, shouting his own name down it to hear it come back.

narrator/e1d7de9423ad06e7.text: The children from the road: the same faces, the same wolf. The varnish has gone brown with age, and the dust on the frame is thick enough to write in.

narrator/e1e479ffc09654eb.text: Patrina screams, and the frozen students at their desks lift their heads to scream with her.

narrator/e1f3cd9e70e6502d.text: She takes the silver horse's head, looks at it for a long time, and puts it in her own ear without a word.

narrator/e1f3f2ca0b5bd53e.text: He says it warmly, and it fits like a borrowed coat.

narrator/e232b0fabd2f9886.text: A yard of frost around a stone hut. Birds hang in the air above it, mid-flight, frozen solid, and nobody has thought to take them down.

narrator/e233df85d560aab3.text: The house is quiet. It has the stillness of something that has been fed and is in no hurry for its next meal.

narrator/e2480cfadcb3b051.text: The parlour is cold. The ring of chairs has been turned to face the wall, and Lady Wachter sits alone in black, with no tea.

narrator/e27535459f65d6cb.text: His boat is still tied at the foot of the jetty. Nobody will mind now if you take it.

narrator/e2870834d4edec97.text: The mirror is cracked clean across now, and a ribbon has been left tied round the crack like a bandage.

narrator/e2b8a4d251c83b7a.text: A great vaulted kitchen gone to straw and bones. A dozen shapes look up from the hearth at once, and every one of them makes the same small noise you just made.

narrator/e2c1417ed0ea6057.text: Someone has kissed the lid so often that the inscription has worn smooth. The prints of lips are still in the frost.

narrator/e2d0c2145cef604c.text: The ravens in the oak shuffle along their branches to make room, as if they'd like you to sit.

narrator/e3182e9f68cc10b5.text: His eyes go over you once, slowly, and stop at your hands. Whatever he sees there, he decides not to ask about it.

narrator/e321a23204a0f562.text: A thread of grey smoke still rises from the crown. Down here the dead blights lie in heaps along the track, like brush cut for a fire nobody lit.

narrator/e3295210a688fb3a.text: You knock. Inside, a chair scrapes, and a woman's voice comes through the wood, close and very steady.

narrator/e35ac154258e5256.text: The chest is full of oiled cloth, and in the cloth, two flasks of holy water and the Order's last pay chest, counted out to the coin.

narrator/e3834f8111612a0c.text: The river goes over the edge in one long white rope and vanishes into its own spray. The rock under your boots shivers with it.

narrator/e38f7424a9f137a9.text: The altar is a single block of grey stone with a sunburst carved into its face. Someone has scrubbed it so often that the sunburst is wearing away.

narrator/e3a2bd773af73762.text: One small cask for every year, set by for a wizard who never came. One of them, low on the rack, is colder to the touch than the rest.

narrator/e40f3433eb20927e.text: The causeway stones are slick and the water laps over them in places. Halfway across, the hair on your arms starts to stand up, all by itself.

narrator/e415e1c0804a2964.text: The great cave: a fire pit in the middle, furs and straw round the walls, a litter of bones, and a long scratched tally on the rock that nobody explains.

narrator/e428dadd25dfb22f.text: Izek's arm bursts into flame to the elbow. Most of the watch backs away from the priest; the ones who don't come with Izek.

narrator/e4344f383d77b115.text: The road crosses the river on a hump of old stone and comes to a crossroads with a signpost, a gallows and nobody else. The gallows, at least, has company.

narrator/e434942709906baa.text: They hesitate, then come on regardless; somebody is paying them more than you frighten them. You meet them at the pole.

narrator/e445a2a226c7095d.text: The lid has no inscription at all, only a keyhole carved in the stone with no lock behind it.

narrator/e45ac6065636a71b.text: Words cut into the archway in a plain, unlovely hand: one must die.

narrator/e45cc0ba9561181d.text: The rite is short, and Exethanter remembers every word of it. One by one, down the gallery and up through the great hall, the sarcophagi go dark, and a silence settles over the temple like snow over a grave.

narrator/e48124cd9896ebe8.text: High above, on a shelf of the mountain, the abbey's bell tower and grey roofs. Even from here you can see that one window up there is always lit.

narrator/e4915dbe9cf78a67.text: A dark little bathroom: a wooden tub on clawed iron feet, a small iron stove with a kettle on it, and a barrel under a spigot that has been dry for years. The tub is full to the brim with water as black and still as a well.

narrator/e49b68dc919129b5.text: Pines, boulders, a trickle of meltwater across the path, and the lake glinting far below through the trees.

narrator/e4a31d28c85f98e1.text: Two cold presences step inside two of you and settle, the way children settle in the back of a cart. Someone is humming now, and none of you started it.

narrator/e4a47b9569a3714f.text: The coffin rests on two trestles beside the open grave. Behind every shutter on the lane someone is watching, and none of them came.

narrator/e4a8ee3f0791f987.text: The wire parts with a ping, the jar drops, and the night turns orange.

narrator/e4de4e3faeca5000.text: A huge man in a red sash sits on the steps of his wagon with a bottle in each hand, shouting at the camp, at the lake, at the sky. The camp walks around him without looking.

narrator/e4e5db1520e048d9.text: The rod runs up the chimney and into the floors above, and it is humming, very faintly. It isn't for cooking. Something at the top of the tower is drinking from it.

narrator/e4e622dcfd54546e.text: The road climbs the last steep stretch to the tower. Faces are carved into the tower's stones, soldiers' faces, all looking down the road toward the valley.

narrator/e5017a8751e1fae8.text: Through the amber, blurred and golden, you can make out heaps of things inside. One of them is not like the rest, and it pulls at you.

narrator/e503b88e1e65ad00.text: The Baron sits at his desk in his shirtsleeves with the festival ledger open in front of him, turning the pages without reading them.

narrator/e508f8cf06e2af6d.text: The hulk in the amber hasn't moved. It never moves. But the floor under your boots hums, once, like a pleased cat.

narrator/e536e19a0841e28a.text: A thick book chained to a stone lectern, its pages beaten from copper so that they would never burn or rot. The wardens kept their most important record where no flame could reach it.

narrator/e53c2f09f22f82c6.text: You tell their story back to them plainly, every piece the house let slip on your way down, and you do not leave out the ending.

narrator/e54f51a5f4f0b67e.text: The wheel slides off the axle twice, the second time onto a foot. Clovin watches with the air of a man whose day could not, in fact, get worse, and has just been proved wrong.

narrator/e5c1fbcb4688940f.text: Ilya opens his eyes, frowns at the ceiling as if it owes him money, and says he's hungry.

narrator/e5c8328f24ee71c9.text: She steps into another of you, apologizing as she goes. Now someone in the party is humming a nursery tune that none of you started.

narrator/e5e86129fb47e418.text: Every blade on this floor has slipped its sheath. You can hear them in the rooms, testing the air.

narrator/e614799c82aab39a.text: The mirror has been turned round. Its owner looks into it, now and then, as if checking that someone is still there.

narrator/e618e314d7308f2a.text: Thorn starts to cry without making a sound. When you look back down the road a little later, the two of them stand exactly where you left them, and have not moved at all.

narrator/e61ac99813c852a7.text: When you let go of it, the bell stops. When you turn your back, it starts again.

narrator/e61d511a2e3d5388.text: One jar on the shelf is different from the others: blue glass, stoppered with wax, and inside it something silver turns over slowly, like a fish in a pool. The label is in a crabbed hand: THE CLEVER ONE ON THE MOUNTAIN, HIS REMEMBERING. DO NOT SHAKE.

narrator/e63264242abc0261.text: The oldest graves, along the north wall, sunk and tilted. Someone still sweeps them.

narrator/e64122d923d67cb1.text: A little wayside shrine to the Morninglord, its paint long gone. Someone has left a dream pastry on the ledge as an offering, still wrapped. Nothing has touched it, not even the crows.

narrator/e664418671dfa9a9.text: The vat's hoops are straining. The mash in it is the colour of moss, and as you watch, a bubble the size of a fist rises, bursts, and smells of the bottom of a pond.

narrator/e676854c4f19ada0.text: Prints, fog and old leaves, churned into one dark mess by something large, numerous and gone. Probably gone.

narrator/e6b04c050885f41d.text: It's warm inside, too warm, and close, and the floor tilts a little as the hut settles its weight. Every wall is papered with drawings of the same handsome boy at every age, in charcoal, in the same loving hand.

narrator/e6e51acfd67f963f.text: The cells empty all at once, and the noise is everyone's voice but their own.

narrator/e6e9355d9aa02725.text: The winch shrieks, the chain runs, and ahead the portcullis grinds up into the ceiling.

narrator/e6edeeed0d10d61c.text: From the top of the tower the whole tarn is laid out below, and the causeway, and Ezmerelda's fire, and far away to the east, small and black on its crag, the castle.

narrator/e6ee96a0760f7493.text: You dream of a lullaby sung through a floor, and a door that never opens.

narrator/e6f6b4445e64b7ad.text: Bundles of herbs hang drying from the roof: yarrow, valerian, and a great deal of wolfsbane. Each bundle is tied with a different coloured thread, in an order only one person understands.

narrator/e75b8fa013c990c1.text: The marks lose themselves in pine needles. The woods are very quiet, in the way that means something is listening.

narrator/e76ba87fb942f468.text: She is too perfect to read. Whatever killed her left her exactly as he wanted to remember her.

narrator/e77925a588a8548c.text: The jars stop humming one by one, like a room of people falling asleep.

narrator/e77be583737789fc.text: The trail is a pale scratch between black pines. Every so often, from the hills above, something howls, and something else answers.

narrator/e7bf52569fd56437.text: The dragon's study: burned bookcases, a broad desk, a map table, and a window facing the valley. It's the only room in the house with a chair too big for a man.

narrator/e7d0246a5db95560.text: It takes all of you. The ratchet screams, then clicks, then clicks, and somewhere below the floor the portcullis lifts out of a groove it has worn into the road.

narrator/e7dec644d407731b.text: A workshop that smells of pine and varnish. Henrik's rooms open off one side; the storeroom off the other, its door scored where the bolt has been forced and mended more than once.

narrator/e7f2c00c4191a623.text: Fiddle music, woodsmoke, and laughter, real laughter, the first you have heard in this valley. Painted wagons ring a bonfire beside a dark pool, and a great patched tent glows from within.

narrator/e83b4d936e04b7a2.text: The seams are finer than any surgeon's: wrists, throat, hairline. The left hand is older than the right; the eyes under the lids don't match. There is more than one woman here, and none of them is anyone any more.

narrator/e848af30639de5a9.text: He turns. Golden hair, a face like a saint carved by someone who had only heard saints described. For a moment the light in the chapel seems to arrange itself around him, and then it remembers itself.

narrator/e872a02d14b483b8.text: At a desk buried in loose pages sits a figure in a warden's robe gone the colour of weak tea, pinned all over with notes.

narrator/e8ac55c3e76bd874.text: A woman carved from the cave's own rock, cloaked and hooded, with no face under the hood at all and her hands held open at her sides. At her feet: bones, teeth, coins, a child's shoe, a heel of bread still soft from someone's pocket.

narrator/e8ca98d6e31e98f8.text: What's left of the stocks: two posts and a pile of slats, half of them already gone for firewood.

narrator/e8ee608c2934d75e.text: Lower down, half hidden by a pressed flower: THE JACKAL IN THE STACKS IS NOT A SCHOLAR. HIS NAME IS ASHKARRETH. SAY IT AND HE MUST ANSWER.

narrator/e8f0e23d380de9f4.text: Inside the ring of stones there's a black stump, a broken earth giant, and a great deal of ash. The wind has started, very carefully, to blow it away.

narrator/e91e41dca2077c1b.text: The cave goes down into the hill, warm, close and dark. Straw rustles in the side chambers. Somewhere deeper, small voices are whispering, and stop.

narrator/e923db339109b6ca.text: Scratches on the wall in groups of five, made with something small and sharp. Six groups and one more. Under them, in a child's careful letters, eleven more scratches, crossed out one by one in advance.

narrator/e97225d6723d3012.text: Somewhere in the walls, the house approves.

narrator/e98c8282945f9242.text: You sleep under wolf furs in a hut colder than the snow outside. Nothing on the mountain comes near the door all night; nothing would dare.

narrator/e9a1abde3f8db87e.text: The table is scarred with centuries of cards being laid down and taken up. The wood is worn into a shallow cross.

narrator/e9de57e36aec7e50.text: Something perches on the churchyard wall like a crow: Doru, his cheeks full now, his lips red, smiling.

narrator/e9e5fff41cc0cdca.text: Blue fire leaps from every nail in the floor at once, and the room smells of a lightning-struck tree.

narrator/e9fe15eb4852cbec.text: A side vault of bottles so old the dust on them has grown a pelt. Nobody has been in here for a very long time except the spiders, who seem to have opened a few.

narrator/ea1ac00f32d43ffa.text: In a hand that shakes: THE JACKAL IN THE STACKS IS NOT A SCHOLAR. HIS NAME IS ASHKARRETH. SAY IT AND HE MUST ANSWER.

narrator/ea2a1836f91119c9.text: He's asleep again before you can answer, mid-thought, the way children and the very sick do.

narrator/ea50e04c06e3cf5b.text: The cuffs are good work, but old, and the locks give to a patient hand. One, then the other.

narrator/ea55847a3d731964.text: An oak-paneled den like a hunting lodge: a stag's head over the hearth, stuffed wolves posed along the walls, two fur-draped chairs facing the fire, a card table under a dusty chandelier.

narrator/ea6840273ff3454e.text: You tell him: the woods, the wolves, the little sister who was never found. The girl the burgomaster of Barovia took in, wandering, with no memory of where she came from. The red hair. The year.

narrator/ea6ea0926eabfcc5.text: The marsh south of the Luna river, where Berez used to be. The track from the road comes in from the south-east along an old causeway. Marina's monument stands on its mound in the west; Baba Lysaga's hut squats on its giant stump in the east, ringed by scarecrows.

narrator/ea8056acb4fa878c.text: Every shelf in the shop is full of toys, and every toy is turned to face the door. When it closes behind you, a music box somewhere starts to play, all by itself, and stops.

narrator/eab975f55ce50b04.text: He takes his hand off the vat. Something in it lunges after the hand; he steps back, and keeps stepping, out of the back door and away west without looking round.

narrator/eb06851fdbc76d56.text: The road climbs out of the pines and stops dead at a wall of grey stone three men high, with one black oak gate in it and the mountain going on up behind. Somewhere inside, a goat is complaining about the weather.

narrator/eb16a4a1e22e1183.text: Blinsky looks at Ireena, and his long face goes slack. He takes off his cap, and puts it back on, and takes it off again.

narrator/eb27d88857151746.text: An earthen chamber held up by rotted posts, an old well in the middle with a rope and pulley, and alcoves around the walls where the cult slept, each with its own chest.

narrator/eb293919f9ed02f3.text: A folded sheet of good paper, written in a fast, educated hand. It's addressed to nobody, and signed with two initials.

narrator/eb322f58499f15c4.text: The first howl came from the rock face at the top of the pine slope, north and a little east of the lake, and every other voice is answering it. That is where they sleep.

narrator/eb4283f7b8035c77.text: A dumbwaiter in the wall, its little car waiting in the shaft. The rope creaks now and then, as if someone upstairs is thinking about pulling it.

narrator/eb5c0275528b4dba.text: You sleep with your backs to a winery wall and ravens on the roof above you. Twice in the night a raven calls, and both times nothing comes.

narrator/eb5c4f9ddff2b4cb.text: The sergeant's eyes, which are not really there, rest on you for a long moment.

narrator/ebb2aa65119f47f5.text: The crowd parts for the priest without being asked. They know who brought St. Andral home, and who stood beside him when he did.

narrator/ebc4c187d6daf907.text: This is what the old man's eyes kept going to, every time a word got away from him.

narrator/ebcac691d24d2fba.text: You sleep in the pavilion with your backs to the statue. In the night the pool gives off a faint warmth, like a banked hearth, and nothing comes near the wall.

narrator/ebd092649458f97c.text: You write it out in a clear hand and pin it to his sleeve among a hundred others: THESE ARE FRIENDS. DO NOT FREEZE THEM.

narrator/ebd18fb7a2fe0c6c.text: A clay stair climbing to a wooden trapdoor, bolted from this side. Fresh air seeps in around its edges, clean and cold.

narrator/ebdc70fe252948c6.text: Two small crypts, carved Rosavalda and Thornboldt, with birth years and nothing after them. They stand open, swept and waiting.

narrator/ebe61a7c22d42e30.text: Vines, flowers, satyrs chasing nymphs. Very fine work, and very ordinary. Probably.
