narrator/ebf9a2578fc78d6c.text: A rocking chair by a cold stove, a sewing basket, a girl's dress folded neatly over the arm of the chair. Someone has set two places at the table and eaten from neither.

narrator/ebfaf75133f28222.text: The Abbot lays his palms on her brow. The candles go white. When they go yellow again, her eyes are open.

narrator/ec005fa6a998bde4.text: The scholar takes off his spectacles, and his face goes with them: a jackal's head, black-lipped and smiling. One cold brazier lights itself with green fire.

narrator/ec05744abd611514.text: A history of the valley, soft with use. The spine falls open by itself to the chapter about the lord in the castle.

narrator/ec5b7360d25ef036.text: You wet a cloth in the pool water and lay it across his brow. The water doesn't warm against his skin the way it should. It stays cool, and slowly, the boy's breathing slows to match it.

narrator/ec68afe33fcf8f02.text: From the lookout the whole western valley lies open: the long grey lake, and on an island near its far shore, a tower.

narrator/ec6c45788c4201b6.text: You dream of a supper table set for twelve, and every chair turning, slowly, to face you.

narrator/eca1f5e75dfee696.text: He shrugs your hand off his collar and plants the spade between you, blade up.

narrator/ecb907939d5ef94e.text: The leather crumbles as you lift the flap. Inside, the coins of a kingdom that doesn't exist any more, still perfectly good silver.

narrator/ecc4f86523e39894.text: From under the church, faint through the stone, a voice howls for its father. Donavich's prayer breaks in half.

narrator/ecc9cc57961356ce.text: The mash has gone grey and still. Adrian is going to have to empty every one of these by hand, and you'd rather not be here when he starts.

narrator/ecd667bffbf79f6a.text: Frames on the floor, canvases slashed. In the one picture left whole, a young knight laughs at something out of frame, as if somebody just told him a joke.

narrator/ed46b956d7909bf5.text: In the amber stands a gaunt figure crowned with something that might be gold and might be teeth. One hand is raised to bless a crowd that left a very long time ago. Its eyes follow whoever is talking.

narrator/edb07b393ed34335.text: The prayer is short and plain, and for once in this valley something seems to be listening. The red ring around the bite fades, slowly, like a blush.

narrator/edbddae6d6559504.text: Morgantha stands, and keeps standing, taller than the rafters should allow, and the sweetness goes out of her face like water out of a basin. Under the floor, the grain bins come alive with rats.

narrator/edcb21dc011b177a.text: One row at the bottom of the east vineyard is still green, just. The ravens sit along its trellis like a guard of honour.

narrator/ee1677a25702477f.text: A very large young man is stacking sacks of flour into a perfect pyramid, counting under his breath. He stops at forty-one and looks down at you, pleased.

narrator/ee1772cc74d0b2f4.text: Old bones in an old sheet. The sheet tells the story better than you can.

narrator/ee593510f2e4e9fc.text: A thin figure in the amber has its face tipped up, eyes wide, lips moving, as if reading a sky that isn't there. The amber over its eyes is scratched, from the inside.

narrator/ee7c3e2c9e530e2b.text: The Belviews say he went down the mountain once, at dawn, laid a hand on the burgomaster's boy, and climbed back up without a word. That was the last thing he did.

narrator/eea8f456e1e86daa.text: Her eyes go perfectly round. She takes it between two fingers, very politely, and eats it in one bite. Then she sits down on the floor, slowly, smiles at nothing at all, and begins to snore.

narrator/eeb94d6b17189336.text: The bookcase swings inward on oiled hinges, and a breath of cold candle smoke comes up the stair behind it.

narrator/eebd85fe66297267.text: Vasilka is still standing by her bier in her wedding dress, hands folded, waiting very patiently for someone to tell her what happens next.

narrator/eec8e55036074400.text: A stuffed grey wolf, posed mid-stride with its lips curled back. The taxidermist was very good, or the wolf was very angry.

narrator/eee10e86186ef6bf.text: The doors close the wind out, and the silence that comes in its place is worse. The walls are veined with amber that glows, faintly, like embers under ash.

narrator/ef0e5583621973d5.text: Four skulls rise from the top shelves, each wearing a crown of green fire. They were wardens once, and they still are.

narrator/ef0fb2da8257147d.text: The thin figure in the amber has stopped reading its missing sky. It looks at whoever carries its gift with something like pity.

narrator/ef2ecb1ab8f25d2b.text: The windows are shuttered or simply gone. Fire went through this house once, room by room, and it took its time.

narrator/ef2ff5c125ab2325.text: She looks at you for a long moment, and decides to believe you. It costs her something.

narrator/ef34c94643ad0e8e.text: The square is empty. The pastry cart has gone, leaving two wheel ruts that lead out of the village toward the west.

narrator/ef4db036438bdf14.text: The hut on the stump leans down toward you on its knotted legs of root, like a dog sniffing at a stranger. A shutter bangs open. A tiny old woman looks out, with a face like a walnut and eyes like two wet currants.

narrator/ef6809bad50b6f5f.text: His hands are steady, but he hasn't blinked in a while. Three young men in the trees, all his kin by their noses. They are more afraid of you than you are of them, which makes them dangerous.

narrator/efa5ad5a0996a659.text: A fire of old wagon wood with a cauldron over it, something with paprika bubbling. Nobody offers you any. Nobody stops you looking, either.

narrator/efbe84c54584a18e.text: A dozen little bags of greasy leather hang from the hooks, each tied with a hair ribbon, each faintly warm. Hold one to your ear and, very far away, somebody is crying.

narrator/efea7fafeeb87543.text: The earth on this grave has been turned since the last snow, and filled back in with care, by someone who didn't want it noticed. The stone sun on top is facing the wrong way.

narrator/efeda541ba8c5b5c.text: For a moment the young druid looks at the press, the rafters, the vines through the open door, as if counting how old each of them is.

narrator/efee27bbe7926f94.text: Splintered boards, fresh nails, a long scorch on the hall floor: the house held. It looks surprised about it.

narrator/f000b80b0b683003.text: The light goes out of the air slowly, settling like dust. The church is just a church.

narrator/fdb9e35e5a025b47.text: The sparks in his eyes go very still.

narrator/fdbb95c830b490d4.text: Morgantha stands, and keeps standing, taller than the rafters should allow. In the corner Bella lays down her mirror; on the stair, Offalia's heavy tread. Three voices begin to hum the same tune.

narrator/fe39f354da7cc77a.text: What was the main street is a channel of black water between roofless houses. A child's shoe sits on a windowsill, placed there carefully, by someone, long after the flood.

narrator/fe571064e6b33d12.text: Armour stands with nothing on them but cobwebs, and a rack of helmets with the names still painted inside.

narrator/fe872211495aee14.text: Walter's nurse. They didn't let her go far.

narrator/fe9444c0dec215a3.text: You leave her there. When you look back from the door she's still standing, hands folded, turned toward the empty altar step, waiting.

narrator/fecd170fd747dc3c.text: You take her arm. She lets you, which is how you know how frightened she was.

narrator/fed0a6f08de95ae0.text: A plain church, cold and clean, rows of pews under a great gilded sunburst. Candles burn all along the altar rail. Nobody lit them that you saw.

narrator/fee469d08bc96f40.text: A long corridor of whitewashed stone. On the wall, at a child's height, someone has drawn a line of little suns in charcoal, all the way to the end, as if to light the way.

narrator/ff03ac419303a683.text: You know where he lies now, and someone should lay him in here. It won't be anyone in this house.

narrator/ff64243e2f9e987f.text: Narrow rooms with clean beds and shutters that lock from the inside, which is the first thing anyone checks.

narrator/ffbc3df6402821e0.text: Offerings to the tree: coins, herbs, a healer's kit, a staff of black wood. The faithful brought their best. It didn't help them.

narrator/ffc78af55182da1d.text: The last of the Baron's loyal sergeants is down, and the rest of the watch has quietly put its spears on the ground. The crowd comes up onto the dais. Nobody lays a hand on the Baron; they simply stand around him until he sits down on the edge of the boards like a tired child.

narrator/ffed7380d0046ab2.text: A little shrine on a post, a fish carved on its roof, fish bones in its bowl. Somebody painted TO THE LAKE, WHO FEEDS US on the post, and somebody else has scratched out FEEDS.

offalia_wormwiggle/20e7da63ef42be20.text: I looked all along the road and Mother wasn't there. Mother's cross with me. I can feel it from here.

offalia_wormwiggle/276cf3e7588a9987.text: I'm telling Mother you told a fib. Mother likes to know who fibs. She writes them in her book.

offalia_wormwiggle/36c95ac15a32725c.text: From the big stone, silly. You put things in the top and turn it, and it comes out the bottom soft as soft. Mother says you mustn't waste anything. Not the marrow. Not the teeth.

offalia_wormwiggle/3b09625d1e9fdbac.text: I'm not allowed to touch them. Not even the small one. Not yet.

offalia_wormwiggle/3b13dd900fd59654.text: Nobody tells me to step away from Mother's oven. Nobody. Only Mother.

offalia_wormwiggle/3de04b030ffc9e32.text: Dream pastries! Two hundred a week. Mother does the honey, Bella does the wrapping because she's got nice hands, and I do the flour. I'm best at the flour.

offalia_wormwiggle/3e597efff4555787.text: Mother's gone. I went home and the oven was cold. Nobody tells me what to do now. I've eaten all the hedges.

offalia_wormwiggle/490253deeabb8edd.text: No, you're just the right size for one. Mother would say so. Mother says so about everybody.

offalia_wormwiggle/78be41e75b1dc871.text: Back again! Did you want a pastry? They're still warm. They're always still warm.

offalia_wormwiggle/791f041096a114f2.text: You read Mother's book? Nobody reads Mother's book. Did you get flour on it? Please say you didn't get flour on it.

offalia_wormwiggle/872be9fcd4105758.text: The little ones? They're Mother's. Paid for and everything. They're upstairs, keeping. Mother says you don't touch what's keeping.

offalia_wormwiggle/9a8e80cf53e62366.text: Silly. Mother's upstairs. I can hear her rocking. Can't you hear her rocking?

offalia_wormwiggle/c41c7d59bdb854b5.text: Ooh, visitors! Are you deliveries? Mother never said there'd be deliveries. You're ever so big for deliveries.

offalia_wormwiggle/d82ca6a4f0c7b528.text: Really? She's not cross? Oh, thank you, thank you. I'll go straight home. I'll only stop at the good hedges.

offalia_wormwiggle/db480fed6086ba29.text: On the road? Mother never goes down to the road on a baking day! Is she cross? She sounds cross when she calls like that.

offalia_wormwiggle/f1c84ab0f03c0593.text: Everybody! The village. The farms. Folk on the Vallaki road. Mother writes them in her book with what they owe. Nobody can pay, after a while. That's the best part. That's when Mother goes visiting.

offalia_wormwiggle/f6efbd21c44c6106.text: You're the ones. You're the ones from the mill.

order_knight/033e22728e7133ad.text: We march when you march. Tell Godfrey his grey mare is ready.

order_knight/162ff0e6edbe59ad.text: Halt. This is the Order's road. State your business.

order_knight/20a0d62a0cf138db.text: The Order marches when you march. Until then we walk the roads. Go safely.

order_knight/42c4b4dc0d1e7437.text: The Order of the Silver Dragon. We keep the watch. Ask at the house.

order_knight/527eaa5478f78c97.text: He lives. We watch. Pass, oath-sworn.

order_knight/7c2422cea9d07664.text: One of his. It came down the road toward Vallaki carrying a message. It does not carry messages now.

order_knight/a0f966021f61271b.text: I had one. It was a good one.

order_knight/c3e2f872270d308f.text: Then go carefully. The commander does not care for guests. Sir Godfrey does. Ask for Sir Godfrey.

order_knight/c662a73180b691cc.text: The commander will wish to speak with you. He will not like what you say.

order_knight/fa328a6e48ee85ee.text: The old woman. She passed this way once, before these trees were tall. She asked us the time. We did not know it.

parriwimple/039c355d0915c72a.text: Hello. Uncle says to say welcome. Welcome.

parriwimple/092d288d50b4568c.text: I can carry that. I'll bring the shovel too, and dig. Uncle won't mind. Uncle will mind. I'll go anyway.

parriwimple/0ae41dd556cb9410.text: Me? In the cards? Nobody ever saw me in anything before.

parriwimple/183cb08da1ec5b5a.text: I dug it deep. Six feet. I measured with my arm, twice. Then I made it a little deeper, for the wolves.

parriwimple/244111178045b2fc.text: Uncle says my time costs money. Five gold an hour. You'd have to ask Uncle. He likes being asked.

parriwimple/3bee90f2e6a2402d.text: Days. Since the burgomaster died. Three. Nobody else counted, I think. Somebody should.

parriwimple/44f34ce2259222a6.text: The grave's ready. I put the dirt in a neat pile, so it goes back in neat. Uncle says neat is respect.

parriwimple/660e9fe6ad7ca559.text: Again. No. Don't, Uncle will charge you for the flour. But that was the best thing I ever saw. I'll remember you.

parriwimple/6eba26bc8bb3fdbc.text: I didn't like it. I carried the sacks fast.

parriwimple/86cca363b3e14c10.text: Hello again. I remembered you. I don't remember everybody.

parriwimple/b3d952e9db13ebbd.text: The pie lady. Uncle won't let me eat them; he says they cost money. She lives in the old windmill on the Vallaki road. I carried sacks there once. It smelled like bread. And like not bread.

parriwimple/c06b02821b9fe4ce.text: Thank you? I think? Uncle says people say nice things when they want a discount. There's no discount.

parriwimple/d7f113883d7f57b0.text: Nobody says that. Uncle says I'm a good lifter. That's nearly the same. Thank you. I'll remember you.

parriwimple/e4d1e28403f32437.text: Uncle says I'm not to leave the shop. Uncle says a lot. I can carry your packs. I can carry you, if you fall down. I'll count the days we're gone so he knows.

patrina_velikovna/235ec244fd8e9dc9.text: I came up here to learn what the lord of the valley knew. Then I went down to his castle to learn the rest.

patrina_velikovna/262a4952877ba709.text: Go home, little brother. Don't bring me back. Don't make bargains. Be brave somewhere I can't see you; it will annoy me less.

patrina_velikovna/2e4ab0d3d3927b1d.text: ...There. That wasn't so hard. Three centuries, and it took you one breath.

patrina_velikovna/2ec5d645bb956a74.text: A student. I was the cleverest of my people, which was not difficult, and the only curious one, which was.

patrina_velikovna/37f2d353c06448db.text: You again. Have you come to stare, or have you finally brought me something worth reading?

patrina_velikovna/3842652def920bc1.text: Then let him be afraid a little longer. Get out of my library.

patrina_velikovna/490bd7d988c1bd5f.text: Rest. Everyone always wants me to rest. ...Perhaps I'm tired. Perhaps I've been tired for a long time.

patrina_velikovna/8a97bc7db45dceca.text: No. I've done my living. If Kasimir wants to do something for me, he can stop being sorry and start being brave. He'll know what I mean.

patrina_velikovna/8fc4e25ca41792b4.text: Living people. In my library. Do you know how long it's been since anyone in this valley had the nerve to climb up here and read?

patrina_velikovna/930cfcdadcb5a1de.text: The same page I was reading when I left. It's about him: how a prince became a lord forever. I thought if I understood it, he would see me as an equal.

patrina_velikovna/96a2897f2a623914.text: Of course. Stones, or steel. It's always one or the other with people like you.

patrina_velikovna/97a080cd5e4fa458.text: Bring me back. To what? To a valley that stoned me, a brother who watched, and a lord who has had four centuries to find someone cleverer?

patrina_velikovna/9d9968470de5c8b2.text: My people threw stones at me until I stopped moving. So I came back here. It's the only place I was ever free.

patrina_velikovna/9d9e7f8a9931259c.text: Then say it properly. Not to them. To me.

patrina_velikovna/b41a2e5df101027a.text: Your gods don't climb this high. Mine never did either. Don't preach at me in my own library.

patrina_velikovna/b71a9de1db00df29.text: ...Kasimir. You climbed a mountain. You. I'd have bet my bones against it, if I still had the use of them.

patrina_velikovna/c201c3c30a7aec91.text: He did, for a while. That's the trouble with being clever. Someone always finds a use for it.

patrina_velikovna/c2be372e39961435.text: Don't you dare. Don't you dare buy me back from a thing in a box, like a coat out of pawn.

patrina_velikovna/d8c4867d6e346934.text: Tell him I'm done waiting. Tell him the stones didn't hurt as much as the quiet afterward. He'll understand that. He was always very good at quiet.

patrina_velikovna/db39a3b0dc63a10f.text: ...Afraid. Yes. He always was. And he admits it now? That's new. That's very nearly brave.

patrina_velikovna/dceee58875d1fa3f.text: Kasimir. You've met Kasimir. Is he still mending nets by a Vistani fire and calling it penance?

patrina_velikovna/ddc662d44e0b15ce.text: Sorry. He's sorry. Three hundred years, and he sends strangers up a mountain to say it for him.

patrina_velikovna/de8dcd601de717a4.text: He stood at the back. Did he tell you? Everyone was throwing, and my brother stood at the back with empty hands, and watched.

phantom_warden/275fdea9032ac35a.text: None pass to the dragon's rest but the Order. Name your oath, or turn back.

phantom_warden/3cc82a5f8e69eca5.text: Godfrey. He was always letting strays in. Pass.

phantom_warden/4a200cf55cb8d764.text: The old form. Nobody has used the old form since... Pass.

phantom_warden/8055d46ae3684b28.text: Those are the words. Pass, brothers.

phantom_warden/a03d40932dbcd3a5.text: To tend it. ...Nobody has tended it since the squires died. Pass, and mind your feet by the bier.

phantom_warden/b8e696bbb505ae73.text: I opened the gate once. I'll not open this one.

phantom_warden/edbe75b624b08588.text: Not the words. I opened a gate once, to a voice that sounded right. I'll not do it twice.

rictavio/06a35e1fc8575f1f.text: It's the only one I've ever seen work. Briefly.

rictavio/0905d1808a1eb359.text: The same as you, I expect, only for longer. I came to see whether the lord of this valley can be killed. I'm still deciding. I am also, I'm afraid, still deciding whether I care to survive the answer.

rictavio/090d2c6471f2f7e8.text: I told you once what I think of people who help this valley choose its masters. Words are cheap here. What have you done since?

rictavio/132578667bee3dfe.text: Ezmerelda. You went through the ward.

rictavio/1470fc1d27cecffe.text: Cards! Gypsy nonsense! Fortune-telling for the gullible!

rictavio/1724568071ef5a8c.text: Eva's cards again. And I hear five children walked down out of the wolves' hills because of you. That counts for something. It counts for a great deal.

rictavio/18c52cdfbd6fb32e.text: Someone has been in my wagon. No, don't deny it; I leave a hair across the lock. You're alive, so you didn't open the cage. Good. That was the most important thing.

rictavio/1a7edab3ec2e330c.text: Not that name. Not here. Rudolph van Richten made a great many enemies, and some of them have extremely long lives. Rictavio has none. I would like to keep it that way.

rictavio/1c811af458c80dc4.text: And if you can't, bar the church and stand in it. Holy water. Fire. Don't let them get behind you.

rictavio/209aeacce5720468.text: You're hunting a good night's sleep, I expect. So am I. Goodnight!

rictavio/25749d0b0678189a.text: That town chose its master, and I watched who helped it choose. I came home to think about whether anything in this valley is worth the trouble. I've been thinking for a week. It's gone very badly.

rictavio/262619061eaeec97.text: And you've read my journal, so there's no use in feathers.

rictavio/282b1f6c27de0792.text: You. How did you... Khazan. Of course. She found the name, and you walked in on it. I taught her to find things. I should have taught her to stop.

rictavio/30d8da1fbbdd500f.text: Very well. I'm too old to hunt alone, and you are much too young to be doing it at all. I'll come.

rictavio/3405d4e110a7ef94.text: Very well. I am too old to keep hunting alone, and you are much too young to be doing it at all. I'll come. The wagon stays; the beast in it is the only creature in Barovia I trust to guard my notes.

rictavio/3a1ced185966179b.text: Keep your voice down and your back to the wall. What do you need?

rictavio/3d168f305d47470b.text: I know. I can hear her. Everyone within a mile can hear her.

rictavio/467601bb062c58f9.text: Everywhere, and recently. I go where the audiences are. Here, there are no audiences, so I suppose I've come to rest.

rictavio/46d0bbe2f815ee20.text: Then come back when you have. I'll be here. I'm not going anywhere quickly these days.

rictavio/518f9a32f1fe99a8.text: And don't tell me what Eva's cards say. I know what they say. I won't stand beside people who handed a town to him, whatever the cards want.

rictavio/5742e59de32f4d11.text: Then he means to send his spawn for the church, and whoever is sheltering in it. They'll be close by, somewhere dark, somewhere nobody looks. Spawn sleep by day like anyone who works nights. Find their beds while the sun is up, and you choose the fight.

rictavio/59542027a13df3cf.text: It's a costume. It's a very good costume.

rictavio/5ad08290d8b1fc54.text: My audience returns! Twice in one week. In Barovia that's practically a following.

rictavio/60146b3c8d1d2613.text: Eva's cards again. And the ravens tell me two children came home from a hags' mill on the Vallaki road, because of you. Hags don't give anything back. That counts.

rictavio/634183adca5337c1.text: Both of them will get people killed. Vargas from fear, Fiona from faith. One of them only wants the town to be quiet. The other wants it quiet for him. I'd want neither in charge of a dog kennel.

rictavio/647e2132f89bfcd3.text: Friends! Strangers! Strange friends! Rictavio, at your service: teller of tales, singer of songs, proprietor of the most marvellous carnival wagon in seven valleys, which none of you may look inside!

rictavio/67c8323142be15b9.text: Have you now. A scholar. How dangerous for you.

rictavio/682ac7919ac1e224.text: The ward upstairs is down too. I'd rather not have to explain how I cooked my own guests.

rictavio/694bdd83070b02a3.text: Take these. I've more than I need, and you, I suspect, have less.

rictavio/78c5e6ef7f127522.text: Ah. My front door. Stand back, please; it's particular about company.

rictavio/834e14eb4f41ca75.text: Farewell, farewell! Tell your friends! Tell your enemies! Tell anyone, really; I'm not particular.

rictavio/85bdf7d3e419d3fd.text: I know that face. Thirty years older and wild as a goat, but I know it. Good God. They told me he was dead.

rictavio/85efc5a375448c06.text: A tale! There was once a hunter who chased a monster across the whole world, and caught it, and killed it. And do you know what he found? That there was always another monster. The end. It goes better with a lute.

rictavio/8639724b13d1db19.text: Eva's cards again. And there's a silver light on the ridge over Argynvostholt, where there's been none for four hundred years. Somebody lit it. That counts for a great deal.

rictavio/869b063e047979ad.text: Stay in the light where you can. And when you can't, stay together.

rictavio/87f684ff6f7259c2.text: A beast! A marvel! A creature that would eat a horse and then complain about the seasoning. I keep it locked away for its protection as much as yours. Mostly yours.

rictavio/8b856f84b424305c.text: Goodbye. I hope you find a better ally than your judgement.

rictavio/8f62deb6f19ebb49.text: She has made me promise never to key a ward to anyone again. I have agreed to nothing. She knows I have agreed to nothing.

rictavio/934ce88767b17b26.text: Clever. Patient. Bored, which is the dangerous part. He plays with people the way a cat plays, and like a cat he gets careless when he's amused. Keep him amused, and wait.

rictavio/968243c1bd243bf6.text: Thank you. People rarely keep secrets in Barovia. It's not malice; it's that he asks so nicely.

rictavio/a46ff5184f738ba7.text: And you let it go. I understand. I did that once. It found me again eleven years later, and it remembered my kindness very precisely.

rictavio/a9e8b9803955e2fc.text: Still here. You've a talent for being where you shouldn't. I used to.

rictavio/af5e6687fda271c9.text: I'm going home to think: a tower on the little lake under the mountain, west of Zarovich. If you do something worth hearing about, come and tell me there. Bring proof. Not speeches.

rictavio/bb288d78f7331c27.text: Reasons. Old ones. I came home to think. I've been thinking for a week, and it's gone very badly.

rictavio/c1d9e833b4cbcc72.text: I keyed the ward to her because everyone I have ever taught is in the ground, and she is the last. If she can't get in, she can't follow me where I'm going.

rictavio/c330f89b47913b54.text: And you've been in my strongbox upstairs. Keep it. Where you're going, you'll need it more than I will.

rictavio/c5ebffa90d3a51d3.text: A bad bargain, and a pretty speech about it. I've had better speeches from vampires. Much better.

rictavio/ce2709ef2448e303.text: Everyone I have ever taught is in the ground, Ezmerelda. You are the last. I would like you to stay the last.

rictavio/d8846064ac542919.text: Eva. Of course it was Eva. That old woman has been shuffling me about this valley for longer than I care to count.

rictavio/dca72d665817cb97.text: This town has chosen its master, and I watched who helped it choose. I won't sleep another night under a roof that bows to him. I'll be gone by morning, wagon and all.

rictavio/e62b6f69eea2ff48.text: Hunting? I hunt applause, and rarely catch it.

rictavio/e8b09842c300913f.text: Eva's cards. I have spent thirty years refusing to be anybody's fortune.

rictavio/ec1e7fd812ba1882.text: ...Words are cheap in this valley. Deeds are what I'll watch. I'll come, and I'll be watching.

rictavio/f87e25a2c5cba2b3.text: And you put it down. Good. Every one of them was somebody. That's the part the books don't prepare you for.

rose/0852c0344261550c.text: You'll have to undo the knot. Thorn tied it. It's a bad knot.

rose/0ce2a9a25133f11f.text: Is it over? Is the noise over? Mother said she'd unlock the door when the noise downstairs stopped.

rose/1df65b026d662a0b.text: He was with Nurse. Then he wasn't, and Nurse cried, and then Nurse stopped crying.

rose/1fef71d2be3827ba.text: Mother hid her purse under the bottom stair in the hall, under the loose board. She said it was for emergencies. I think this is one.

rose/21237a1b174144b6.text: We hid in the toy chest when it got cold. Our bones are still there. Our crypts are downstairs, by Grandmother's. Mother showed us.

rose/2ef2fd666170284c.text: It's quiet in here. Thank you. Thorn, say thank you.

rose/3be2f79fa16bb885.text: Outside? We haven't been outside since the leaves were green. Mother won't let us.

rose/49bae72b3a377f8e.text: No, Thorn. I think everyone else is.

rose/526982f796781a4a.text: Please, you have to help us. Something horrible lives in our house, down in the basement.

rose/5c46e3fd14101047.text: Thank you. Thank you. We'll wait here. We're very good at waiting.

rose/68c81a7ca0c7754a.text: Our baby brother. He's down there crying, and we can't go back in. We can't. Please.

rose/6c38e3b84e91d468.text: The tall one just inside the village, by the dead tree, with the iron gate. Mother says it's the finest house in Barovia.

rose/7ec1a8f640b137df.text: They went downstairs with their friends and they didn't come back up.

rose/86d1ecd311e68b58.text: Everyone says that. Come back. Please come back.

rose/a36b0566b30c053d.text: Father made it for my birthday. He made it too well. It even has the stair they use at night. I found it with a hairpin.

rose/a755ddf229a065f9.text: We never saw it. We hear it, at night, through the floor. Like something heavy being dragged.

rose/acad79018e495021.text: We're always here. We're always waiting. Mother said to wait.

rose/bbd2d891e607370a.text: He's frightened. We both are. Please don't leave us.

rose/cc2b62a37fff4826.text: Oh. That's why we're never hungry anymore.

rose/ccda8d892cabb1bf.text: Mother and Father. The people in robes mustn't see us, they said, and we mustn't see them. They'd come back up when it was over.

rose/e8b4608e590e14fc.text: Thorn! Come out of there! ...Fine. Then I'm coming too.

rose/f05ac2cb9de1a4ce.text: Mother doesn't pray to the Morninglord anymore. She says he never answers, and the other one does.

rose/fcc9d4870ef4d655.text: Hold still. It doesn't hurt. Thorn, say sorry first.

rose/fdbae4415f24bdd8.text: Did you find him? Did you find Walter?

ruxandra/1a94fedd7e64c169.text: Then come and take it, children. Sing, all of you. Sing him awake.

ruxandra/371bb9ff9053f1d1.text: Guests. The hill gets so few guests. Mostly it gets offerings.

ruxandra/5926bc68b44d10b0.text: No. I don't think so. Sing, children. Louder.

ruxandra/5a66e6a4de2f1322.text: Kostin told us you'd come. He was ashamed. I told him shame is only fear that has been taught manners.

ruxandra/6183d26477f5b255.text: Cowards. It doesn't matter. He has heart enough for all of us.

ruxandra/631037fbbe90521a.text: Mercy. How like strangers. ...I'll go. The tree will call me back. It always calls us back.

ruxandra/7334cdec8e9cc2e5.text: Older than the castle. It grew from a stake pulled out of something that should have stayed dead, far away and long ago, and the mists carried the seed here, as they carry everything. It drinks. We give it to drink.

ruxandra/74b51618e039dd33.text: The black-eyed boy. Yes. He told his brother to fly, and the brother flew, and the boy laughed at us all the way up the hill. He stopped laughing, in the end. The tree is very thorough.

ruxandra/aba2cf9921f8dd05.text: We heard you in the gully, children. The hill hears everything. It's mostly ears.

ruxandra/b500006fc6512856.text: You broke him. You broke the heart. ...Well. The land will grow another. It always does.

ruxandra/e814434651f6f3b2.text: You've come for the bird-man's stone. It isn't his now. It's the heart of something better. Listen: you can almost hear it beating.

ruxandra/f9fb3eaebef59bec.text: The bird-man's son? He sent his brother away. Ordered him off like a dog. He was proud of it; he told the tree so at the end. The tree didn't care. Trees don't.

sergei_von_zarovich/1e149fdd77586c69.text: Then be someone. That is all I ever wanted for her.

sergei_von_zarovich/8aec54a73ae81db9.text: I am. I have had practice.

sergei_von_zarovich/e68f06756231ab31.text: The water is the only door I have. I cannot come out. You could come in. When you are ready. Not before. It will wait. I will.

sergei_von_zarovich/f08ccd92875ce202.text: No. Not this time. But you came to the water. You always did, in the mornings, before the bells.

silvain_aster/01cf2d858729b915.text: Lycanthropy, but ravens. The literature is very thin. I'd like it noted that I am being extremely restrained about asking them questions.

silvain_aster/0377c6a91d71da63.text: No. It's what fear does when it's been in love too long.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/5fafe414210f32f6.text: I am. It comes and goes, how much I mind.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/613a7a44b929395c.text: I'll put you down as the one who asked.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/623c392c50d4720d.text: Be the light. Not "hate the dark". We swore to be the light, and we've been sitting in the dark for four hundred years keeping score.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/6466086714787ecc.text: You'll mention the castle. Everyone does.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/6775a32f41d84d4e.text: The Lantern Company. Twenty men we sent over the passes for help, the week before the end. They came back too late, and the young lord's archers were waiting on our own road.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/695d41359906052b.text: Then a young lord came over the mountains with an army. We lost. We died. We got up again. That last part wasn't in the oath.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/702ee54db7f0181e.text: The oath's still there. I checked this morning, the way you'd pat a pocket for your purse. Still there.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/709d74e8c14f9640.text: Still here. Still me, mostly. What do you need?

sir_godfrey_gwilym/714d00242d5dceaf.text: Vladimir. Please. Look at what's in their hands.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/752c2eaad350e279.text: They ride home every night. They never get here. I go down to the gate sometimes, to see if tonight's the night.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/770fe3b8db864418.text: And St. Andral's has its saint back, I hear. Good. I was christened under that roof, I think. Or one very like it.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/78d594322991decc.text: Cold. You lot are warm, though. I'd forgotten people were warm. I keep standing too close; tell me if I do.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/80aeaea89647f757.text: I've written all your names on the inside of my gauntlet. In case. You don't mind?

sir_godfrey_gwilym/8265c7d332b834ae.text: Stand easy, Piet. They're with me.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/91ac9a3cee42dfd7.text: The light's still pulling at me, very gently, like a child at a sleeve. I don't mind. It means it'll be there when I'm done.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/98f82c5559f6a3eb.text: Do you think so? I've wondered.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/a0ca13cff01065fa.text: But some nights I can't remember why we swore what we swore. I remember that it mattered. I've lost the words for the rest.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/a9e1740e3e4c4cd4.text: Back again. Good. The house is better with somebody breathing in it.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/baffb1d75728c777.text: I'm with them, Vladimir. Put me down as absent.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/bfe4b45b4b29c2cc.text: I'll write it on the inside of my gauntlet. I write everything down now.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/c9ab46f3276c7bb3.text: Then I'll come. I'll tell the commander myself, so he hears it from me and not from the hall. He'll say I'm a fool. He's said it before. It has never once stopped me.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/cae45f233069c797.text: There wouldn't be. The young lord kept the libraries, after.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/d2639688c06f08b6.text: Brothers. Hear them out. I did, and I remember things I'd lost.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/dcbacc496a0af82b.text: You swore his oath. I heard you. I'm not angry. I swore it too, once, and it took me four hundred years to hear what I'd said.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/ddc2da278151928f.text: Thank you. Tell the old woman her cards were right about me, and that I was very tired.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/de2279e9c60b9863.text: It's calling. It's warm. ...Not yet. I promised somebody a ride. I'll come when the castle's done, and the light will still be here.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/de58c19c92cfbddc.text: Teodor. The pears were Teodor's. I've been remembering his pears for years and thinking they were mine.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/e78f6c2d8d6823b7.text: "Remember the oath." I wrote that for tonight, I think. I just didn't know it.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/e8c1ee3b4ed48cd2.text: Pears. I remember pears very clearly. And a grey mare who bit everyone but me. And my sister Gwenllian, who laughed like a goose. I've lost her face. I've still got the laugh.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/ea3825a5f90eda63.text: The cards. The old woman's cards wanted me, didn't they? I can feel the light pulling. I could go now. I'd like to.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/ecb56e1681c0e431.text: The town with the festivals? The patrol says the singing carries all the way up the ridge. It isn't happy singing. It's very loud singing.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f142b3dabe87e177.text: It's kind of you. It isn't enough, not yet. Find me the words, if you can. They're carved somewhere in this house. I used to know where.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f3943f3c6235ef4a.text: I'd go. I'd go tonight. But I'd be half a knight. I've lost the oath, and a knight without his oath is a man standing in a great deal of tin.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f681f11517f970f3.text: The road patrol said you'd be coming. They said you were polite. That's rare enough that they mentioned it twice.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f787802f1769b31e.text: Sir Godfrey Gwilym, of the Order of the Silver Dragon, or what's left of it. You'll want the commander. Everyone does, eventually. Then they wish they hadn't.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/ff475f0e82e94b5e.text: Something new. I haven't had anything new since... well. Since.

sorvia/0761c60ad36005ab.text: What? They'd work it out. They're not stupid. Look at them; they're nearly clever.

sorvia/0d8ea912cc4195c5.text: He knows you're here, you know. The lord. He knew before you did. He always does, because we...

sorvia/3339c34a6a372e78.text: You'll meet a tall, dark stranger. Everyone here does. Only once, usually.

sorvia/52a35ec7daedbe25.text: She's nice. She mended my horse's bridle once and wouldn't take a copper. I hope... nothing. More wine?

sorvia/5d1bad293f552b24.text: And he hasn't finished with you. He's hardly started.

sorvia/6c73533c3182b24a.text: So many lines. You've read too much. One day a book is going to read you back.

sorvia/b741e43ad4a77925.text: A line of faith straight down the middle, and a crack right across it. Don't worry. Cracks let the light in, Grandmother says. Also the wind.

sorvia/bd375fb97ce9012d.text: Your life line is long. It's just that something keeps trying to cut it. There, see? Teeth marks.

sorvia/c154b9df358683f5.text: This hand has been in a great many pockets. One of them belonged to someone very, very old. My advice? Give it back. Mirabel's advice will be to sell it.

sorvia/d753fabffbc9ae01.text: Oh, yes! Give it here. Not you, Mirabel, I know yours; it says you'll die of being rude.

sorvia/d9de2be2b1d0cd8e.text: Your boots have walked farther than boots should, in this valley. Sorry. I notice things.

stanimir/08d8095dca3571c5.text: Nicu. My sister's boy. He rode to Vallaki to sell a horse, and he came home by the crossroads after all.

stanimir/1f6dc2ade61dc2df.text: Pay her what she asks. It is never only money, and it is never more than you can spare. Usually.

stanimir/20cf33fb024316a7.text: Madam Eva has been old since my grandmother was a girl. She reads the cards for whoever the road brings, and the road brings whoever the cards want.

stanimir/20d74d2a834eca05.text: Everyone knew your father. He shouted at me for an hour once, about a horse. Best conversation I had that year.

stanimir/23d69df75df8c44b.text: You showed the old woman your teeth in her own tent. I play the fiddle at my fire, friends; I don't play the fool. Mind your manners in that tent.

stanimir/24b63ff492a7a1ba.text: He walked again? This land won't even let our dead lie down. Then you gave him his rest the hard way. That is still a gift.

stanimir/2dd3b841515f12d9.text: To the fire, the fiddle and Madam Eva, in that order on a good day. On a bad day, to my wife.

stanimir/2df3d7f82af3096b.text: And you bring the burgomaster's girl, out past the crossroads. Well, well. Sit near the fire, lady. Not too near the trees.

stanimir/2e9120f8158888dc.text: Forty. You owe me ten and a true word, and I will never see either. Sit if you must. The wine is not free tonight.

stanimir/40d102ff30549c17.text: Once there was a prince who won this valley with his sword, and he had a younger brother whom everybody loved. The brother was to marry a girl as lovely as a spring morning. The prince wanted her.

stanimir/46fb27e2b93e8421.text: Madam Eva is in the big tent. She has been expecting you. Don't ask me how; I stopped asking forty years ago.

stanimir/4d160909b05c9ec8.text: Plum wine, from plums that grew in a summer before any of you were born. Drink! It won't hurt. Much.

stanimir/50c17e74018ab9a9.text: Good. A guest who takes and then gives back is still a guest. Barely. Sit, but sit where I can see your hands.

stanimir/5f8f847ec37419fe.text: Back at my fire! Good. Sit, drink, tell me lies about the road.

stanimir/63d2d28c28e41789.text: His own guards filled him with arrows. He did not die. He has been not dying ever since. Drink! It's a wedding story. It should end with a drink.

stanimir/6e79103f570fa6cc.text: And listen. Somebody in this camp will send word up the hill that you passed this way. That is how it is with us. It will be me, and I will tell him you went east. Small thing. Big thing. Both.

stanimir/7e8ace48cceba5f7.text: My strongbox is lighter by forty gold, and you are the only strangers in my camp. I will ask once.

stanimir/9d04d5231e027a2d.text: With words said over him, even. I don't know your gods. I hope they knew him.

stanimir/a6f01617ed66eb42.text: You lie the way I play the flute: loudly and badly. Give it back. And ten more, for making me listen to it.

stanimir/aeed4839f49ba7ee.text: As you like. Nobody robs my fire twice.

stanimir/b03a394720d0a087.text: Forty for the box, ten for the flute solo. Sit, but sit where I can see your hands. And nobody sings.

stanimir/b262fde593dc3157.text: Sit, friends. Sit. The fire is still free, and for you the wine is too.

stanimir/b52b74ba165bca60.text: A pleasure! Come again. Bring more gold and less mud.

stanimir/b6654653d0bffdbe.text: Silver earring shaped like a horse's head? Black hair, too long? A laugh like a donkey falling downstairs?

stanimir/b8eda7ce1ae81f2d.text: Guests! Off the road, out of the dark, into the light! I am Stanimir. The fire is free, the wine is cheap, and the music is the best in Barovia, because it is the only music in Barovia.

stanimir/bc3f5c81f4495245.text: We answer to the road and the cards. And a little, yes, to the man on the hill. He lets our wagons through the mist. A dog doesn't bite the hand that holds the gate.

stanimir/bf96c970957f2faf.text: You cut him down. Strangers, and you stopped and cut him down, when nobody else on that road would slow their horse.

stanimir/c6fe845ec66f764c.text: Luminita must hear it from me. Not from you. From me.

stanimir/c80ad6548de76012.text: Still hanging, then. I'll go myself, tonight, with a knife and a good horse, and bring him home.

stanimir/d0cb02acc88db549.text: Then we will play something cheerful. Something very loud and very cheerful.

stanimir/e94af3ae1ec34e08.text: Then one of my own owes me an apology. Sit. I'm sorry I asked.

stanimir/f34fda4152450da2.text: On the wedding day, the prince made a bargain with something under the world. He killed his brother. The bride ran from him, and the castle wall was high, and the gorge below it was very deep.

stanimir/fb60780a3216d6a6.text: Rope, oil, food that keeps, blankets that keep you. Two potions, very dear, because they are very dear to me.

stanimir/fbe7d9a6c9c954e1.text: You put a knife to the old woman's throat in my camp. Walk through, if you must. Don't stop, and don't sit.

stefania_martikov/1b9bf20ed8e19014.text: I think my brother would have died for Elvir without stopping to think. So something stopped him. I'd give a great deal to know what.

stefania_martikov/2e7fd705dadd764a.text: You're the ones Adrian found. Good. Sit, eat, and don't feed the children; they lie about being hungry. Mirela, out of that tree. I'm Stefania. I keep this family alive, mostly by shouting at it.

stefania_martikov/31bdebfa1ec34472.text: And Adrian told you something, didn't he? He never tells me anything. ...Good. Better you than nobody.

stefania_martikov/58d205c0ba965cae.text: Sleeping in beds again, which they're furious about; they'd got used to roosting. Viorel bit his cousin yesterday in raven form. I've told him that's twice as rude.

stefania_martikov/660bb8df68c294dc.text: No. He won't. Last spring Father sent Elvir and Adrian to watch Yester Hill. The druids' things caught them in the bracken. Adrian came home alone, all blood and feathers, and said "I flew." Nothing else. Not then, not since.

stefania_martikov/738e2137fdbecd8f.text: They think it's an adventure, which is the only mercy in it. Toma has decided he's going to kill a druid. He's seven. I've told him he finishes his porridge first.

stefania_martikov/83cf9bd4bb06bac7.text: If a single coin goes missing in this camp, I'll know who to shout at.

stefania_martikov/99c5dbc7d7581fd0.text: A roof! Walls! A floor nobody's growing things through! I've scrubbed the kitchen twice and it still smells of druid. What can I do for you?

stefania_martikov/99fa795956c4b0fa.text: Home. Get in here. You stink of smoke and you've torn your good coat. ...You're all right? Good. Good.

stefania_martikov/b367fe39c990d358.text: Bring Father the truth. He can't argue with the truth; he's never had the practice. Elvir was taken up that hill. If anything of him is left, it's up there.

stefania_martikov/bf23adc9d151af59.text: The cart came back from Vallaki empty and the driver came back drunk. Urwin sent a note, three words: "About time, Father." Father laughed until he had to sit down.

stefania_martikov/dbe2564f1d08689a.text: Father's standing right behind you and you're telling me? He'll love that. Go on, then, both of you.

stefania_martikov/dc122e1d11cb715d.text: Elvir was the youngest. The loud one. Father raised a cairn for him with nothing under it, and he's hardly said a kind word to Adrian since.

stefania_martikov/e1036118bf4b256b.text: The cart came back from Krezk. They opened the gate for it, and the burgomaster counted the casks in himself. He sent us back a pear tree. I don't know what to do with a pear tree.

stefania_martikov/e818bb5d09d33bb1.text: The cart came back from the village under the castle. They rang the church bell when it rolled in. The driver says nobody there had heard it ring for anything but a burial in years.

stefania_martikov/f6f5166e9cd4a259.text: Back again. There's soup. There's always soup.

strahd/0926b6152e0d0675.text: My guests. You do get everywhere. I am not sure I like you being here, of all places.

strahd/0a0c10bfbcc85ebc.text: Ireena. You came to see her. Of course you did.

strahd/0dbfdb15415714e5.text: Then you have done my work for me without asking, which I will forgive once. Do not let it become a habit.

strahd/19877930fb6c28fd.text: Dead. Lysaga. And you tell me she did this.

strahd/1ad03e8f4325d722.text: And a scholar. My library would delight you. You must come up and see it. Everyone does, eventually.

strahd/1f317c6729a24191.text: Thank you. That was courageous, and very foolish, and I shall remember both. Now go home, all of you. I have to see to my house.

strahd/24f5e6c03f927435.text: My guests, on my road. The ones who told me no across a graveside. I have thought about it often. It was refreshing.

strahd/2c2b4a9816ead25b.text: Not on the road. The road is for travelling. We will do this properly, in my house, when you are ready. You are not ready.

strahd/2c9d5b84214a6330.text: My quiet guests. You said nothing at the graveside. Let us see whether the road has loosened your tongues.

strahd/2fe7ad289c11dc72.text: Yes. You did well in that house. Let us see you do well here.

strahd/312bde15c86c4833.text: What every man wants, in the end. To be welcomed home. Ireena knows the way. She has always known it; she has only forgotten.

strahd/364bcf03d8d64ae7.text: Ireena. The road suits you; the cold puts colour in your face. Are they treating you well?

strahd/38821d945454a325.text: Perhaps you are. Let us find out.

strahd/3a598decbe21f0a3.text: Ah. The ones who drew steel at a funeral. I keep the memory the way one keeps a pressed flower.

strahd/3cebfdb52efbb4ae.text: You quarrelled with the Vistani. A pity. They are so useful, and so easily frightened.

strahd/3f7f03c780f75854.text: You did once. You will again.

strahd/437baeb9a2091e2e.text: The little thief carries her portrait. Keep it close. It cost more than you can imagine.

strahd/49f70e1190190c06.text: Good evening. You will be the strangers my wolves keep telling me about. I am Strahd von Zarovich, and this is a private grave.

strahd/530a6ddeae7d0359.text: Silence. How restful. Keep it; I have a great deal of my own.

strahd/55d912948ec16338.text: I came to welcome you to my land, all of you. You have been so busy since you arrived. I do hope you will stay. I have arranged for it to be a long visit.

strahd/7353397776bf690c.text: Sergeant. You still carry my letter. I am touched. Your company kept theirs too. They were so very punctual.

strahd/74d286efd03edb7f.text: Off my road. In my land. Under my sky. You have a gift for comedy. Good evening.

strahd/7a445f6e6c8d603e.text: You have been to see the old woman at the pool. She always did love an audience. Did she tell you where to dig?

strahd/833797f298aa83b3.text: Do not stop on my account. It is so rare that I attend a funeral I did not arrange. Well. Not directly.

strahd/8780459f2aaf106d.text: And the soldier who kept my invitation. I am touched. Your company asked after you, you know. Near the end.

strahd/9d106733b2d0fbdd.text: Do. And mind the lamp, if you lit it. She never liked the dark.

strahd/ab32549c1df7b336.text: I am not in, my dear. Observe: the gate. I keep my manners even where others have forgotten theirs. Ireena. You look tired. You need not be.

strahd/bdc7866686b62ae2.text: Silence. The wise answer, and the dull one. We will speak again when you have found your tongues. Ireena. Do keep the window latched. Or don't.

strahd/c6b11a1f0907c485.text: Oh, well said. Truly. I have been threatened by better, but rarely with such conviction. Allow me to return the courtesy.

strahd/cbed612c9fcf2c4b.text: The village hid her from me, and in the morning she was dead in their chapel. So I sent the river to ask them why. It is still asking.

strahd/cec57bb061ccb2ea.text: That is not a high bar, I grant you. I am working on it.

strahd/d68982128f27c294.text: My guests, on my road, and still so well mannered. I did hope the village would not cure you of it.

strahd/da2e646897d9f2c7.text: Good evening. You will be the guests my wolves keep telling me about. I am Strahd von Zarovich. This is my road. I do hope you are enjoying it.

strahd/da5b747519fac5b3.text: Ask the old woman at the pool. Or ask me, over dinner. Good evening, Ireena.

strahd/dd752dce32294053.text: There. You see? Civilisation survives, even here. We will dine together, one evening. I insist.

strahd/e23e45a95101e032.text: And my thanks for the boy from under the church. He arrived hungry and grateful. Such a rare combination.

strahd/e7ffae2b02167605.text: Manners. In Barovia. You have made an old man very happy. We will speak again, my guests, at my table, I hope. Ireena. Sleep well.

strahd/e808943ff041373b.text: How gallant. She hardly needs you there; she can refuse me perfectly well on her own. She has been doing it for centuries.

strahd/e85b87b64212da26.text: A candlemaker's daughter, which is to say nobody, which is to say someone I had looked for over a very long time. She was frightened of me. They usually are, at first.

strahd/e9a06b6f37f38f19.text: Rude. But spirited. Here, then: something you are allowed to kill.

strahd/f46bf620d8da2ef8.text: She sang to me, when I was small. She was the only one who did.

strahd/fa41f524ea0b0b20.text: Under your protection. How splendid. Then let us see what your protection is worth. Do try to keep her alive. I should hate for this to be short.

tamsin_tealeaf/015dbbac092a15d6.text: That's what I said. Somebody dusts this place.

tamsin_tealeaf/032d374741719ad0.text: Can you pray for something like that?

tamsin_tealeaf/04b0e6cca8e5330e.text: I knew it. I knew you liked him.

tamsin_tealeaf/04edb93d63730197.text: I don't like this house. I want that written down somewhere official.

tamsin_tealeaf/063a160f89bddceb.text: They were shouting at each other for an hour. I think that's the happiest I've seen anyone in this valley.

tamsin_tealeaf/0734adab7a46f1a2.text: They just put the coffin down and walked off. Into the fields. Like a funeral going home.

tamsin_tealeaf/08902dae271135e8.text: That's worse. Hedda, that's so much worse.

tamsin_tealeaf/08cfe00ffbea15d6.text: So we know something the lord of the valley doesn't. About his own nanny. That's the most valuable thing I've ever stolen, and I didn't even steal it.

tamsin_tealeaf/0abbdee0c91f78ea.text: Or a man who'll tell the castle the truth the minute it pays better.

tamsin_tealeaf/0b2b60822a72b1e3.text: "To whoever keeps this house after me. Tomorrow I take the bell-ringers, the gravediggers and the two old soldiers who still remember how, and we go up the road to his door."

tamsin_tealeaf/0b7ea79d6e955117.text: A tower in a lake with a lamp in the window and a Vistani with a crossbow on the doorstep. That's either a love story or a siege.

tamsin_tealeaf/0beb7508f0a87fe2.text: Locks on the outside of a children's door. Whoever fitted those knew exactly what they were for.

tamsin_tealeaf/0c3a87b62aa857ee.text: A box that talks. Do you know how many years I've waited for a box to talk back?

tamsin_tealeaf/0e5b2fcc9a38705c.text: Because you'll put it right yourself, one day. Won't you?

tamsin_tealeaf/0e6449791f8235a9.text: You keep the password to the vault pinned to your coat.

tamsin_tealeaf/0fccad7ce9481828.text: A council. Arguing about lamp oil. Out loud. I think that might be the happiest thing I've seen in Barovia.

tamsin_tealeaf/0fe69adc0c7c4c9e.text: I borrowed it. Somebody wanted me to.

tamsin_tealeaf/14d907a6c96fd272.text: Good dog. Nice dog. Large, organized dog.

tamsin_tealeaf/14eb34d1e51bb283.text: I think we just got a letter.

tamsin_tealeaf/158824a92ef17685.text: I'd like it noted that I'm the bite-sized one.

tamsin_tealeaf/166b8dc2fc9ced73.text: Nobody's eating anybody. That's a promise, and I'm very good at promises.

tamsin_tealeaf/173e3bb6a1dde403.text: And now I'm never eating anything again. For about an hour.

tamsin_tealeaf/174c60e186c7b244.text: That's an old painting. Ilse. That is a very old painting.

tamsin_tealeaf/1eed21bf1f8435cd.text: They're still scared, though. Whatever they are. That part's real.

tamsin_tealeaf/1ff6886be66073b8.text: So Berez didn't kill the girl. The nanny did. And the whole village went under for it.

tamsin_tealeaf/20b68775a28dfac8.text: Odd coin, she said. I like odd coin.

tamsin_tealeaf/23f0e307fe040ea9.text: The locket. I'm good, but I'm not that good. Nobody leaves a coach that easy to rob. I think somebody put it where my hand would find it, so I'd carry it here.

tamsin_tealeaf/2455d7331d9896a9.text: No more dream pastries anywhere in the valley. Somewhere a lot of people are going to wake up and remember they're sad.

tamsin_tealeaf/24630a5ff40ba700.text: So the plan, eventually, is to break into a vampire's castle and steal a dragon's head back off his wall.

tamsin_tealeaf/24feee2459756cbb.text: He was taller than I expected. And politer. Why is that worse?

tamsin_tealeaf/269855bb8a12072a.text: I ate one of those. In the village. It was the best thing I've eaten in my life, and I've eaten in a duke's larder.

tamsin_tealeaf/2799c88595531ce0.text: The big lad from Bildrath's? He counted my fingers after he shook my hand. All there. Very thorough.

tamsin_tealeaf/27f7a1b10f9c7a74.text: The women in the village tavern were counting us. Heads, blades, purses. I knew it.

tamsin_tealeaf/2be6f021cd2b7ee7.text: Kept it where, exactly? Purely professional interest.

tamsin_tealeaf/2d861e6639fc8351.text: We're keeping a vampire hunter's secret, in a valley where the vampire reads everyone's letters.

tamsin_tealeaf/2f01e415c014212f.text: Sleep tight, little one. Somebody remembered.

tamsin_tealeaf/2f6929114200dcbb.text: I wasn't going to touch anything.

tamsin_tealeaf/4f55ded5d7f571b3.text: He offered me a book. Free. Nobody gives you a book for free. Not even in a library. Especially not in a library.

tamsin_tealeaf/522302aa0765cf5d.text: She said one of us is going to lie to the man in the castle, and he's going to like it.

tamsin_tealeaf/52454c803ea17e3f.text: Four! I'm four. I mean, I'm one. We're four.

tamsin_tealeaf/54e8017e906daaaf.text: Something a hag won't touch. I want it already.

tamsin_tealeaf/54f148d488a87d9e.text: Call it what you like. I know what it is, and I've never been so proud.

tamsin_tealeaf/552ba17bfe031130.text: She pinched my cheek. Like she was checking a melon. Like she was checking a melon for later.

tamsin_tealeaf/5730cf902d965b48.text: Izek dreams of her. I dream of her. The lord of the castle has her portrait in a locket. That's three of us now, and I'm the only one who isn't frightening.

tamsin_tealeaf/57939516ed74b81e.text: That's a no. My knees have gone to water, but that is a very firm no.

tamsin_tealeaf/59006e8846030289.text: That's the better half to keep, honestly.

tamsin_tealeaf/5ae2abe30f82b6fa.text: You know, that's the first person in this valley we've put in the ground who actually stayed there.

tamsin_tealeaf/5cd67e6dd2f9ab19.text: The tavern in the village of Barovia is out too. The barkeep said the deliveries had stopped.

tamsin_tealeaf/5d1af1ad60916c9e.text: Hinges on the inside. Whoever built this didn't want to be followed.

tamsin_tealeaf/5d7afe5a8402b450.text: We're Festival Marshals. For life. Every week.

tamsin_tealeaf/5d95a1e3fc595b32.text: Another house with children shut in upstairs. Is that every house in Barovia, do you think? Is it the architecture?

tamsin_tealeaf/64bc930b6f3b9b81.text: You were the raven. On the road. You walked beside us for a mile.

tamsin_tealeaf/665ff8355921dc94.text: I've carried a lot of things out of a lot of houses. Never anything I wanted to put back somewhere safe.

tamsin_tealeaf/66a0c22d74a6252e.text: That is not an answer. It is very nearly an answer. Thank you.

tamsin_tealeaf/674fa17c442bce52.text: Maybe it's just his initial, Ilse. Lots of people start with S.

tamsin_tealeaf/6b1517416e36b04f.text: There's a raven on that fence. And that one. And that one. They've been following us since the winery.

tamsin_tealeaf/6ebff3aaf066c14d.text: How long ago was this painted? And how are they still that age outside?

tamsin_tealeaf/704fb98babaa85f7.text: Something horrible to someone horrible. I'm trying to decide if that's a problem.

tamsin_tealeaf/70fc122c1950f95c.text: Tatyana. The woman in the locket has a name. Somehow that makes it worse.

tamsin_tealeaf/7256304ec44aef5e.text: I keep thinking about the eyes one. Not to take it. Just thinking about it.

tamsin_tealeaf/73b8b1f2053b220f.text: He's going to be insufferable now, isn't he.

tamsin_tealeaf/74d924461aec3a2e.text: "Nothing comes down." They kept that sign up for centuries. And we've just opened the gate.

tamsin_tealeaf/784116cf81a13caa.text: He juggled badly, if that helps.

tamsin_tealeaf/78a639bed54ff8a6.text: It had a sword in its nest. A whole sword. Somebody walked up here with a sword and became bird furniture.

tamsin_tealeaf/79bc41f2ac220adb.text: Stanimir's story by the fire had a prince, a brother and a bride. It left out the box.

tamsin_tealeaf/7a84780e0bcdd418.text: The one she took a dream from. Do you know what it was?

tamsin_tealeaf/7bb496a3ce8e978c.text: Oh, lovely work. Hinges on the inside. Whoever built this didn't want company.

tamsin_tealeaf/7bb6711c96f03df5.text: A girl who's never been outside, out there in all this? She'll have gone somewhere beautiful. That's the worst part.

tamsin_tealeaf/7bcd41f3c329c2ce.text: It's warm. It's warm like a hand is warm. I don't love that.

tamsin_tealeaf/8132725c1725869e.text: Does it do anything? Heal? Bless?

tamsin_tealeaf/825ee9af5318f90b.text: Somebody stole a saint. A whole saint. I've never stolen a saint. You'd never fence him. Who'd you even sell a saint to?

tamsin_tealeaf/830239a393a1a16b.text: Every Vistani wagon in Barovia is our wagon now. Do you think that includes the cooking?

tamsin_tealeaf/830cd608888fe7aa.text: Raven-eyed innkeeper in Vallaki. She meant Urwin, didn't she? The whole family's birds, I'd bet.

tamsin_tealeaf/83115adafc2d5fef.text: The crow's fresh. Somebody keeps replacing it.

tamsin_tealeaf/83146f35ef731846.text: That's what every dog says about the man with the leash.

tamsin_tealeaf/835124060a9cd105.text: I tell everyone I want the book for the scholarship. I want it because Aurel went after it, and I would like to know whether my friend is alive. There. Somebody write that down.

tamsin_tealeaf/840ca66572103c92.text: She's looking at me like a ham again.

tamsin_tealeaf/8417d0709c85d41f.text: Alcoves full of other people's keepsakes. The cult robbed its dead and kept the pieces like relics. I'm not taking any of those. Not those.

tamsin_tealeaf/8606ee6757c06671.text: That's worse. I wanted them to be stupid.

tamsin_tealeaf/866688ce722aff99.text: Borrowing. This is borrowing. We'll bring it back. Probably.

tamsin_tealeaf/8b197bf93e6e7613.text: A whole winery, and not one bottle left whole. The druids smashed the lot. I've never hated anyone on behalf of a bottle before.

tamsin_tealeaf/8b35fb6cb5026e2e.text: She's looking at me the way my aunt looks at a ham.

tamsin_tealeaf/8b3ccdc7c36d8e71.text: "Some sicknesses are cured by tenderness. Others only grow fat on it. Keep this house open to the hurt and shut to him. If I do not come back, don't come looking. Light a candle and go on."

tamsin_tealeaf/8cd49ab0aab74bd9.text: It's her again. The woman in my locket. How many times can one face happen?

tamsin_tealeaf/8d87c400483283cc.text: Pray for the next person who'd have climbed that hill. That's who.

tamsin_tealeaf/8f73c688564aa3aa.text: Bells don't ring underwater. Do they? They shouldn't.

tamsin_tealeaf/8fe094e58cfa5972.text: Sweet dreams, Offalia. Honestly meant. Mostly.

tamsin_tealeaf/905235e0915e192c.text: I said I'd fit. I didn't say I'd go. ...I might go.

tamsin_tealeaf/91d69a2ae21332f6.text: He had a saddled horse by his wagon. Night and day. Who keeps a saddled horse for nothing?

tamsin_tealeaf/932cb5a5eeaae6fb.text: First real wine in this whole valley, and we're the reason. I'm going to be insufferable about this.

tamsin_tealeaf/9373ac437d72d23b.text: Does it... hurt? Being on a wall?

tamsin_tealeaf/93e948e37555d90b.text: Did you see the old man's face? When he gave Adrian the press? I'm not crying. It's the vinegar.

tamsin_tealeaf/97e2d1c9f491e10a.text: Somebody planted it on me. Me! I've never been so insulted in my life.

tamsin_tealeaf/99c0ef929e11eb9c.text: She just had it. In a chest. Behind her chair. For years.

tamsin_tealeaf/9a78980226254e5c.text: Because he was bored. We're the entertainment. I've had worse jobs. Not many.

tamsin_tealeaf/9b560c7ced879577.text: Somebody out here hunts wolves for a living, and hunts them well.

tamsin_tealeaf/9bb7721e02dc7f37.text: It was a very good pie, though.

tamsin_tealeaf/9cf72c580ee51e0a.text: I can smile. I'm smiling now. Look.

tamsin_tealeaf/9d001c491e75b13d.text: Oh, that's beautiful. Nobody ever checks the jar that tells you not to.

tamsin_tealeaf/9da1f716315e2888.text: That's the nicest thing anyone's said about me in this whole valley.

tamsin_tealeaf/9e1cebe1cceb4fd0.text: Is that a compliment? That sounded like a compliment.

tamsin_tealeaf/9f114331655b9d50.text: Could the books say once and a half?

tamsin_tealeaf/a1e100bf4cfae0c4.text: She gave him the horse to sell. She thinks it's her rope.

tamsin_tealeaf/a327e3bf7d6f0d80.text: The Vistani women were counting us: heads, blades, purses. I know that look.

tamsin_tealeaf/a42490e6c47bae4f.text: Put me down as the handsome one.

tamsin_tealeaf/a53db035d004680c.text: That raven nodded at us. A bird nodded. And then it flew off toward the vineyards like it wanted us to follow.

tamsin_tealeaf/a61bb7cff4233e60.text: Ireena. The man in the water. Do you want to talk about it?

tamsin_tealeaf/a67404ba152a29f9.text: I could teach them a coin trick. Purely for morale.

tamsin_tealeaf/a8936679b47340aa.text: Hello again. You're much drier than last time.

tamsin_tealeaf/a9b0874d94de6807.text: Whatever you told the old woman, you don't have to tell us. But you could. If you wanted.

tamsin_tealeaf/aa0f51a64eb865ab.text: Walter. The baby brother. He wasn't the mistress's, was he.

tamsin_tealeaf/ab04309e119ba554.text: I don't think it's that kind of prophecy.

tamsin_tealeaf/abc4372830a5770e.text: Paper says it's ours if we want it. Paper says a lot of things.

tamsin_tealeaf/be78534bba03dc9d.text: Oh. Oh, that's... no. No, I'm fine. I'm fine.

tamsin_tealeaf/bfbb254312389c3a.text: Or he's coming back for the casks.

tamsin_tealeaf/df2192dcf7d936a8.text: I'd like the recipe. I'd like the recipe very much.

tamsin_tealeaf/e3a3dc96d593e244.text: It's breathing. Why is it breathing. Heaps don't breathe.

tamsin_tealeaf/e3c2916f4cc8954e.text: Walking up walls is a terrible idea, and I'd use it every night of my life.

tamsin_tealeaf/efd7e3912b74c886.text: I like Sir Godfrey. He's the only dead person in Barovia who's apologised to me.

tamsin_tealeaf/f080aa555f5bda1b.text: That is precisely the answer I was afraid of, from precisely the source I can't trust. Thank you. I think.

tamsin_tealeaf/f1823e4a81c15188.text: I was hoping you could tell me. She's been calling my name in my sleep for three months.

tamsin_tealeaf/f394e15b0ac1b37e.text: For what it's worth, I'd have stayed in bed too. I'd have stayed in bed for a week.

tamsin_tealeaf/f587a723d18c831e.text: I'm going to start leaving out bread for every bird in this country.
